On certain occasions, Adrien (as Cat Noir) can be hasty sometimes, evidently when rushing to face certain akumatized villains without a plan.
Due to this rashness, he often needs to be restrained or stopped by Ladybug or at one point Master Fu.
This recklessness is exacerbated by his anger and fear of losing those dear to him or becoming useless to them, which blinds him from the consequences of his actions.
This caused Cat Noir to harshly renounce his Miraculous in "Kuro Neko", not realizing that Ladybug shouted at him not to waste her time because she was stressed as the Guardian and that they should talk again after they both calmed down; furthermore, he left his Miraculous abandoned on a roof, which had a chance of being stolen, especially if Shadow Moth lurked around like he did in "Sentibubbler".
At times, Adrien can be persistent and curious about his Miraculous powers or when wanting to figure something out, as seen when he continuously bribed Plagg with cheese until he spilled the truth about what Ladybug was hiding.

Nevertheless, he knows that his mother is dead, which is why he told his father it was fine with him wanting to pursue a romantic relationship with Nathalie, showing that he has more fortitude than his father; Adrien, despite being in the dark, accepted her passing and it didn't lead him down a dark path like his father or counterpart.
Adrien knew that he would have his father, Nathalie, and some friends to have all the love he needs to be happy; while he did confess of being tempted to use the wish to reunite with his mother, he knew he would need to sacrifice another person and that the price was too high; furthermore, when proposing to use the wish to get rid of Monarch and all the bad things in the world, upon Ladybug's explanation that the wish would simply cause these calamities in another way to maintain balance, he quickly accepted the fact and immediately gave up.

Similar to Chloé, it's also understandable as to why Adrien hates secrets because of his father and possibly mother as he had to live his whole life as one big secret as he was homeschooled meaning he was unable to interact with anyone else beside her.

In "Kuro Neko", believing if he reinvented himself as Cat Walker things would change.

Much of his exaggerated personality, especially his flirtatious behavior with Ladybug, stems from entertainment such as anime, television, and movies due to his lack of experience with people his age beyond Chloé.

As a Civilian

Other than fencing, Adrien does Karate and Kung Fu, which enables him to fight in hand-to-hand combat and briefly fight his akuma-controlled bodyguard. Furthermore, Adrien takes basketball lessons.

This was also seen in "Miraculous Paris" as Cat Noir tricked and surprised Claw Noir multiple times before Claw Noir stole the Cat Miraculous from him. He also tricked Ladybug (and indirectly the suspicious Hawk Moth) into believing he wasn't Adrien in "Gorizilla".

In "Copycat", he learned who the fake Cat Noir was, where he may be, and suggested a way to defeat him. Cat Noir has enhanced physical skills such as superhuman speed, agility, and near-invulnerability. These abilities allow him to react to and evade light-based attacks, as well as jump and leap several times his height and length. Like a cat, Cat Noir has enhanced senses such as hearing, smell, night vision, and super stealth, which he sometimes uses to find opponents. Also, like a cat, he can use his claws to climb up surfaces or use them to cut through things.

Adrien Agreste - Abilities
He is fast enough to outrun a pair of panthers, being capable of running at least between 35-50 mph. His increased strength allows him to do things such as being able to over shoulder throw his own bodyguard into an elevator, use his staff as a lever to knock over a city bus, roundhouse kick, punch and stomp vending machines and kitchen appliances with just one strike. His increased stamina, durability, and endurance allow him to survive being smashed into a series of cars, a face-plant into a traffic pole, falling several stories, being flung by Gigantitan, and take a crash landing through André's ice cream stand without being dazed or injured. He has even survived attacks from Ikari Gozen and Bakerix, both of whom are akumatized villains who are strong enough to lift and throw around entire city buses. He also has good hand-to-hand combat skills when needed. Even out of "Aqua Mode", Cat Noir is a good swimmer. He can even handle temperatures as severe as absolute 0.

Adrien Agreste - Abilities
Cat Noir has remarkable talent with wielding his tool, the staff, wielding it as a sword, throwing it with great precision, and having it be deflected back to him. He is able to spin it at high speeds to form a shield or take advantage of its duplication and length-changing features. To travel long distances, he uses his staff and its variety in length to vault over obstacles. In and out of "Aqua Mode", he can also use his staff as a breathing apparatus for those who can't breathe underwater.
His special power, Cataclysm, allows him to negatively affect and essentially destroy anything that he touches with his ring hand. While it is usually used for object destruction, it can be used for a variety of different effects, for example, causing a bus's controls to go haywire and creating a platform in a structure. However, like other superheroes, using Cataclysm drains his Miraculous power, causing him to revert back to Adrien five minutes afterward. But, after the events of "Revolution", that is no longer the case, as he has learned to control his adult powers, allowing him to use Cataclysm as much as he wants without transforming back.

title: Adrien Agreste

text:
Adrien Agreste - Etymology
The name Adrien comes from the Roman cognomen "Hadrianus", which means "from Hadria". In the days of the Roman Empire, Hadria was a town in northern Italy and the namesake of the Adriatic Sea. The Adriatic Sea is known for the dark-colored sand on its beaches, and for this reason, the name is also commonly translated as "dark one".
This might reference the dark coloring of Adrien's suit as Cat Noir.
His last name Agreste means "rural" in French. It is also the French name for the grayling butterfly. Hence, his full name may be taken as meaning "dark butterfly".
His name's meaning, "dark butterfly", is a reference to his father's alter ego, Hawk Moth, and the dark butterflies (Akumas) he uses to akumatize people.
The name "Chat Noir" is French for "Black Cat". Some sources have called him "Black Cat" instead of Chat Noir or Cat Noir.
The reason for that change is that the partners at Disney thought that calling him "Chat Noir" might be confusing for young children, while translating it to "Black Cat" isn't very original.

title: Adrien Agreste
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste - Etymology
In many of the dubs (including the Korean, Bulgarian, Czech, Hungarian, Polish, Romanian, Arabic, Turkish, Hebrew, Slovene, Croatian, Serbian, Vietnamese, and Mongolian dubs) Adrien's superhero name is "Black Cat".
In the Russian and Ukrainian dubs, Adrien's superhero name is "Super Cat".
In the European Portuguese version, Adrien's superhero name is "Gato Noir", which, like "Cat Noir", is a mix of Portuguese and French, as "Gato" means "Cat" in Portuguese.
The name Cat Blanc is French for "White Cat" which refers to how in "Cat Blanc", where he was left in an empty blank world after his powers went wild during his akumatization.
Aspik's name is a version of aspic, the French word for "asp", an archaic name for venomous snakes that inhabited the Nile region that is believed to refer to the Egyptian cobra.
Snake Noir's name translates to "Black Snake" which refers to a species of snake that lives in North America.
The name Cat Walker comes from 'catwalk', a term used for the motions and poses done by models on the runway during a fashion show. That's because Adrien as Cat Walker uses the same perfect, gentlemanly golden child persona as in his civilian life.

title: Adrien Agreste
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste - Etymology
In the French dub, his name is instead Patte de Velours (Velvet Paw), which is a slang term for a declawed cat. This is likely meant to reference that he is "declawing" his personality to be a more dependable partner by putting on the persona he uses in his civilian form rather than the Cat Noir persona he feels more comfortable using. This could also double as a reference to the phrase "faire patte de velours", meaning to disguise one's true feelings under a kind attitude.
Rabbit Noir means "Black Rabbit" in French. In the terms of symbolism, the black rabbit means many things, including insecurities, fear of intimacy, lies, or weakening or disappointing relationships – such as the ones Adrien has with family and friends shown continuously throughout the series, especially in the fifth season.
Trionyx means genus of softshell turtles.

title: Adrien Agreste
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste - Development
The earliest known appearance of Cat Noir was on the fake cover of issue #12 of The Mini Menace Ladybug.
Cat Noir's civilian self was originally a character called Félix.
Fans originally called him this, after a famous cartoon cat. For some time, this name appeared on the original French version of Zagtoon's official website, but later disappeared with newer, equally reliable sources calling him "Adrien".
His design included more formal clothing with black and gray colors, desaturated green eyes, and a tidier hairstyle. As Cat Noir, Félix's hair was much longer in a shaggy bob style and he wore higher boots.
Félix-Cat Noir didn't have a staff for a weapon.
His personality differed from current Adrien's – Félix was less social, not openly friendly, and unkind to Marinette.
Adrien was created around 2012.
As opposed to the show's current conceptualization of the how Miraculouses work, when PV Félix was Cat Noir, his ring could not come off unless he got a kiss from Ladybug. In addition, while wearing the ring, Félix was cursed to have bad luck.

title: Adrien Agreste
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste - Development
Because Félix was Cat Noir in the Ladybug PV, Adrien was never seen in 2D form until the Miraculous: Tales from Paris webisodes. He will be seen again in 2D in the Miraculous Ladybug OVA, as Adrien is confirmed to still be Cat Noir instead of Félix.
In the "Art of the Miraculous", Cat Noir's powers included Black Storm and Black Hole.
Adrien was originally supposed to be disabled, and use a crutch. However, the producers and the broadcasters didn't trust themselves to write him well, so the idea was scrapped, and the crutch later became Cat Noir's staff.

text:
Adrien Agreste - Trivia
Cat Noir admitted that Marinette was the first girl who ever told him she was in love with him in "Weredad".
According to Gabriel Agreste's voice actor, Adrien is not allowed to play Pokémon Go.
Miraculous Holder and Akumatized Villain
Cat Noir's ears and tail are parts of his costume, however, they can move and respond to his mood and senses.
During "Dark Cupid", when Cat Noir isn't able to confess to Ladybug because their transformations are about to run out, his ears move down.
In "Animan" and "Troublemaker", his cat ears move when he hears the akumatized villains approaching.
In "Anansi", he seems to react with discomfort when the titular villain pulls at his ears.
In "Mega Leech", Malediktator's miniature clones access his brain through his faux-cat ears, not his human ears.
The bell of Cat Noir's costume functions as a zipper and was added "because it looks cute".
The bell is a reference to a domestic kitten, conveying his inner desire for a loving home.
He and Cat Noir don't appear in some episodes of the show:
Adrien doesn't appear in "Prime Queen", "Christmaster", "Furious Fu", "Qilin" and "Evolution" – he is transformed into Cat Noir the entire time.

title: Adrien Agreste
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste - Trivia
Cat Noir doesn't appear in "Style Queen", "Mr. Pigeon 72", "Transmission", "Emotion" and "Conformation", since Adrien is unable to transform for different reasons.
Out of all members of the Miraculers, Adrien/Cat Noir has been affected the most by akumatized villains' powers.
However, this is mostly because he either protected Ladybug or sacrificed so she could find a solution and because the other heroes were not nearly as active as the former two.
Ironically, Adrien is the only member to not have been directly akumatized or infected with an akuma in the permanent timeline.
Mister Bug mentions in "Reflekdoll" that he always wanted to capture an akuma with Ladybug's powers.
Adrien is the only character in the show whose akumatizations all occurred in alternate, erased timelines.
Cat Blanc holds the record for the highest kill count in the series, since his Mega Cataclysm destroyed all inhabitants of Earth, as well as the record for the longest time a person has been akumatized – a few months.
Thanks to Ladybug and Bunnyx, the timeline was rewritten and those events were erased.

title: Adrien Agreste
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste - Trivia
Interestingly, Cat Noir's nightmare in "Representation" is eerily similar to the events of "Cat Blanc", down to his Cat Blanc-like dream akumatized form: Anticat.
Of all Miraculous holders, Adrien has used the second-most Miraculouses – the Black Cat's, the Ladybug's, the Snake's and the Rabbit's. He also has the second-most Miraculous transformations, with a total of six.
When it comes to the Ladybug Miraculous the second male to use it following Micazoyolin.
He is tied with Marinette as the fifth person of French origins to a Miraculous overall following Jeanne d'Arc, Aramis, Gilbert and his father
And the first male person of French origins to wield the Ladybug, Cat and Snake Miraculouses.
Is the second person of English origins to wield the Cat Miraculous following Dark Grimalkin but the third overall to use one following Dark Grimalkin and his mother.
Overall in the first, known person of English origins to use the Ladybug, Snake and the Rabbit Miraculouses.
Adrien is the only member of his family to actually be chosen by a guardian (Master Fu) to wield a Miraculous.

title: Adrien Agreste
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste - Trivia
And the only member of his family not to have ever been struck with permanent damage caused by using Miraculouses and their powers.
Out of his extended family (including his adoptive mother Nathalie), Adrien, his grandfathers and his maternal grandmother Gabrielle are the only ones to not have been akumatized or partially akumatized in the permanent timeline (not counting Émilie or Colt).
Adrien is the first known sentimonster to use a Miraculous.
He is tied with Félix and Kagami as the oldest still existing sentimonster, after the 172-year-old dormant sentimonster/Feast.
After Season 5, he is the fourth known Sentimonster to have control of himself, following Kagami, Félix, and the Dormant Sentimonster.
Currently, only five characters know Adrien is Cat Noir: Luka, Alix, Aeon, Re-Verse Adrien and Re-Verse Marinette.
The count rises to ten if it includes kwamis like Plagg, Tikki, Wayzz, Kaalki, and Fluff.

Sass might also know from being used by Adrien as Aspik in "Desperada" and later being unified Cat Noir with Plagg so he could become Snake Noir in "Miracle Queen", in addition to possibly finding out his identity through Luka/Viperion in "Wishmaker", making the count rise to eleven.

Miscellaneous

title: Adrien Agreste

text:
Adrien Agreste - Trivia
Cat Noir has displayed many feline behaviors throughout the series – caressing his tail after it being pulled, responding positively to his chin being scratched, cleaning himself by licking water off after getting wet, purring, growling at villains, running on all fours during battles, and so on.
Cat Noir often comes to the Grand Paris hotel to ask for some glasses of milk when he's feeling down, as shown in "Lies".
However, cats can actually die from drinking too much milk, so he is technically endangering his own life.
Cat Blanc made a brief reappearance in "Sentibubbler" as one of the people terrorizing Marinette in her nightmare.
As of Season 6 Adrien's hair is combed downwards and more natural compared to his hairstyle in Seasons 1-5 which was more swept and styled, symbolising how he is now free and can be himself, and no longer has to represent the "perfect image" his father wanted.
The episode "Destruction" reveals that Cat Noir carried a silly message written on a piece of paper inside his bell for a long time as part of a plan Ladybug made in case Monarch discovered where she lives.

title: Adrien Agreste
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste - Trivia
Before this information was confirmed in "Representation", there've been hints throughout the show suggesting that Adrien is a sentimonster:
Adrien's appearance has all of his mother's genetic traits, such as the colors of his skin, eyes and hair, but he doesn't have any genetic traits of Gabriel.
He is always very obedient towards his father, even in small situations.
In "Ladybug & Cat Noir", Gabriel tells his son that he "is not like anyone else" after Adrien complains about not being allowed to go to school and make friends.
In "Simon Says", Gabriel states that Adrien is "the image of perfection" while showing a frame with his picture to Ladybug.
The commercial for Adrien the Fragrance (first seen in "Gorizilla") includes feathers around his pose.
In "Ladybug", when Ladybug gave the titular sentimonster freedom, Cat Noir made an awkward shocked face.
Also, in the episode's end card, an amok was placed near Adrien.
In the erased timeline in "Cat Blanc", when Hawkmoth infected Cat Noir with an akuma, the later tried to resist despite the emotional stress he was in, and only succumbed after Hawkmoth explicitly told him "Obey!".

title: Adrien Agreste

text:
Adrien Agreste - Trivia
In "Félix" and "Risk", Félix criticized Adrien for always doing what his father told him to, and not being free enough.
In multiple episodes of season 4 (such as "Mega Leech" and "Ephemeral"), Adrien does as he is told by his father after the man rubs his wedding ring, just like how sentimonters can be controlled using their amokized objects.
In "Gabriel Agreste", when Félix gave one of the twin rings' copy to his uncle, Gabriel burst into anger claiming that he knows every and each scratch from Émilie's ring, finding out that it was actually a fake one.
When Gabriel entrusted one of the Graham de Vanily Twin Rings to Nathalie in "Risk", he said that he was entrusting his son along with it.
In "Wishmaker", Adrien/Cat Noir's childhood dream, exposed by the titular villain, is very simple, unlike those of the villain's other victims.
In "Emotion", when Argos created his new free world after making everyone disappear, Adrien was one of the only three remaining people in Paris.
In "Representation", when Adrien escaped from London to see Marinette in Paris, Gabriel retrieved the ring from Nathalie, saying that he would only obey him.

Adrien Agreste is one of the two titular main protagonists (alongside Marinette Dupain-Cheng) of "Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie". He is a student in Collège Françoise Dupont.
With the Cat Miraculous, when inhabited by Plagg, Adrien transforms into Cat Noir ("Chat Noir" in the French version), a black cat-themed superhero with the power of Destruction to stop Hawk Moth and his Akumatized villains.

title: Adrien Agreste/Movie
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Adrien is a teenage boy of medium height with green eyes, blond hair, and tanned skin.
Civilian Attire
He wears a white jacket with a black T-shirt with three stripes across his upper torso. He also wears a pair of blue jeans and is often seen with black earbuds. He wears a white and black wristwatch on his right wrist.
As Cat Noir
As Cat Noir, Adrien's hair becomes wild, untamed and longer covering his normal ears and his normal eyes to switch to cat eyes. He wears an all black jumpsuit with two black cat ears sticking out the top of his head, a black mask and when during a close up his mask are covered in white sparkles and a long black belt that acts like a cat's tail. His stick is commonly attached to his waist.

text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie - Personality
Due to his mother's death, Adrien is emotionally distant from others likely out of fear of intimacy just to lose them again, but due to him having more of a life outside of the mansion he is a bit more confident, outspoken and willing to ask for advice such as how to approach a girl. Over time he begins to open up towards others especially Marinette about his mother. However, he's not as naive as his TV counterpart accepting that his father is emotionally gone.
As Cat Noir, Adrien is more goofy, such as teasing Ladybug for her suit. He is also more cocky than his show counterpart, calling Ladybug his sidekick as well as for celebrating too soon when it came to their first battle. But he quickly humbles himself when admitting he needs help and also tends to take advice from others. His affection for Ladybug like his tv show counterpart still remains yet he showed more subtly and he is less hesitant on using his powers on others such as Hawk Moth.

As Cat Noir
As his alterego, he has enhanced physical abilities, such as being able to jump great lengths in a single bound as he did in Notre Dome as well as rooftop to rooftop effortlessly, skilled in hand to hand combat as an seen when sparring with Ladybug, has an observant eye and special power Cataclysm.

Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Ladybug
At first, he meets Marinette while she is hiding the library noticing that she was looking sad, he asked if she was ok and helped her to her feet after she tripped then quickly left the library commenting that she was weird. Then, they meet again at the carnival fair where he was fascinated over Marinette's designs and how much she enjoys her parents but their conversation was cut short by their fathers. Over the months they bond more becoming friends, to the point where he talks with her about his mother.
After his rejection by Ladybug, the next day at school, he was asked by Marinette if he'd go to the winter ball with her but just like the heroine he tells Marinette that he is in love with someone else too. After his father has possibly been arrested, at the Winter Ball, Adrien was happy that the world was at peace but he missed Ladybug that is until he was approached by Marinette calling him by his hero name watching her put on his mask, she unveils herself as his heroine partner causing Adrien to cry in tears of joy that he had found the girl he loves as they share a kiss.

As their alter-egos, Cat Noir meets Ladybug for the first time when she accidentally crashed into him through the stained glass window of Notre Dame causing them to get tangled in her yoyo. He introduces himself and quickly asserts his cockiness and confidence to her as Paris new hero all the while teasing Ladybug about her costume, as well as her methods of fighting crime. During their first fight against an akuma he continued to call the heroine his sidekick, but soon he came to admire her quick wits, instincts in combat and when she saved him. By working together they were able to stop the Magician and Mime and save everyone when surrounded by an applauding crowd Cat Noir playfully demoted himself to sidekick status until Ladybug affirmed they were partners. As time went on he and Ladybug turn into great friends but every once in while he couldn't resist glancing at her at the same time did an excellent job protecting the city. Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Intro
Adrien Agreste is one of the two titular former main antagonists (alongside Marinette Dupain-Cheng) of Miraculous World: Paris - Tales of Shadybug and Claw Noir.
He is the villainous version of Adrien Agreste from the Re-Verse. When Plagg inhabited the Cat Miraculous, he transformed into Claw Noir, a black cat-themed supervillain with the power of Destruction.
In "Miraculous Paris", after Betterfly crossed multiverse to get help from Ladybug and Cat Noir, he followed him along with Shadybug to steal the Butterfly Miraculous. After his counterpart was able to inspire him to get the life he wanted to have, Claw Noir gave up on his evil purpose, revoked his Cataclysm, and, in this way, got a new costume. Now allying himself with Betterfly and having joined his Resistance, he adopted a brand new form as Furry Paw, and became a superhero.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Adrien is a tall and fair-skinned teenage boy with blond hair that is swept all over to the left and faded shaved on the right. He also has emerald-green eyes and has a rosy tint on his cheeks, nose, and the tips of his ears.
Due to repeatedly using his Miraculous for evil, Adrien gained black veins in his face which he often covered in makeup as Shadybug discovered, however after she used her Miraculous Shadybug, the affliction is cured.
Civilian Attire
He wears a black turtleneck with vertical yellow, green, and blue stripes on the right side of the collar, a white leather jacket, dark gray jeans, a black belt with a silver buckle, and black boots.
He wears a thick layer of black eye liner, his fingernails are painted black, and he wears a pair of small silver stud earrings.
As Claw Noir

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Appearance
Before his redemption, he had a wild mane of spiked green hair, purple eyes with slitted pupils, and black lips. He wore a black bodysuit with tears in the knees, a black mask over the top half of his face, fake cat ears on his head with a hole in the edge of the left ear, a black leather jacket and on the back is a green and black paw print that has been scratched out, a spiky silver ball hanging from the front of his neck, a long black belt with silver spikes around his waist that stuck out the back like a tail, tattered at the end, and a pair of calf high steel-toed black boots with spikes at the top. He also had a crack in the center of his chest from his heroic counterpart's Cataclysm.
As Furry Paw
After his redemption, he no longer has black lips, the under-cut of his hair grew and turned blonde, his eyes became green and his spiked bell turned into a golden normal one. While retaining his jacket but thinner and all the spikes he had on his costume are gone, and fake cat ears on his head have no hole in the edge of the left ear.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Personality
Unlike his quantic counterpart who is kind and caring, Adrien was cold and distant towards others after losing his mother Émilie, as he missed her so much. He also bore a strong resentment towards his father over how he got over his mother's death and moved on as well as being distant torwards him. Strange enough, he also felt attracted to Marinette Dupain-Cheng, admiring her from afar, despite that both of them had never actually known each other personally.
Despite his deep yearning for his mother like the villainous version of his father, both were acting very naive, especially if they thought about what was going to happened beyond their wish.
As Claw Noir, Adrien became more aggressive and destructive with his powers, showing no hesitation or fear of hurting others or himself with them. But he was more impulsive and lazy as he let his guard down, allowing Shadybug to easily steal his ring, but he also showed his vulnerable and naïve side, feeling hurt about how much info the Supreme kept from them and even briefly tried to comfort his partner after seeing her sad about her Quantic Universe counterpart having a better life.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Personality
During his final confrontation with Cat Noir, like his partner Claw Noir poured out all his frustrations and anger towards him about what it felt like to be left behind, alone and forgotten after losing a loved one.
It could be that he was also hesitant to change as well as to defy The Supreme, because Adrien feared what he would do and that would include taking away his powers or worse, meaning he was afraid to go back to the way he was similar to his partner, implying that maybe after all the things he said or did to his father and any possible friends like Nino, maybe he felt he didn't deserve any friends or forgiveness.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Personality
Similar to Monarch, while fighting his heroic counterpart, he wanted to get his and Ladybug's Miraculouses to summon Gimmi and use the wish to bring back his mother. But when Cat Noir mentioned feeling the same, he still didn't believe him until he took Cat Noir's ring and saw his counterpart's true face shocking him even more when he realized that the latter's mother suffered the same fate. Cat Noir was able to convince Claw Noir that he too could change his life if he chose not to be alone, honor his mother's memory and give friendship a chance. This inspired Claw Noir to give up on his mission to retrieve the Butterfly Miraculous and pursue the wish, returning his counterpart's ring. This results in his costume changing in order to adapt to his newly found heroism. Now deciding to become a superhero and like Shadybug, he allied himself with Betterfly and adopted a new name, with that one being Furry Paw.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Abilities
As Claw Noir/Furry Paw
As Claw Noir, he exhibited most of the same abilities as his heroic counterpart as he exhibited massively enhanced strength, speed and agility, to the point where he and Shadybug proved superior during their two clashes against their heroic counterparts, though this could be attributed to their unrestricted powers and their more aggressive nature. Despite his physical superiority however, Claw Noir seemed less intelligent than his counterpart, as he was overall much more aggressive and wasn't able to realize Cat Noir intentionally exposed himself.
Much like Cat Noir, he also possessed the ability to use Cataclysm. Due to removed restrictions on his Miraculous however, he could use his power as many times as he liked and to greater extents. He was even able to split his staff into a pair of nunchucks and form it into a spear to fight his counterpart.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Abilities
However, Claw Noir's power came at a price as a result of the safety restrictions being removed on his Miraculous (due to him using the Cat Miraculous for evil), Claw Noir suffered side effects as a result from using his Miraculous (shown as a series of black veins across his neck and face), alongside his partner Shadybug.
According to her, the effects were gradual, though Marinette attempting to summon Gimmi ended up accelerating the process, resulting in the affliction spreading to her face, though according to Shadybug the use of their Miraculous superpowers "will slowly destroy them". The affliction seemed to affect the user physically however, as both him and Shadybug were able to feel the affliction when it was removed. Overall, the effects are similar to the effects caused by wearing a broken Miraculous.
After his counterpart convinced him to use his powers for good and become a hero, Shadybug used the Miraculous Shadybug to restore the damage from their battle, resulting in the removal of the affliction infecting him and Shadybug. Since Claw Noir now uses his powers for good, it's unknown if he still possesses the ability to use Cataclysm multiple times.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Etymology
In the original French dub, his supervillain name is Griffe Noire, with the first part being the French translation for the word "claw".
His supervillain name in the French version uses the term "Noire" which is the feminine form of the adjective "Noir" (meaning "black") and, in the series, has been used on the names of female Cat Miraculous holders (such as Lady Noire, Bug Noire, and Kitty Noire).
However, its use has nothing to do with the user but with the first part of the supervillain name, as "Griffe" is a feminine word in the French language. Because "claw" is a neutral name, the term "Noir" in the English version is meant to refer to his own gender.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Trivia
Being his a villainous counterpart of Adrien/Cat Noir, Claw Noir is the first known holder of the Cat Miraculous to be a supervillain, following Gabriel Agreste who had used it to become Shadow Noir for a brief moment and to summon Gimmi, the kwami of reality.
It's unknown if he's a sentimonster like his Quantic Universe counterpart.
However, considering his mother used to be a Peacock Miraculous holder as well, with Betterfly even confessing to Quantic Universe's Marinette and Adrien that he only joined the Supreme in order to get something he wanted very much, it's very possible that Re-Verse Adrien is a sentimonster like his counterpart.
Contrary to his Quantic Universe counterpart, he became depressed by his mother's death and was obsessed with bringing her back by using the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses to summon Gimmi, much like the evil counterpart of his father, who ironically wasn't able to move on from his wife's death and find happiness in his life.
Unlike Quantic Universe's Gabriel, he was able to come into terms with Émilie's death before it was too late for him, being able to move on from it and try to find happiness again.

title: Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Re-Verse - Trivia
After being unmasked by Shadybug, who transformed back into Marinette, alternate Adrien was shown to have a crush on her, with her unaware of this. Contrary to his Quantic Universe counterpart who was unaware of good Marinette having a crush on him.
Alternate Adrien only has a line in the special when transforming, while Claw Noir has more dialogue.
Claw Noir is considered the villainous representation of Adrien in the Quantic Universe, serving as what would happened if he went down the same path as his father, then Adrien and Gabriel would have team up and work together as supervillains, like father and son to bring back EmilIe.
He is the third person to physically touch an Akuma, in addition to Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch, following Cerise Bianca and Adrien as Cat Noir (in an alternate timeline).
Claw Noir is the second Miraculous holder to receive an (albeit unintentional) Cataclysm from Cat Noir, following Monarch in "Destruction" (which happened at that same day). However, unlike Monarch, Claw Noir was healed in time by Shadybug's Lucky Charm.

Adrien Agreste/Alternative Universe - Abilities
As Mister Bug
He has the same abilities as Ladybug: enhanced skills like speed, agility, and strength, and near invulnerability to physical damage.
Like Ladybug, Mister Bug can wield his yo-yo remarkably well, like using it as a grappling hook, a rope to restrain others, a projectile, and a shield if he spins it fast enough. Whether this Adrien has the same life as Marinette in the Quantic Universe (having both parents who are the owners of a bakery), he has a similar life to his own counterpart from that universe except for getting the Ladybug Miraculous, or a life that is different altogether.

text:

Physical Appearance

As Cat Noir
Cat Noir has cat eyes with green sclerae, dark green irises and slitted pupils. His hair becomes longer and untamed and it covers his normal ears. Cat Noir wears a textured black skin-tight catsuit with metal details. He wears matching gloves that have claws on the fingertips and boots with a hidden wedge, silver toes, and paw-shaped treads. He has a golden bell on his neck, connected to a zipper on the front of his costume, and a long belt that wraps around his waist and hangs out from the back like a tail. title: Adrien Agreste/Giuliaverse
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Adrien Agreste/Giuliaverse - Abilities
As Cat Noir
Cat Noir has enhanced physical skills such as superhuman speed, agility, and near-invulnerability. He is fast enough to outrun a pair of panthers, being capable of running at least between 35-50 mph. Like a cat, Cat Noir also has enhanced senses such as hearing, smell, night vision, and super stealth.
Cat Noir uses his staff efficiently, wielding it as a sword, throwing it with great precision, and having it be deflected back to him. He is able to spin it at high speeds to form a shield or take advantage of its duplication and length-changing features.
His special power, Cataclysm, allows him to negatively affect and essentially destroy anything that he touches with his ring hand. While it is usually used for object destruction, it can be used for a variety of different effects, for example, causing a bus's controls to go haywire and creating a platform in a structure.

text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - Intro
Adrien Agreste is the son of famous fashion designer Gabriel Agreste and actress Émilie Agreste. He is also the current holder of the Cat Miraculous, who uses it to transform into Cat Noir.

title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - Past
Adrien was born to Gabriel and Emilie Agreste and they spent a happy life together but everything changed when Emilie died. Gabriel blamed himself for this, believing that he should've died instead of her and became too helpless to face Adrien's sadness. Ever since then, Gabriel became emotionally neglectful of his son and Adrien swore that he would never get close to anybody again out of fear of losing them like his mother.

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::0
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
On the the day of Emilie's birthday and the first day of school, Adrien is in the library where he first meets Marinette Dupain-Cheng and notices that she's crying (due to her being sad about being clumsy and fearing that she'll let everybody down) but she tries to deny it as as allergies to pollen much to his confusion. While reading and working, he doesn't notice Marinette starting to fall for him and she actually falls with some books and he helps her up and puts the books away before leaving. He finds her to be weird until his best friend Nino Lahiffe invites him to the fair and Adrien reluctantly accepts. After coming home, he overhears his father refusing to have dinner with him much to his sadness. In his room, Adrien is still very saddened by his mother's death. He leaves his home and goes to the closed and abandoned theatre where his mother used to perform.
After returning home, he is busy with homework till he notices something strange and notices a black cat (Plagg in his animal form) in his room before noticing the Cat Miraculous under his desk.
He meets Plagg who informs him of the Miraculous and that he is the chosen wielder of the Cat Miraculous.

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::1
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
After transforming into Cat Noir, he goes to the Notre Dame cathedral until Ladybug (Marinette) crashes into him and they are both tied upside down before falling.
He treats her as a nobody and claims that he's the hero that's come to save the world.
He even treats her as looking like a watermelon and decides to reduce her to a sidekick much to her annoyance.
While revealing what he has, he doesn't notice Gargoyle (an Akumatized Raymond) behind until too late.
He gets chased by Gargoyle before getting into a tackle ride on the Akumatized villain.
Ladybug's yo-yo attaches to Gargoyle who begins to fly and crash through everything out of Notre Dame with the people of Paris seeing Ladybug and Cat Noir for the first time.
Gargoyle then flies them into the river before crashing into the train station.
Cat Noir tries to distract gargoyle with the "fetch" technique but it ends up with Gargoyle chasing him after the technique fails.
Cat Noir gets stuck in the tracks until Ladybug saves him from an incoming train that crashes into Gargoyle which De-Akumatizes him in the process.

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::2
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
This causes Cat Noir to fall in love with Ladybug as she helps him up the same way he did for her in the library and they both leave when the police arrive.
They both notice the Akuma butterfly leaving (after leaving Raymond) and they meet Master Fu (in disguise) who tells them to discover who they are but they bicker about each other until the old master stops them. Fu reveals to them what they stand for, that they must defeat Hawk Moth and capture the Akuma's who Akumatize anyone in supervillains and that they must work together before he disappears. Ladybug refuses to continue being a hero but Cat Noir realizes that failure is her fear but she still continues to refuse be a hero or be a sidekick to him before leaving for home. Cat Noir then becomes happy for the first time since his mother died due to Ladybug coming into his heart.
After returning home, Adrien continues to think of Ladybug but Plagg continues to annoy him with his flatulence and the way he'll wreck everything. However, Adrien continues to talk about Ladybug and what she thinks of her and asks Plagg for advice on how to get together with her and Plagg tells him that two halves are stronger together.

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::3
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
The next day at the fair, Adrien is with Nino asking for advice with the latter claiming to know about love but gives bad advice. They are then met by Marinette and her new best friend, Alya Césaire. Their best friends assume they like each other but Marinette and Adrien try to deny it. Alya and Nino then leave for one of the rides to let Marinette and Adrien be alone but the two try to make excuses to leave. However, when Marinette mentions the bakery that she lives in, Adrien is amazed by it and believes that her father is awesome. After Marinette drops her stuff to get macarons for him, he notices her sketching's and likes them. However, they both notice Marinette's father standing right next to them much to the girl's embarrassment. Gabriel (as Hawk Moth) calls his son to come home (also due to knowing that the fair won't be safe due to the new Akumatized villains he unleashed).

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::4
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
When the Magician and the Mime attack the fair and Adrien becomes Cat Noir again. When Ladybug is about to be crushed by the balloon monster, he saves her but she accepts him being around this time. They are both confronted by the two villains but stop their attacks before the villains decide to cause chaos with the coaster and the wheel. They both take care of the coaster and wheel while taking on the Magician and the Mime at the same time, but the balloon monster also makes things difficult. However, the two heroes defeat the balloon monster and the two villains while also saving the coaster and wheel with everybody on it. Hawk Moth creates a giant hologram of himself and swears to the two heroes that there will be no mercy next time. All of Paris then see the two as heroes.
The two heroes become Paris' protectors while defeating Akumatized villains and becoming famous. During all this, Adrien starts to get close to Marinette, their friends and everybody else in school.

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::5
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
Months later, the two heroes are having ice cream together before they playfully fight together but after an awkward moment, Ladybug leaves for home. The next night, Cat Noir calls Ladybug to the abandoned theatre where he reveals his fears about getting close to anybody that he might lose ever since his mother died but since he met her, he's happy again. He reveals that he prepared a surprise for which is a song that they both sing together and he confesses that it was she that saved his heart and they both dance. He tries to kiss her to confess his love for her but she sadly reveals that there is somebody else (not knowing that Cat Noir is Adrien who is the somebody else) and leaves. This causes Cat Noir to feel heartbroken and Plagg reminds him about having warned him to never fall for his partner.

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::6
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
He returned home, being greeted by Gabriel asking his whereabouts since he did not come home the other night. Adrien angrily snaps at him for never being there for him since Emilie died and that he lost his father a long time ago. At school, Adrien is approached by Marinette who confesses her love for him by inviting him to the ball and giving him a tie as a gift but he sadly uses the same words she did by revealing that there is somebody else (not knowing that Marinette is Ladybug who is the somebody else) and leaves.

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::7
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
When Hawk Moth akumatized himself and unleashed his final attack on Paris, Adrien at first was too depressed to notice the destruction or answered Ladybug's call until Plagg finally snapped him out of it by getting him to notice the destruction outside. Becoming Cat Noir again, he saved Ladybug from an akuma swarm but they were both still emotionally hurt by each other's rejection and failing to show up. Notice Hawk Moth on top of the Eiffel Tower, Cat Noir went to confront him alone, but after making his way to the top he tried to attack Hawk Moth with his Cataclysm, but was knocked down into accidentally destroying the Eiffel Tower, which caused it and him to fall into the river and with debris knocking him out. Despite being saved by Ladybug, he was still knocked out but regained enough consciousness to noticed Hawk Moth attempting to steal his Miraculous, but managed to use Cataclysm again, scarring the villain's face yet nothing else. Too weak, he begged his partner for help allthewhile his suit was ripped apart by Hawk Moth until he saved by Marinette taking the hit causing both land but separated.

id: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History::[[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]::8
title: Adrien Agreste/Movie/History
text:
Adrien Agreste/Movie/History - [[Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie]]
However, once Cat Noir woke up, to his and Marinette's shock, they both discovered that Hawk Moth was his father and that his father knew who he was. Heartbroken, that his father caused all this damage he asked why to which Gabriel explained it was all for his mother but realized he was wrong. But despite it all Adrien forgave his father and shared a loving hug but knew what was going to happen next, they said goodbye as Gabriel turned himself in and wass arrested offscreen for the damage he  did to Paris.
Months later, Adrien attended the ball but was outside lamenting how much he missed Ladybug with his heart in turmoil. However, he was approached by Marinette revealed that she knew he was Cat Noir and that she was Ladybug much to his joy and they both shared a kiss.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Intro
, also called evilized villains, are people (or оther sentient beings) transformed into supervillains by the holder of the Butterfly Miraculous with Akumatization, the evil version of the superpower of the Butterfly Miraculous.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Transformation
A prerequisite for akumatization to occur is someone experiencing strong negative emotions, which can be sensed by a holder of the Butterfly Miraculous. Once they select a target, they can charge a butterfly with Nooroo's power, transforming it into an akuma. The akuma then flies away to its chosen victim. Upon reaching them, the magical butterfly possesses an object that belongs to the person.
Once the object is possessed, the area around the victim's eyes turns red. A telepathic link between them and the Butterfly Miraculous holder is created, allowing them to communicate through a butterfly-shaped light mask that appears in front of both's faces. The mask doesn't need to appear when the two are speaking face to face, as depicted in "Ladybug" and "Heart Hunter".

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Transformation
Once the connection is established, the Miraculous holder can manipulate the akumatized person into accepting superpowers that'll allow them to achieve their dreams and desires, and/or help resolve the issues that caused their negative emotions. The Miraculous user can also ask for a favor in return. The victim is either given a name for their new supervillain identity or can choose one themselves. They also get to decide what they will look like, as well choose their power and weapon, after metamorphosis.
Once a deal is made, a dark purple ether spreads from the possessed object and covers the person. Once it recedes, it reveals the victim has transformed into a supervillain. The light mask can appear again at any time for further communication after a completed transformation.
Corrupted villains usually reject their civilian identity, demanding to be referred to by their new name. However, they still remember the reason for their akumatization, as well as who they consider a friend, an enemy and a romantic interest.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Transformation
A Butterfly Miraculous user can akumatize themselves. They must, however, de-transform after creating an akuma and before it entering any object. In a situation like this, no telepathic conversation occurs – rather, they transform immediately.
Despite humans making up the majority of those akumatized, any creature or thing can fall victim to an akuma as long as it's capable of experiencing emotions – that includes animals, robots, Sentimonsters, artificial intelligence programs and other beings. Additionally, sometimes, other beings or objects (other than the one holding the akuma) are transformed along with the main victim.
As shown in "Sapotis" and "Félix", multiple people can be akumatized with just one akuma and object as long as they are all holding it at the time of infection, or, like in "Gang of Secrets" and "Dearest Family", all have some emotional link to the object.
If the first target's emotions dissipate before an akuma can infect one of their belongings, the butterfly will instead attack whoever is nearest and also experiencing negative feelings. This happens in, for example, "Gigantitan" and "Crocoduel".

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Transformation
If an akuma infects something that has multiple, separate parts or is broken at the exact time it gets possessed (like the vinyl record in "Crocoduel"), a full transformation is still possible – the butterfly will spread its essence evenly into all the elements.
In season 5, after Monarch reformed the Miraculouses into special rings, he transferred the magical jewels' powers to his akumatized victims through their Alliance rings, either right before or immediately after they transformed into supervillains. Since only one power could be granted per Alliance ring, a target needed to wear multiple rings to receive multiple superpowers.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Abilities
An akumatized villain has an appearance and abilities that relate to their infected object, occupation, circumstances, and/or interests. For example, because of Xavier Ramier's love of pigeons and his possessed object being a bird call, he becomes Mr. Pigeon, a villain with a suit based off of pigeons and the ability to command pigeons. It appears that the powers come with all the knowledge and muscle memory the akumatizated victim needs in order to use them effectively. Quite often (but not always), a villain's akumatized object changes into their weapon.
Aside from their unique superpowers, akumatized supervillains all have enhanced strength, durability, agility and fighting skills. For example, Lady Wifi manages to pin down Cat Noir when they are both disarmed, and Reflekta is able to jump long distances.
Because of Hawk Moth's and the villain's mental connection, the villain can sense the location of Hawk Moth's lair if they want to find him, as seen in "Robostus", "The Dark Owl" and "Party Crasher".

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Abilities
In "Timetagger", it is shown that akumatized villains can communicate with any Butterfly Miraculous holder, even if they are not the one who akumatized them initially, as seen with the titular villain who came from the future and was akumatized by a future Hawk Moth.
After Shadow Moth stole almost all of the Miraculous and turned into Monarch, he reforged them into rings that are connected to the Alliance rings. The rings of the Miraculous allowed Monarch to give his akumatized champions the powers of the Miraculous remotely.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Weaknesses
For a person to accept akumatization, they must be manipulated, which is why people in a bad situation are usually targetted. They cannot be brainwashed or mind-controlled. In the event that a villain misuses their powers or rebels against the Butterfly Miraculous user, the latter can cause physical pain to the former to force them into submission.
The connection between a holder of the Butterfly Miraculous and their akumatized champion has a distance limit and is lost if the villain moves too far away. For this reason, Hawk Moth was unable to control and contact Startrain, who went rogue.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Weaknesses
To defeat an akumatized villain, the object in which the akuma is hidden must be broken. When that is done, the butterfly flies off and the villain is immediately transformed back into their civilian self. Along with their powers, they lose all memories of their actions, which seem "very blurry, like a dream you can't clearly remember". Akumatized objects that consist of multiple parts (such as Véronique's set of flyers in "Determination") or have been broken right before transformation (such as the vinyl record akumatized in "Crocoduel") must have all their pieces destroyed for a successful deakumatization to occur.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Weaknesses
After the object is broken, the owner of the Ladybug Miraculous can use their yo-yo to capture the akuma and cleanse it of negative energy. This will revert it to a normal butterfly. However, if the akuma is not captured, it will multiply, and the clones will possess anyone they come across. The people will be transformed into physical duplicates of the villain, frozen in time like statues until the original's emotions become negative again and re-akumatization occurs. Once the original becomes a villain again, the duplicates will come to life and serve as the original's personal clone army. It is currently unknown if there is any way to revert the duplicates back to normal without the original first getting re-akumatized and purified for a second time.
The Butterfly Miraculous holder can also simply release the akuma of their own choice, by either snapping their fingers or outstretching their arms. The akuma will purify itself in this situation.
Resistance can cancel out the effects of an akumatized villain's power if the power is used for attacking.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Weaknesses
It's possible for a victim of akumatization to resist it or even entirely break out of it both before and after transformation. This requires lots of willpower and strength, but has been achieved by multiple characters – Chloé Bourgeois, Alya Césaire, Félix Fathom, Nino Lahiffe, Sabine Cheng, Jalil Kubdel, Marinette Dupain-Cheng, Kagami Tsurugi, Luka Couffaine, Lila Rossi, Caline Bustier, Sabrina Raincomprix, Mylène Haprèle and Fred Haprèle.

title: Akumatized villains
text:
Akumatized villains - Trivia
Many of the supervillains' face masks, such as those of Stormy Weather, Lady Wifi, and the Evillustrator, resemble the shape of a butterfly, most likely in reference to the akumas. Similarly, the four eyeholes in Darkblade's helmet resemble the four wings of a butterfly.
When an akuma infects the object of the new villain and the light mask appears around their face, the darkened area is almost always an indication of the shape of their mask.
So far, only Stoneheart's akuma was mutilplied and akumatized others into Stonehearts in "Origins".
Most of the villains are seen near Marinette and/or Adrien shortly before the akuma infects them.
The ability to cause pain to transformed people is supposed to be used to keep kamikotized heroes from turning evil.
Several times, akumatized villains identify themselves as heroes, such as Dark Owl and Sublimation. Some villains call themselves heroes as a ruse, such as Volpina.
"Miraculous Paris", "Emotion", "Re-creation" and "Miraculous Tokyo" are the only episodes so far in which no akumatized villains appear in any way.

title: Agreste mansion
text:
Agreste mansion - Intro
The  is the residence of the Agreste family accommodated by Nathalie Sancoeur and Placide I.T..

title: Agreste mansion
text:
Agreste mansion - Appearance
Exterior
The Agreste mansion is at least four stories tall and has a basement. On the outside, it is tan and cream with black shingles on the roof. The first two stories are cream and tan, except for the right side of the house, which is covered in ivy. Two domed roofs are on the third story, the space between them having more interior room. The fourth floor is a large attic. At the very top of the house is a cupola. The windows are mostly vertically long, and they have white panes.
The front of the house is surrounded by a large fence, preventing people from getting into the large courtyard. This fence does not prevent people from looking into Adrien's room. There is a garage on the lower right at the front of the house. There also appear to be doors on the inside right and left of the walls. Awnings are covering these doors, and the doors do not lead to the outside of the walls.
The back of the house has a large wall of windows on the second floor, looking into Adrien's room. There is also a small backyard.
During an emergency, the house can go on lockdown, and metal will shield the windows and walls from the attack. The front gate will also be reinforced.
First floor

title: Agreste mansion
text:
Agreste mansion - Appearance
On the main floor and many of the rooms, the walls are mainly white with sections of gray marble and black details. Large cylindrical lights hang from the ceiling. The floor is white, but in some places, it has secluded black designs that resemble peacock designs, and in other places, there are black and white patterns.
The front of the mansion opens into a large foyer with a huge white staircase directly ahead of the entrance. Red plants are placed on each side of the front door, and pictures hang on some of the gray marble sections. Above the back of the staircase is a large framed photo of Gabriel and Adrien.
There is a door on the right side of the stairs on the first floor, and there is a sitting area to the left of the stairs. The door on the right leads to the kitchen.
There are several rooms in the Agreste mansion, some of which have not been seen yet. Inside on the first floor is Gabriel's atelier, a large dining room.

title: Agreste mansion
text:
Agreste mansion - Appearance
Some of the walls in the dining room have black and white vertical stripes, while a section of the floor is deeper and wooden. The dining room includes a large wooden rectangular table surrounded by dark brown chairs with white cushions. A bronze candelabra is placed towards one end of the table. There are also long vertical windows with tan curtains, and tall dark gray trim on the walls. Above a white and silver fireplace in the room is a large portrait on the wall with Gabriel, Émilie, and Adrien. To the right of the fireplace is a framed painting, and on the opposing wall from the fireplace is a white ledge, where a black and gold clock is set, and a huge mirror with a bronze detailed frame.
Second floor
The second floor is mainly Adrien's room. Both doors beside the painting above the stairs from the first floor lead to the room. The stairs leading off the sides of Adrien's room loop around to an indoor balcony above the entrance.
There are two rooms off the left and right staircases on the second floor, directly above the atelier and dining room.

title: Agreste mansion
text:
Agreste mansion - Appearance
The room to the right of the staircase leads to Nathalie's room, while the room to the left of the staircase leads to Gabriel and Émilie's room.
Third floor
A third floor's windows can be seen in many episodes depicting the outside of the mansion. It is currently not known what rooms it houses or how it is accessible.
The Crypt
The Crypt is a garden located beneath the foyer as seen in "Re-creation".
It was a large room with an arched ceiling, barely lit by lights along the sidewalls and what appears to be a beam of sunlight from a skylight. A catwalk extends the length of the room down the middle. The far end of the room appears to have a tree growing from the floor below, and the main wall at that end features a design identical to the "butterfly window" in Gabriel's lair.
At the end of the catwalk was a circular platform covered in greenery; grass covers the floor, bushes and flora decorate the platform, and what appear to be trees snake across as well as underneath the platform. A green glow emanates from underneath the platform where Émilie Agreste is held in a glass-covered cryogenic pod.

title: Agreste mansion
text:
Agreste mansion - Appearance
As revealed in "Queen Wasp", Gabriel accessed this room via the same secret passage from his atelier that he uses to get to Gabriel's lair.
In "Miraculous London", in order to erase any trace of Monarch in the Agreste mansion, Bug Noire destroyed any access to the Crypt, using Cataclysm on both the catway and the elevator shaft.
Gabriel's lair
Gabriel's lair was a room or observatory located inside the Agreste mansion. Gabriel Agreste/Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch stored many white butterflies that, once corrupted, become akumas, which he used to akumatize his victims.
The room was large, dome-like, and dark when Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch is not using an akuma. It had a large window with a butterfly (or flower) design that opens whenever Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch plans to send an akuma to a person who feels strong negative emotions. In the far back of the room, a circular shape is on the ground, on which Gabriel stood on to travel from the Agreste mansion to his lair.
Once a villain gets defeated, the window closes, encasing the room in darkness once again.

title: Agreste mansion
text:
Agreste mansion - Appearance
It was connected to Gabriel's atelier in the Agreste mansion by a pathway. In the portrait of Émilie Agreste, there was a pattern of buttons Gabriel presses to get to the lair.

title: Agreste mansion
text:
Agreste mansion - Trivia
During season 1, the Eiffel Tower is sometimes depicted as being behind the mansion, and being able to be seen from Adrien's room. However, starting from season 2, it's depicted in its correct location.
Interestingly, it's depicted behind it in "Stormy Weather 2", as the shot seems to have been reused from "The Bubbler".
The front door camera is similar to Jabba the Hutt's Palace in Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi.
The residents can get room service, as seen in "Ladybug & Cat Noir" when Adrien has camembert delivered to his room for Plagg.
An instance of the mansion going into emergency lockdown is seen in "Simon Says".
After the destruction of the Order of the Guardians and their temple, this is the only location at which all Miraculouses from the Chinese Miracle Box have been at the same time. This has happened two times, the first time in "Party Crasher", during the boys-only party, and the second time in "Strikeback", after Félix gave Gabriel the Miraculouses from Ladybug's yo-yo.
In "Werepapas", it's revealed that the mansion used to belong to Emil and Milly Graham de Vanily as their house in Paris, before giving it Émilie and Gabriel to live in.

title: Aeon
text:
Aeon - Intro
is one of the two deuteragonists (alongside Jessica Keynes) of Miraculous World: New York - United Heroez. She is a student in Professor Gate's class at Armstrong High School. She is also Uncanny Valley, an android superhero who was constructed by Majestia, with whom she has a mother/daughter relationship and is a member of the United Heroez.
__TOC__

title: Aeon
text:
Aeon - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Aeon is dark-skinned, has brown eyes and brown hair done in dreadlocks.
Civile Attire
She wears a blue and white Majestia top and a gray pleated skirt.
As Uncanny Valley
She has a beige technological body with golden lines at the edges of her exterior plating. She has three brilliant magenta eyes with light cerulean outlines and roseish black sclerae, with her third eye located on her forehead. As well as this, she has three golden stars on her upper chest. Her dreadlocks have gold accessories on them to resemble optic cables.
In Season 6, her eyebrows are thinner.

title: Aeon
text:
Aeon - Personality
Aeon is depicted as an informative and helpful person. She is willing to give advice to people to encourage them, like when she did with Jess to let Ladybug and Cat Noir help them. She seems to have a good relationship with her mother Majestia, taking her advice on board whenever she needs it. She is also quick to forgive people, like when Cat Noir accidentally used his Cataclysm on her, nearly deactivating her permanently.

title: Aeon
text:
Aeon - Abilities
Being an android, Uncanny Valley has the ability to fly using small jets located in various parts of her body. She can also fire lasers with enough heat to weld metal back together. She can hack into nearby systems, such as a plane's intercom or the lights in a museum. She also has scanning capabilities and is able to create visual projections. She can also alter her own memory and is able to delete any part of it she desires, promising Ladybug and Cat Noir to do so in order to keep their identities secret. Finally, much like a Miraculous user, she can switch her appearance and clothing from that of Aeon to Uncanny Valley or back in a manner of seconds via an unspecified mechanism.
She is also able to see through the magical nature of Ladybug's and Cat Noir's suits that normally prevents humans from recognizing their true identities.

title: Aeon
text:
Aeon - Relationships
Family
Jessica Keynes
Aeon has a close friendship to Jessica. They always fight together as their alter egos. During the battle with Miraculizer, she reasoned with Jessica that they would need Ladybug and Cat Noir's help to win the battle. Later, Aeon - as Uncanny Valley - tried reasoning with the Monk, saying that Eagle is a responsible Miraculous holder.
Majestia
Being her creator and mother figure, Aeon loves Majestia, refering to her as mother, even. When she was accidentally destroyed by Cat Noir's cataclysm, Majestia was furious, but she was revived by Ladybug's lucky charm.
Ladybug and Cat Noir
She gets along with Ladybug and Cat Noir, noting how their civilian forms are made for each other. Later, she helped their plan to get them together by creating a simulation of a villain called Solitude.
Even though Cat Noir accidentally nearly permanently deactivated her, she still holds no grudge against him and during the battle with Miraclonizer, she located Marinette and Adrien, encouraging them to help as Ladybug and Cat Noir. After the battle, Aeon deleted the memories of their identities from her memory.

title: Aeon
text:
Aeon - Relationships
In "Re-creation", she, along with the rest of the United Heroez, fought in defense for the French duo against the Miraculized.
In the last scene of "Miraculous Tokyo", Uncanny Valley and Cat Noir were revealed to have teamed up to fight against an unknown villain. She also learned that Adrien Agreste was Cat Noir again
Acquaintances
Monk
It is unknown if they get along, but she reasoned with him, convincing him that Eagle is a responsible Miraculous holder. She was also agreeing with the idea of beginning a new generation of heroes, something the Monk showed interest in.

title: Aeon
text:
Aeon - Trivia
Because she is an artificial intelligence that possesses an electronic body, she is unable to perceive kwamis, as they cannot be captured by any form of technology.
She refers to Majestia as "mother", suggesting Majestia built her. Alya references her creation earlier in the episode.
Being an android, she is genderless, however she was built with a female body type and female programming. Thus, she is referred to as female.
When Aeon called herself and Jessica "just teenagers", that should technically be incorrect because robots don't age, despite Aeon being given the appearance and programming of a female teenager, and it's unknown when she was created.
This fact bares a resemblance to Jenny/XJ9 from the My Life as a Teenage Robot franchise.
And also being an android, she is the second robot to be seen in the series following Markov.
Aeon's alter ego Uncanny Valley's design bears a slight resemblance to the manga incarnation of Alita Battle Angel.
Despite Aeon being an android with supposed high intellect, she is able to get an education by attending Armstrong High School.

title: Aeon
text:
Aeon - Trivia
According to Jess' English VA, Jess and Aeon are sisters; this implies both are daughters to both of Barbara Keynes and Olympia Hill.

title: Albert
text:
Albert - Intro
Albert is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is Denis Damoclès' computer program assistant.
In "The Dark Owl", when Mr. Damoclès' computer was infected by an akuma by Hawk Moth and Mr. Damoclès was akumatized because of it, Albert was akumatized along with him.

title: Albert
text:
Albert - Appearance
Normal
Albert takes the form of a circular, pixelated blue face on Mr. Damoclès' computer screen. He has large, black circular eyes and a black handlebar mustache as well.
Akumatized
When he was akumatized, his face was distinctly more human, and he was yellow instead of blue. He also had various computer monitor screens attached to cables that displayed his face.

title: Albert
text:
Albert - Personality
As programmed, Albert is polite and obedient to Mr. Damoclès. However, because he functions imperfectly, he gets confused by any command given to him or questions.
When he is transformed by Mr. Damoclès' akumatization, Albert was a lot more intelligent, functional, and helpful, following through on every request by Dark Owl. He also expressed horror when Ladybug managed to knock his computer screen off of the desk.

title: Albert
text:
Albert - Abilities
As a computer program
Mr. Damoclès programmed Albert to activate the panel containing the Owl's suit, which Albert fails at because he doesn't recognize the code word "hoo-hoo."
As a villain
Albert controlled most of Dark Owl's technology and traps, like his Owl-Signal, his holograms, and the shipping crate's trap door, from Principal's office. He activated, deactivated or otherwise manipulated these objects on command.

title: Albert
text:
Albert - Trivia
Albert's akumatized form is portrayed by Jun Violet, one of Miraculous' co-directors.
He is a reference to Batman's butler Alfred Pennyworth.
In-universe, Albert is based on Knightowl's personal butler, a character seen in the Knightowl comic books.

title: Agent Red
text:
Agent Red - Intro
is a minor character of Miraculous World: New York - United Heroez. She is a superhero and member of United Heroez, a team of superheroes, that protects the United States of America.

title: Agent Red
text:
Agent Red - Appearance
Physical appearance
Agent Red, like Agents Blue and Yellow, wears a face covering helmet with silver mechanical features on the bottom, including two antennae like points at the ears. She also wears a full body suit with silver bands on the upper chest and shoulders and a silver belt, the silver bands on the chest and belt have a W on both. The bodysuit and the helmet are both colored red with darker red patches on the inner arms and sides. The suits also have black stripes on various spots and triangle shaped logos with two Ws on the shoulders.

title: Agent Red
text:
Agent Red - Personality
Given that she started running around stealing everything she wanted after being hit with Liberation, she is presumably normally very selfless and generous.

title: Agent Red
text:
Agent Red - Personality
Agent Red's personality is not exactly known. In "Miraculous New York", she is brave and courageous. She is not afraid to stand up to fight the enemy to protect people. She is also loyal to other heroes. Given that she started playing around with her powers after being hit by Liberation, she is presumably normally very selfless and generous.

title: Agent Red
text:
Agent Red - Abilities
At the moment, Agent Red's abilities are unknown. Thanks to the power of the Miraclonizer, she could not limit her abilities and started shopping for fashionable things.

title: Agent Red
text:
Agent Red - History
Miraculous New York
Agent Red is seen on the news with the other members of the United Heroez, where President Camilla Hombee/Victory makes a statement about the hunt for Techno-Pirate and postpones the French-American Friendship Week celebration ceremony.
