title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Intro
is a recurring character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. She is a student at Collège Françoise Dupont and a former student of Olga Mendeleiev's class, before Mayor Bustier reformed the school. She is Aglaé's best friend. Starting from season 6, she is a well-known influencer on Zoo, known for her passion for climatology and meterology.
In "Stormy Weather", after losing the KIDZ+ contest against Mireille Caquet to become the weather forecaster, she was akumatized by Hawk Moth and became Stormy Weather, a weather-controlling supervillainess.
In "Stormy Weather 2", it is revealed that she has since succeeded in becoming a weather forecaster. After being bullied by Chloé over her low grades in school and previous akumatization, she was re-akumatized by Hawk Moth into Stormy Weather, gaining the power to control nature and weather abilities at the same time.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Intro
In "Climatiqueen", after she despairs, assuming she will lose in Chloé's contest on her Bee Community, she was akumatized by Chrysalis into Climatiqueen, an upgraded version of her previous akumatization as Stormy Weather, gaining not only the power to control the weather, but also to turn people struck by her lightning into her devoted followers. She also received a Magical Charm from Ladybug that prevents her from being akumatized again.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Aurore is a fair-skinned, slender teenage girl of medium height, with light cornflower blue eyes and long, straight honey-blonde hair with bangs, and a tiny cowlick on the right. Her hair is tied in low-hanging twintails with light blue hair ties.
Civilian Attire
In the first saga, Aurore is seen wearing makeup; a pale amaranth nail polish that fades to light cerulean nail polish, light fuchsia lipstick, and a light brilliant cerise-colored blush. She wore a light blue mini dress that reaches slightly below her hips with short puffed sleeves with tiny white lace lining on the edge, a small yellow cloud pattern, a white Peter Pan collar, a white broad band around the waist, three layers of frilled edges at the hem, and small white lace lining at the dress openings and second frilled edge, and light yellow dress shoes with moderate amber soles.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Appearance
From season 6 onwards, Aurore wears more natural makeup and nail polish. She now wears a light blue dress with the same Peter Pan collar style as her previous one, this time in baby blue. It has a sun pattern, six buttons, two of which are unbuttoned, and a small tie at the waist. Over the dress, she wears a clear, open rain jacket with a cloud pattern. She also wears white tights, a pair of yellow heels, and two earrings: the left one shaped like a 7-pointed yellow star with a smiley face, and the right one shaped like a silver cloud with a frowny face. Her hair has become a lighter blonde and slightly wavy.
As Stormy Weather
Stormy Weather had light brownish gray skin, grayish mulberry-colored lipstick, and brilliant violet eyes. Her hair was two tones with dark purple base and very pale blue bangs, while her large, pointed, low-angled pigtails were striped with dark purple and very pale blue streaks. On her face, she had jagged black face paint that surrounded her eyes and came down to her cheeks as lightning bolts.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Appearance
She wore a tight, muted purple upward rounded midriff top that had small shoulder puffs and white sleeves that turned into gloves with two of the lightning bolts above her elbows also featured five white lightning bolt patterns that had bright purple outlines over a poofy, bell-shaped, and muted indigo dress with a narrow-ended-tube-shaped collar, and muted purple tights with white low heeled knee high boots that were angled at the "opening" near the calf, and two of the lightning bolts came out of the boots around the outsides of her legs near the knees (the last of the pattern was a sole lightning bolt centered squarely near her abdomen). They all had a lilac trim. Her weapon was a closed dark purple parasol that faded to brighter purple at the tip and had a black handle with a double spearhead at the bottom.
As Climatiqueen

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Appearance
Climatiqueen had a similar appearance to when she was Stormy Weather. However, there were significant changes to it. Her top was now a bodice. The collar was high and sharp, with a glowing white inverted V-shaped opening at the chest resembling lightning that revealed part of her cleavage, with a brilliant purple glow to accent the lightning adorning her two-tiered puffy sleeves. At the hips, she had a puffy waistband resembling clouds to accent the thick skirt trim, which had crackling lightning around it. Her boots were taller and slanted at the side while her gloves were a little shorter but pointed. Her parasol was more spiraled and had a darker ombre when it was open.
Her bangs were swept to the left, with forelocks. She had the same jagged face paint from before, but with less spikes near the sides. Her hair was styled into high drilled pigtails resembling cyclones that faded to brilliant purple near the end. On her forehead were two white markings with a brilliant purple glow, and on top was a big, matching three-pointed outline resembling a crown on her head.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Personality
Normally, Aurore is charming and prideful, but also shy and soft. Because of her arrogance, she was angry with Mireille for winning instead of her, but kept it to herself, only lamenting about it once she was alone. Over the series she has also been shown to be able to forgive people as she happily worked with Mireille as co-host for the Friendship Day event. She can also show appreciation to others, such as thanking Marinette for standing up for her against Chloé. Evident in "Stormy Weather" and "Climatiqueen", she takes winning popularity contests seriously, blinding her from her original desires in the first place such as a signed book from Claudie Kanté.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Personality
Despite looking prideful and put on a brave face for others, Aurore is a very sensitive person, especially when it comes to disappointment. That can lead her to sometimes make the wrong choices in order to deal with it, like using Marinette and Adrien's private life to boost her presence online in order to win a contest she really wanted to win, when her original content failed to do it (even if the ones winning had posted the same type of content as her). However, she can come down and own her mistakes, apologizing and making amends.
Aurore is very passionate about meteorology, admiring very much all types of climatic phenomena. She even incorporates that passion into her own style, including always being accompanied by a parasol. That same admiration extends to those that work and/or document any form of climatic phenomenon, like Claudie Kanté, an astronaut that took photos of some of those phenomena from space. She was aware that not many people are interested in her passion in weather phenomena which makes her sad. After Ladybug helps her accept that passion is more important than success, she learns to not let anything stop her passion for weather.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Personality
As Stormy Weather, she became a lot more outgoing about her aggression, rudeness, and selfishness. Her jealousy for Mireille ramped up even higher, as she trapped Mireille with ice in an elevator, destroyed any images of her, and even attacked her fans. And in "Stormy Weather 2", she became vengeful towards Chloé and even trapped her in a block of ice showing how she was calculative enough just to get what she wanted.
As Climatiqueen, she was an ambitious and fame-hungry attention seeker, determined to go great lengths with cheating by forcing civilians into becoming her followers, justifying that people cheat on the internet anyway and herself winning is what mattered. Changing her goal, she became greedy after Chrysalis told her to gain more followers than Chloé.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Abilities
As a Civilian
Aurore is very knowledgeable about meteorology and can recite facts from memory.
As Stormy Weather
With her parasol as her weapon, Stormy Weather was able to control the weather. She could control air and create strong wind. This also allowed her to levitate, fly at high speeds and create small hurricanes. She could create snow and freeze air currents, along with forming snowstorms and hailstorms. She could fire purple lightning bolts from her parasol that cause small explosions on impact. Also, she could aim them towards the sky; by doing that, the sky clouded up and, after a few seconds, a massive lightning struck.
In "Stormy Weather 2", Stormy Weather's powers became expanded to include "all the forces of nature". Consequently, she was able to create a volcano which generated enough force to move Earth out of its orbit. Ladybug noted during the battle that she was far stronger than she was before.
As Climatiqueen
She had most of the same weather powers as Stormy Weather, except if she hit someone with a lightning bolt, they were brainwashed into becoming her online followers.

title: Aurore Beauréal
text:
Aurore Beauréal - Relationships
Allies/Friends
Mireille Caquet
Aurore competed against Mireille for the title of KIDZ+ TV weather girl. When Mireille won instead of her, she was very angry, though she kept it to herself and only lamented about it once she was alone.
As Stormy Weather, her resentment for Mireille grew as she trapped her in a block of ice and destroyed anything that had an image of her.
Despite this, it is shown that as of "Ikari Gozen", that the two seem to get along very well as they both host the Friendship Day game. Since Aurore was known to be working as a weather forecaster in "Stormy Weather 2" and Mireille won the contest, they are probably working together.
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Ladybug
Aurore is grateful towards Marinette when she stands up for her after Chloé makes fun of her and tells her to ask for help if she needs it.
Aglaé
TBA
Adrien Agreste/Cat Noir
In "Dark Cupid", it was revealed that Aurore is a fan of Adrien and was jealous of Chloé, who had a large poster of him.

In "Hack-San", she and the other Parisians fall under the influence of Robostus, causing her to be against Cat Noir for a time.
In "Perfection", Aurore witnessed Adrien performing a song for Marinette.

title: Aurore Beauréal

Aurore Beauréal - Etymology
Aurore's name is a pun on the atmospheric phenomenon aurora borealis, also known as the Northern Lights, reflecting her interest in the weather.
In the Serbian dub, her name is changed to Aurora Borealis.
In the Brazilian, Spanish and European Portuguese dubs, her name is changed to Aurora Boreal.
In the Thai dub of Season 6, her name was also changed to Aurora.
In the Irish dub, her name is changed to Áine.
In the French version, Aurore's supervillain name is Climatika.
In the Brazilian Portuguese dub, her name is changed to Tormenta, which is a Portuguese word for "storm".
In the European Portuguese dub, her name is changed to Tempestuosa, which is Portuguese for "tempestuous", which can describe a severe storm or strong and turbulent emotions.

In her climactic fight against Ladybug and Cat Noir, she was further transformed by Aset's power into Mega Stormy Weather, the final boss of the game.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Intro
Armand Louis Charles D'Argencourt is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is a fencing and PE teacher at Collège Françoise Dupont. He is also the Count of Caduque and Pétaucasque.
In "Darkblade", after losing Paris' mayoral election to André Bourgeois and being publicly humiliated for it, Armand was akumatized by Hawk Moth into Darkblade, a medieval knight supervillain.
In "Representation", following André Bourgeois's resignation of his position as Mayor of Paris, Armand once again ran for the candidacy against former teacher Caline Bustier, but lost the election to the former in "Re-creation".
In "The Dark Castle", after Alim Kubdel's continous refusal to give in to his demands to turn the Louvre back to its former glory before it became a museum, especially dismantling its pyramid, and his threat to forbid him from entering the museum again, Armand was akumatized by Chrysalis into the Dark Castle, a castle-themed supervillain that became the palace itself. He also received a Magical Charm from Ladybug to prevent him from being akumatized again.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Armand is a tall, thin and muscular man with a small amount of dark brown hair atop his head and blue eyes. He has a long and narrow chin with a large curly mustache.
Civilian Attire
In the first saga, the only outfit shown by him was a white fencing outfit, with thin red, white, and blue lines on the sides. On top of it, he wears a black fencing guard that is attached with two gray straps. On the left side of the guard, there is a silver shield symbol with a black phoenix-like creature. He also wears white boots that end below the kneecaps with thin red, white, and blue lines over the toes. When he is fencing, he uses a white fencing mask.
In second saga, he wears a tan dress jacket, a white dress shirt with an unbuttoned collar, a light red polka-dotted ascot, matching his solid vest, and dark brown slacks.
As Darkblade

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Appearance
Darkblade wore a full suit of dark gray armor, some parts of it having lighter gray with dark gray stripes. The visor on his helmet had four red leaf-shaped marks, and the helmet's comb was large and red, its shape a bit zigzagged. The besagues had red curled outlined designs on them, and on the center of the breastplate, there was a red family crest design with a black outline and a black phoenix-like creature inside. His couter, poleyns, and the end of the sabatons were pointed. His sword was large, with a silver and dark gray striped hilt and a dark gray blade with red lines making a design on each side. At the middle of the cross-guard, there was the same family crest symbol as the breastplate, except with inverted colors. It glowed when it was shooting energy.
As Dark Castle
Dark Castle fused and took on the appearance of the Louvre palace. He adopted a dark coloration of it and becoming a massive, humanoid mecha giant.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Personality
Armand is a serious and proper man who is inspired by the ideals of knights from the medieval ages, and he is bitter with how underhanded tactics resulted in his ancestor losing his rule over Paris. He didn't run for mayor of Paris because he wanted revenge, but he is frustrated with his loss to André Bourgeois and how everyone takes him for a man obsessed with medieval times, whether true or not. To Adrien Agreste and his other fencing students, he is challenging, but good at teaching them and helping them improve.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Personality
Armand possesses a great passion towards France's history and tradition and (possibly due his noble upbringing) he wished that his country would return to be a monarchy. This was reflected on his constant demands to turn the Louvre palace back to what it used to be before it became a museum after the French Revolution, his disdain towards the pyramid at the courtyard (wanting it dismantled), and the Liberty leading the people painting (wanting it burned). After being deakumatized as Dark Castle, Ladybug advised him to look at the past as a way to make a better future instead of attempting to rewrite it, while also helping him gain a new appreciation towards the Louvre's pyramid.
As Darkblade, he was commanding and obsessed with conquering Paris. Power-hungry and enraged with the current government system, Darkblade wanted to take over the country his ancestors lost centuries before, and he had nothing against turning everyone into knights that would follow him to victory.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Personality
As Dark Castle, he was able to put into action his desire to turn the Louvre museum back into the fortress it used to be, commanding knight armors to dismantle the pyramid. He also saw himself as the one worthy of becoming king of France.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Abilities
As a Civilian
Armand is very skilled at fencing, and is knowledgeable enough about it to be a teacher. A special move he uses, which was created by his ancestor Darkblade, involves pretending to be open for attack, just to suddenly fight back and knock the opponent's weapon away.
As Darkblade

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Abilities
Darkblade was able to create energy from the shield symbol in the middle of the cross-guard of his sword and shoot it into people's eyes. His victims knelt down, and then he touched their left and right shoulder with his sword as a way of knighting them. After that, the victims glowed bright green and transformed into knights wearing dark gray armor with bright green designs on their epaulets and helmets. Each knight carried a dark gray and neon green battle axe, the blade being green with a black design and the handle having the family crest of Darkblade where it was connected with the blade. All of the knights were in full armor and have the same size, height, and attitude regardless of their previous proportions or personalities. Under Darkblade's control, the knights followed his orders and did any action he required of them. He could also transform a vehicle, with the same process that he uses for his knights, into an old-fashioned catapult. He also had improved swordfighting abilities, and he still liked to use the Darkblade technique.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Abilities
Additionally, if Darkblade managed to plant his family's flag on top of the City Hall, a dark cloud spreaded over Paris. After the cloud stopped expanding, it created a circular black barrier on the extremity that shrunk inwards, turning everyone it passed through into his knights. They would glow dark green and stand up when struck. The knights would begin marching to him, awaiting instructions.
As Dark Castle
As Dark Castle, he has complete control over everything within the Louvre Palace, being capable of using the objects inside as weapons, even commanding the suits of armor as his personal army. He can also transform the entire palace into a giant humanoid being, while controlling the location where the flag is placed.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Etymology
Armand is the French variant of the German Herman, meaning "army man" or "army's man".
D'Argencourt is a combination of the German word argen ("bad") and court, preceded by the suffix "D'", denoting a place the person in question is from; together, it means "of/from the bad court".
D'Argencourt might also be a pun on the French expression à court d'argent, which means "short of money".
This surname is likely a pun on "Agincourt", a commune in northern France and the site of a battle during the Hundred Years' War where England managed a victory that crippled France, and acted as the centerpiece of Shakespeare's Henry V.

title: Armand D'Argencourt
text:
Armand D'Argencourt - Trivia
Darkblade's name comes from that of his ancestor.
As such, Darkblade is one of the villains whom Hawk Moth technically didn't name, the others being Horrificator, Volpina, Sapotis, Anansi, and Queen Banana.
Unlike most villains, Darkblade never made an attempt to acquire the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses.
A scarlet version of Darkblade reappeared in the two-part special event "Heroes' Day".
* In "Gamer 2.0", Darkblade returns as a playable akumatized villain as part of the Gamer 2.0's powers.
A statue of Darkblade appears in the Musée Grévin in "The Puppeteer 2".
In "The Dark Castle", it's revealed that Armand is a count, therefore part of the French nobility.

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Intro
is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is an employee at Le Grand Paris, where he works as a butler to the Bourgeois Family and a waiter in the hotel's restaurant.
In "Despair Bear", after being fired by Chloé Bourgeois, he was akumatized by Hawk Moth into Despair Bear, a tiny supervillain who controlled a small teddy bear.

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Appearance
Physical appearance
Armand is tall with short dark brown (or purple, black or gray hair, depending on the episode) and brilliant spring bud eyes. He also has a thin dark brown mustache.
Civilian attire
He wears a dark blue velvet dress tailcoat with a black bow tie, and the sleeves each have two black buttons and a pale yellow line around the cuffs. Underneath the jacket is a white collared shirt with four visible black buttons. He also has black slacks and black dress shoes.
As Despair Bear
When akumatized, he was doll-sized. His eyes were glowing green, and his mustache was long and black, bending upward at the tips. A black tear mark was on his left cheek below his eye. He wore a greenish black head cover that only left his face exposed, matching with a greenish black leotard, with glowing green lines around his neck and on his chest and glowing green line around his left knee, and dark colored gloves.
He controlled Mr. Cuddly, which was dark purple with a white chest, white muzzle, white inner ears. It also had a black mouth, black nose, and glowing green eyes.

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Personality
Armand is dignified, helpful, and quite polite. In "Mr. Pigeon", when Cat Noir needs a bathroom and Camembert, he assists him. At their request, he also tells Ladybug and Cat Noir about the events with Chloé Bourgeois the previous day in "Antibug". He is willing to pretend to be a super-villain to please Chloé and Sabrina Raincomprix, and he is concerned for Sabrina after Chloé gets upset at her and ignores her. As seen in "Despair Bear", he likes to encourage people's best traits.
As Despair Bear, he was very strict in expectations on how people should act and he was vengeful towards Chloé for being a terrible person. He didn't like losing, getting very angry and trying to attack Cat Noir despite being very tiny and unable to do damage without the bear.

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Abilities
As a civilian
Armand knows how to act professionally, and follow orders, and he has useful skills as a butler, serving others and keeping the hotel clean by sweeping.
As Despair Bear
Despair Bear controlled an akumatized Mr. Cuddly from the inside using strings and metal levers. The bear moved very quickly and was able to crawl on walls.
The bear could latch onto humans' bodies (often their legs), which gave Despair Bear control of the mind of the human. When under his control, the person's eyes turned the same color of Despair Bear's eyes. Despair Bear used the strings and levers to control the person, and he could talk through the person he is controlling. Once he was knocked off, unable to hold on, or willing to let go of the victim, the victim gained control of themselves but didn't remember what happened during his control over them.

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Relationships
Friends/Allies
Zoé Lee
He has a good relationship with Zoé as she is polite towards him and they often converse with each other. As seen in "Adoration", he often helps Zoé by distracting Chloé whenever she is mad at her. Zoé is usually quite polite to him back as they greet each other around the hotel when they do see each other. In "Delflagration", he was seen delivering food to someone while Zoé was trying to get Camambert for Plagg.
Acquaintances
Sabrina Raincomprix
Because he sees Chloé and Sabrina' interactions, Armand feels bad for Sabrina whenever she and Chloé get into arguments. He tries to vouch for Sabrina when Chloé is ignoring her, upset for Sabrina being shunned for an unintentional mistake, but it doesn't work.
Status unknown
Chloé Bourgeois

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Relationships
As an employee for André Bourgeois, Armand obeys his daughter Chloé's requests and commands, such as blocking a door to prevent Princess Fragrance's minions from following her and Prince Ali. He knows how much Chloé reveres Ladybug, even pretending to be a villain for whenever she and Sabrina play as Ladybug and Cat Noir respectively. However, he also gets to witness Chloé's awful behavior and mistreatment towards Sabrina. Aware of Chloé's nastier traits, he wants her to treat others better for her own sake and their sake. He worries about her relationship with Sabrina, and he suggests to no avail that Chloé should talk to her in "Antibug" when she is ignoring Sabrina's presence.

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Relationships
He encourages Chloé to be nicer by using Mr. Cuddly to remind her during the party, but he unintentionally embarrasses her because of it. He feels bad when she rejects his help and fires him, and while akumatized as Despair Bear, his intention is to punish her for her bad behavior. However, when he reverts back, he shows gratefulness towards her for letting him keep his job and he shows happiness that Chloé did a few good deeds. In "Revolution" he was fired by Chloe and was imprisoned by her. It's unknown whether he was rehired after Chloé was forced to leave for London with her mother.

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Trivia
Armand's hair color and dress coat randomly change within "Mr. Pigeon"; he has his regular colors in the first shot featuring him in the elevator, but in the next shot, his hair is black, and when he lets Cat Noir into a room, his hair and coat are both black.
In "Antibug", Armand reveals that as part of one of Chloé's games with Sabrina, he was made to act out the part of the fictitious villain "Big Mustachio". His outfit is the same while he's acting as Big Mustachio, but he additionally wears Groucho glasses.
In the French dub, his fictitious villain name is "Super Mustache".
Starting in "Despair Bear", Chloé Bourgeois refers to Armand by various names starting with Jean, from "Jean-Luc" to "Jean-Something". One of the names she uses is Jean-Yves, the same name as the Director of Studios.
Ironically, his real name doesn't begin with Jean at all.
Also, in the same episode, there was a big hint suggesting that even his name wasn't Jean. This is evidence when he answered to Chloé: "Uh, my name is... hm, never mind."

title: Armand
text:
Armand - Trivia
Despair Bear and the Sapotis the only akumatized villains to become smaller when transformed and have a smaller size by default. Horrificator, Animan and Animaestro can become smaller, although smaller sizes are not their default forms.
A scarlet version of Despair Bear reappeared in the two-part special event "Heroes' Day".
In "Gamer 2.0", Despair Bear returns as a playable akumatized villain as part of the Gamer 2.0's powers.
Depending on the episodes he appears in, his hair changes between dark brown, purple, black or gray.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Intro
is a recurring antagonist of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. She is the famous director of the fashion magazine, Style Queen. She is also the ex-wife of André Bourgeois and the mother of Noé Luxus, Chloé Bourgeois and Zoé Lee, all three fathered by different men. She was living in Paris, but she is now currently staying in London with Chloé.
In "Style Queen", which is part of the "Queen's Battle" special, after being humiliated by Gabriel Agreste, Audrey was akumatized by Hawk Moth into Style Queen, a glitter-themed supervillain.
In "Heart Hunter", when Audrey and her husband argued with each other during their 20th wedding anniversary, they were akumatized into Heart Hunter, a love-devouring supervillain.
In "Optigami", after being humiliated on live television by Sentialec, Audrey was reakumatized by Shadow Moth into Style Queen, bent on getting revenge on any who defied her. Ladybug also hid a Magical Charm in Audrey's hat, in order to prevent her from being reakumatized.
In "Revolution", after Chloé lost her position as Mayoress of Paris, she and Audrey left for London where she vows to take control of her daughter's life again, no longer loving or respecting her.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Intro
In "Noe", it's revealed that Audrey is part of the secret organization, The Kingdom, and that she helped her son Noé Luxus to impulsionate himself as the new King of Luxury to the eyes of the public and spread his influence.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Audrey is a slender, fair-skinned woman with short, chin-length golden-blonde hair that is much darker and cut into a sharp bob cut with short bangs that frame her face, blue eyes and she has a round heart-shaped face that is obscured by a pair of dark oval-shaped shades which cover her eyes.
Audrey physically resembles her daughter Chloé Bourgeois with the exception of her hair color, which is a couple of shades darker than honey blonde.
In Season 6, she no longer wears her light pink lipstick.
Civilian Attire

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Appearance
Audrey wears a white strapless jumpsuit with a thick black stripe down the right side that is long in length and bares around the shoulder blades. On her head, she adorns a black hat with black-and-yellow color stripes on the underside, yellow hat band and a black-and-yellow flower on the left side. She occasionally wears a pair of dark, oval-shaped sunglasses that cover her eyes. She wears a pair of bright golden high-heel shoes and white evening gloves which reach up to just under her elbows. She wears a gold ring with a modern design on her ring finger, though it is uncertain whether this is her wedding band or not and a golden bangle-like necklace around her neck with black gemstones and white outlines.
From season 6 onwards, her necklace appears more gold.
As Style Queen

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Appearance
Style Queen had bright and sparkly golden skin and teeth, moderate gamboge sclerae and very dark gold eyes. She wore sunglasses with very dark gold shades over her eyes and her head appeared to have pulled-back gilded hair in the style of a crown with five very dark ambers pointed stones attached around the front. She wore a golden strapless jumpsuit designed with vertical strips of cloth with a black strap on her left shoulder and pointed very deep gold edges around each leg. She also had medallion high-heeled boots. She held a long-gilded staff/scepter, having a bud-shaped tip with a black chevron line around it on top.
As Heart Hunter
As Heart Hunter, Audrey's body did not exist and she had pale, light grayish crimson face skin, a smaller nose, vivid raspberry colored-upside down heart shaped-earrings, vivid amaranth eyes and brilliant amaranth eyebrows and flapper styled hair.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Personality
Audrey is a bossy and demanding woman who only accepts what she wants and is "exceptional". She is considered to be "the harshest fashion critic in the world" and has no problem causing a fuss for those who do not meet her demands, such as having an issue with the red carpet being made out of fabric instead of marble. Like her daughter Chloé Bourgeois, Audrey has a fierce and explosive temper who will get upset over minor things, such as being denied a front-row seat. She also will attempt to "fire" anyone who displeases her.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Personality
To an extent, Audrey seems to have little care for her family, or at least their opinions. She expected her ex-husband André Bourgeois to agree to her demands of firing anyone she dislikes. When she is akumatized, she does allow Chloé to assist her but fires her the moment she catches her helping Ladybug. However, this changes after Audrey learns how much she has in common with her daughter and decides to spend more time in Paris with her. But even this does not last though, because after she and Chloé were banished from Paris, Audrey becomes devoted to being an abusive mother in complete control of Chloé's life rather than teaching her to be a better person or even caring for her, much like how Gabriel Agreste abused Adrien Agreste.
Audrey proves to be a neglectful mother to her children, only paying them attention once they achieve success.
She feels deep pride in her eldest son, Noé, whom she affectionately calls "my little diamond," due to his accomplishments and reputation. However, she shows marked contempt for her younger daughters, Chloé and Zoé, whom she abandoned in their infancy. Both later tried to emulate her behavior in the hope of gaining her affection.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Personality
Audrey only showed interest in Chloé when she noticed that she shared her haughty and domineering attitude, but she never truly cared about loving her or fulfilling a maternal role. Although she was proud of Chloé for ruling Paris "with an iron fist," her pride turned to humiliation when Chloé was dethroned from her position as mayor. At that point, Audrey reprimanded her, stating that "the Bourgeois don't raise losers," and took her to London with the intention of controlling her life, showing her neither affection nor understanding.
As for Zoé, Audrey completely ignored her from a young age, leaving her at a boarding school in New York under her father's supervision. When Zoé expressed her desire to move to Paris, Audrey reluctantly agreed and remained indifferent to her life, even supporting Chloé in her attempt to send her back to New York. Although Zoé tried to imitate her mother to gain her approval, she eventually accepted that Audrey would never truly accept her and decided to get closer to André, who became her true parental figure.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Personality
Audrey is rather bold as she doesn't seem fazed by the Akumatized villains. In "Malediktator", she didn't seem worried by her husband's akumatization and even made non-stop remarks that it doesn't make him a better father. In "Queen Wasp", when she was stung and paralyzed by a wasp controlled by her daughter, her position shows that she wasn't scared by her, to where everyone else in the hotel was paralyzed when trying to flee from Queen Wasp. She isn't ignorant about the dangers going on in Paris as seen in "Mayura" where she prepares to go off in the helicopter after the string of akumatizations by Scarlet Moth.
As Style Queen, she was more malicious and vengeful, but still tends to forget names quickly. Her main goal was getting revenge against Gabriel for giving her a second-row seat at his fashion show instead of a front-row seat. When he was nowhere to be found, Style Queen instead turned his son into a glittering statue along with bystanders at the show.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Personality
When she was akumatized in "Optigami", Style Queen wanted revenge on all the people who laughed at her after being humiliated on television by Sentialec. She didn't hesitate to attack anyone who got in her way, including Chloe and Zoe, and turned every person she encountered into gold dust, refusing to let her victims escape.
As Heart Hunter, her and Andre's goal was to devour all the love they came across in Paris, no matter what kind it was. Heart Hunter showed no mercy to anyone, turning hearts into consuming anyone they saw, even persistently chasing Ladybug for a few moments, seeing that the heroine had love for everyone. They also showed no qualms about attacking Chloé, wishing to consume her love for themselves.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Abilities
As a Civilian
Audrey has an eye for detail and great sense of fashion as she was the one discovered Gabriel Agreste's talent, which she later compared to Marinette Dupain-Cheng's derby hat.
As Style Queen
Style Queen could transform people or objects into golden statues and make domes around them using her scepter. She could also absorb the glitter statues into her scepter and could then release them where she wanted. When reakumatized, she gained extra abilities: She could not only turn people into piles of glitter but also objects. She was also able to glittery or cover objects with glitter examples of such as was a large building covered in glitter. She could also add a glitter copy of her face on top of an affected object, which was on the large building covered with glitter.
Style Queen also had an intangible body made of golden glitter which she could scatter into a cloud to fly. She could teleport herself and other people extremely quickly, which causes a puff of golden smoke.
As Heart Hunter

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Abilities
Heart Hunter manifested as a giant head capable of flight. They could sense love and shoot magic beams at a person(s) that turned them into a heart, which embodied said love, which they then ate.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Etymology
The name Audrey means "noble strength".
Audrey's surname Bourgeois is a French term that is used to describe a member of the middle class within France.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Trivia
Audrey's name was revealed in a Brazilian synopsis for Season 2 on O Universo da TV.
As seen in "Style Queen", Audrey's phone number is +33642198.
Interestingly, in "Despair Bear", it is implied that Audrey left former husband and Chloé. However, in her debut episode, it is revealed that she simply lived in New York most of the time.
In "Feast", Audrey showed a strange reaction to the Order of the Guardians. Just like with Tomoe Tsurugi, this foreshadowed her interest in the miraculouses as the part of The Kingdom.
Style Queen has some similarities with Golden Queen from Skylanders, as they both hold staves and they can turn people to gold.
Style Queen was first revealed on September 8, 2016, when Jeremy Zag posted an image of her on Instagram, with the caption, "Miraculous Season 2, new powers, new villains!"
Style Queen seemingly got her akumatized villain name from the magazine she directs.
A scarlet version of Style Queen reappeared in the two-part special event "Heroes' Day".
In "Gamer 2.0", Style Queen returns as a playable akumatized villain as part of the Gamer 2.0's powers.

title: Audrey Bourgeois
text:
Audrey Bourgeois - Trivia
Audrey tends to forget names (or perhaps only her daughter's name) as she keeps calling Chloé 'Claudette', 'Casserole', 'Clara', 'Kylie' or 'Chlorine'.
She also called Marinette "Martha" in "Queen Wasp".
As seen in "Mr. Pigeon 72", Audrey has been akumatized into Style Queen three times. ("Style Queen", "Mayura" and an off-screen akumization).
As of the events of "Optigami", she has been akumatized into Style Queen four times.
With her akumatization into Heart Hunter, she's been akumatized a total of five times.
While Audrey and André have been married for twenty years, Zoé's existence (and age) implies that Audrey had an affair of some sort while in New York.

title: August
text:
August - Intro
August is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is a baby boy who debuted in "Glaciator".
In "Gigantitan", after becoming upset for not getting a lollipop, he was unintentionally akumatized by Hawk Moth into Gigantitan, a giant baby supervillain.
Before the episode "Weredad", after he didn't get a late night cake, he is reakumatized into Gigantitan. He was shown at the start, but quickly deakumatized.
In "Miraculer", he was amokized by Mayura, and his frustration formed a lollipop-themed sentimonster in order to distract Ladybug from reaching Chloé Bourgeois.
In "Kuro Neko", he was reakumatized into Gigantitan by Shadow Moth.

title: August
text:
August - Appearance
Physical Appearance
August is short and small, having dark brown skin, short reddish-brown hair, and light brilliant sap green eyes.
Civilian Attire
On his left wrist, August wears a gold bracelet that has a sign which is spell his name. He wears a white and purple striped hood-less baby onesie jumpsuit along with plain white leggings and purple shoes.
As Gigantitan
Gigantitan's eyes were light brilliant mulberry color with blue-violetish black pupils and light brilliant harlequin sclerae. He wore a purple hood that protected his entire head with a green object on his forehead and a pink mask covering his face. He also wore a purple one-piece bodysuit with pink sleeve cuffs and a green and purple colored bracelet on his left wrist. On the center of the bodysuit was a logo which was mostly green with a magenta outline that has a picture of a pacifier on it. Gigantitan also wore pink and green ankle cuffs that were attached to his ankles, above his feet.

title: August
text:
August - Personality
August is a very content, lively, and positive child. He likes to play around with objects and is, for the most part, well-behaved. However, according to his mother, he can be very stubborn. He has a tendency to cry if he loses items important to him or doesn't get what he wants, and sometimes he doesn't immediately calm down, as is common for young children. Even though he is too young to eat them, he adores sweets and becomes very enthusiastic and eager when he comes across them. He knows how to be polite, thanking Ladybug and Cat Noir when they return him to his mother.
As Gigantitan, he was inquisitive, joyful, and bold. He liked to play with any object that he discovers, but he wasn't very attentive to his surroundings, and when not able to discover anything to entertain himself, he got upset and downhearted until he was satisfied by another object or distraction. Not old enough to know and understand many things, including common virtues, he often disobeyed or misunderstood Hawk Moth's orders, and he didn't have an issue sticking structures or humans in his mouth because he mistook them for lollipops.

title: August
text:
August - Abilities
As Gigantitan
Due to his enormous strength and size, Gigantitan could easily pick up almost any object with a single hand, and he could throw them a great distance. His weight and strength made it easy for him to destroy or crush objects, such as pulling the string of Ladybug's yo-yo, causing it to cut the Eiffel Tower, and he traveled distances faster when following or chasing other objects.

title: August
text:
August - Etymology
Gigantitan is called "Babyzilla" in the German dub.
Interestingly, he and Santa Claws are the only akumatized villains or amokized sentimonsters to have unique names in the German dub, not using the name from the English dub.
In the Korean dub, Gigantitan is called "Baby Giant".

title: August
text:
August - Trivia
Gigantitan was first revealed in an email response from a Customer Service Representative from TF1 to the MLadyblogFrance Twitter fan account.
Gigantitan is, so far, the youngest human villain to be akumatized, and the youngest human to be amokized.
He is unintentionally akumatized by Hawk Moth after Placide I.T. suppresses his negative emotions in "Gigantitan".
He is the first akumatized villain to disobey Hawk Moth, due to being too young to understand most of his orders.
A scarlet version of Gigantitan reappeared in the two-part special event "Heroes' Day".
In "Gamer 2.0", Gigantitan returns as a playable akumatized villain as part of the Gamer 2.0's powers.
Gigantitan also reappeared in "Weredad" and "Kuro Neko".
He is the first non-Miraculous wielder and non-akumatized victim to be amokized. He's later followed by Rythm in "Kuro Neko".
Interestingly, August was akumatized in "Kuro Neko".
It's unknown whether August was amokized in "Truth"/"Lies", "Qilin", and "Ephemeral", or Lollipop Boy was manifested from someone else's emotions.
In "Befana", "Gorizilla", "Chameleon", and "Backwarder", August can be seen being taken care of by different women and not his mother.

title: Art classroom
text:
Art classroom - Intro
The  is a classroom at Collège Françoise Dupont where Jean-Pierre Monlataing teaches art.

title: Art classroom
text:
Art classroom - Appearance
The art classroom is painted in an artistic style representing the theme and purpose. It includes a high wooden door which is a common architectural design in the school, and the windows are a transparent icy blue color with 7 light yellow rectangles of different shapes on the left. It also has a teal starfish with rainbow lines and a colorful circle in each section. On the right, there is a painted 8-bit picture of Ladybug with black frames. There are 4x4 and different sized windows supported by the entrance window.
On the left of the door, there is a black wall with a floral green aspect. In the front of the class, there is also a white stage with a mainly multicolored wall that consists of mainly teal with yellow graffiti-like writing on it. In the area in front of the stage, there is a spray-colored picture of a rainbow dash.
On the right wall, there is a painted white-pink streak with a white line across in the middle of it. Below, there is a brown wall with a 3-meter window outside with 2 horizontal frames and two vertical frames that have 8-bit drawings of characters from arcade games on them. The back area is also filled with multicolor paintings put on wooden frames.

It is revealed that many students in Miss Bustier's class visit the room after school.
Nathaniel goes there frequently to draw, while others such as Marinette and Rose visit the room occasionally, too.
According to the Jean-Pierre in "Reverser", it is 'Room 33'.
As shown in "Queen Banana", the room was used to prepare for the movie.

title: Arlette
text:
Arlette - Intro
is a minor character in Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. She is boss at TVi Tower, for the TVi and TV 5 channels.

title: Arlette
text:
Arlette - Appearance
Physical appearance
In the first saga, Arlette had her hair cut in a short bob that ended at the center of her neck.
From season 6 onward, her hair is straight, almost platinum blonde, pulled back in a bun, and her eyes are an amber-brown color.
Civilian attire
In the first saga, she wore a white work jacket with a folded collar and a pink shirt underneath.
From season 6 onward, she wears a white tailored blazer over a dark slate-teal shirt. She also wears four-leaf clover earrings.

title: Arlette
text:
Arlette - Personality
Arlette is a strict boss, constantly reminding Nadja that her show, and by extension her prime-time slot on television, will be cancelled should Side by Side have a low reception. Even as the ratings climb during the interview with Ladybug and Cat Noir, she still considers cancelling the show should Nadja's "big scoop" not live up to her expectations.

title: Arlette
text:
Arlette - Abilities
As a producer within TVi Tower, she is the person responsible for authorizing the creation, scheduling, and broadcasting of programs on the TV 5 channel. If unsuccessful, she is able to cancel programs with low viewership, which could then pose problems for the affected hosts' careers.

title: Arlette
text:
Arlette - Relationships
Friends/Allies
Nadja Chamack
Because she has the ability to cancel Nadja's television program, Arlette is very tough on her. Arlette frequently cautions the television host about the reception and quality of her interview over an earpiece, scolding her frequently. When the show ultimately does well during its second episode, which features an interview with Alya Césaire about the Ladyblog, Arlette grows pleased with Nadja and compliments her on a job well done.
Later, following the acquisition of TVi by Luxus Corp., Arlette had no choice but to fire Nadja at the request of Noé Luxus, as Nadja wanted to denounce the film "Le Secret de Ladybug" of which Noé Luxus was the producer.

title: Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel
text:
Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel - Intro
The  is a monument built at the request of Napoleon I in 1808 and located in the Place du Carrousel, in the 1° arrondissement of Paris, near the Louvre Palace and the garden Carrousel, being in the continuity of the Jardin des Tuileries.

title: Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel
text:
Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel - Description
Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel measures 14.6 meters high, 19.5 meters wide and 6.7 meters thick. It is built of beige Liais stone. It consists of three arcades on its two main facades, the largest being in the center and the two small ones being of the same size. In addition, the two side facades also have an arcade similar in size to the small arcades of the main facades.
The two main facades each have four Corinthian columns supported by pedestals. Large Roman-style tailors and Corinthian basket capitals surmount its columns. There are high-reliefs above on the upper part.

title: Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel
text:
Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel - Trivia
The Arc de Triomphe del Carrousel has been classified as a Historical Monument since 1888.
This monument served as the main entrance to the Tuileries Palace until its fire in 1871 and the destruction of the aforementioned palace in 1883.
In reality, the Arc de Triomphe del Carrousel is covered with statues and more noticeable reliefs, but they aren't seen in the series.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - Intro
August is a baby boy who debuted in "Glaciator".

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Glaciator", August was crossing the street in his stroller with his mother when they stopped as a runaway bus was about to hit them. They are saved by Ladybug and Cat Noir who effectively stopping the bus before hitting them. This makes his mother fall to the ground while August started babbling.
In "Gigantitan", August is seen taking a stroll with his mother at the Trocadéro. There they past by Adrien Agreste, whom waves at August. Vincent then shows up with a lollipop, which makes August become excited at the sight of the candy. He soon becomes upset as he is taken away from it, and his mother gives him his bottle to compensate him. They then continue their stroll, his mother is having trouble getting her son's stroller up the stairs. As she continues to struggle, August wants a lollipop but his mom says no and he cries. They finally makes it to the top and his mother feeds him again, which calms him down.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 2]]
August and his mother then continue to go up the stairs, with his mother dropping her phone and Marinette Dupain-Cheng going over to help her. Helping them Marinette gives his mother her phone, says hello to her son and helps her the rest of the way expressing her thanks. They then finally make it to the very top, but August drops his bottle causing him to cry until Marinette gets it for him. After Marinette leaves, his mother tries to calm him down by giving him his bottle, with August pulling away.
Continuing their stroll, they pass by Placide I.T. as August continued to cry. This makes his mother angry as she stops to try to calm him down. Just then, an akuma flies into August's ID bracelet, leaving Hawk Moth mortified as he wanted Placide to be akumatized but nonetheless goes with the idea and improvises. He tries to get August to understand in exchange for his powers he'll get the Miraculous, but he's more interested in lollipops nevertheless he gets transformed into Gigantitan, a giant baby supervillain.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 2]]
Gigantitan almost steps on his mother and pulls up a statue from its pedestal and sucks on it, thinking it was a lollipop. After tasting it, he tosses down the statue and started to cry. Gigantitan then noticed Placide I.T. and thinking he was a lollipop, he picks him up and starts to suck on him. After tasting him, he throws the bodyguard away and he lands on a tree. Gigantitan then noticed Alya Césaire, Mylène Haprèle, Rose Lavillant, and Juleka Couffaine and he tries to grab them, but they run away.
He attempts to follow the girls when he suddenly hears the sound of a bell, which is shown to be Cat Noir jingling the bell he wears. Gigantitan then attempts to grab him, but fails. Cat Noir then decides to play chase with him bringing the baby villain to an area where he can't do any damage. Gigantitan then manages to grab the hero and almost puts him into his mouth until Ladybug intervenes and Cat Noir uses his staff to escape. Understanding that the akuma is in his bracelet, Ladybug tries to lasso it but Gigantitan sents her flying to the top of a building where Cat Noir soon joins her.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 2]]
Gigantitan attempts to grab them, but Ladybug seeing his hand tries to get the bracelet but he throws her off again. He then follows the heroes until he spots the lollipop truck. Gigantitan then tried to get one but he accidentally crushes the truck causing him to cry but he hears the beeping of another car with Cat Noir inside; once Gigantitan finds it he starts to play with it leaving Hawk Moth very annoyed. Cat Noir then comments on how he liked to play with cars when he was little too as Gigantitan started to go to the Eiffel Tower while playing with the car. However, Hawk Moth was displeased and commanded him to attack the two heroes but Gigantitan was too busy playing.
Proceeding with her plan Ladybug creates an area with her yo-yo but Gigantitan is not happy about being in a playpen (Eiffel Tower) and pulls on the string. Cat Noir then tried using his Cataclysm his bracelet but just as he tried to do so, Gigantitan sents him flying. Then, with his enormous strength, Ladybug's yo-yo string ends up breaking the Eiffel Tower's supports, and the whole tower starts to fall behind Gigantitan.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 2]]
Ladybug then desperately tried to restrain on Gigantitan to no avail until Hawk Moth commands him to grab her. He then grabs her along with the lamppost she was holding on to. Seeing what's going on she tells Gigantitan not to put whatever he sees in his mouth until Alya and the others intervened as she riding the rickshaw, with Mylène, Juleka, and Rose sitting on the passenger seats holding onto the fake No-Parking sign. Thinking that the fake No-Parking sign was a lollipop, Gigantitan releases Ladybug. But, Hawk Moth who was furious told him not to let Ladybug get away but doesn't listen.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 2]]
Alya gets exhausted and the girls ditch the bike and Gigantitan finally gets his lollipop but when he puts it in his mouth it doesn't taste like one and he starts to cry again. Until Cat Noir calls him over with his bell seeing a real treat he picks it up and finds Ladybug inside she finally manages to break the bracelet and releasing the akuma. Gigantitan is transforms back into August in mid-air, and Cat Noir catches him when he falls. Soon August and his mother are reunited and just as their transformations are about to wear off they take their leave before saying goodbye while August and his mother express their thanks.
In "Befana", Jean Duparc helps August and the woman taking care of him get his stroller out of the subway. August then watched as Jean was transformed into a fairy by the titular villain.
In "Gorizilla", August is seen at the subway station in his stroller. There the woman taking care of him brought August along in his stroller as she chased after Adrien Agreste.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Catalyst", August became one of the victims akumatized by Scarlet Moth, being transformed back into a scarlet version of Gigantitan. He was then instructed by Scarlet Moth to head to the Eiffel Tower where he is. At the Eiffel Tower, Gigantitan watched as Scarlet Moth arrive and made a statement to the Ladybug and Cat Noir.
In "Mayura", Gigantitan is first seen at the Eiffel Tower, chanting Scarlet Moth's name. He then watched as the French Miraculous superhero team battled the Scarlet Army. Later, Gigantitan and all the other giant scarlet akumatized villains are ordered by Scarlet Moth to destroy the heroes and anyone else who tries to stand in your way as they all saluted their leader. Gigantitan then goes into the city, where a civilian calls his attention using a car. Gigantitan then starts playing with the car.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 3]]
In "Chameleon", August and the woman taking care of him were crossing the street, when the titular villain jumped in front of a bus causing it to swerve off the road. It nearly hits August and the woman, but their thankfully saved by Ladybug just in time.
In "Backwarder", the titular villain touches August and the woman taking care of him with her clock-hand sword, making them move and talk backwards in time.
In "Weredad", August is transformed into Gigantitan again by Hawk Moth, with the akuma going into his pacifier. Gigantitan then starts causing havoc throughout Paris looking for some cake. When he approaches the Tom & Sabine Boulangerie Patisserie. Ladybug tries to restrain Gigantitan with her yo-yo, but he flings her into a giant Adrien Agretse advertisment. Ladybug then calls on her Lucky Charm, receiving a giant plastic donut and Gigantitan grabs the donut and puts it in his mouth. Though upon realizing that it isn't food, he throws it away and it smashes through Marinette's room.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 3]]
Ladybug and Cat Noir then defeat Gigantitan and turn him back into August in mid-air, and Ladybug catches him when he falls. Ladybug then picks up pacifier and kisses him, causing Cat Noir to remark that he's jealous. Ladybug gives August to him and takes off and Cat Noir notices how sad August looks all of a sudden and at first believes that he misses Ladybug, but soon realizes that he wants his pacifier.
August then accompanied Cat Noir as he took off after Ladybug but is surprised when he instead finds Marinette. There he watched as Cat Noir commented on how Marinette always appears just after Ladybug detransforms, Marinette telling the superhero that she's in love with him, and Tom Dupain inviting Cat Noir to have brunch at his house on Sunday. Once they leaves, Cat Noir tells August that he'd assumed that Marinette was just a fan and is surprised that she's in love with him.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 3]]
In "Miraculer", August and his mother are seen taking a stroll at the Place des Vosges. He asks his mom for a lollipop and when she says no, August starts sobbing. Mayura who was watching them then sends an amok his way. It infects his pacifier and causes a giant lollipop sentimonster to appear. August then drops his pacifier as he sees the sentimonster and soon his mother runs away with him in his stroller.
In "Gamer 2.0", August was one of the many former akumatized villains that the titular villain zapped into his video game dimension. Gigantitan (played by Ladybug) fights Sandboy (played by the titular villain) and easily wins. After the villain is defeated by Ladybug and Cat Noir, August and the others are freed by Ladybug's Miraculous Ladybug.

title: August/History
text:
August/History - [[Season 4]]
In "Hack-San", August is seen in the background taking a stroll in his stroller with his mother near the Jardins du Trocadéro.
In "Kuro Neko", August is transformed into Gigantitan again by Shadow Moth and takes Clara Contard hostage. He is seen on the news causing a panic, but luckily Ladybug and her team save the day. Carapace uses Shell-ter to capture Gigantitan, then Pegasus using Voyage, which opens a portal towards Gigantitan face. Pigella uses Gift on him, which shows him his mother which causes him to stop.
Then Carapace removes the shield and Vesperia uses Venom to immobilize him. Ladybug takes his bracelet and breaks it to release the Akuma and deakumatize it. This causes him to detransform back into into August and drop the reporter, Clara Contard but Ladybug manages to catch them both and then returns August to his mother.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - Intro
Audrey Bourgeois is the famous director of the fashion magazine, Style Queen. She is also the ex-wife of André Bourgeois and the mother of Chloé Bourgeois and Zoé Lee by different fathers. She was living in Paris, but she is now currently staying in London with Chloé.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - Before [[Season 1]]
When Audrey was younger, she spent her time in a little attic room with Anaximandre Bourgeois (later André Bourgeois), Gabi Grassette (later Gabriel Agreste), and Lady Émilie Graham de Vanily (later Émilie Agreste). Anaximandre had fallen in love with Audrey and to win her over he got into politics just like his father. To declare his love for her, Anaximandre wrote, directed, and produced the film Solitude.
Sometime after, Audrey married Anaximandre, who had changed his name to André for her, and together they both had their daughter Chloé. At some point, Audrey also started her own fashion brand, Style Queen. When Chloé was a toddler, Audrey left her in Paris and moved to New York, USA. While there, she presumably had an affair with someone and had her second daughter Zoé Lee. She also started running her fashion empire from New York.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Style Queen", Audrey returned to Paris to watch a "Gabriel" fashion show, but after being denied a front-row seat, she was akumatized into Style Queen, a glitter-themed villain. The first thing she did as Style Queen was turned Adrien Agreste into a glitter statue and then other spectators. When Chloé offers to be her assistant, Style Queen accepts but later turns her into a glitter statue when she catches her helping Ladybug. After being deakumatized, Audrey walked down the Eiffel Tower and back to the fashion show with Chloé. Despite Chloé's attempts to bond with her mother, Audrey dismisses her.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Queen Wasp", Audrey returns to watch Gabriel's fashion show. Afterward, she was approached by Gabriel himself, who apologizes for the misunderstanding and says that only the front row is befitting for Audrey Bourgeois. Then, she notices Marinette Dupain-Cheng's hat and takes a liking to it, even offering her a chance to come with her to New York to become a famous fashion designer. When asked by Chloé why she was taking Marinette instead of her own daughter, Audrey said it was because Chloé wasn't exceptional like Marinette, angering her to the point where she revealed Pollen and the Bee Miraculous to be in her possession. After she transforms into Queen Bee and takes off, Audrey calls her daughter a showoff and later calls her out on her irresponsibility after a subway train incident, causing Chloé to become akumatized into Queen Wasp. Once deakumatized, Audrey announces on live TV that there is nothing exceptional about her daughter. However, thanks to Marinette, she later learns that she has a lot in common with her daughter, takes back her earlier comment, and embraces her. She decides to stay in Paris and be a part of Chloé's life.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Malediktator", after hearing about Chloé's failed presentation, Audrey and Chloé demand that André close down the school and banish Marinette from Paris. When he cannot, she decides that they should move to New York instead and is annoyed when André refuses to come with them. When she and Chloé are confronted by Malediktator, Audrey tells her husband that getting himself akumatized does not make him a cool or hip father. While she rants, Malediktator turns her into a loving and devoted wife willing to stay in Paris with him. While under his spell, she constantly clings onto him affectionately and talks in a sweet tone. She takes a liking to the cat-like Cat Noir and begs Malediktator to let her keep him a little longer. After Malediktator's defeat, Audrey is turned back to normal and is furious with her husband for his actions, yet calms down when Chloé intervenes and suggests that they go home.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Mayura", Audrey, along with her husband and butler, are preparing to leave Paris on the Bourgeois helicopter but they are struck by Dark Cupid's arrows, causing their emotions about Chloé being a superhero to become negative. She is akumatized into a scarlet version of Style Queen as a result and battles Queen Bee, along with Malediktator and Despair Bear.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 3]]
In "Feast", Audrey was watching the news about the reappearance of the Guardians' temple with a smile.
In "Gamer 2.0", Audrey was one of the many former akumatized villains that the titular villain zapped into his video game dimension. Style Queen (played by Ladybug) fights Vanisher (played by the titular villain) and easily wins. After the villain is defeated by Ladybug and Cat Noir, Audrey and the others are freed by Ladybug's Miraculous Ladybug.
In "Heart Hunter", Audrey and her husband are celebrating their twentieth wedding anniversary but Audrey's foul mood causes an argument to take place and get the two akumatized into Heart Hunter, a villain who devoured love. They are freed from being akumatized when Hawk Moth keeps his promise to Chloé to free them if she joined the villain. When the couple is saved from falling by the heroes, they are shown embracing.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 3]]
In "Miracle Queen", Audrey and André are brainwashed by Chloé when she gets akumatized into Miracle Queen. After her defeat, Chloé attempts to get her parents to move them to New York, but the couple is revealed to have rekindled their affections for one another, leading Audrey to decide to stay in Paris and try to repair their familial bond.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 4]]
In "Sole Crusher", Audrey greets Zoé, who has flown from New York. However, Audrey does not greet her younger daughter warmly as she makes a comment about her appearance and has Armand introduce her to Chloé. After Zoe was deakumatized and made friends with Marinette and the others, Audrey is with Chloé and André when she returns to the hotel. When Chloé demands Zoe be returned to New York, Audrey appears to agree with Chloé and only stops when her husband points out that there would be a lot of paperwork to be done first and provides an arrangement to keep the girls apart while living in the hotel.
In "Gabriel Agreste", Audrey was invited to Gabriel Agreste's party.
In "Optigami", after being insulted and mocked on live television by Sentialec during her magazine's awards event, Fashion Icon of the Month, Audrey was akumatized again and transformed into Style Queen Queen. She later received a Magical Charm from Ladybug, who hid it in her hat.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 4]]
In "Hack-San", after Robostus sends out a signal to all Parisians with a message sent through their phones, Audrey is hypothesized offscreen. Audrey is then sent by Robostus to Musée Grévin and she is positioning where her statue used to be. There after Scarabella and Cat Noir arrived, Audrey unfreezes from his position. She then pulls out her phone and moves towards the heroes. Audrey is then commanded to seize the Ladybug and the Cat Miraculous, along with other high-profile hypothesized the individuals. She then watched as Scarabella and Cat Noir delivered themselves to Robostus. Later, Audrey is freed from Robostus' control by Scarabella's Miraculous Scarabella.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 5]]
In "Adoration", Audrey is seen walking down the hotel's main staircase during Chloé's outrage. When Chloé informs her of what Zoé did, she shrugs it off and threatens to send both of her daughters to New York if they continue to confuse her. She receives three credit cards from her husband, then exits the hotel.
In "Emotion", Audrey is seen with André and Chloé when they enter the Diamonds' Dance, and walks away after her daughter makes a remark about Adrien. She is once again seen standing at the entrance at the right side once Marinette enters the area, then she walks along the path with the rest of the adults. She is once again seen in the ballroom, sitting with her husband, Gabriel Agreste, and Tomoe Tsurugi. Once Félix reveals himself, he poofs her along with everyone else in the room using his sentimonster. Félix later reverts the damage he caused, bringing Audrey back.
In "Confrontation", Audrey told André not to have Chloé and Lila expelled by having principal Dennis fired from his job.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 5]]
In "Revolution", Audrey was proud to see her daughter being the new mayoress and outlawing Ladybug, Cat Noir, and Monarch. Later, in the evening she was seen with some of Chloé's supporters, beaming over her rule over the city. She was shocked to see a revolution against her daughter and ran away from the chaos.
When Chloé was deakumatized and ousted as mayor, they left for London, and Audrey was very ashamed and upset that her daughter lost her powers foolishly and ruined their family name and reputation; reminding her the Bourgeois family don't raise losers. She assures Chloé that she was not going to London for a vacation and vows to take control of her life again; beginning with her education when they get to London.

title: Audrey Bourgeois/History
text:
Audrey Bourgeois/History - [[Season 6]]
In "Noe", Audrey was inside a car, where she was joined by her son. When he announced that he had already presented himself to Paris and the next phase of their plan could begin, she complimented him before smirking.
In "Queen of the Dreadzone", Audrey sat on a director's chair next to Noé at Collège Françoise Dupont as they watched the setup and shooting of Chloé's movie. She was getting irritated and trying to stop her daughter from going against their plans for the day, but was convinced otherwise by her son. She was relieved that, as a world famous influencer, Chloé was finally serving a purpose, even if she didn't understand it. She watched the whole interaction between her daughter and Marinette, Sabrina and Zoé, exchanging glances with Noé the moment Chloé was about to get akumatized.

title: Aton Kurtzberg
text:
Aton Kurtzberg - Intro
is a minor character in Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir first introduced in season 6. He is the husband of Shirel Kurtzberg and the father of Nathaniel Kurtzberg.

title: Aton Kurtzberg
text:
Aton Kurtzberg - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Aton is a man of medium height, white skin, and blue eyes. He has auburn hair with wild upward curls that flares out in different directions, though has one short, downward strand against his forehead.
Civilian Attire
He wears a purple jacket with pink edges open over a white long-sleeved button shirt and matching purple pants. He wears a black belt with a brown buckle, a pair of sunglasses tucked in his shirt, and a pair of brown dress shoes.

title: Aton Kurtzberg
text:
Aton Kurtzberg - Personality
Aton seems to be a very calm, laid-back, and rather open person, who enjoys the arts. Compared to his stricter wife, Aton is more relaxed and affable, but this attitude makes him more submissive to Shirel, especially in parenting their son whom he has a more positive relationship with.

title: Aton Kurtzberg
text:
Aton Kurtzberg - Abilities
Aton is an artist, although it is unknown what type of medium or field he works in. Since his son began publishing his work with Marc, he has been his beta reader, although he isn't very good at it; for example, in his last work, he told him to pair one of the male protagonists with the villain just because she was a woman, even after his son explained it to him.

title: Aton Kurtzberg
text:
Aton Kurtzberg - Relationships
Family
Shirel Kurtzberg
Aton disagrees with his wife about Nathaniel's future: he supports and advises him on his comic strip, while his wife wants him to focus on a more prestigious artistic career, such as architecture. As Shirel was the more assertive of the two, Aton tends to get pushed into following along with her opinions, even though deep down, he doesn't want to and lacked confidence to stand up to Shirel.
Nathaniel Kurtzberg
Aton supports Nathaniel in his passion for comics and uses his knowledge to advise his son on the plot of his work, especially regarding the relationships between the characters. Nathaniel, however, seems to be a bit skeptical of his father's advice, as his father does not seem to have understood the nature of the relationship between the two main characters. In the end, after reading the next comic book, he gives out a better opinion by saying that there were strong sentiments of the comic book and that he wouldn't change anything about it.
Acquaintances
Marc Anciel
Aton supports his son's collaboration with Marc and displays more warmth to his son's partner, as such inviting him into a group hug at the end of "The Ruler".

title: Aton Kurtzberg
text:
Aton Kurtzberg - Etymology
The name "Aton" is of Egyptian origin and means "solar disk", which is a visual representation of the Egyptian sun god, Aten. It also has a meaning of "reconciliation" in Hebrew, being the root word for "atonement".
Aton's surname "Kurtzberg" is variant of "Kurzberg", which means "short mountain" in German and Jewish origins.
His last name Kurtzberg is a reference to the famous American comic book artist Jack Kirby, who was born as Jacob Kurtzberg.

title: Aton Kurtzberg
text:
Aton Kurtzberg - Trivia
He is based on Aton Soumache, an executive producer of the series, having received the same name.
