title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Intro
is a major character in Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir, serving as the secondary antagonist of Season 1, the deuteragonist of Season 2, a major anti-hero turned final antagonist of Season 3, a major antagonist in Season 4, one of the three secondary antagonists (alongside Lila Rossi/Cerise Bianca and Tomoe Tsurugi) of Season 5, and a minor antagonist in Season 6.
She is a rival of Marinette Dupain-Cheng (and later Ladybug). She is also the daughter of André and Audrey Bourgeois, the younger half-sister of Noé Luxus and the older half-sister of Zoé Lee.
She is a former student in Miss Bustier's class at Collège Françoise Dupont, a former resident of Paris and former interim Mayoress of Paris following her father's resignation, all until the end of "Revolution", when she was expelled from school and left Paris along with her mother for her many abuses of power.
In "Antibug", after Ladybug ignored her suggestions on how to beat Vanisher and even called her a liar, she was akumatized by Hawk Moth and became Antibug, a supervillain copy of Ladybug with an inverted color scheme and Anti-Charm as her superpower, which unlike Lucky Charm, granted her real weapons.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Intro
In "Queen's Battle", after Ladybug lost the Bee Miraculous that she wanted to entrust Alya Césaire with, Chloé found it. When the Miraculous was inhabited by Pollen, she became Queen Bee, a bee-themed anti-hero who helped Ladybug and Cat Noir "during particularly difficult missions" in Seasons 2 and 3.  After a failed attempt at impressing her mother, Queen Bee was akumatized by Hawk Moth and became Queen Wasp, a wasp-themed supervillain.
In "Miraculer", after being manipulated by Lila Rossi and believing that Ladybug would not recruit her as Queen Bee anymore, she was nearly akumatized by Hawk Moth. However, Chloé resisted and rejected the akumatization. After the titular villain was deakumatized, Ladybug told Chloé that she could no longer call upon her to be Queen Bee due to the risk her identity being public knowledge placed upon both her and her family.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Intro
In "The Battle of the Miraculous", after being passed over too many times by Ladybug and being manipulated by Hawk Moth, Queen Bee joined the villains' side and was akumatized into Miracle Queen, an upgraded version of Queen Wasp who could brainwash Miraculous holders by stinging them with wasps, setting in motion Hawk Moth's "elaborate mortal plan". After being deakumatized by Ladybug and losing her army of brainwashed superheroes, the Miracle Box, and the Bee Miraculous, Ladybug terminated Chloe from being Queen Bee. Chloé became bitter towards Ladybug and declared she would no longer be her fan and friend.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Intro
In "Queen Banana", after being removed from the movie Kreatika and being replaced by her half-sister as the main character, and after ending her friendship with Adrien Agreste, Chloé was akumatized and amokized by Shadow Moth into Queen Banana, a banana-themed supervillain. Her anger, pride, sadness, and frustration form Banana Boom-Boom, a banana-themed gorilla sentimonster. Ladybug tried to give her a Magical Charm to prevent her from being akumatized again, but she initially rejected it. However, she accepted the Magical Charm after Zoé claimed it was a gift from their mother.
In "Penalteam", after getting fed up by the class playing soccer, Chloé's Magical Charm was destroyed by Shadow Moth and she was voluntarily akumatized into Penalty, a soccer-themed supervillain multiplied into ten clones capable of trapping people in force fields. With her clones, she formed the supervillain team Penalteam.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Intro
In "Deflagration", after being confronted and subsequently humiliated by Zoé in front of the whole school, Chloé was voluntarily akumatized by Monarch into Sole Destroyer, a villain resembling her own half-sister's akumatized form, Sole Crusher, transforming anyone she stomped on into singing heeled shoes.
In "Confrontation", Chloé and Lila framed Marinette for forging their classmates' study option forms in order to get them to turn against her. Their plan backfired when she and Lila fell into a trap set up by Marinette and Sabrina to reveal their true plan in front of their entire class and the school faculty. Following this, while Lila was expelled from school, Chloé received special attention from Miss Bustier as punishment.
In "Collusion", with the help of Cerise ("Lila"), through Gabriel's manipulation, and after her father resigned as mayor, Chloé took over her father's position as the mayoress of Paris, effectively banishing superheroes from Paris.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Intro
In "Revolution", Chloé allied herself with Monarch for the last time and was akumatized into Queen Mayor, a political supervillain. Her police robots received the superpowers of the Ox, Turtle, Rooster, Bee and Horse Miraculous, allowing her to enforce "Chloé's law" and imprison dissidents as she pleased. After being defeated, she lost her position as Mayoress of Paris and she is forced to leave Paris with her mother.
In "Queen of the Dreadzone", Chloé returned to Paris to shoot a movie. After discovering Sabrina was able to move on from her and Marinette is no longer afraid of her, she was akumatized by Chrysalis into Dread Queen, a queen bee-themed supervillain with the ability to create a "dreadzone" that made anyone in its radius afraid of her. At the end of the episode, Mayor Bustier revoked her permit to shoot her movie at the school, and with no one left to fear her, Chloé was forced to leave Paris once again. Ladybug also hid a Magical Charm in Chloé's purse as a reminder of her actions, but Chloé discovered it and had her employee discard it.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Chloé is a slender light-skinned teenage girl of medium height. She wore pale, light grayish cerulean eye-shadow, pale, light pink lip-gloss, and a light scarlet blush. She has slit brilliant cobalt blue eyes, pale pink lips, and honey blonde curly chest-length hair. Her hair is parted in the middle and pulled back into a high ponytail held in place by a white hair tie. She had thin forelocks that curled upwards in front of either ear.
From Season 6 onwards, her hair has grown longer and her forelocks form into ringlet curls at the ends, with a curled strand in front of the left ear. She also has light yellow nail polish with a bee design.
Civilian Attire

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Appearance
In the first five seasons, Chloé wore a sparkly brilliant yellow bolero that went halfway down her forearms with a light blue button on the right side and one pocket on the right side, which was over a white shirt with black horizontal stripes around the chest running down to the bottom of the waist. The rest of her outfit included white capris with a dull gold belt that had pyramid-shaped bumps, and white flats adorned with white laced bows, with black lining around the toe, and black soles. For accessories, she had a gold chain necklace with a small gold disco ball, and white-rimmed sunglasses with dark brown transparent lenses on her head.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Appearance
From Season 6 onwards, her thicker bolero is darker with a dark gold outlined honeycomb pattern with hexagons inside, and a bee-shaped necklace. Her button is now on the left and is cream with three more below it, and she accessorizes with a silver beaded bracelet and a goldenrod wristband on her left wrist. She wears a skirt to match her bolero in replacement of her pants, and white knee-high boots with black heels. Her sunglasses also have a more angular design and the lenses become cherry pink. The Bee Miraculous, as the shape of a bee on a gold comb, was placed on the upper right side of her head next to the hairband.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In her childhood, Chloé was a curious girl who liked to wander around the hotel to spy on people; however, in her adolescence, she became a narcissistic, bossy, egotistical, superficial bully who does everything in her power to crush others and loves making her rivals' lives miserable, particularly Marinette Dupain-Cheng who she despises; even calling Marinette by her surname just to get at her. She thinks highly of herself and lowly of others, believing that she deserves everything and takes pride in her luxurious lifestyle. This has also caused her to view herself as above any consequences of her actions. To the point where she believed in "Derision", "what was the point of having power or status if you can't use it on those who don't". As well as similar to Gabriel, Chloé too misunderstood the meaning of her powers, learning from what she wanted instead of what she needed.
She believes that she is the most important person in the world and everyone adores her, a part of herself that stems primarily from her desire to be viewed with as much importance as Ladybug and her mother, who both sustain a high sense of power within the world and retain a sense of privilege among society.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
If there is something that she wants, like attention, revenge, or a greater sense of control over others, Chloé will do anything, including underhanded actions, to succeed. She occasionally steals and tampers with other people's belongings or moments in an attempt to humiliate them or remove them from what she believes is an opportunity to steer a situation in her favor and obtain what she personally wants, even calling her father to forcefully use his position as mayor to threaten adults, such as Denis Damoclès, into turning a blind eye to her actions and punish others, such as Alya, regardless of being at fault for a situation. Chloé was rarely seen treating any of her peers respectfully, being bossy and overbearing to her "best friend" Sabrina and claimed to her mother that she was just using the former. Her sour attitude comes across openly to whatever and whoever she despises, but will sometimes pretend to be innocent and emotionally distressed to manipulate others in front of her father.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
While being callous and careless to anyone but herself, Chloé can be cowardly and easily scared of danger often caused by akumatized villains. Having caused certain people to be akumatized (especially throughout Season 1), to her horror and confusion, she found herself their victim for revenge. Despite some of them calling her out for her nasty behavior, she narcissistically disagreed with them, believing she had no fault in the matter leading to their akumatization, seldom for a select few, such as her father. Chloé sometimes acted like a daddy's girl, as her father spoiled her immensely, and would often call on him (or at least threatened to) to enforce her will with her peers and even superiors to, allowing her to avoid consequences and instead enforce consequences upon others.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Despite all of these traits, Chloé did have moments of courage as she was willingly helpful when asked by those she was close to or admired, such as helping Ladybug defeat Despair Bear and asking her to help save Adrien from her akumatized mother. Like her mother, she has a fierce temper when angered. Chloé remains awful most of the time, but has brief moments of kindness, expressing happiness when Ladybug was saving her or towards Sabrina. She also listened to advice at rare moments, like following Ladybug's suggestion to reconcile with Sabrina. If requested for a purpose, particularly by Adrien so that she could still be friends with him, she knew how to act congenial around others, although she often came off as forced and couldn't keep it up for long.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
On rare occasions, Chloé has been shown to be willing to say or do the right thing, even being remorseful towards her actions. As seen when she apologized to Miss Bustier about forgetting her birthday, ruining the present Marinette made for her and her temper. After being deakumatized in "Queen Wasp", she sincerely apologized to Ladybug and Cat Noir for selfishly using her superpowers and for what happened to Pollen because of her actions. In "Animaestro", when Chloé found out about Marinette's crush on Adrien, she decided not to tell him as she believed that Marinette didn't deserve attention, showing that although her actions had moments of goodness, they were only motivated by her inner selfishness.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Ultimately, Chloé's abrasive and selfish attitude stems from a massive inferiority complex, born from the neglect her mother showed her as a child. As seen through their interactions, Audrey cared little for her daughter up until the events of "Queen Wasp", even failing to remember her name on many occasions, and only gives attention to things that interest her. This caused Chloé to try and emulate her mother's unpleasant behavior in a vain attempt to win her affection. Additionally, she sometimes shows a lack of self-confidence behind her arrogance, feeling that nothing she does has any real value no matter what she tries, even referring to herself as "useless" to Ladybug in "Malediktator". Yet, once she received the Bee Miraculous, she finally began to feel that she had true worth and value. However, her desire to help others stemmed from her love for attention, not from any willingness to do the right thing.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In "Stormy Weather 2", when she insulted Aurore and caused her to be akumatized, Chloé's shown waiting for Ladybug to give her the Bee Miraculous. This either suggests she might've deliberately provoked the akumatization or, alternatively, that while she didn’t intend for it to happen, she was nonetheless eager to seize any opportunity to become a hero again. The latter option seems to be the more likely of the two due to it being behavior consistently shown with Chloé, as she is shown waiting for Ladybug’s call to action during "Catalyst", on two separate akuma during "Miraculer", and one last time in "Heart Hunter".
As Queen Bee, she was proud of her abilities and wanted to prove herself to her mother by causing a subway train accident to save it so the civilians would be grateful towards her, feeling no remorse over the lives she would endanger in the process if they were saved in the end.
She didn't care about hiding her superhero identity in the process, revealing Pollen to the public, and transforming in the eyes of everyone in the area.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
She wanted to be a famous, well-known, and well-liked hero just like Ladybug, so she called Nadja Chamack to film her saving the said subway train.
After Marinette helped her repair her relationship with Audrey, by making them realize their similarities as mother and daughter, Chloé expressed a sense of pride in taking much delight in tormenting others, same as her mother.
However, after a talk with Ladybug, she tearfully revealed that she is aware that no one in her class likes her and felt useless.
When given the Bee Miraculous by Ladybug, she heroically helped her defeat the titular villain and returned the Miraculous without hesitation.
Afterward, she attempted to be a better person by cleaning up her lair instead of having her butler do it.
She was happy that everyone at school threw her a party in honor of her saving Paris, but quickly took it as an opportunity to boast about her wealth and new-found popularity among the student body as her title as hero was acknowledged.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Although Chloé had finally obtaining the title of a hero she had always dreamed of having, her focus gradually steered away from the lessons the heroes taught her and the promises she made to do better upon realizing her new found title bared privileges she deemed of a higher priority to uphold over the work and sacrifices needed to become a better person, not understanding that her role as the bee miraculous holder was granted to her temporarily and was initially intended on Ladybug's part with the hope that it would help give her the motivation needed to push her towards fixing her messes and finding a better path for herself in life.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Similar to Cat Noir, Queen Bee had a bit of a habit of leaping before looking, meaning she was hasty or quick to act, as she quickly apologized to her father instead of listening to Ladybug's plan first and when she was eager to battle Scarlet Moth's akumatized army. Although she would claim to understand Ladybug's reason for not wanting her to use the Bee Miraculous for the sake of the safety of Chloé and her loved ones, she often used her Bee Signal light in hopes of Ladybug giving her the Bee Miraculous for any situation that arose, convincing herself that Queen Bee was needed to defeat every villain that surfaced and believed Queen Bee could do the job far better and more efficiently than the other Miraculous holders. Each time that Ladybug did not give her the Bee Miraculous, Chloé became angry but still felt confident that the heroine would call upon her during the extremely difficult situations.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
However, in "Heart Hunter", Chloé was shown to have grown resentful towards Ladybug after being passed up to help out so many times, believing that she was entitled to the powers of the Bee Miraculous, and deserved them regardless of the consequences, refusing to understand that the Bee Miraculous power did not belong to her. According to Ladybug, while she isn't impressed by others in power, she has grown possessive of her own powers, unwilling to let them go or share them with others. When her parents were akumatized in this episode, she hoped that Ladybug would give her the Bee Miraculous so she could save them. Instead, she saw that Ladybug chose another heroine over her and became very upset. Hawk Moth, who managed to steal the Miracle Box, gave Chloé the Bee Miraculous and used her anger to manipulate her into turning against Ladybug, all without akumatizing her. Chloé's allegiance to him ultimately stemmed from the realization that he was willing to ensure he could provide her whatever power she wanted rather than keep it from her in the same way Ladybug did.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In "Miracle Queen", regardless of her betrayal, Ladybug was willing to offer her another chance to refrain from allying with Hawk Moth and return all the Miraculous in her possession. However, by openly expressing her resentment towards Ladybug for not providing her the power of the Bee Miraculous, Chloé revealed that she refused to understand that the power of the Miraculous was not her right to use, much to Ladybug's shock and disbelief. After Ladybug deakumatized her, took back the Miracle Box and the Bee Miraculous, and terminated her from the French superhero team, Chloé bitterly renounced her loyalty to and friendship with Ladybug, officially becoming her enemy.
In the two aforementioned episodes, it is shown via Chloé's behavior that, because of her attitude and life long belief that her rich upbringing granted her the right to target those she deemed beneath her, she didn't fully understand one of the main responsibilities of being a true hero is selflessness.
By giving up her powers, she was unknowingly protecting everyone in her life from Paris' villains.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Through her actions, just as Hawk Moth used his family's love to cover his guilt of akumatizing innocent civilians, Chloé did the same to cover up her desire for power and glory.
Although Chloé was eager to do good as a superhero, she lacked commitment to continue her duties without her superpowers.
Even though Chloé made efforts to make up for some of her mistakes before "Miracle Queen", she did not make an effort to maintain this change or attempted to make up for them, implying that she did not feel compelled to acknowledge her past mistakes, let alone admit that she needed to change her behavior and apologize to those she wronged and took advantage of so long as she still bared the title of a hero, leaving the impression that Chloé did not see the need for self-improvement so long as she continued to obtain what she wanted and to become Queen Bee at her own request rather than Ladybug's.
Yet it seems the neglect she suffered because of her mother also had lasting effects: when Chloé was told she couldn't be a hero anymore, she was consumed by the fear that Ladybug considered her worthless and would neglect her as Audrey did.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Sadly, she didn't have the maturity to separate the two instances and gave into her anger and Hawk Moth's false promises under the pretense that the heroine didn't care for her.
Ultimately, Chloé fooled herself, because if it wasn't for Ladybug and Cat Noir constantly saving her from the messes that she caused by getting people akumatized, she wouldn't be present, and despite all that the pair went through with her, the heroes continued to show her real love and kindness as real parents should.
Although she was so eager to become a superhero again, Ladybug's encouragement and Marinette's willingness to let go of their complicated past to show her kindness, did not convince her to abandon her ways, resulting in her succumbing to Hawk Moth's manipulations.
In the end, regardless of the many chances others were willing to give her, Chloé's need to prioritize herself and not lose the privileges she had grown accustomed to, ultimately led her to lose everything (powers, superhero status, reputation, etc.) to the point of becoming enemies with her former idols.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Throughout the fourth season, Chloé remained sore over the events in "Miracle Queen", with her selfishness, pettiness and anger being amplified over losing her hero status and powers. As such, her subsequent mistreatment towards other grew stronger while her kindness diminished towards everyone even more than in previous seasons: she treated Sabrina even more like a slave than ever, repeatedly and forcefully attempted to send her half-sister back to New York after the latter befriended Marinette and her other classmates, ended her friendship with Adrien in "Queen Banana", and further despises Ladybug when she chose a new Bee Miraculous user, believing the jewel was hers alone. Her anger became so intense that Shadow Moth admitted that it is limitless and Ladybug commented that she needs to control it. Despite this, she still accepted the Magical Charm when Zoé lied about it being from her mother, showing that she still cares for her mother, despite her increased aggression towards the citizens.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In "Sole Crusher", Chloé is shown to have gotten worse since the Season 3 finale, and has become more sadistic, cruel, mean, rude, uncaring, toxic, stubborn, manipulative, overly impulsive and selfish than ever, as she attempts to get her half-sister, Zoé to be more like her by convincing and manipulating her with her own beliefs that there are "winners and losers" in this world, a mindset inherited from their mother and ultimately becoming Chloé's preferred way of viewing the world around her regardless of understanding of how frowned upon it was among those who had attempted to guide her on the right path and serve as a better example for her to look up to.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Despite being related to and loved by Zoé, Chloé is unwilling to recognize anyone as family if they do not adhere to her strict rules of conduct of high society as well as finding the joys in viewing those like Marinette and Sabrina as people whose existence only serves to suffer for the entertainment of those in high society who can use them as doormats in whatever way they please. In order to ensure Zoé could uphold their family beliefs, she had Zoé reject Marinette's offer of friendship publicly and act mean toward her to earn her approval, seeing no wrong in threatening Zoé after catching her texting Marinette.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
When chased down by Zoé who got akumatized into the titular villain Sole Crusher, she uses several civilians as human shields to get away and pushing Marinette and her family into Sole Crusher's path, although Sole Crusher spared Marinette by holding her in her hand rather than absorbing her because of her kindness. Shortly following this, Chloé later tried to force Sole Crusher into attacking Kitty Section by cruelly threatening and blackmailing Sole Crusher of sending her back to New York if she doesn't comply with her demands while insulting her in the process, calling her a "ridiculous copy of her", showing zero care nor remorse that she deeply hurt her half-sister's feelings and shouted her catchphrase "Utterly ridiculous!" to taunt Sole Crusher. This forced Marinette to interfere and reason with Sole Crusher in hopes of preventing further violence and solving the situation peacefully before Sole Crusher could do anything and knowing that Chloé has gone too far this time and exposed Chloé's lies, false beliefs and mindset.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In "Gabriel Agreste", she implicated that she still cares for Adrien to some degree, despite having ended their friendship so spitefully, and chose to reconcile with him under her own terms. However, her attempts to reconcile were done selfishly as she tried to have him all to herself by attempting to expose her classmates' plan to bring him and Marinette together to Gabriel, and by extension, forcing Adrien's return to homeschooling which, in her mind, would allow him to seek her as the only source of social interaction again, with no outside interference, and return him to a state of being her Prince Charming, regardless of it being at the cost of Adrien's loneliness.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In "Penalteam", Chloé continued her mean streak by refusing to participate in the class's exhibition soccer game, forbidding Sabrina to play even though she enjoys the sport and is skilled at it, and even voluntarily accepted Shadow Moth's akumatization to ruin it. After being tricked into deakumatizing herself, she reluctantly allowed Sabrina to play while dressing her down as a "loser" like the rest of her class, though their friendship didn't end like with Adrien. Soon after, she voluntarily formed an alliance with Lila over their mutual hatreds of Marinette and Ladybug.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In the fifth season, with Monarch having stolen all the Miraculous, Chloé's bitterness towards Ladybug worsened, as she believes she and Cat Noir lost the Miraculous for being incompetent, and made no effort in hiding it, even going as far as to express her thoughts on live TV and social media. She also expressed believing that none of this would have happened if she was still Queen Bee, revealing that despite the consequences of her actions in previous seasons and despite her willingness to betray the heroes in favor of Hawk Moth, Chloé is willing to disregard her actions and genuinely believes she is still entitled to the power of the Bee Miraculous.
As the season continues, Chloé's anger, hatred, and desire for revenge grew, and as her status and power diminished, so did her emotional state, with her becoming more demanding, selfish and unreasonable than ever, to the point that Adrien finally gave up on ever reconciling with her and even her father admitted that she became completely heartless, which likely stemmed from her jealousy and fear of losing what little power she had left, from "Miracle Queen" to "Collusion".

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
This especially continued with Lila as her ally as they pushed forward in their alliance in plots and schemes to stymie Ladybug in her hero duties or ruin Marinette's life.
Chloé even went as far as to permanently throw away the chance to reconcile her friendship with Adrien, and her "friendship" with Sabrina worsened as she continued to treat her like a slave but treated Lila like an equal.
This culminated in Sabrina finally turning against her as she helped Marinette expose her and Lila's plan to destroy Marinette and ruin their classmates' futures, effectively stripping Chloé of the last possible friendship she had left.
Following this, Chloé went far above and beyond to destroy her enemies with her remaining power, such as unjustly getting Marinette expelled for something she didn't do and Ms.
Bustier fired for trying to talk sense into her.
She eventually accepted an offer from Monarch to become an interim mayoress of Paris after the villain engineered her father's resignation just to continue in her revenge and avoid the consequences of her actions.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In "Revolution", after labeling Ladybug, Cat Noir, and Monarch as fugitives and outlawing all superheroes and supervillains, Chloé, at Lila's urging, hypocritically made a deal with the latter to be akumatized and receive more powers from the Miraculouses, which she used to imprison people at will, particularly all who have ever stood up to and/or defied her, including her father; this shows just how mad she had gone with her power after losing respect for him in "Collusion".
She also set a trap to publicly expose Ladybug and Cat Noir's identities after forcing them to use their powers and confined them using robots supplied to her by Gabriel until their powers run out and they detransform.
However, the heroes managed to overcome the time limit and master their powers, and urged the citizens to revolt against Chloé's tyranny.
In quick succession, Chloé was deakumatized, ousted as mayor, abandoned by those who brought her to power, and finally forced to face the wrath of the entire population of Paris, who have come to despise her for her rule.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
She was even finally disciplined by her father, but sided to leave Paris with her mother to avoid further consequences, believing leaving with her mother meant she would go on vacation, but to her surprise was not intended by her mother who harshly reprimanded her for ruining their family name and reputation, and vowed to take control of her life again, starting with her education.
This left Chloé deeply upset that she even lost her mother's love and respect for her failure.
She briefly softened herself and considered calling Sabrina for consolation or to try and reconcile, but soon hardened again and decided to take one last shot at Marinette over Adrien's departure to London, demonstrating that, even at her lowest point, Chloé's instinct is to make someone else suffer to validate herself.
This, however, backfired as Marinette turned the tables on Chloé, revealing that she already knew about Adrien's departure (having just witnessed it beforehand) and reaffirming their love for each other, as well as telling Chloé, point-blank, the cold, hard truths that she no longer has any power over anyone or anything anymore, and that she is the "utterly ridiculous" one.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
Seeing her once-favorite punching bag stand up to and shut her down so harshly finally shattered Chloé's pride and spirit, and she broke down in tears after finally realizing that she has truly lost everything and hit rock-bottom.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In the sixth season, Chloé is revealed to have become a popular fashion model, actress, and social influencer while under her mother's teaching in London. In spite of her departure and lack of presence in Paris, Chloé has attracted a substantial following in the Bee Community on the new social media network Zoo, to the point of managing said community, and holding contests in which she grants the winner anything they desire. However, her grudge against Paris's heroes, especially Ladybug in particular, and some of the vile aspects of her personality seemingly remain intact, as shown in "Climatiqueen" when she bans members from communities whose animal corresponds with the heroes (especially the Ladybug community) from participating in her contests. In "Daddycop", when she hunts for a new minion to replace Sabrina, she throws shade at Sabrina for her previous "betrayal", while boastfully claiming to love her new life in London. It is currently unknown as to how much of Chloe's claims and personality are genuine.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
In "Queen of the Dreadzone", despite Sabrina's hopes, Chloé is shown to have learned nothing from the events of Season 5, wishing to mistreat the whole school by taking the building from them, especially Marinette, Sabrina and Zoé. When none of them were fazed, her anger grew so strong she didn't even talk to Chrysalis and immediately accepted being akumatized, choosing her own powers to make the three she despises be terrified of her presence. Her bitterness towards Vesperia and the team has only grown, resenting them when they deakumatize her, and rejecting the magical charm. After losing her permit to shoot a movie in the school, she immediately returned to London without having to reconcile anyone.
It is implied that the main reason Chloé has not changed her behavior is that her half-brother, Noé, allows her to act freely and do whatever she pleases and he convinces their mother to let her have her way by pointing out that Chloé can gain a large following and become famous which serves his own plans, while Chloé has begun turning to Noé to get what she wants, since she can no longer rely on her parents.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
As Antibug, most of Chloé's personality remained the same, except that she was more vengeful towards Ladybug. She enjoyed taunting her and Cat Noir about their teamwork, believing she was weak without him and Cat Noir was playing second fiddle.
As Queen Wasp, Chloé was prideful and arrogant towards Cat Noir and Ladybug, believing herself to be a more exceptional hero worthy of her mother's praise than both of them. She also wanted to prove herself by taking away their Miraculouses and felt angry towards everyone who dislikes her and paralyzed them.
As Miracle Queen, most of Chloé's personality remained the same except that she became meaner and more power-hungry, using her power to take control of all of Paris and turn the Miraculous holders into her own army.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
As Queen Banana, Chloé became immensely vengeful towards her half-sister Zoé, searching to turn her into a banana and blaming her for everything, all while turning everyone that crossed her and her sentimonster's path. She was also not afraid to show dishonesty, as she promised Zoé she wouldn't hurt anyone else if the latter gave herself up, but immediately turned a nearby bystander into a banana. Queen Banana was also very cunning and loved chaos as well. This was shown when she purposely allowed Cat Noir to use Cataclysm on her Sentimonster, causing him to go out of control and cause more chaos in Paris.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
As Penalty, since she was akumatized voluntarily, Chloé's personality remained the same as she was still cruel, unfair, hypocritical, and demanding, and didn't play fair by making her own rules, and yet, she didn't appreciate it when others cheated despite her doing the same. With her Penalteam, they worked well and cheated together, but started arguing and insulting each other when the Miraculous superheroes used their superpowers and made them all angry. As the heroes used her anger against her, she became fed up with Shadow Moth's demands, realizing his power was incapable of allowing her to torment the heroes like she wanted. Believing she lost the advantage in the game, regardless of how much she cheated, she willingly destroyed her own akumatized object.
As Sole Destroyer, since she was akumatized voluntarily, Chloé's personality remained the same. Unlike Zoé's akumatized form Sole Crusher who had a soft spot for Marinette, Sole Destroyer was willing to attempt to turn her into a singing shoe if it weren't for Adrien's interference.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Personality
As Queen Mayor, since she was akumatized voluntarily Chloé's personality remained the same. But she acted much more tyrannical than usual, as she was willing to imprison anyone who ever dared to confront her, including her own father.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Abilities
As a Civilian
Having grown up in politics due to her father's position, Chloé knows how to cheat, manipulate, fool, and humiliate others for her own personal success. If she has a goal in mind, she will do whatever it takes to achieve it, even if it means sabotaging others and bringing them down. For example, she told Sabrina Raincomprix to lock Juleka Couffaine in the bathroom so that she could stand next to Adrien in the class photo. She is very clever when she puts her mind to something, as displayed in Animaestro, where she came up with a genius plan to humiliate Kagami Tsurugi.
Due to eight years of practice, Chloé is a very skilled dancer in ballet. She even manages to do acrobatics in the process.
She is shown to able to manipulate and lie to people similar to Lila by using a false beliefs. Although, unlike Lila, who is very clever and skilled enough to not have her lies found out, her lies can be easily exposed.
As Queen Bee

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Abilities
Queen Bee had enhanced physical capabilities, such as flexibility and agility. She was easily able to do a backflip from the floor to the top of the stage. However, she was not strong enough to stop a subway train by herself, requiring both Cat Noir and Ladybug's help. Queen Bee was skilled in hand-to-hand combat.
Queen Bee could yank the pull string on her spinning top to send it onto the ground and let it spin, which then allowed her to travel with it by either riding it or letting the top pull her. She could reach her destination much quicker than other Miraculous holders, with the exception of Pegasus. She could also use her weapon for offense and defense, as a communication device, and activate her power, Venom, allowed her to use the top as a stinger, immobilizing her target for a set amount of time.
As Antibug
Antibug had the same abilities as Ladybug, including enhanced strength and agility. She had her own yo-yo, which she preferred to mostly use offensively.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Abilities
Antibug had her own special superpower to summon objects called the "Anti-Charm". Unlike Lucky Charm, which gave Ladybug random, inherently normal objects, Anti-Charm gave Antibug a weapon, like a large and bulky sword. However, she shared the same time limit to her transformation after using her superpower, but it is unknown what would have happened had it run out. It is implied the time limit would have caused her to be deakumatized.
As Queen Wasp
As an akumatized Miraculous holder, Queen Wasp was considerably powerful. She was able to summon swarms of wasps and direct them. Like her original superpower Venom, she could use her wasps to sting her targets and immobilize them indefinitely. She could form her wasps into different shapes and forms such as arrows, rockets, binoculars, and telescopes. She could also ride on her wasps by letting them carry her. However, her wasps had a weakness and dislike for water, avoiding their target if they managed to go underwater.
As Miracle Queen

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Abilities
Miracle Queen possessed similar powers to her past form, Queen Wasp, being able to control a swarm of wasps. The sting of these wasps could brainwash the victims. The stung victims would follow Miracle Queen's commands without hesitation; they would even obey if they were out of hearing range as her servants. Without receiving any commands from Miracle Queen, the stung victims would then remain motionless. Those who were stung gained a bright yellow with black outlines to their entire eyes. Like the wasps used by her previous Akumatized form, Queen Wasp, Miracle Queen's wasps also had a weakness and dislike of water.   Furthermore, she could teleport using her wasps, and upon arriving at a location, she would emit a golden glow similar to that of her mother's akumatized form, Style Queen.
As Queen Banana
Queen Banana was armed with a banana gun that could shoot out bananas, causing any human it touched to turn into a banana. She also possessed a floating banana-themed car equipped with circular weapons, that could also shoot out bananas. She was given minimum control of her sentimonster, which had the same exact ability as her.
As Penalty

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Abilities
Penalty was able to create a team of clones of herself, where they shared the same powers. Each one could trap people in floating, soccer ball-shaped force fields, either by kicking them with their shoes or by throwing red cards at them. She could also control the soccer field she created, being able to move the goals around the city or control the time of the game, either by making a time limit or making the game infinite.
As Sole Destroyer
Sole Destroyer had the power to turn her enemies into singing shoes by touching them with her high heels and the people who were transformed repeatedly praised her. She even had enhanced strength as seen when she threw away the table that Marinette and Adrien were hiding behind.
As Queen Mayor
Queen Mayor looked exactly like her civilian self aside from her golden jacket to avoid suspicion of being akumatized. Her police robots had the power of Voyage, Resistance, Sublimation, Venom and Shell-ter. She could control the robots in any way she wanted to as they could immobilize whoever she wished, teleport people to "detention", create shields that were immune to any kind of superpowers, and turn invisible and visible at her will.
As Dread Queen

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Abilities
Dread Queen wielded a spinning top similar to Queen Bee's, and by spinning it on the ground, she could generate a yellow dome that covered a large part of Paris. The dome was invulnerable to the powers of the Miraculers, even Cat Noir's Cataclysm. People trapped in her Dreadzone began to feel intense fear, which increased the closer they got to her and decreased as they moved away. Wherever she went, a yellow glow on the ground followed her, indicating the level of fear felt by those near her. She also wielded a scepter that allowed her to broadcast live on Zoo.  Moreover, she was very agile, able to leap across rooftops and cover great distances with ease, despite wearing a large dress.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Etymology
The name Chloé means "blooming, fertility, green sprout/young green shoot" in Greek.
Chloé's surname Bourgeois is a French term that is used to describe a member of the middle class within France.
The fact that she looks down on people who aren't as popular or rich as her is a reference to this.
In the Slovenian dub, her name is changed to Clara Bourgeois.
The names of her superhero and akumatized alter-egos also have meaning to them:
"Queen Bee" which was Chloé's former hero name before she lost her powers permanently and is also a term used to describe a woman who dominates, leads a group or is in a favored position; in her case, the term signifies her dominating personality and former position of power as the mayor's daughter then in turn mayor herself.
Chloé's superhero name, Queen Bee, is a play on the bug "queen bee". A queen bee is normally tended to and protected by all other bees in a hive, correlating to Chloé's rich life style and expectations to be put before others within any social circle, regardless of a situation.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Etymology
Alternatively, "queen bee" could also be referring to a queen bee personality which is often described as having an overly heightened self-esteem, which may lead to arrogance and bossiness as well as being overly aggressive, selfish, manipulative and confident, behaving like a bully or sociopath.
"Queen Wasp", Chloe's second alter-ego, involves switching to a wasp which in turn are more aggressive than bees and also correlates to Chloe's rise in anger as well as her parasitic downward spiral in her relationships with everyone especially Marinette and her Re-Verse counterpart.
"Miracle Queen" and "Queen Mayor", where Chloe had all the power of a ruler but she lacked compassion, mercy and reason causing her to be stripped of her power due to her desire for revenge and her refusal to change.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
Character Development and Design
In the earlier concept art of Chloé, she didn't have her hair in a ponytail. She wore a purple vest with a diamond pattern around the waist, a white long-sleeved shirt, and blue jeans.
This is very similar to Sabrina Raincomprix's current outfit.
Also, in one concept art, Chloé was watching a fashion show with Marinette Dupain-Cheng and Alya Césaire, suggesting that she may have been friends with them in an earlier concept.
A later concept art design for Chloé included a white cardigan with a black edge, white shorts with black stripes, and high white boots with black edges and soles.
Chloé's character description on the official Miraculous Ladybug website used to state that one of her favorite pastimes was "bullying her punching bag Marinette Dupain-Cheng". As of recently has changed to a more neutral stance regarding her character.
Queen Bee's existence was first revealed in 2015 in an illustration by ZAG celebrating MIFA's 30th anniversary.
The character was eventually confirmed to be Queen Bee during the Miraculous Ladybug panel at the 2016 San Diego Comic-Con.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
She was later teased in a concept poster for the "ZAG Heroez" franchise that Jeremy Zag posted on his Instagram, the poster showing her lower body and legs.
She was teased again by Jeremy Zag in a three-second storyboard video.
The finished version of Queen Bee for the ZAG Heroez poster was released by Jeremy on Instagram, showing Queen Bee's face. He also tagged the image with #queenbee, suggesting that Queen Bee might be her name.
Her identity was later revealed to be Chloé at a Miraculous panel at New York Comic Con 2016.
Queen Bee's design changed in many ways from the earliest known concept art of her.
She didn't tie up her hair as she lets it hang loosely and she had bangs.
She had a black and yellow striped round cap on the side of her head from which protruded two antennae.
Her hands were covered with yellow gloves, with the black sleeves ending at a point at the center of the front and back of them.
The top part of her torso--including her upper arms--was fuzzy.
She had a circular, yellow with black circles purse around her waist.
Revealed by the Staff

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
According to Thomas Astruc at Mangafest 2017, Chloé was intentionally created since the beginning to be as unpleasant as possible.
At the same panel, he would also state that Chloé will not end up in a romantic relationship, but her relationship with Sabrina will improve.
At the time of speaking, Season 3 had already been finished, and there was no significant, positive or negative, change in their relationship, either before or after "The Battle of the Miraculous". Their relationship would continue to deteriorate until "Confrontation", when Sabrina exposed Chloé and Lila to the whole school, ending their friendship. While initially unable to retain their friendship or find a permanent sense of understanding when together, both characters were content with their lives when apart.
According to Thomas Astruc on Twitter, Chloé was initially never planned to have a redemption arc and this was purely assumed by fans based on the reveal that she would use the Bee Miraculous. He added that she remains unchanged as her 'purpose of the show is to warn about the people who willingly refuse [to change]'.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
Despite the improvements she displayed before the events of "Miracle Queen", Thomas states her character was being presented exactly as she was written; someone who refuses to change and can often pull others into a toxic relationship by having them focus on her potential good and overall suffering, rather than the ongoing cruelty she continued to display towards others.
Although her past explains her act like her mother leaving her as a child, it doesn't excuse the choices she made, and despite the initial changes she made about herself to make up for some of her mistakes, Chloé never saw the need to fully change herself if she continued to obtain what she wanted.
Despite the many chances others were willing to give her to change her ways, Chloé felt such change was not worth the effort if it came at the cost of her privileges.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
According to Feri González, colorist for ZAG inc and the ambassador for the show in Latin America, Chloé had never changed at all during the later parts of Season 2, and the entirety of Season 3. She only wanted to be Queen Bee, not only to help others, but to get recognition, her motivations to be a hero stemmed primarily from her own selfish reasons. The series had always presented Chloé's fate and unchanged personality, the viewers simply needed to observe her character for what it was rather than what they had envisioned it to be.
Despite the few moments of good Chloé has throughout the series, Chloé will revert back to her original personality either near the end of the episode or the following to show that she is still the same person. Despite what she experiences or expresses, those moments never made her want to change who she was and are quickly left in the past the moment she knows things are once again within her favor.
Feri states Chloé's downfall was marked in "Queen Wasp"; the moment she used the Bee Miraculous to endanger hundreds of lives on the train simply to make herself look good.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
Feri states a Miraculous is a privilege, it is not someone's right to use. Despite Ladybug's explanation, Chloé refused to understand that the power of the Miraculous was not her right to use and had determined it was a privilege Ladybug had wrongfully taken from her.
Although Chloé was quick to resist Hawk Moth's control in "Miraculer", her willingness to resist did not stem from her need to be good, but rather from her belief that Ladybug would still provide her the power of the Bee Miraculous, a power she felt she was entitled to.
Chloé has her own official Instagram account: @theofficialchloebourgeois.
The manager of the character accounts announced that she no longer works at ZAG. The future of accounts is unknown.
Since September 2020, Chloé has her own Facebook account.
She mentions that she used to do ballet when she was younger. (In "Frightningale", she mentioned that she took private classes with Aurélie Dupont for eight years.)
Her signature color is canary yellow.
She aspires to be a fashion queen like her mother and gets her looks from her too.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
When she was little, she would wander through the halls of the hotel exploring the rooms and seeing what guests were talking about.
As a Miraculous Holder and Akumatized Villains
Chloé's akumatized form appears as Antibug in the theme song animatic.
Like Copycat with Cat Noir and Volpina with the Fox Miraculous holder, Antibug is a copy of a Miraculous holder. However, her appearance and superpower, Anti-Charm, are the opposite of Ladybug's.
Her suit and mask having inverted colors to that of Ladybug is similar to the DC Comics villain the Reverse-Flash having an inverted but similar suit to the Flash.
She is the third person to be akumatized for the second time following Alix and Ivan Bruel.
However, she's the first one to be akumatized for a second time with a new identity and powers.
Chloé is the first Miraculous wielder shown not to maintain a secret identity onscreen.
The first one in the modern era to have their identity known to the public after she transformed in front of a news camera in "Queen Wasp", which was broadcasted live throughout Paris. Because of this, she holds the record for having the largest number of people to know her identity as a Miraculous holder.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
In addition, despite being a former member, she is also the only Miraculous holder of the Team Miraculous where every other member knows her identity as Queen Bee.
Chloé is the second known person after Gabriel to have a Miraculous that wasn't meant for her. But unlike Gabriel, who uses the Butterfly Miraculous for evil, she used the Bee Miraculous to become a superhero until her betrayal.
Following Alya Césaire, Chloé is the second person to become a Miraculous holder and akumatized villain, excluding Gabriel Agreste, who akumatized himself.
Queen Wasp was first revealed on August 31, 2017, at a TFOU press conference.
A scarlet version of Queen Wasp reappeared in the two-part special event "Heroes' Day".
Similar to Copycat, Antibug and Volpina, Queen Wasp and Miracle Queen are other akumatized villains based on a Miraculous holder.
The first 3 of Chloé's akumatizations were based on superheroes (Antibug/Ladybug and Queen Wasp/Miracle Queen/Queen Bee).
As of "Miraculer", she is the first person to be able to successfully reject Hawk Moth's akumatization.
Antibug appears in "Gamer 2.0" for Gamer's powers and as a statue in the Musée Grévin in "The Puppeteer 2".

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
Chloé is the fourth person to voluntarily akumatize themselves following Gabriel Agreste, Nathalie Sancoeur and Lila Rossi.
As seen in "Mr. Pigeon 72", Chloé has been akumatized into Antibug three times. ("Antibug" and two off-screen akumatization).
With her two akumatizations into Queen Wasp and her others into Miracle Queen, Queen Banana, Penalteam, Sole Destroyer, Queen Mayor and Dread Queen, Chloé has been akumatized 11 times in total.
Chloé is the only character to have been akumatized at least once per season in the first 6 seasons.
Chloé is the first and only character to be akumatized into two different new supervillain forms in the same season and two seasons in a row. In Season 4 she was akumatized into Queen Banana and Penalty and in Season 5 she was akumatized into Sole Destroyer and Queen Mayor.
Chloé is additionally the only character to have 8 different akumatized forms. Her repeated akumatizations is the result of Hawk Moth, and Chrysalis viewing her as an easier target compared to the rest of their victims.
Chrysalis even goes as far as to give Chloe a locked box with an akuma inside, showing she knew someone would get akumatised from her actions.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
Chronologically from "Revolution", Chloé is the last victim chosen by Monarch to be akumatized.
With her 10 akumatizations, Chloé comes in second place for having been akumatized the most number of times behind Mr. Ramier and ahead of Kagami, Juleka, Lila and Roger.
However, unlike the others, she, along with Kagami and Lila, haven't been re-akumatized into the same villain all of the time.
Chloé is the second person following Marinette that has worn multiple Miraculous (more than two) at one time with a total of nine.
However, unlike Marinette, she was unable to activate any besides the one she was already using.
Chloé is the first Miraculous holder to be renounced from the French Miraculous superhero team.
She was also the first member of the team not to be chosen by Ladybug's instinct, followed by King Monkey and Argos.
As seen in "Mayura", Queen Bee is the first person who isn't Ladybug or Cat Noir to break an akumatized object.
Chloé is the first person to destroy their akumatized object themselves, destroying her own sunglasses in "Penalteam" while akumatized into Penalty.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
She is also the third villain to be content with their akumatized object being destroyed, following Christmaster in "Christmaster" and Reflekta in "Guiltrip".
She currently holds the record for facing the most Miraculous holders at once, facing 15 Miraculous holders, which is all of the Miraculers except for Rena Rouge, Bunnyx, and Argos.
Chloé is the first person to possess an Alliance that didn't have any superpowers transmitted to it.
In "Deflagration", as Sole Destroyer, she is the first akumatized supervillain in Season 5 not to receive a Miraculous superpower through an Alliance.
She is also the fourth victim to have her akuma revoked in that same episode, following Lila Rossi in "Catalyst" and her parents in "Heart Hunter".
Chloé's akumatization as Queen Mayor is similar to her akumatization as Penalty (Penalteam):
In both of these two akumatizations:
She was voluntarily akumatized.
Had a group as part of her akumatization.
But as Penalty her group were clones of herself being named Penalteam, while her group as Queen Mayor were her police robots.

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
She had protective spheres to capture anyone she wanted, but as Penalty they came from her own akumatization while as Queen Mayor they came from the Miraculous' superpowers.
Gabriel almost came close to discovering the identity of one of the heroes and ensuring their victory thanks to the powers of Chloé's akumatized forms that were able to trap them until they de-transformed back after using their powers.
It took the work and collaboration of many people for her to be defeated, but while as Penalty she was defeated by heroes, as Queen Mayor she was defeated by civilians.
Her akumatized object was never broken by any of the heroes, as Penalty she herself broke it due to not wanting to become akumatized anymore while as Queen Mayor her akumatized object was broken when Caline Bustier learned where the Akuma was.
Both chronologically, Penalty was the penultimate akumatized form of Season 4 just as Queen Mayor was the penultimate akumatized form of Season 5.
Miscellaneous
Originally, Chloé and Sabrina Raincomprix were supposed to be in a trio with Alix Kubdel, which was a reference to the trio Sam, Clover and Alex in Totally Spies!

title: Chloé Bourgeois
text:
Chloé Bourgeois - Trivia
Interestingly, Fily Keita, who voices Zoé in the French dub, voiced Clover in the French dub of "Totally Spies!".
In "Antibug", it is hinted that Chloé is seen to be a left-handed person.
However, in "Sole Crusher", Chloé is seen writing with her right hand on her journal.
Some of Chloé's Ladybug paraphernalia can be seen in her locker in "The Evillustrator".
According to Sabrina in "Zombizou", Chloé never remembers people's birthday, just like her mother Audrey Bourgeois.
Chloé is the first person to not want a Magical Charm, but later, she takes it when Zoé Lee tricks her by saying it's from their mother and from Miss Bustier's class to own a Magical Charm.
She is the fourth person to have her Magical Charm destroyed by a Megakuma following Gabriel Agreste, Roland Dupain and Sabine Cheng.
The Bee signal that Chloé would shine in the sky whenever a villain came is a reference to Batman's Bat signal.
"In "Miraculous: Rise of the Sphinx", Chloé gets willingly akumatized into Clonika, with the power to make clones of people with her cellphone.

are an expensive pair of diamond heels owned by Chloé Bourgeois. She keeps them in a large, black box.
In "Sole Crusher", after hiding her true self in order to please her half-sister, they become part of Zoé's akumatization into the titular villain.

text:

Normal

title: Chloé's limousine
text:
Chloé's limousine - Intro
is a former modern limo which Chloé Bourgeois usually rides in.
In "Queen Banana", after being removed from the film Kreatika and seeing her half-sister be the main character, and after she ended her friendship with Adrien, Chloé was akumatized and amokized by Shadow Moth in Queen Banana, even transforming her limo together to her.

title: Chloé's limousine
text:
Chloé's limousine - Appearance
External
Chloé's limousine is a long metallic gray sedan almost five meters long. It has a gray bumper surrounding a black radiator grille. At the front of the hood there appears to be a small metallic gray statuette. Its windshield, side windows and rear window are completely tinted. It only has four doors, two at the front and others at the back. We can also make out a small fuel hatch in the left rear area.
In "Sole Crusher", the color was changed to pink following yet another whim of Chloé, before returning to her usual color later.
In "Miraculous Chibi", the color is instead black.
Internal
The limousine has a very spacious interior. The interior appears to be comfortable and has the predominant color of grey. There are several particularly impressive armchairs, a latest generation home cinema system with flat screen, round speakers and electronic controls. This cabin is also illuminated by small lights built into the roof. There is also a sunroof.
Akumatized

title: Chloé's limousine
text:
Chloé's limousine - Appearance
Under the effects of Chloé's akumatization into Queen Banana, the limousine had transformed into a yellow and black spider-like car with purple headlights and white and purple wheels. In addition, four cannons from which bananas were fired had been added.

title: Chloé's limousine
text:
Chloé's limousine - Abilities
Akumatized
Under the effects of Chloé's akumatization into Queen Banana, the limousine was capable of reaching high speeds. Thanks to its four cannons, it could shoot bananas at Parisians to turn them into bananas. Furthermore, the limousine was capable of flying.

title: Chloé's limousine
text:
Chloé's limousine - Trivia
Although this is Chloé's personal limousine, legally the owner of the vehicle is her father.
Indeed, French law has provided since 2017 that the registration of a vehicle must imperatively be in the name of a person with the driving license corresponding to the type of vehicle.
For example, Marinette has an AM license and so her scooter can be registered in her name.
Chloé's limousine is the seventh item, after Roger's police car in "Rogercop", Gina's motorcycle in "Befana" and "Dearest Family", Anarka's boat in "Captain Hardrock" and "Crocoduel", Santa Claus's sleigh in "Santa Claws", the train in "Startrain" and Tomoe's car in "Ikari Gozen", "Multiplication" and "Pretension", which has been akumatized together with its owner.

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Intro
(called Laura Nightingale in some episodes) is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. She is an American pop star based off of the singer Laura Marano, who performed the Miraculous music video.
In "Frightningale", after Chloé convinced André Bourgeois to prohibit production for Clara's music video "Miraculous" in Paris, she was akumatized by Hawk Moth into Frightningale, a singing, dancing, and rhyming supervillain.

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Clara is a fair-skinned young woman with long wavy chocolate brown hair that is split on both sides, brilliant amaranth lipstick, and brown eyes.
Civilian Attire
She wears a short sleeved midriff revealing dress which consists of  white crop top with a matching skirt, both having a pattern of yellow, magenta, cyan, and green triangles. On her right wrist, she has 3 bracelets: a puffy yellow bracelet, a black bead bracelet, and a wide magenta bracelet with cyan horizontal stripes. Additionally, she has black leggings that fade into dark blue at the bottom and black spool high heel shoes.
As Frightningale

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Appearance
Frightningale had straight blonde hair tied back into two high ponytails with pale, light grayish blue-violet star-shaped hair bands. She had heterochromia as her left eye was light brilliant sea green and her right eye was a vivid raspberry color. The tips of her hair on her left ponytail and right side bang were red, and the tips on her right ponytail and left side bang were green. Her face was amaranthish white, and she wore multicolored shades with star-like side edges. She also painted her lips with vivid amaranth lipstick. She wore a grayish violet jumpsuit that had a light blue pointed tip over each shoulder. A cyan star with a black outline is printed on her chest, her upper back included an upward shooting star design, and the rest of her suit was decorated with light brilliant arctic blue, yellow, and luminous vivid rose colored shapes. At her feet, she had luminous vivid cerise rectangular wedges and luminous vivid cyan high heels. She also held a wand with a strong blue swirled handle, a rounded pink bottom tip, a black star at the top, and a white-edged pink circle between the star and the handle.

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Personality
Clara is very energetic when talking with Alec Cataldi about her new music videos. She is constantly dancing to the tune while talking, and according to Marinette, she's very passionate about her music. Clara is clever; knowing she has to choose among many auditioners, she purposely trips to find someone who would act like Ladybug.
As Frightningale, she remained energetic, but was mischievous and cunning, as shown when she almost tricked Cat Noir into not rhyming and becoming a statue. She was also childish, saying that Ladybug and Cat Noir being tied together was cheating and would not be permitted.

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Abilities
As a Civilian
Clara is exceptional at singing and dancing. She speaks in rhymes and is able to do so without fail. Is also very agile and flexible as shown during the opening song where she did an 360° acrobacy while singing and holding her microphone even if her ankle boots were equipped with high heels.
As Frightningale
Frightningale had enhanced physical prowess: she could jump incredible heights despite her high heels, hurl huge objects (such as buses), and run extremely quickly. Using her microphone, Frightningale could extend a pink energy whip which colored them with a pink aura whenever it hit people. If the victim was struck with the whip and failed to speak in rhymes or dance, the aura turned them into a magenta statue.

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Relationships
Friends/Allies
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Ladybug
When none of the people who audition to play Ladybug seem right, Clara purposely trips in front of the extras to see which one of them would act like Ladybug. When Marinette helps her up, Clara concludes that she has found the perfect Ladybug and asks Marinette to play the heroine. She doesn't mind when Marinette turns down the offer to be with her friends. However, when she changes her mind, Clara excitedly gives her the part.
Clara admires Ladybug so much that she makes a music video dedicated to her and Cat Noir. When Frightningale is defeated, Clara expresses excitement over being saved by her and takes her suggestion on how to finish her music video.
Adrien Agreste/Cat Noir
According to Gabriel, Clara is a huge fan of Adrien and immediately gives him the role of Cat Noir in her music video when Gabriel suggests it.
Clara admires Cat Noir so much that she makes a music video dedicated to him and Ladybug. When Frightningale is defeated, Clara expresses excitement over being saved by him.
Status unknown

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Relationships
When Chloé auditions to play Ladybug, Clara comments on her talent and upon Gabriel's suggestion, decides to use her in her music video. However, she soon gives the part to Marinette instead, angering Chloé and prompting her to cancel Clara's music video, leaving the musician to run to her trailer crying and vulnerable to akumatization.

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Etymology
The name Clara means "clear, bright, famous".
Rossignoble, her villain name in the French dub, is a portmanteau of the French word rossignol, which means "nightingale", and the English word ignoble, meaning "not honorable in character or purpose".
Nightingales are known for their singing, relating to Clara's career as a singer.

title: Clara Nightingale
text:
Clara Nightingale - Trivia
Clara is based off of Laura Marano, who performed a cover of the English theme song as part of the promotion for her second half of season 1.
Nightingale's akumatized form as Frightningale references to D.C. Character Harley Quinn.
Clara's civilian outfit is an homage to the techno-pop unit Perfume, one of the creators' favorite bands.
Her villain form was first revealed in concept art shown during a Nolife interview.
Like Jagged Stone and XY, Clara's record label is Bob Roth Records.
In "Captain Hardrock", Clara is named Laura Nightingale; her first name Clara comes in later episodes.
In the French dub of "Captain Hardrock", her name is Laura Rossignol, the first name Clara likewise coming later on.
In Spain her name in that episode is Laura Nittingel, fully changed to Clara Ruiseñor afterward.
According to Thomas Astruc, Clara is supposed to rhyme at every occasion.
A scarlet version of Frightningale appeared in the two-part special event "Heroes' Day".
In "Gamer 2.0", Frightningale returns as a playable akumatized villain as part of the Gamer 2.0's powers.
