title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - Intro
Clara Contard is a TVi news reporter.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 2]]
In "The Dark Owl", Clara and other TVi staff arrive on the scene at the Place des Vosges. Clara interviews The Owl. The Owl claims that he will try to do better next time, being oblivious to Ladybug's and Cat Noir's real point, before running off, not realizing that the camera was following him the entire time, leaving Ladybug and Cat Noir to deal with the press. Both Ladybug and Cat Noir advise the children of Paris to not act like The Owl and try to be superheroes like him, as it is dangerous.
In "Catalyst", Clara is seen during the Heroes' Day parade on a helicopter. But, when Volpina uses her power of illusion to create an "akumatized Ladybug" fighting Cat Noir, she reports on how the two heroes were fighting each other. She then witnessed as the akumatized Ladybug that uses Cat Noir's own cataclysm against him causing him to be destroyed.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 3]]
In "Oblivio", Clara hands Nadja a tablet with a script after her memory was erased by the titular villains.
In "Feast", Nadja announces the mysterious reappearance of a temple in the Tibetan mountains that went missing 172 years ago. Clara, who is on a helicopter flying above the temple, adds that all the monks who used to live in the temple also reappeared.
In "Stormy Weather 2", Clara reports on the battle between Ladybug, Cat Noir, and the titular villain with Nadja. Though the screen freezes and stops working, Clara continues to report that Ladybug has called on her Lucky Charm and received a pencil while Cat Noir has grabbed a photocopier. Ladybug makes a photocopy, and eventually, the villain is defeated and everything is returned to normal.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - "[[Miraculous New York]]"
Clara goes to New York City to report that the "necklace" that the Marquis de Lafayette gave to George Washington during the Revolutionary War was put on display for the first time. She later is seen on Ladybug's yo-yo when Mayura revokes the amok of the Robostus sentimonster, witnessing the Sentimonster mysteriously disappear on a helicopter while reporting on it.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 4]]
In "Queen Banana", Clara is seen at Collège Françoise Dupont reporting on a student film called Kreatika in the Art classroom.
In "Sentibubbler", Clara is seen on a helicopter reporting that Alya's family, Nino, and Marinette are prisoners in the bubbles resembling of those of the Bubbler, but yet in one of them was the original akumatized victim.
In "Simpleman", Clara is simplified by the titular villain. When Nadja turns things over to her, Clara introduces herself, telling the viewers that she is a reporter in a helicopter. She then talked about how the people were not happy as their cars were all immobilized.
The cameraman soon tells Clara that the helicopter is going to fast. She then told the pilot to stop and he turns off the engine keeping the helicopter up in the air. This causes the helicopter to fall, with Clara and the other helicopter's passengers jumping off and landing at the Eiffel Tower. There soon rescued by Ladybug and Cat Noir.
In "Qilin", Clara is first seen interviewing the owner of the Cocoa Shop Factory on the Morning News. She is later seen reporting the return of Lollipop Boy near Scipion Street Square.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 4]]
In "Ephemeral", Clara is seen during the conference of the 100th collection of Gabriel brand. She asks Adrien Agreste on how he feels about the 100th collection being dedicated to Émilie Agreste. She later asks him about his lasted commercial.
In "Kuro Neko", Clara is taken hostage by akumatized villain Gigantitan who causes a panic. Ladybug, Carapace, Pegasus, Pigella, and Vesperia then manage to deakumatize the villain, which causes him to detransform back into August and drop the reporter, Clara Contard but Ladybug manages to catch her.
Ladybug returns August to his mother, while Clara asks her about Cat Noir, mentioning that she has saved Paris multiple times without him. Ladybug looks towards her team and replies that Cat Noir is like any other partner and she can save Paris with or without Cat Noir.
Following the events of "Risk", Clara was marked offscreen by the titular villain and forced to take risks. In "Strikeback", Clara still under the effects of the previous villain approachs the titular villain in a helicopter, putting herself in danger. The villain then knocks the helicopter out of the way with Clara and the other passengers being saved by Cat Noir.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 5]]
In "Multiplication", Clara is seen in a helicopter reporting on how all the Miraculouses that Ladybug was supposed to be guarding where stolen by Monarch. This is seen when Ladybug watches a live TVi channel broadcast on her yoyo about what happened during the events of "Strikeback".
In "Jubilation", Clara is seen in Gabriel Agreste's Alliance ring, where she is seen  in a coverage of her in a helicopter near the scene where Ladybug is capturing Anne-Jeanne Théoxanne du Bocquale's Tyrannosaurus-pigeon hybrid dinosaurs that escaped. She then reports on how Ladybug once again saved Paris.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 5]]
In "Deflagration", which takes place after the events of "Transmission", Clara is seen at the scene of Kikou's defeat: Les Olympiades. There she interviews the new holders of the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses: Scarabella and Kitty Noire. Clara asks if Ladybug and Cat Noir were forced to step down. Scarabella declines to answer directly, but she does say that their predecessors have nothing to feel guilty about. Clara then remarks Ladybug and Cat Noir may have renounced their Miraculouses to live their supposed love story. Scarabella answers that neither Ladybug and Cat Noir nor her and Kitty Noire are in love or in a relationship. Clara then asks for their names. The new heroes introduce themselves as their new hero personas then leave.
Later, Clara appears on a helicopter, where she is reporting on how Monarch is alone and standing in a huge crater that devastated Arènes de Lutèce. Then she points out that he is wear the Ladybug Miraculous, wondering if that explained the absence of Scarabella and if Monarch have succeeded in seizing her Miraculous.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 5]]
In "Perfection", Clara is seen on a helicopter near the Jardin des Tuileries, reports on the situation with akumatized villain Ryukomri. She gets close enough that Ryukomori tries to shoos her off with her hand. Clara doesn't leave, so Ryukomori shocks her with her lightning power, sending the helicopter hurtling to the ground. Cat Noir then saves and helps Clara and the other passenger down from the crashed helicopter with his staff.
In "Collusion", Clara goes to Hôtel de Ville with Chloé Bourgeois and her Police robots to watch as the new mayoress of Paris attempted to arrest Ladybug and Cat Noir. Clara then watched as Chloé stated that the duo has used their powers on Democracy and declared them villains, with the heroes trying to fight back against the robots but fled due after being captured by a net.
In "Action", which takes place between the events of "Confrontation" and "Collusion", Clara was first seen walking outside of the TVi Tower. Sometime later, she was supposed to report a story before being cut off by Max Kanté, who had hacked the TVi news broadcast.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 5]]
Later, Clara reports on how Bertrand King has financed the repair of Liberty, the location where she is at, which has cleaned the Seine of all the plastic waste that was polluting it. She then goes to Tom & Sabine Boulangerie Patisserie, where she interviewed Tom Dupain and Sabine Cheng. Clara was soon seen outside reporting on how Marinette and her friends's awareness raising campaign had succeeded in creating a world-wide movement.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - "[[Miraculous London]]"
Bug Noire arrives on the roof of Tsurugi laboratory, when the voices of Nadja and Clara are heard in the background, telling about the latest events in the world related to the Miraculized. Clara went on the air with a reporter from a helicopter over Paris, where they saw Ladybug's magic ladybugs flying by, repairing all the damage. After that, she appears on the screen in Kagami's room.
Later, during one of the Chronobug and Timestalker fights that takes place while watching Kagami's news, Nadja and Clara's report is heard in the background.

title: Clara Contard/History
text:
Clara Contard/History - [[Season 6]]
In "Climatiqueen", Clara appears among the many reporters who want to interview the famous couple Adrien and Marinette when she tries to get off her scooter and get into the mansion, but gets a jet of water from Placide, forcing her to flee.
In "Noe", Mylène is the host of a new television program and talks about the innovations of Paris, after which Clara can be seen on the big screen as students in Collège Françoise Dupont pursue their hobbies.

title: Chloé Bourgeois/Movie
text:
Chloé Bourgeois/Movie - Intro
Chloé Bourgeois is a supporting character of "Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie". She is a student at Collège Françoise Dupont and the rival of Marinette Dupain-Cheng.

title: Chloé Bourgeois/Movie
text:
Chloé Bourgeois/Movie - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Chloé is a bit taller than average height, with messy dirty-blonde hair tied into a messy ponytail. She wears vivid blue eyeshadow. She is pale-skinned, and has teal eyes.
Civilian Attire
Chloé is shown to typically wear a white t-shirt with nine black stripes on it. She wears sport jeans capris in color white, and a golden, crystallized belt. Chloé wears a yellow cardigan and has white sunglasses on the top of her head.
Her design resembles her original counterpart, but there is a major difference, her cardigan has two pockets on the left and right instead of just one pocket on the right.

title: Chloé Bourgeois/Movie
text:
Chloé Bourgeois/Movie - Personality
In comparison to her portrayal in the series, Chloé is much kinder and less mean in the movie. Although she still exhibits some of the same behaviors as her series counterpart—such as being bossy, egotistical, and superficial—there are notable differences. Chloé is particularly vain, as evidenced by her obsession with her hair, weight, and clothing. An example of this is when she gets upset with Marinette for a drop of coffee falling on her Gabriel brand cashmere sweater, as well as when Marinette lies to her about another girl having the same sweater.
Chloé often goes out of her way to crush her rivals and derive pleasure from their misfortunes. This is especially evident in her relationship with Marinette, as she begins to stalk her out of a desire to make her pay for ruining her sweater. She also ridicules Marinette for having a crush on Adrien while believing herself to be superior to others. Chloé takes great pride in her luxurious lifestyle and believes she deserves everything.

title: Chloé Bourgeois/Movie
text:
Chloé Bourgeois/Movie - Personality
Despite her self-centered nature, Chloé is also easily frightened by danger, particularly when akumatized villains are involved. When she finds herself in a perilous situation of her own making, she tends to shift the blame to others. For instance, she blames Sabrina for being at the ferris wheel when it becomes detached and starts moving during the attack of the Magician and the Mime, even though the idea to go there was hers and Sabrina did not want to attend.
Unlike her main series counterpart, Chloé is careful about her social image and how others perceive her. She doesn't misuse her status as the mayor's daughter to bully others or escape accountability. This is illustrated when she grabs Marinette after the coffee incident but is forced to let her go and pretend they are friends upon realizing that Alya is recording the entire confrontation.
Despite her flaws, Chloé does show moments of kindness, such as when she helps Sabrina stand and wishes Marinette a nice evening.

title: Chloé Bourgeois/Movie
text:
Chloé Bourgeois/Movie - Relationships
Sabrina Raincomprix
Much like in the original series,  Sabrina serves as Chloé's "all-purpose girl," and though she is a valuable asset to Chloé, Chloé often bosses her around and treats her as inferior rather than as a true friend. When Sabrina makes a mistake or behaves in a way that Chloé considers incompetent, Chloé reprimands her harshly.
However, unlike the original series, the relationship between Chloé and Sabrina appears to be more of a realistically toxic friendship rather than a master-servant dynamic. Chloé frequently employs emotional blackmail to manipulate Sabrina into doing what she wants, rather than simply giving her orders. Chloé makes Sabrina feel selfish and like a bad friend for not wanting to comply with her demands or for not always following her lead. Despite this, Chloé does show that she cares for Sabrina, as evidenced by her helping up on her feet after Hawk Moth's attack.
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Ladybug

title: Chloé Bourgeois/Movie
text:
Chloé Bourgeois/Movie - Relationships
Just like in the original series, Chloé harbors a strong dislike for Marinette, viewing her with disdain and believing they have nothing in common. In the movie, Marinette accidentally spills coffee on Chloé's sweater, which leads to Chloé becoming extremely frustrated and ready to retaliate against her. Fortunately, Alya intervenes by recording Chloé's behavior and threatens to post the video online. This stops Chloé in her tracks, and she storms off in a huff.
By the end of the movie, it appears that Chloé has softened her animosity towards Marinette. In her own way, she encourages Marinette to enjoy herself at the party and to pursue Adrien, suggesting that she's trying to become a better person.

title: Chloé Bourgeois/Movie
text:
Chloé Bourgeois/Movie - Differences
It is unknown if Chloé met Adrien as a toddler like her TV counterpart or why she wants to go to the ball with Adrien, as he is not a famous model in the movie.
It's also unknown whether she has the same family (André, Audrey and Zoé).
She calls Marinette by her first name, calling her "Marinella", while her series counterpart calls Marinette by her last name, "Dupain-Cheng".

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - Intro
Clara Nightingale (called Laura Nightingale in some episodes) is a famous pop star who is always dancing and speaking in rhymes.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - Before Season 2
Ever since Clara started in the music industry, Gabriel Agreste has designed all of her costumes for her music videos, such as her hit single Big Bang. Her producer is Bob Roth, owner of Bob Roth Records.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Frightningale", Clara is being interviewed by Alec Cataldi about on how she has become really famous and about her style. He asks her if she ever stops dancing and singing, with Clara responding with never while rhyming. Then she announced that the theme for her new music video is "Miraculous", which centers around Ladybug and Cat Noir. Clara then claims while rhyming that they have already found their Cat Noir but is looking for a Ladybug and some extras and invites the people watching to audition.
At the Grand Palais, Clara thanks everyone for coming while rhyming. She then introduces Adrien Agreste as Cat Noir, whom is actually the real Cat Noir. After Adrien claims that he couldn't find the mask, Clara tells him that it's okay and begins auditions. There are several girls and boys eager to play Ladybug, but none of them are right as shown by Clara's face impressions.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 2]]
When no one else is left, Clara comes up with a plan to find the right Ladybug. She offers the extras a snack and then trips on purpose. Marinette Dupain-Cheng, whom is the real Ladybug, runs to help her up and Clara declares that she has found her Ladybug, claiming that Marinette did exactly what Ladybug would've and that she'd be perfect. Marinette politely turns down the offer, stating that she'd rather be an extra with her friends. Clara understands and leads Marinette to a chair to wait for her friends and makeup.
Chloé Bourgeois, dressed as Ladybug, then arrives and thanks everyone for coming, adding that they can leave now. Clara then lets Chloé audition for the role and she nails it. Clara commends Chloé on her talent and asks Gabriel what he thinks. He thinks that Marinette would've been better but decides that they have no choice but to use her for the video since she refused, with Clara agreeing.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 2]]
Marinette then has a change of heart and decides to be Ladybug, to Clara's happiness. She allows this and tells Chloé that she can still be an extra, with Chloé being disgusted by the thought of being a mere extra and angrily exits the building. Clara then greets Marinette in costume on stage for rehearsal. Clara then directs them on how she wants them to move, until a member of the staff finds the masks. Clara wants them to wear it, and after insisting so much, Marinette and Adrien begin to slowly put the masks on, but are interrupted by Chloé and her father Mayor André Bourgeois.
André then shows Clara a bunch of papers that supposedly show that she doesn't have permission to make a music video in Paris or anywhere else in France. Chloé taunts Clara and throws her microphone on the floor, breaking the star decor on it. Humiliated and disheartened, Clara runs to her trailer crying. Hawk Moth senses Clara's emotions and sends an akuma her way. When the akuma arrives at Clara's trailer, it possesses her microphone and transforms her into Frightningale, a supervillainess capable of turning people into pink metallic statues if they don't sing, dance, or rhyme.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 2]]
As Chloé was dismissing all the extras, Frightningale makes her entrance and whips both her and the mayor. When Chloé confronts her, she fails to sing, dance, or rhyme, immediately turning her into a metallic statue. Her father frantically begs Frightningale to return his daughter to normal with a rhyme after she explains how he can avoid Chloé's current condition, but fails to reason with her. Frightningale then leaves and starts to whip people all across Paris, turning them into metallic statues.
Ladybug then arrives and manages to stop Frightningale on the roof. She tries to convince her to give her the akuma, but to no avail. Frightningale then starts using Ladybug's own yo-yo against her until Cat Noir appears and trips her with his staff. Despite initially getting the upper hand, Frightningale manages to dodge their attacks, making them accidentally attack each other instead. With Hawk Moth's advice, Frightningale manages to whip both Ladybug and Cat Noir, and they realize they must sing, dance, or rhyme in order to keep fighting or else they will be turned into statues.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 2]]
Ladybug and Cat Noir then start to talk with each other in rhyme while dancing, avoiding Frightningale's attacks. Frightningale tries to distract them and make them fail the rhyme, but they manage to get away from her to make a better plan. After Ladybug's Lucky Charm then gives her a pair of handcuffs and she uses them to handcuff herself to Cat Noir, the duo start attacking Frightningale in sync. Cat Noir uses his Cataclysm and holds it in until they get close enough to Frightningale. He takes her microphone and destroys it, releasing the akuma and Frightningale is transformed back into Clara.
Clara is excited to know she was saved by Ladybug and Cat Noir themselves. Ladybug then gives her an idea on how she can finish her music video, which Clara likes. The idea was to show many people dancing with Ladybug and Cat Noir masks, including all of Marinette and Adrien's classmates (except Chloé), the teachers, and some of their other friends.
In "Captain Hardrock", for the National Music Festival, Clara hosted a concert at the Louvre. While performing at her concert, the titular villain blasts speakers onto the performing area making Clara jump offstage.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Style Queen", Clara is seen as she arrives at the Grand Palais, where the fashion show of Gabriel takes place. There Clara sat on the front row, next to Mireille Caquet and Jagged Stone. When the fashion show was interrupted by the titular villain, Clara was seen running away from the scene.
In "Queen Wasp", Clara is on a recording on the news of the fashion show was interrupted by the previous titular villain. Clara is then seen back in her sit when Gabriel arrives and hugs his son, Adrien.
In "Catalyst", after Volpina creates an illusion of an akumatized Ladybug that uses Cat Noir's own cataclysm against him causing him to be destroyed, Clara is seen on the TVi news being interviewed by Nadja Chamack about the situation. There Clara sadly hugged Jagged Stone after releasing that they'll have to cancel a concert they had planned, since there was no point in celebrating Heroes' Day anymore.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 2]]
Then suddenly, a swarm of scarlet akumas fly into the scene causing Clara and Jagged to run away. Clara then falls victim to one of Scarlet Moth's scarlet akumas, being transformed back into a scarlet version of Frightningale. Soon, after Nadja and Jagged were also transformed back into Prime Queen and Guitar Villain respectively, Frightningale was seen celebrating Scarlet Moth with the second on Akuma TV news.
In "Mayura", Frightningale was seen at the Eiffel Tower. There Frightningale and Guitar Villain were ordered by Scarlet Moth to play music, with Frightningale singing. She then continued to sing as the French Miraculous superhero team battled the Scarlet Army.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 3]]
In "Animaestro", Clara attends the movie premiere of Thomas Astruc's animated movie about Ladybug and Cat Noir as she sang all the songs in the movie. After waving the all her fans, Clara is greeted by the security guard that was letting people into the event. The guard tells her that he is her biggest fan and lets her in. Later, Clara is seen talking to other guest at the event various times throughout the episode, such as Alec and Nadja.
In "Gamer 2.0", Clara was one of the many former akumatized villains that the titular villain zapped into his video game dimension. Frightningale (played by the titular villain) fights Weredad (played by Cat Noir) and is easily defeated. After the villain is defeated by Ladybug and Cat Noir, Clara and the others are freed by Ladybug's Miraculous Ladybug.

title: Clara Nightingale/History
text:
Clara Nightingale/History - [[Season 4]]
In "Hack-San", after Robostus sends out a signal to all Parisians with a message sent through their phones, Clara is hypothesized offscreen. She is then sent by Robostus to the Musée Grévin, positioning herself where her statue used to be. There after Scarabella and Cat Noir arrive, Clara unfreezes from her position. She then pulls out her phone and moves towards the heroes.
Clara is commanded to seize the Ladybug and the Cat Miraculous, along with the other high-profile hypothesized individuals. She then watched as Scarabella and Cat Noir delivered themselves to Robostus. Later, Clara is freed from Robostus' control by Scarabella's Miraculous Scarabella.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - Intro
Claudie Kanté is the former conductor of Startrain and a recent astronaut. She is also the mother of Max Kanté.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 3]]
In "Startrain", Claudie drives her son Max Kanté, along with his robot Markov and his two friends: Alya Césaire and Marinette Dupain-Cheng, to the Gare du Nord. When they all get out of her car, she looks at her smartwatch for any messages but finds none. With a sigh, Claudie gets out of the car and offers to show a sneak peek of the Startrain's operator cab. Alya then comments that it'll be a great addition to her astronomy blog, surprising Marinette.
In the Startrain's operator cabin, Claudie explains the Deadman's Switch to Alya and Marinette, which is a switch that the operator must keep their hand on at all times otherwise the train will stop. She also explains that it's a safety feature in case the operator feels faint. Max then says that he likes traveling with his mother on trains because they get from Point A to Point B in the time they're programmed, with Markov agreeing that programming is the best.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 3]]
Alya asks Claudie if she always wanted to drive a train, with she saying it had always been something she wanted to do. However, Claudie then says that her true dream is to be an astronaut, but since space missions can take months, she decided to operate trains while Max was growing up. Now that Max is older, she has taken a test to start astronaut training. She is expecting an email today that will tell her if she passed or not. Claudie fears that she might not pass, though Max assures her that she will.
Soon, Claudie starts up the train, and it leaves the train station to go to London. While driving the train, she anxiously opens her email multiple times but finds no new ones. She then announces that the Startrain is going under the Channel Tunnel in a few minutes.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 3]]
Claudie checks her messages again but still finds no new ones. Convinced that she has probably failed her test, Claudie becomes upset enough that the akuma onboard senses her negative emotions and attaches itself to the Deadman's switch. Claudie is transformed into Startrain, a train conducting supervillain. She then sends the train with everyone onboard into space. Max attempts to reason with his akumatized mother through a speaker on the wall but to no avail.
Marinette suggests that she and her friends go to the operator's cabin to drive the train back home. they head to the operator's cabin, Startrain notices them and makes the train go faster in order to push them away, telling them to stay in their seats so no one gets hurt. Soon she notices Ladybug and Cat Noir have teamed up with Max and Markov to stop her as their attempt to get through a car that can take them to the operator's cabin. To this, Startrain changes the temperature in the car and it gets very hot.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 3]]
After they get out of that car and they try to make it through the next one, Startrain makes the car become freezing cold, with Max noting that the temperatures will reach below zero. Soon the heroes are joined by Pegasus and they enter the car, with Startrain sending the service drones to attack them. They eventually manage to open the door to the operator's cabin, with Ladybug tying up Startrain while Cat Noir uses his Cataclysm on the Deadman's switch.
Pegasus then teleports the train to London, with Startrain transforming back into Claudie. The train, now back to normal, crashes through Big Ben. Ladybug then fixes everything with her Miraculous Ladybug and teleports everyone back to Paris, with Claudie checking her email again at the train station. She has one new message stating she passed her test. Claudie then reunites with her son and Markov and tells them the news, with Max congratulates her.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 3]]
In "Miracle Queen", Claudie is seen receiving her space suit. She and Max celebrate the moment by hugging before they are both stung by the titular villain's hornets, which brainwash their victims. Claudie was later freed by Ladybug's Miraculous Ladybug after she defeated the villain, along with her son.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 5]]
In "Illusion", Claudie attends the parent-teacher conference for Miss Bustier's class. There she is seen sitting behind Sabine Cheng and in front of Anarka Couffaine as Miss Bustier started with the conference.
In "Intuition", Claudie is now at the commands of Tsurugi Industries' most sophisticated space jet in space and makes time to answer questions from her son's class, with minutes to go before test launch. She introduces A.D.A. the artificial intelligence on the jet to the class, when asked by Marinette. Claudie then explains to Lê Chiến Kim that today she'll be testing how a pilot and an artificial intelligence like A.D.A. can support each other in stressful situations in space.
When they start the test launch, on Claudie's command, the thrusters on the space jet powers down and begins its descent towards the Earth's surface. A.D.A. manages to pass the first test by reactivating the space jet when she senses Claudie's stress levels and emotions.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 5]]
Claudie is then ejected out of the ship and A.D.A. flies off to rescue her for the second test. Unbeknownst to everyone, Monarch taps the Snake Miraculous to mark this moment and shuts off all of A.D.A's sensors. As Claudie is back into the ship, A.D.A. asks her where she is and believes the test is a failure, much to Claudie's despair. A.D.A. believes it's too dangerous for it to exist and decides to fly the space jet to the ends of the universe, with Claudie still inside.
Soon, Cosmobug arrives, calms down Claudie, and tries to convince A.D.A. to let her help her. However, A.D.A. refuses, saying she does not need to be fixed. A.D.A is then transformed into Bugfighter by Monarch while Claudie is still on the space jet. After an attempt at capturing Astrocat fails, Monarch uses the Snake Miraculous to go back to the marker, in which he was about to shut off A.D.A's sensors, multiple times, with him succeeding in his second try.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 5]]
While Monarch tries to take the Cat Miraculous, with the help of Cosmobug, Claudie uses the emergency hammer to smash the window and escapes. Bugfighter senses damage inside of her and when she asks Monarch, he tells her it is a result of an asteroid as Claudie is pulling apart Bugfighter's wires.
She then realizes Monarch lied to her and rejects her megakuma and transforms back into A.D.A. Monarch then goes back in time to when he created the marker various times, but fails each time to achieve his goal. He eventually gives up and falls to his knees, with Claudie and A.D.A. passing the second test as her son and his classmates cheer.
In "Revelation", Claudie gets hypnotized through her Alliance ring by Hoaxer. She, among others, surround a Cat Noir detained by Nora Césaire and Fire Captain Hessenpy as Hoaxer arrives. After she is defeated, Claudie is freed by Scarabella's Miraculous Scarabella.

title: Claudie Kanté/History
text:
Claudie Kanté/History - [[Season 6]]
Claudie is mentioned as Aurore Beauréal's idol in "Climatiqueen", who is very passionate about meteorology and especially of the photos of climatic phenomena Claudie took from space. After Aurore is freed of her akumatization in an attempt to win a copy of Weather From Space signed by Claudie herself, she receives a like directly from the latter after joining the online Ladybug Community.

title: Christ the Redeemer
text:
Christ the Redeemer - Intro
is a monumental statue of Christ that dominates the city of Rio de Janeiro from the top of Corcovado Mountain in Brazil. It is one of the main symbols of Rio de Janeiro.

title: Christ the Redeemer
text:
Christ the Redeemer - Description
Built in collaboration with Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa, French sculptor Paul Landowski, Romanian sculptor Gheorghe Leonida (for the head), and French engineer Albert Caquot, the Christ the Redeemer statue stands in the heart of Tijuca National Park, atop Corcovado, 710 meters above sea level. Inaugurated on October 12, 1931, it is a 30-meter statue atop an 8-meter pedestal, for a total height of 38 meters. It depicts Jesus Christ standing with his arms crossed, gazing out over the city. His pose calls for the redemption of the Cariocas, and his face, at once stern and calm, commands respect.

title: Christ the Redeemer
text:
Christ the Redeemer - Trivia
The Statue of Christ the Redeemer has been classified as a Brazilian Historical Monument since 1973.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Intro
"" is a season 1 episode of the series, Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. According to the series' production/written order, it is the 8th episode of season 1, as well as the 8th episode of the series, overall.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Synopsis
A jealous sculptor in love with Ladybug akumatizes into Copycat, a duplicate of Cat Noir who tries to take his rival's place by Ladybug's side.
Disney+
Ladybug and Cat Noir face Copycat, Cat Noir's evil twin.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
Marinette is on the balcony of her house, talking to Tikki about Adrien. Whenever Marinette tries to talk to him, she can't say anything. Tikki suggests talking to him on her cellphone, and Marinette calls Alya to ask for Adrien's number.
Meanwhile, at the Place des Vosges, a statue is about to be revealed. Sculptor Théo Barbot is congratulated by Mayor Bourgeois for putting the effort into making the statue. Théo wishes to meet Ladybug and get her to autograph a picture of her.
Inside Marinette's room, Alya has prepared a speech for Marinette to read to Adrien over the phone to invite him to the movies. Marinette protests, saying that she sounds awkward and unnatural when she reads out loud. Alya replies that Marinette should memorize the text. Before Marinette can back out, Alya presses the "call" button.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
Marinette dances around with the phone in her hand before she is directed to Adrien's voicemail. He is currently at fencing practice, as seen by Adrien's schedule on the calendar attached to Marinette's ceiling. Alya tells her to leave a message. Panicked, Marinette leaves an impromptu voicemail and throws it on her chaise lounge back to Alya. She then accidentally records herself confessing her crush since she never ended the call. They try to delete the message, but Adrien's phone saves it. To save her dignity, Marinette and Alya hurry to the school to delete the message from Adrien's phone before fencing practice ends.
Meanwhile, Adrien takes a break from practice to get some water. Hidden away in his locker, Plagg tells him he has a new voicemail on this phone from an unknown sender. When Adrien goes to check his messages, he notices that it is nearly 2:00 and that he'll be late to the statue reveal. He quickly transforms into Cat Noir.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
Just as they leave the bakery, Marinette and Alya notice Cat Noir jumping over the rooftops and landing in front of the statue at the Place des Vosges. Only then do they remember that the statue reveal was supposed to be today. Alya stays in the park to take pictures of the ceremony for the Ladyblog while Marinette runs ahead to the school to erase the voicemail, hoping to return in time as Ladybug.
Théo is disappointed that Ladybug has not yet shown up to the ceremony, but Cat Noir assures him that she should be there soon. He goes as far as calling himself the leader of the duo. Mayor Bourgeois thinks Ladybug might show up sooner if they start the ceremony without her, but Théo convinces him to wait a little longer.
Marinette sneaks into the boys' locker room and calls Adrien's cell phone to figure out which locker is his. Simultaneously, Mayor Bourgeois ultimately starts the ceremony without Ladybug and unveils the statue, much to Théo's disappointment, and Marinette finds Adrien's locker. Tikki unlocks the door by phasing through it.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
The statue ceremony ends and people leave. Cat Noir stays behind to thank Mayor Bourgeois while Théo expresses his sadness at not being able to meet Ladybug. From Théo's words, Cat Noir realizes that Théo is in love with Ladybug. He becomes jealous, insinuating to Théo that he and Ladybug are already in a romantic relationship. Théo leaves angrily, wondering what Ladybug sees in Cat Noir.
Back at the school, fencing practice is over and the boys are returning to the locker room. Tikki is impatient to get to the statue reveal ceremony, but Marinette has been unable to delete the message from Adrien's phone; she cannot get past the pattern lock to open it. When the fencers enter the locker room, she hides behind the door, takes the phone, and sneaks out of the school just as Adrien returns. Adrien takes his bag from his locker and leaves, not realizing that his phone is missing.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
In his studio, Théo rages about how Cat Noir does not take love seriously and how he, not Cat, deserves to be with Ladybug. Hawk Moth, sensing Théo's jealousy and anger sends out an akuma. The akuma lands on the photo of Ladybug, and Théo transforms into the supervillain Copycat. Hawk Moth promises that Théo can have Ladybug forever if he brings back Cat Noir and Ladybug's Miraculouses.
Back at home, Adrien realizes he can't find his phone and suspects that Plagg might have done something to it. He grabs the house phone and calls his cell, which startles Marinette. She panics at the thought that Adrien might figure out she took it, worrying that she could be arrested for grand theft, spend the rest of her life in jail, and worst of all, miss out on going to the movies with Adrien. Thinking he left his phone at the gym, Adrien takes Plagg with him and rushes out of the house. Meanwhile, Copycat sneaks into the Louvre and steals the Mona Lisa while the museum visitors watch in shock, intending to frame Cat Noir for the crime.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
In the car, Adrien hears of the theft and hurries into the school, transforming into Cat Noir and running off to the Louvre. His driver waits outside the school.
Marinette is still trying to break into Adrien's phone, wearing ridiculous gear while doing so, when Alya calls from the Louvre, informing her about Cat Noir (Copycat) stealing the Mona Lisa. At first, Marinette is confused, thinking someone has robbed Cat Noir, but Alya clarifies. Marinette does not believe that Cat Noir would do such a thing. She transforms into Ladybug and goes to investigate.
At the Louvre, Cat Noir convinces the police to let him investigate the scene of the theft, telling them that the thief was an impostor. Under the guise of believing him, Roger Raincomprix tricks Cat Noir and locks him in the room. Roger refuses to let Ladybug see him when she arrives, telling her to leave this case to the professionals. Cat Noir uses his Cataclysm to escape, fighting off a squad of officers waiting in the entrance of the Louvre.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
When Roger hears of Cat Noir's escape, he and Ladybug run inside, only to find the officers on the ground. Ladybug realizes that Cat Noir was holding back against the police. Ladybug leaves, letting the "professionals" take care of Cat Noir.
Outside, Cat Noir uses his staff to contact Ladybug's yo-yo, telling her he has to find the impostor and flees the police helicopters and squad cars. He disappears into an underground metro station and de-transforms into Adrien. Across the street at the Metro he entered is a pileup of police cars. Plagg suspects that the impostor is a new akuma victim and Adrien realizes it must be Théo, recognizing the lollipop stick that Copycat had planted in the Louvre.
Cat Noir arrives at Théo's studio and calls Ladybug, letting her know that he found Copycat's hideout. She asks where he is, but Cat Noir decides that—since this situation is his fault—he has to handle it alone so he doesn't tell her where he is before hanging up. Ladybug uses the tracking device in her yo-yo to find him.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
Inside, Cat Noir finds a note in front of a Maneki-neko on top of a box from Copycat that says, "Cat's in the bag". The note turns out to be a trap, as the box springs open and catches him in a pair of shackles. He tries to use Cataclysm to break the chains, but Copycat appears from behind and forces his hand to touch a random plank of wood, wasting the Cataclysm. Copycat also steals Cat Noir's staff and poses as the real Cat, calling and informing Ladybug that he has captured the "fake". Cat Noir tries to tell her it's a trap, but Copycat hangs up before she can hear. He then reveals to Cat Noir his plan to win Ladybug's love from him and proceeds to taunt him.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
Ladybug arrives just as Copycat is about to remove Cat Noir's Miraculous. He tells her that the akuma is inside the ring, encouraging her to take it off Cat Noir's finger just as the ring loses its second dot. The real Cat Noir begs Ladybug to ask the impostor about their relationship while using a nickname only the actual Cat Noir uses. Ladybug, realizing something is fishy, asks Copycat if he kept their secret promise. Not knowing that Ladybug and Cat Noir never made any promise, Copycat says he kept the secret, revealing himself as the fake. He says he loves Ladybug and insists that he would be much better for her than the real Cat Noir. Ladybug replies that while Cat Noir has his flaws, he has never lied to her. Cat Noir kicks Copycat off of him.
Copycat activates Cataclysm, claiming that if he can't have Ladybug, then no one will. Ladybug retorts that she belongs to no one and uses Lucky Charm, a spoon appearing. Cat Noir gets into a defensive stance. Copycat lunges to attack Ladybug, but she shields herself with Cat Noir's chains, using Copycat's Cataclysm to break them and free her partner. Freed, Cat Noir kicks Copycat into the opposite wall.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
Cat Noir reveals that the Akuma is inside the photo in Copycat's pocket, but they have to hurry as his ring has lost another dot, while Copycat's countdown has only just begun. The two battle with Copycat, who is armed with both his and Cat Noir's staffs and is surprisingly skilled. When Copycat is distracted, gloating about himself, Ladybug uses her yo-yo to steal one of the staffs, returning it to Cat Noir. She also uses her yo-yo to catch the arm of one of the Cats, who protests that he is the real Cat Noir. The other Cat immediately insists that the first one is lying. Irritated with both of them, Ladybug demands to see how many pads they have left on their rings. The Cat she caught with her yo-yo turns out to be the real one, as he is down to one pad, while Copycat hisses in frustration, hiding his ring and making three pads disappear at once. Ladybug releases Cat Noir, and the two Cats resume fighting.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
Using her lucky vision, Ladybug spots one of the staffs (lost earlier during the fight), a support beam on the ceiling, her yo-yo, and the spoon from her Lucky Charm. She makes a fishing rod with the staff, the yo-yo, and some duct tape that she tears off, bending the spoon into a hook shape. She catches Copycat by the belt with her fishing rod and swings over the beam, suspending him from the ceiling. She then takes the photo from his pocket and tears it. The Akuma flies out. Ladybug catches it, purifies it, and summons the Miraculous Ladybug to return everything back to normal; the Mona Lisa is returned to the Louvre and Copycat turns back into Théo.
Cat Noir is relieved that Ladybug could tell him apart from the fake. She retorts that it wasn't so difficult once she knew who was really in love with her, referring to Théo.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Plot
Down to his last dot, Cat Noir takes his leave, remarking that Ladybug has broken his heart as well as Théo's, but she doesn't hear him. Ladybug apologizes to Théo for not showing up to the statue reveal earlier that day and autographs his photo, complimenting him on his work. Still believing that Ladybug and Cat Noir are in a relationship, Théo says he is okay and promises not to tell anyone, to which Ladybug responds with confusion.
Cat Noir returns to school as Adrien but eventually goes home, unable to find his phone. With Alya's assistance, Marinette manages to bypass the pattern lock and delete the voicemail. The next day, she sneaks the phone back into Adrien's bag at school.
Adrien is puzzled to discover his phone in his bag, as he has checked there countless times. Nino suggests that they clear their heads by going to see a movie that night. Alya asks Nino if she and Marinette can join them, and Nino agrees that it would be cool. Adrien turns around and smiles at Marinette, making her jump for joy, which ends the episode.

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Trivia
Internationally, this episode first premiered in Korea.
This episode was the ninth to air in France and the third to air in Korea.
This episode didn't air in Saudi Arabia because of the censorship of the channel MBC3.
The French title for this episode is "L'Imposteur".
The Ladyblog is mentioned for the first time.
When Cat Noir and Copycat are fighting, Cat Noir is mostly on the left.
References
Inside the Louvre, there are several banners advertising the same Tutankhamun exhibition that appears in "The Pharaoh".
Despite Adrien becoming Cat Noir three separate times in this episode, his transformation sequence is never shown meaning this is the second time he transforms off screen following "Mr. Pigeon".
Also in this episode, the three uses of Cataclysm that occur never show the activation sequence.
Additionally, the same music for Cataclysm plays when Cat Noir and Copycat use it.
This is one of the four episodes of season 1 in which Hawk Moth doesn't hold his end monologue after being defeated. The other three being "Princess Fragrance", "Simon Says" and "Antibug".
Allusions

title: Copycat
text:
Copycat - Trivia
The Maneki-neko (a cat figurine) that appears inside his studio bears a resemblance to Néko, the main antagonist of Kobushi, which is an another ZAG-produced show.
According to Thomas Astruc, Néko's cameo in Théo's studio is a reference to one of ZAG animation's future projects. He might be referring to the upcoming CGI feature film of Kobushi that is in production at that time.
Coincidentally, in the English dubbed version of Kobushi, Néko is voiced by Matthew Géczy who also serves as Jagged Stone's French voice actor and the scratch voice director for Miraculous.
Errors
When Adrien accuses Plagg, there are only two monitors on his wall, while in other episodes, there are three visible monitors.
When Tikki tells Marinette to leave Adrien's phone behind, Adrien's shoes are outside the bag, while when Plagg is eating Camembert, the shoes are inside his bag.
Adrien's phone is entirely white and sleeker looking, but the phone model is inconsistent and switches between the same phone with a black back, and the plainer phone Marinette and other characters use (white on the front and edges and black on the back).

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Intro
, called Françoise Dupont Middle School/High School (see note below) in the English version, is a public middle school (collège in French) that Marinette, Adrien, and their classmates attended.
From season 6 onwards, due to the changes done by Mayor Caline Bustier in the Paris educational system, Françoise Dupont became a school suited for at least 10 graders, allowing Marinette, Adrien and the other previous 9th grade students to not only continue study there, but also allow them to have classes with students of grades below theirs.
Students below elementary and middle school age can seemingly attend as well, given Manon and Chris's presence in "Climatiqueen" and "El Toro de Piedra".
Note: The French word "collège" does not translate to the English word "college." Its meaning is "junior high school/middle school." Middle school in France lasts four years, starting in "sixième" (French equivalent to 6th grade) until "troisième" (French equivalent to 9th grade), which explains why the protagonists are between 13 and 15.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Intro
There are some inconsistencies in the English dub regarding the grade level of the students. The English dub often calls it a high school, and Alya in "The Pharaoh" says that Ladybug's history textbook is a 10th grade book in the English dub. The original French dub says it is for "troisième (ninth grade)" which is the last year of collège/middle school in France. These changes are likely to not confuse American audiences where ninth grade is the first year of high school. However, in the English dub of "Illusion", it is said that Marinette's class is at the last year of Junior High, meaning they are in 9th grade. This change was possibly made both to not confuse American audiences and to be in agreement with the original French dub.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Appearance
Exterior
The exterior of the school is tan with a slate blue cobblestone roof. The building is three stories tall.
Entrance
The front of the building has eight large arched windows, each slightly inset with a striped design above them. The steps leading up to the entrance door widen as they approach the sidewalk and vice versa towards the entrance. The double entrance doors are dark oak, with gray handles. Above the doors is a white banner with a red outline hanging down. Above the banner are four rectangular windows, a large circular window, and a smaller circular window on each side.
Courtyard
The central portion of the school is an open-air courtyard. The entrance to the courtyard has a diagonal black and white checkerboard pattern, with a slate cream under this design. On either side of the entrance doors are a wooden bench and two chalkboards. Along one side wall of this area is a door leading to a utility room. The nurse's office, which a placard indicates is handicap-accessible, is located along the opposite side wall.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Appearance
The courtyard is made up of slate-gray concrete, with white lines painted on to make a basketball court. On either side of the courtyard is a basketball hoop hanging by a white rope. There is also a set of green metal stairs on either side of the courtyard, leading up to the second-floor rooms. Next to the stairs are green support pillars, supporting the platforms above.
Around the perimeter of the courtyard are various rooms, including locker rooms with adjoining restrooms, and several classrooms, among them a science classroom.
Following Mayoress Bustier's ecological reformation, the courtyard is now pathed with grass and plants, like bushes and trees.
Second Floor
The second floor has a green overhang, cream slate walls, and thin green metal pillars for structural support of the overhang. The platform jutting out from the wall, designed to allow people to get around the second floor, is made of green metal.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Appearance
The second floor also has the entrances to the various classrooms, including an art studio room. Most of the classrooms have large windows and a birch door. Other rooms have no inward windows and a dark oak door with a window. At the bottom left of the stairs leading to the library is the headmaster's office.
Third Floor
The third floor at the front of the school has only one room, the library. The stairs leading up to the library are a light slate cream, with a slate orange and light brown banister. Just underneath the slight overhang of the banister are small white stone rectangles, positioned evenly throughout. Just at the apex of the two stairs is a stone design of a fleur-de-lis, with a downward-facing bow and flowers within the bow. The doors to the library are dark oak, with large windows and no discernible handles.
The third floor along the school's rear perimeter houses the cafeteria. Access to the cafeteria has been shown to be via stairs from the first-floor courtyard.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Trivia
The collège is based on the Lycée Carnot.
The collège's name is a tribute to the real name of Fantômette, Françoise Dupont, the first female superhero of French literature.
The collège is located near the Eiffel Tower, in front of the Place des Vosges, and across the street from Tom & Sabine Boulangerie Patisserie.
In the English dub of "The Pharaoh", Alya reveals she and her class are 10th graders when she finds Marinette's history book.
"10th grade" may refer to the American education system of 10th grade, consisting of ages 15-16, or to the British education system of the 10th year, consisting of ages 14-15.
As Alix turned 15 in "Timebreaker", and France collèges have students until that age, it most likely indicates that it follows the British system. It is also possible that "10th grade" could be a dub discrepancy.
In the French dub, Alya says that they are in troisième, the equivalent to US 9th grade.
In the Korean and French dubs, Alya says they are 9th graders.
In the Polish dub, Alya says they are highschoolers.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Trivia
Based on the fact that Luka is stated to go to Collège Françoise Dupont and to be older than Marinette's class, and that Marinette turns 14 in "Befana," it is likely that the class is in quatrième, the second-to-last year of collège and the equivalent to 8th grade in the US.
This could also imply that "The Pharaoh" and "Timebreaker" take place in the same school year, which then implies that this is the year after "Befana".
Théo Barbot has been seen at the collège, although it is uncertain whether he is a student, a staff member or a visitor.
The collège building is used by Mr. D'Argencourt and Sabine Cheng to teach their respective classes, which are held after school hours and on the weekends.
Despite not being a faculty member, Sabine is able to teach her painting class within the building's art classroom.
Both their classes aren't exclusively for Collège Françoise Dupont students.
In "Qilin", Nadja Chamack is shown to attending Sabine's painting class and is the only adult present.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Trivia
While "Miraculous on Instagram" is level 2 canon to the Quantic Universe continuity, it revealed that the building's front entrance and the courtyard are opened during summer vacation. Mr. D'Argencourt's fencing class also occurred at that time during the Instagram campaign, so this likely means Sabine's painting class is also held during the summer.
Alya also revealed in a comment that Kagami Tsurugi didn't attend Collège Françoise Dupont. Rather, she is a visitor who only arrives at the school for Mr. D'Argencourt's fencing classes. This is also officially confirmed in "Determination" since Marinette gave Kagami a ride to the school and dropped her off there.
The collège has been part of multiple akumatized villain attacks:
In "Lady Wifi", Lady Wifi broadcasts Mr. Damoclès confessing to unjustly suspending her to the entire school. As a result of a villain being present on the campus, Miss Bustier evacuates her class for their own safety.
In "The Evillustrator", the Evillustrator attacks Chloé in the library.
In "Rogercop", Rogercop searches for the collège for André Bourgeois.
In "Horrificator", the building is covered in Horrificator's goo.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Trivia
In both "Ladybug & Cat Noir" and "Stoneheart", multiple doors and walls are broken and smashed by Stoneheart.
In the former, specifically, cameras are also destroyed.
In "Reflekta", everyone, including students and staff, are all turned into Reflekta's likeness.
In "Robostus", Markov is akumatized in Principal's office and captures Max.
In "Zombizou", Zombizou turns multiple students into kissing zombies in order to make Chloé a kissing zombie.
In "Reverser", Reverser goes to the art classroom to search for Marinette and Nathaniel to reverse them. He also reverses the art teacher and the students present in the classroom destroy all art.
In "Malediktator", Malediktator makes teachers and students destroy the school. He also searches the school for Marinette.
In "Chameleon", Chameleon disguises herself as Adrien and steals Nino's cap.
In "Gang of Secrets", the Gang of Secrets attack the school, and transform many people in the school into Reflekta's likeness, in search of Marinette.
In "Guiltrip", Guiltrip is attached to one the bathroom stalls and traps students and teachers inside itself.
In "Multiplication", it's the first place attacked by Ikari Gozen.

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Trivia
In "Deflagration", the school's students are transformed into singing shoes by Sole Destroyer.
It's one of the places where Ryukomori reminisces in "Perfection".
The students of Miss Bustier's class are Hoaxer's first brainwashing victims in "Revelation".
Reflekta returns in "Confrontation". She once again transforms students into her clones, then destroys the school's walls using Clout.
As mentioned in "Reflekta", the collège has at least eighteen classes.
A class photo from a previous year reveals that Miss Bustier's class that year included Marinette, Chloé, Sabrina, Rose, Juleka, Max, Kim, and Nathaniel.
Various students started attending the collège throughout the series:
Adrien and Alya begin going to the collège in "Ladybug & Cat Noir", Adrien specifically being a homeschooled student beforehand.
Lila, an Italian exchange student, joins in "Volpina".
Zoé Lee, a teenage girl from New York, joins the school in "Sole Crusher".
Sublime Varlette, an athlete from Belgium who moved to Paris in "Sublimation".
Raymond Pugnant, a teenage boy from New York and Zoé's previous classmate in "Daddycop".

title: Collège Françoise Dupont
text:
Collège Françoise Dupont - Trivia
Collège Françoise Dupont becomes one of the schools to implement Mayoress Bustier's educational reforms, with now students beyond 9th grade being allowed to study there (like Marinette and her class who had just graduated).
Also, as seen in "Daddycop", students of different grades can share classes together, as seen how Zoé, who is a grade bellow her friends, has classes with them.

Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1) - Intro
"" is a Season 5 episode of the series Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. Based on the series' production order specifically, "" is the 25th written and produced episode of Season 5. It is also the 129th written and produced episode of the series overall.
This episode is also the first part of the two-part Season 5 finale, "The Final Day".

title: Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1)
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1) - Synopsis
Monarch has just placed the final pieces of his villainous plan on his chessboard of evil. He has nothing left to lose, because today will be his final day. The plan he has put in place is more ambitious than ever. Global, merciless, radical. If he were to fail at seizing Ladybug and Cat Noir's Miraculous, the world would live forever in chaos. The unsuspecting Marinette and Adrien have already fallen victim to this plan. Are Ladybug and Cat Noir doomed?
Will Monarch win in the end?
Disney+
Is it the final day for Monarch, Ladybug and Cat Noir?
Netflix
In the grip of Monarch's psychic nightmares, the world turns to a hypnotizing app that could give Gabriel enough power to destroy Ladybug and Cat Noir.

title: Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1)

text:
Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1) - Plot
The episode opens with a news broadcast by Nadja about summer break in Paris and people voting for Caline Bustier to be the Mayor, then the arranged "perfect" couple Kagami Tsurugi and Adrien Agreste will be doing their modeling careers in London and then it goes on to a commercial break of Perfection water bottle.
Seeing this, Kagami angrily throws her shoe on the TV screen as she is annoyed by those news.
At his lair, Gabriel Agreste and Tomoe Tsurugi launch Operation: Perfect Alliance.
In a single day, they did all this for their children.
Gabriel transforms into Monarch and summons a Megakuma.
He then de-transforms and tells the Megakuma to evilize him into Nightormentor and then asks Mullo, Kaalki and Orikko to grant him their powers.
First, he gains the power to fly through Sublimation, and then Multitude to make clones and have them use Voyage to travel all across the globe to spread nightmare dust.
No one and no country is safe as everywhere the Nightormentor clones go, people are infected with the nightmare dust, including many of Ladybug and Cat Noir's allies around the world, including the United Heroez and Ladydragon.

The Nightormentor clones returned and fall back in with the original, who then coughs out the Megakuma turning him back into Gabriel.
He tells Tomoe that the nightmare has been spread.
Phase 1 is complete.
In a dream, Marinette in a Ladybug Knight outfit drove to the Agreste mansion asking the camera that she wants to see Adrien, and the camera wants nothing to do with his son.
Ladybug Knight slashes through the gates and climbed the beanstalk to fight an akumatized Dragon.
Once she defeated it, the creature turned out to be none other than Gabriel.
Ladybug Knight slipped and slashes him, making him disappear like a Senti-being vanishing.
When Adrien, horrified, asked her why she did that, Marinette wakes up from her nightmare.
Tikki reassured her that he's in London now.
Marinette calls her to make sure he is okay, she tried to call him, but it instead went to voicemail.
Marinette decided to talk with Nathalie about Adrien's whereabouts.

Outside, Alya bumped into her. Since she is terrified that she'll blab her secret identity, she runs away, since they can't be seen together. Marinette tries to reach out to her friend, but her nightmares started to return, so she decides to talk to Nathalie and see Alya later. Adrien has a nightmare as Anti-Cat and Monarch has asked him to give him his Miraculous and Ladybug's. Adrien wakes up from that bad dream and then tries to ask the Gorilla to let him out. Gabriel tells Tomoe to start distributing the antidote as part of Phase 2 of their master plan and the process is launched. Adrien receives an Alliance ring with a message about the Perfect Alliance app. Adrien tries to put on the ring, but he throws it calling his father insane. Plagg tells him to transform into Cat Noir and find Ladybug, but Adrien tells him to hide. Plagg then reminds and reassures him that kwamis cannot be seen or heard through cameras, but Adrien then responds that Gabriel could see or hear him transform, so Plagg then turns the camera off and then proceeds to leave, but Adrien refuses to do that, and Gabriel notices he's not getting a signal and asks Tomoe to activate the camera in Adrien's robot.

It's making him sick. He also gets worried that he'll get akumatized if he transforms into Cat Noir and destroy everything with his Cataclysm, so he decided to take off the Cat Miraculous and gives it to Plagg so that since he can't help, he tells Plagg to find Ladybug so she can use it and that they'll meet each other again. Monarch carries her unconscious body back to her room where Ladybug was looking for Nathalie, but much to her shock, finds Master Fu's tablet with images from the Grimore and of the previous Miraculous holders in their civilian identities, then Ladybug heard Monarch's footsteps and her shock intensifies when seeing him de-transform back into Gabriel and that he confiscated Nathalie's tablet and Master Fu's as well so he let bygones be bygones and let her calm down with Perfect Alliance.

Ivan hugs Mylene that he's scared when Nadja tells everyone that Ladybug and Cat Noir kidnapped Adrien and Kagami. The Resistance all suffered a nightmare due to Gabriel's earlier actions as Nightormentor and there is nothing left to protect them from being akumatized. text:
Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1) - Plot
Monarch decided to create a quantum imprint for Ladybug and Cat Noir using a bit from his Cataclysm injury and a Magical Charm to create an app which turns people into Miraculized, superhumans with only the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses in mind. Ivan is transformed into a Miraculized and asks Mylene to help him find Adrien and Kagami, but she refuses as she asked him to take off his ring. Plagg then asks Alya to be his holder but she can't because she'll be akumatized back into Lady Wifi, so Plagg decides to find Ladybug. At the Agreste mansion, Ladybug tried to contact Cat Noir, but before she tried to finish her sentence, she is trapped as the mansion entered lockdown mode as the Ladybug and Cat Noir quantum imprint detector has been activated.

title: Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1)

text:
Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1) - Plot
Miraculized used Voyage to travel via the portal through the mansion without breaking in and fought Ladybug, asking where are Adrien and Kagami. Plagg notices the fight from inside and decides to travel through the portal to find Ladybug. After a long battle she decided to de-transform and hear Nathalie's words and then the quantum imprint is lost, forcing the Miraculized to leave the mansion since they lost Ladybug's signal. Monarch then decides to meet Ladybug in person in his mansion so he takes the powers of Stompp, Pollen, Wayzz, and Kaalki and then uses Voyage to travel through the mansion to find her.
Hidden in the kitchen, Marinette expresses her frustration, stating that she can't contact Cat Noir or transform, as the Miraculized would recognize her as Ladybug again.
Plagg then enters the cupboard to find Marinette, but he accidentally drops the ring, creating a faint noise that Monarch hears.
Marinette asks Plagg where Cat Noir is, and he informs her that Cat Noir has fallen victim to the Alliance ring.
Marinette explains that she is in the Agreste mansion, which is where Monarch resides.

title: Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1)

text:
Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1) - Plot
Tikki nods in agreement with Plagg as she picks up the previously dropped ring and puts it on.
Suddenly, Monarch drags Marinette out of the cupboard.
Determined, she glares back at him with a smirk.
Monarch is shocked to discover that it is Marinette Dupain-Cheng, recalling the numerous times he attempted to akumatize her.
However, she quickly corrects him.
She then unifies Tikki and Plagg to become a fusion of Ladybug and Lady Noire, delivering a kick to Monarch's face and flipping back.
After this, she strikes a heroic pose, raises her fists, and declares, "Call me Bug Noire," ending the episode on a cliffhanger as she prepares to confront her arch-enemy and put an end to his threat once and for all.

Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1) - Plot Developments
Gabriel and Tomoe's plan "Perfect Alliance" that they were planning since "Revolution", included to awaken dormant nightmares in each human's mind all across the world. Then make them wear their Alliance rings, that provided them peace from their nightmares and finally transform them into weapons against Ladybug and Cat Noir with Miraculous powers.
The places Nightormentor spreads his bad dream dust include Paris, London, New York City, Shanghai, Rio de Janeiro, Tokyo, Rome, Giza, Mexico City, Moscow, Barcelona, Amsterdam, Sydney, Berlin, Seoul, Bamako, Hạ Long, and Varanasi.
Monarch and Tomoe used Ladybug's Magical Charm that was given to Gabriel in order to locate Ladybug and the Cataclysm dust from Monarch's cataclysmed hand in order to locate Cat Noir.
To transfer the essence of Cat Noir's cataclysm, Monarch is seen to bare his left hand, which is followed by Cat Noir in "The Collector" and other episodes as well as Bunnyx in "Timetagger", that it's true that holders can remove parts of their costumes even though they are magical.

Conformation (The Final Day - Part 1) - Plot Developments
This is strange when remembering that, in "Lady Wifi", the villain of the same name was unable to tear off Ladybug's mask as it was attached to her face.
The two ways it could be possible is that when a holder activates the Miraculous transformation it's done by the holder's desire or by the kwami's magic or the quantum masking.
The fact that Monarch still has a Magical Charm given to him as Gabriel by Ladybug looks like an inconsistency, as he destroyed a Magical Charm belonging to him when he created the megakuma back in "Dearest Family". However, that inconsistency does not belong to "Conformation", but to "Illusion", as the episode's screenplay had a deleted scene where Ladybug would give a Magical Charm to Gabriel after he apparently "rejected" the akuma after being "re-akumatized" in The Collector.
Their idea is a callback to what Team Miraculous wanted to do back in "Mayura", use Hawk Moth's cane to track him.
As of this episode, Marinette and Gabriel know each other's identities as well as her knowing that Nathalie was Mayura and the ultimate price when using a damaged Miraculous.
