title: Furious Fu
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Furious Fu - Plot Developments
Master Fu and Marianne are revealed to be married and living in London, with the former having found a love for painting.
It's revealed that Marianne covers up the truth behind Master Fu's amnesia by claiming it was from a "paddleboat accident".
A Guardian's staff is revealed to contain a compass that can locate the Miracle Box.
It's also revealed that Master Fu's cane also possesses a compass.
When Master Fu had lost his staff that means in "Feast", he must have made his cane implying that the Guardians are trained to make Guardian staffs and possible replacements in the event of the Guardian ever losing theirs or to blend in.
According to Su-Han, the Miraculouses were never meant to be used by children or teenagers meaning they were strictly for adults only and that he was the previous Guardian of the Miracle Box before the incident with Fu's sentimonster.
Which sort of contradicts that the belief that the Miraculouses can be used by anyone regardless of age, it could be that at some point in the past maybe the Guardians did put the use of the jewels under teenagers, but something must have gone wrong, and the Guardians believed that teenagers wouldn't make good holders.

title: Furious Fu
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Furious Fu - Plot Developments
Before the French Miraculous superhero team, if the Kwamis always had adult partners, it's unknown how Tikki and the others knew about the five-minute time limit as it was only for teenagers and yet this could imply that what was mentioned above, either really did happen or the adult holders had their powers limited by other means.
And yet, in Monarch's case what Su-Han said is partially true as Monarch broke and committed several crimes leaving in the hands of adults.
With the reveal of other parallel universes and how the Kwamis are connected to all of them in "Miraculous Paris", it could be that in one of them, they lived working with only both good and bad teenage Miraculous holders. But in the event of ending up with bad ones, the Kwamis must have discovered what happens to their owners when used for evil. Seeing the seriousness of the situation they must have informed their Guardians likely agreeing that the jewels must not be used under teenagers unless they follow the rules, as a last resort or emergency.
Which likely foreshadows Ladybug and Cat Noir learning the full extent of the kwami's warning in "Miraculous Paris".

title: Furious Fu
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Furious Fu - Plot Developments
Su-Han also says that the shape of the Mother Miracle Box was incorrect implying that when a Miracle Box is passed down from one trained Guardian to another, it's supposed to retain its normal shape and said that its incorrect shape is an indication of it being owned by someone who isn't a real or full Guardian.
Regardless, the Guardian's Code applies to all Guardians of the Miraculous; both full-fledged and in training, so in Ladybug's case, if she renounced her title then, her memory would be magically erased like Fu's.
Upon noticing that Plagg wasn't accounted for (already having an owner), Su-Han also mentioned it wasn't only the extinction of the dinosaurs Plagg was responsible for; he also caused the ending of the dragons.
This proves that dragons were once real in the Quantic Universe.
The image of Jeanne d'Arc slaying a dragon it could imply that this happened before or after Plagg used his powers to make the rest of them go extinct meaning that these creatures were around until the 15th century.
Marinette transforms in front of Su-Han, revealing her secret identity to him.
This is the second time she deliberately reveals it, the first being in "Gang of Secrets".

title: Furious Fu
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Furious Fu - Plot Developments
The Chinese Miracle Box is revealed to be the first Miracle Box ever made and the one with the most powerful Miraculouses, being also called the Mother Box.
This is the third time where Adrien remains as Cat Noir for a whole episode, following "Prime Queen" and "Christmaster".
This is also the seventh time Adrien is a minor character in the permanent timeline, following "Mr. Pigeon 72", "Gang of Secrets", "Truth", "Cat Blanc", "Silencer" and "Style Queen".
This is fifth time where Plagg doesn't appear and the seventh time Alya doesn't appear.
More insight is shown about the Order of the Guardians:
According to Su-Han, there are at least 133 rules, or "Perfect Precepts", within the Order of the Guardians. However, he only explained four:
Precept 14: Kwamis must not live outside the Box.
Precept 52: Guardians must never lose a Miraculous.
Precept 133: A Guardian cannot, under any circumstances, wear a Miraculous.
There's also an unnumbered Precept about not involving humans without powers in a fight.
Although it's unknown if they count as Precepts, Su-Han mentions Guardians must have good instincts and should understand the world around them.

title: Furious Fu
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Furious Fu - Plot Developments
They are fiercely trained in a Martial Arts style called Mirakung Fu.
The art is used to stop rogue Miraculous holders but not people affected by Miraculous magic.
Them being taught on how to subdue any rogue Miraculous holder is similar to the Sentinel Dragons on Vanaheim of the "How to Train Your Dragon" franchise just like the dragons the Order managed to figure out the "perfect defense".
They are taught with a certain technique that allows them to block an akuma, powered up or not.
Su-Han is one of the few characters ever to completely drive away an akuma.
This is one of the few times a character sees an akuma before it infects someone.
This episode has the fifth highest number of Kwamis seen interacting and onscreen, with a total of 16, with only "Sandboy", "Kwamibuster", "Miracle Queen", and "Truth" passing this episode.
This is the eleventh time where Cat Noir used his powers on someone else following "Dark Cupid", "Princess Fragrance", "Despair Bear", "Troublemaker", "Malediktator", "Miraculous Shanghai" "Miraculer", "Cat Blanc", "Ladybug" and "Miraculous New York" but the eighth time of his own free will and this time was a result of an accident.

Marinette is sad during her transformation, similarly to "The Bubbler", "Santa Claws", "Zombizou", "Style Queen", "Anansi", "Miraculous Shanghai", "Félix", "Truth", and "Gang of Secrets".

This would also explain why he didn't come to Paris while Fu was still the Guardian.
Not only that taking into account how far the Tibetan Mountains where the temple is located from Paris, France to get there by foot which is almost 10,000 miles away (actually close to 9,740 miles which is also about 15,674 km and 3448 hrs) it would've taken Su-Han roughly 4.5-5 months to get to Paris.
However, despite Su-Han trying to get the Miraculouses back, let alone attempting to pick new holders, he was unaware of the consequences he could have caused or that could've happened:
He has no idea how long he and the Guardians had been gone.

Even if he could find new holders:
They wouldn't have the level of experience that Ladybug and Cat Noir have.
The life of a Miraculous holder isn't for everyone.
The minute Hawk Moth discovers there is a new pair of heroes running around, he'll know something is wrong. Which will lead him to believe that Ladybug and Cat Noir either picked new holders or that there is a new Guardian.
Su-Han doesn't even know Hawk Moth as well as the French duo does.
Since his staff acts like a compass if Su-Han had lost it, it was stolen or ended up with Hawk Moth, it would only be a matter of time before the villain figures out that it can be used to find the Miracle Box and the Guardian, therefore Su-Han could've put Marinette in serious danger.
As such, if Master Fu hadn't lost his memory or if Su-Han hadn't repelled the akuma, Hawk Moth would have certainly known about the staff's compass.
Not only to mention, the other Guardians, Miraculouses, Miracle Boxes and information they have about them would be in serious danger, if Hawk Moth discovered that Su-Han was in Paris or goes back to the temple with Hawk Moth and his villains following him.

text:
Furious Fu - Plot Developments
As Su-Han mentioned the Guardian's fighting technique only works against rogue Miraculous holders not people affected by Miraculous magic leaving them vulnerable.
But it's also strange that the Guardians were never trained to be prepared under those conditions which could imply that the Guardians were able to retrieve the Butterfly Miraculous and other jewels back before it happened or had someone else to act in their steed.
Usually when Kwamis are active, they can wonder as far as they want or need from their owners unless being restricted to a certain distance but when Marinette became the Guardian, the other Kwami were able to travel without their jewels being worn.
When they are fighting at the soccer field, the ZAG logo can be seen along the sidelines.
Internationally. This was the first Season 4 episode to air.

title: Fu's letter to Marinette
text:
Fu's letter to Marinette - Intro
is a note that Fu had written in advance for Marinette, in the event that he would lose his memory after passing on his guardianship to her. He stored the letter in a locker at the Gare du Nord train station, alongside a photo of his love, Marianne, and the gramophone in which he used to keep the Chinese Miracle Box.

title: Fu's letter to Marinette
text:
Fu's letter to Marinette - Appearance
The letter is handwritten on a sheet of plain white paper. It was inside a light blue envelope that had "Marinette" handwritten on its frontside, with a nondescript, red wax seal closing it on its backside.

title: Fu's letter to Marinette
text:
Fu's letter to Marinette - Content
"Experiencing loss is a part of life: some people lose their first love, some lose the harmony in their relationship. Some people lose hope, others lose patience, while others lose their soul. Some lose their certainties, and some have nothing to lose.
Experiencing loss is a part of life, but good things come, too. Expect the unexpected, and embrace it. Each first-time is an adventure, and who knows how far these adventures will lead you. You find people to whom you entrust your heart, as much as they entrust theirs to you. That trust is sometimes broken, but it can always be restored. Yes, sometimes the road can be winding - you might even get lost along the way. But with the help from the right people, you'll always find your destination.

title: Fu's letter to Marinette
text:
Fu's letter to Marinette - Content
As we grow old, we realize life doesn't always give us all the gifts we hoped it would. I would have loved to tell you all this in person, Marinette, but if you're reading this, it means I've already lost my memory. But you mustn't be scared, and you mustn't be sad. As I was telling you at the beginning of this letter, experiencing loss is a part of life, but it doesn't define it. Because what really matters isn't whether you win or lose. It's the ability to accept changes in ourselves. It's accepting that even if life doesn't always give us the gifts we were hoping for, the real gift is life itself."

title: Fu's letter to Marinette
text:
Fu's letter to Marinette - History
In "Miracle Queen", Ladybug's Lucky Charm resembled the key chain to Master Fu's locker, making him realize that it was time to pass down the title of Guardian to her. By relinquishing his Miracle Box, he lost all of his memories of anything related to the Miraculous, including those of Ladybug and Cat Noir. Despite this, he still gave Ladybug his key chain, because he recognized that it matched her Lucky Charm. Later, Marinette is able to find his locker using this key chain, and subsequently finds his letter as well.

title: Fu's letter to Marinette
text:
Fu's letter to Marinette - Trivia
Marinette's narration throughout "Heart Hunter" and "Miracle Queen" is revealed to be Master Fu's letter at the end of "Miracle Queen."

Furious Fu: (gesturing with his arms and hands) Phantom Palms of the Awakened! The wise man moves mountains without touching them! (he sends Ladybug and Cat Noir back with a burst of energy. He points to Su-Han) You're next.
Su-Han: (shouting fighting techniques) A Hundred Thousand Dragon Talons! The Pagoda Breaker Iron Feet! The Rage of the Sunscreen with Ingrown Nails!
Furious Fu: (writes 雕像 (Diāoxiàng) with his paintbrush; places the paper on Su-Han's forehead) Statue! (As he said this, Su-Han freezes like a statue and Fu takes his cane back) Finally!
Shadow Moth: Well done, Furious Fu.
Shadow Moth: Now you must keep your word and bring me Ladybug and Cat Noir's Miraculous.

title: Furious Fu/Transcript
text:
Furious Fu/Transcript - Intro
Furious Fu: Very well. So, I have to take the wingless bat's bell, right?
Shadow Moth: (annoyed) No! Not his bell! His ring!
Cat Noir: I am not a wingless bat! (about to start fighting again)
Ladybug: Cat Noir, wait. We'll never defeat him.
Cat Noir: What?
Ladybug: We just need him not to defeat us either.
Cat Noir: You lost me.
Ladybug: I have to make a call, cover me!  (opens her Bug-Phone)
Cat Noir: That I can do.
(Cat Noir jumps onto the field, swordfighting with his staff against Furious Fu, who parries with his cane.)
Furious Fu: The kitten can meow all he wants, but he will never roar like a tiger!
Ladybug: (finishes her call) Lucky Charm! (receives bolt cutters, then looks around for what to do. She notices Cat Noir's ring, some soccer ball in a locked cage, her yo-yo, and the bolt cutters) Perfect!
Furious Fu: (notices Ladybug going to the cage) What is she up to? (kicks Cat Noir away, plants his cane on the ground, then writes 视力 (Shìlì) with his paintbrush) Vision! (sees the items Ladybug intends to use) Oh, so this is your silly little plan. I know what you gonna do. (starts heading for Ladybug)

title: Furious Fu/Transcript
text:
Furious Fu/Transcript - Intro
Cat Noir: (stops Furious Fu by jumping on him from behind) We're not done yet!
(Ladybug uses the cutters to break a lock, then grabs a ball from the cage)
Cat Noir: Cataclysm!
Ladybug: (reacting to Cat Noir) No!
Furious Fu: (grabs Cat Noir, takes his activated hand, and threatens to cataclysm him with it) You're going to turn yourself into cat food.
Ladybug: (sends her yo-yo at Furious Fu) Take this! (Furious Fu catches the string between his teeth) And that! (Furious Fu catches Ladybug, holding her up by one arm. With her other arm, she puts the soccer ball between her legs and then wedges it between Cat Noir's activated hand and his chest) There! Voilà! We win!
Furious Fu: (while still holding the yoyo string between his teeth) Win? You foolish beetle, we're just stuck, now! I can't defeat you but you can't defeat me either!
Ladybug: (confidently) Oh, but my plan was never to defeat you myself.
Marianne: Sorry, I need to borrow that. (takes the paintbrush off Furious Fu's ear and breaks it) There, exactly like you said on the phone, Ladybug. (Furious Fu drops both Ladybug and Cat Noir as he is deakumatized)

title: Furious Fu/Transcript
text:
Furious Fu/Transcript - Intro
Ladybug: Thank you, Marianne. That was perfect. (opens her yo-yo) No more evil doing for you little akuma. Time to de-evilize! (catches the akuma) Gotcha! Bye bye, little butterfly! (throws the bolt cutters into the air) Miraculous Ladybug! (the storm clears and Su-Han is unfrozen)
Ladybug, Cat Noir, and Marianne: Pound...
Cat Noir: Whoops, sorry! (realizing his cataclysm is still active, he bends down to use it on the ball)
Ladybug, Cat Noir and Marianne: (they, along with Marianne, fist bump) Pound it!
Ladybug: (Ladybug takes a Magical Charm out of her yo-yo and hands it to Fu) Here, carry this with you at all times. It will protect you from future attacks.
Wang Fu: And it will remind me of you everyday. Thank you, Lady Beetle and Mister Bat. (Ladybug laughs)
Su-Han: (to Wang Fu; awkwardly, but sincerely) I'm terribly sorry. Forgive me, Whiny... Uh! Sir. I... I mistook you for someone who has been long gone. (returns Wang Fu's cane)
Wang Fu: (reclaims his cane) Don't worry about it, it's already forgotten.
(Su-Han and Fu bow)
Shadow Moth: Be careful with your Magic Box, Guardian of the Miraculous. You wouldn't want to lose it again.

title: Furious Fu/Transcript
text:
Furious Fu/Transcript - Intro
Wang Fu: The bat and the red beetle were incredible! Paris is always filled with good people ready to devote themselves for the greater good. Like you, Marinette.
Marinette: You should really thank Marianne, you know. From what I heard, she was the true superhero of the day.

title: Furious Fu/Transcript
text:
Furious Fu/Transcript - Intro
Su-Han: (upset) Involving Marianne in the fight - a human without powers was against the precepts too. (Marinette looks down, saddened) This has proven two things: the first thing is that you have the audacity to invent your own rules, and as crazy as it may seem, somehow they all work. (Marinette is surprised) The second thing is that your natural instincts tell you who you can trust, an essential quality for a Guardian. Whiny Chicken- uh, sorry... Master Fu may not have made such a bad choice after all. (Marinette smiles) The Miracle Box is the mother of all boxes. It's the very first one that was created, and the one that holds the most powerful magic jewels. I cannot imagine what would happen if it were to fall into the wrong hands. But I am going to trust you. (hands Marinette the box, she takes it happily) I will keep watching you from a distance, but be wary, one failure and I will take the Miracle Box back. (Marinette nods as she walks over to her special hiding place for the box, inputs the code, and sets it inside) I will make the most of my time here in Paris to get accustomed to modern life. How can I be a good guardian if I don't try to understand the world around me?

title: Furious Fu/Transcript
text:
Furious Fu/Transcript - Intro
Marinette: Thank you, Master. I have something for you too. I think you're gonna need these. (She holds up a new pair of shoes, causing Su-Han to look down at his old and worn out pair. Marinette and Su-Han share laugh.)

title: Fu's tablet
text:
Fu's tablet - Intro
is a tablet formerly owned by Wang Fu. It has a deciphered version of the Miraculous spellbook.
In "Miracle Queen", Hawk Moth and Mayura capture him, and Nathalie takes the tablet in her possession.
In "Truth", Gabriel used the translated information of the tablet to successfully repair the damaged Peacock Miraculous, thus making it safe to use.
In "Conformation", Ladybug finds it in Nathalie's room and leaves it on the bed, which makes her to begin to realize Gabriel and Nathalie's villainy. Gabriel later takes it alongside Nathalie's tablet.

title: Fu's tablet
text:
Fu's tablet - Appearance
Fu's tablet has a widescreen and thick depth. It has a white or black border (depending on the episode) and a silver casing; the tablet lacks a camera or home button.

title: Fu's tablet
text:
Fu's tablet - Trivia
In "The Collector", Fu uses his cellphone to take pictures of the Grimoire. Later, in "Miracle Queen", Nathalie says that the images are on his tablet. This means that they were probably transferred between the two devices.
After Gabriel passes away in "Re-creation", it's currently unknown what happened to the tablet, but Marinette likely took it back along with the spellbook.
Errors
On some occasions, it appeared with the black cover instead of white.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - Intro
is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is a young child who wants to ride his bicycle on his own and doesn't feel the need to listen to others' advice in any cases. Luckily, he isn't even aware of the risks around his way.
In "Risk", due to not being able to take any risks while riding his bicycle from his parents, he was akumatized by Shadow Moth into Risk, a frog-themed supervillain with the power to force people to take risks.
In "Strikeback", after his Megakuma was finally captured, Froggy also received a Magical Charm from Ladybug to prevent him from being reakumatized.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Froggy has brown skin, curly dark brown hair, and honey-colored eyes. He has two prominent buck teeth.
Civilian Attire
Froggy wears yellow, round-framed glasses over his eyes, an olive-green helmet, and a green, frog-themed shirt. He has black shorts and yellow-and-green knee pads.
As Risk
Risk wore a light green frog-themed hoodie, dark green gloves and rain boots, and big yellow goggles that functioned as eyes.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - Abilities
As Risk
Risk was able to create green particles from his bicycle horn that could attach to the back of a person's neck taking the shape of a frog's footprint.
If he sang his song: ♪ I'm Froggy, here I come! I'm not afraid of anyone ♪, the frog footprint on their necks would beep and glow green faintly making the person or people lose their fears and take all the risks they normally wouldn't take, but his powers didn't work on kwamis so they wouldn't be influenced to take any risks.
However, he knew karate, as he used his skills on Cat Noir when he tried to get Risk away from the battle against Strikeback and he was even shown to have nunchucks while introducing himself.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - History
Season 4
In "Risk", Froggy is first seen at the Ménagerie du Jardin des Plantes. He is upset about his parents not letting him ride a bike without a helmet and without training wheels. Froggy in his bike then rides away from his parents.
Taking advantage of Froggy's frustration, Shadow Moth sends an Megakuma and it manages to reache Froggy's stuffed toy. Froggy is akumatized into Risk, a frog-themed supervillain with the power to force people to take risks. Froggy's parents catch up to him, unaware that he was akumatized. Risk then marks them and starts singing. Immediately, both the marks on the back of Froggy's parents' necks glow. They wave to their son, and Froggy's dad comments that it's not so dangerous to ride a bike without training wheels after all. Shadow Moth then contacts Risk, telling him that they are going to have a lot of fun, but that he must be careful to hide his stuffed toy, or else Ladybug will come and break it and he'll lose his powers. Risk then replies that he'll hide it where she'll never find it, in a singing tone.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - History
Later that night in the streets, Risk continues to mark everyone in Paris, including Ella Césaire, Etta Césaire, Nora Césaire, Alya Césaire, Roger Raincomprix, Jean Tretiens, Marinette Dupain-Cheng, and Adrien Agreste onscreen, unknowingly to them.
The next day, Risk passes by the Agreste mansion singing, causing the mark on the back of Adrien's neck glows making him snap and forcing him to take risk. Later, Risk passes by Collège Françoise Dupont singing, causing the mark on the back of Marinette's neck glows making her want to tell Adrien her feelings for him. Risk then passes singing by the school again, causing chaos like making Marinette decide to save Adrien from his father without the help of her friends, Hessenpy drive his fire truck without a helmet, Lê Chiến Kim swim the entire Seine, and Max Kanté to accompany the previous despite not knowing how to swim. Risk is then seen near the Eiffel Tower singing and causing people to take risk.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - History
In "Strikeback", Shadow Moth tells Risk to sing as loud as he can to ensure that Ladybug and Cat Noir take risk, making Parisians approach the titular villain and put themselves in danger with his powers, thus distracting the heroes. Risk is also putting himself in danger as he also approaches the titular villain, being saved by Ladybug multiple times, whom believes Risk is a regular child.
Ladybug then takes Risk to Hôtel de Ville where she meets with her team. Risk taunts Ladybug and continues singing, and Cat Noir decides to carry him away. Rena Furtive notices that all the heroes and civilians have a frog mark on their necks as Risk launches Cat Noir, who realizes that they are dealing with an akumatized villain. Ladybug then brings part of the team to neutralize Risk while the rest limit the damage caused by the titular villain. Risk admits that he hid the akumatized object after they destroy all his belongings.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - History
Unifying the Ladybug, Horse and Rabbit Miraculouses to become Pennybug and Flairmidable enter a Burrow and return to the point when Froggy was akumatized, touch his stuffed toy with the ball and return to the present. In the present, Flairmidable uses his power to get Froggy's stuffed toy and Ladybug destroys the toy. After his Megakuma is finally captured, Froggy is de-akumatized and receives a Magical Charm from Ladybug to prevent him from being akumatized again.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - Relationships
Family
Froggy's parents
Froggy's parents were angry at him for riding his bike without his helmet and training wheels. After he was akumatized, he infected them with his power, and they let him do that.
Acquaintances
Ladybug
When he was akumatized, they were enemies. After she found out he was an akumatized villain, she deakumatized him with Flairmidable's help, and gave him a magical charm.
Shadow Moth
When he was akumatized, he worked for Shadow Moth, who had promised him that his parents would let him ride his bike without his helmet and training wheels. The supervillain was friendly towards the child, praising him and motivating him to sing as much as he can.

title: Froggy
text:
Froggy - Trivia
He is the fourth villain whose objective is not to obtain Ladybug's and Cat Noir's Miraculous after Catalyst, King Cash and Heart Hunter.
Considering that his song has him calling himself Froggy rather than Risk, that makes him the fourth villain to not reject their previous identity after Luka Couffaine as Truth, Zoé Lee as Sole Crusher and Nino Lahiffe as Rocketear in the eponymous episodes.
Although, it's currently unknown if Froggy is his actual name or just a pet name given by his parents.
However, in one of his songs, he also calls himself Risk as well, making him the second akumatized person to refer to both their previous and akumatized identity after Vivica.
The song Risk sings has the same tune as the "Rain Rain Go Away" song.
Froggy receives a Magical Charm in the season 4 finale.
He's also the last character to receive a Magical Charm in season 4.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Intro
is a major character in Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir, serving as the titular main antagonist of the episode "Félix", a major antagonist in Season 4, a major anti-hero in Season 5, and a recurring character in Season 6.
He is the son of the late American billionaire Colt Fathom and the British aristocrat Lady Amélie Graham de Vanily. He is also the nephew of the late Émilie Agreste and the late Gabriel Agreste, as well as the maternal cousin of Adrien Agreste. In "Representation", it is revealed he is a human sentimonster created by his father from his emotions of jealousy in order to make his wife pregnant.
In "Gabriel Agreste", when he became convinced that Gabriel was Shadow Moth, Félix was nearly akumatized. However, the akumatization failed as Félix rejected it and managed to escape.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Intro
In "Strikeback", while disguised as his cousin Adrien, Félix was temporarily given the Dog Miraculous by Ladybug which, when inhabited by Barkk, allowed him to transform into Flairmidable, a dog-themed superhero with the power of Adoration. After capturing Ladybug's yo-yo using the power of Fetch, Flairmidable traded all of the Miraculouses in the yo-yo, including the Dog Miraculous and his uncle's ring, for the Peacock Miraculous. He thus became Duusu's new owner and secured his own existence.
In "Emotion", Félix returned to Paris. Wanting to rid the city of everyone while ensuring what he believed was the happiness of those he cared about, he used the Peacock Miraculous. With Duusu inhabiting it, he transformed into Argos, a peacock-themed supervillain with the power of Emotion. He used his anger and hate to create Red Moon, a moon sentimonster that allowed him to make anyone under its light disappear and reappear with a snap of his fingers.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Intro
In "Pretension", Félix returned once again to free Kagami Tsurugi, a fellow human sentimonster, from her strict mother and to get to know her better. After Félix recovered the ring used to control her and returned it to Kagami, they developed feelings for each other and became a couple in secret.
In "Representation", Félix returned to reunite with Kagami in order to help her tell Marinette (after Kagami discovered that Marinette is Ladybug) the truth through their projector sentimonster, Once Upon a Time. They revealed that he and his cousin Adrien are sentimonsters, explained why (to his regret) he betrayed Ladybug, and disclosed that he was created by his late father out of jealousy towards Adrien's parents for having a child before him. His father constantly abused and tortured him throughout his childhood before his passing. They urged Marinette to stop Monarch so everyone could be free and have a happy ending.
At the end of "Re-creation", Félix became the newest member of the French Miraculous superhero team as Argos, thus recovering the Peacock Miraculous.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Intro
In "Sleeping Syren" and "Miraculous Tokyo", it is shown that Félix, as Argos, has been meeting Kagami, as Ryuko, midway between Paris and London while using the space power-up.
In "Revelator", it is shown that Félix, along with the other secondary heroes of Ladybug's team, was trained to unlock his adult powers, no longer detransforming after using his power.
In "Lady Chaos", Félix and his mother move in to Paris in order to be closer with Adrien.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Félix stands 150 cm tall, with blond, combed-down hair parted on the left with a piece hanging in the front, and bright green eyes that are slightly darker than his cousin Adrien's. He is nearly identical to Adrien, including sharing the same skin tone. The only noticeable differences are their clothes and the different ways they style their hair.
From Season 6 onwards, his hair grows longer at the back.
Civilian Attire
He wears a white long-sleeved dress shirt with a black necktie underneath a black vest, black dress pants, and black dress shoes. He also wears a silver ring on his right hand, which contains his amok.
From Season 6 onwards, while Félix looks the same, he no longer wears his necktie, his collar is up, and his sleeves are rolled up.
As Argos

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Appearance
Argos wears a stunning sapphire blue jumpsuit adorned with light mint lines running down each side of the legs. The lines feature diagonal dark blue peacock feathers, trimmed in cerulean with a light pink button on top. This design is accented by the button on his zipped-up turtleneck, which has dark blue lining, and appears on the top of his boots acting as a slider, as well as on his cuffs, around the feet, on the three straps securing each side of his torso, and on the large pieces on either side of his hood. Over the jumpsuit, he dons a stunning sapphire blue tailored jacket, which can also be considered a cloak and has a light mint interior.
The outer garment resembles a tailored jacket flowing into a cloak, especially given the presence of lapels as part of the hood — a possible nod to Félix's love for formal attire, a style he also follows in his civilian form, where he dresses in a vest, tie, and shirt. The bottom of his tailored jacket is widely jagged, with a main downward point in the middle.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Appearance
The jacket-cloak features a five-pointed tail resembling a peacock tail, with each point designed like a dark blue peacock feather featuring a light blue center. The hood of the cloak has pieces on top adorned with three light turquoise linear appendages with blue diamond-shaped feathers on top. He completes his look with dark blue gloves and blue high boots with darker soles.
Argos has pale indigo skin, light magenta irises, and vivid violet sclera. His hair is light green, retaining his normal hairstyle as Félix, and he wears the Peacock Miraculous at the center of his jumpsuit.
As Flairmidable
Given that his appearance was similar to Cat Noir's, Flairmidable had messy hair which, unlike Cat Noir's, did not cover his ears and was instead combed to the left.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Appearance
His outfit consisted of an orange suit with white on his torso and arms, and black pauldrons on his shoulders and legs. The leg pauldrons had sections extending up to the sides of the thighs. His weapon, a ball, hung on his turtleneck, which had black sides and a swan neck. He wore white boots with black outsoles. He also wore orange and white corgi ears and a mask in the same colors to cover his face. The mask had a white bottom with arched sides and a diamond-like point on top, similar to the design of his kwami, Barkk. He also had a small orange scraggy tail. When transformed, the collar necklace appeared as it normally does when Miss Hound transforms.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
Félix changed when his father passed away, meaning he wasn't always mischievous. This is later shown in "Representation" to have been because of the control his father had on him due to the amok placed on his ring. As Colt would abuse his control over his son due to the deep hate he had for him, considering him the reason his life force was being drained slowly. Félix was always perceived as an obedient son who would do what his father wanted, not only because Colt controlled him through the amok but also because he was genuinely afraid that his father might actually kill him. After Colt's death and Félix inheriting his ring (the object that contained his amok), the latter was able to obtain his own freedom and be who he really was.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
Despite their identical appearance, Félix is the complete opposite of his twin cousin in terms of personality. This is due to the fact that their childhoods were way too different. To be more precise, Adrien spent his with a loving mother, while Felix was mercilessly beaten and abused in other ways by his father. Unlike Adrien who is kind and gentle, Félix was rude, sneaky, and very pushy, especially when it came to getting what he desired, even being willing to negotiate with Hawk Moth and put others in danger.
Adrien, as Cat Noir, annoyed with him for indirectly causing the akumatizations of Alya Césaire, Rose Lavillant, and Juleka Couffaine, said to him, "I bet you don't have a lot of friends, acting the way you do", implying that Félix didn't get along well with others because of his mischievousness. That fact is actually confirmed in "Emotion" where he tells Ladybug that he wants to create a better world without excluded people like him.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
And yet, it could be that Felix wasn't mischievous for the sake of it. In "Félix", for example, he might have behaved that way due to the effects of and PTSD after his father's death, as he felt a sense of impunity because his freedom was now his own and no one could tell him what to do.
As for "Strikeback", Felix acted so much like a villain because Ladybug sun-burned the Sentimonster Strikeback, which led him to feelings of deep sadness and helplessness due to his inability to save one of his own kind. Before "Emotion", Felix considered all people to be evil and incapable of empathizing with beings like the Sentimonsters, and he also had significant trust issues with others. Thus, he chose not to have a heart-to-heart talk with Ladybug, but rather revenge. The desire to avenge Strikeback against her, combined with the wish to attain ultimate freedom, led him to exchange all the Miraculous for the Peacock Miraculous at the episode's end.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
Moreover, he still likely did not let go of this whole situation even after he got his revenge on Ladybug, since in "Emotion" he returned and snapped everyone out of existence. This is probably a reference to the fact that Felix created the Red Moon out of hatred for how people treat Sentimonsters like objects to be used and discarded with a snap. He also personally states that he wants to create a world where no one decides between what is right and wrong, who gets power and who doesn't, which refers back to the situation where Ladybug offered Felix the Dog Miraculous to help destroy Strikeback, indicating that his pain is still alive.
He only fully healed from his pain, tamed his desire for revenge, and understood that not all people are evil at the episode's end, after which he began to change for the better, becoming more open and trying to learn to trust someone. Nevertheless, he might also be so mischievous out of fear of losing those he loved or felt close to. To be more precise, Felix's father strictly forbade him from communicating with anyone, and even if the boy liked a person, his father's order was enough to trouble his feelings.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
Despite these negative traits, Félix is shown to genuinely care for his family. With the exception of his father and uncle, he has a deep affection for the rest of his family members, especially his mother, aunt, and cousin. This is especially shown in his relationship with his mother, as he is willing to do anything to please her, including stealing the Graham de Vanily ring. Despite the fact that he doesn't like how Adrien is too nice (something that causes him to tease him by pretending to be him and cause him some trouble), Félix does love his cousin and would do anything to make him happy, including freeing him from the oppression of the latter's father on the grounds that Felix thinks that Adrien is suffering as much as himself.
By "Gabriel Agreste", he hasn't changed that much, but he is seen having a much more heroic figure as he became determined to discover if Gabriel was Shadow Moth and threatened to expose him. This could indicate that the initial shock and the overwhelming sense of impunity after his father's death were gradually fading away, and he was slowly coming back to his usual self.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
In "Risk", it also seemed that he became much more heroic, less villainous, and somewhat rebellious. He was perceptive enough to convince Adrien to disobey his father for once. He was also very stubborn, as seen when, upon seeing Adrien's message about his cousin telling him to stop (saying he was on his way), Félix disregarded and deleted the message, and continued his act. However, he was understandably horrified when he found that his aunt was in a comatose state and hidden in Gabriel's bunker.
Felix's personality before the episode "Emotion" is perhaps best characterized by sneakiness, selfishness, and a lack of culpability or concern for others as long as he got what he wanted. These traits became exacerbated in "Strikeback" when he became Flairmidable and carried out his plan to get revenge for what happened to Strikeback and other Sentimonsters. He explained to Ladybug that the newfound power she gave him made him feel invincible.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
His actions before "Emotion" — namely, his proposal of an alliance with Hawkmoth in exchange for the twin rings and his voluntary surrender of nearly all the active Miraculous to his villainous uncle in exchange for the Peacock Miraculous — make it clear that he did not experience the slightest hesitation or remorse, as he was convinced that people despised Sentimonsters and his revenge would help him prove that Sentimonsters (himself and those like him) cannot be treated that way.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
Without realizing it, despite his dislike for the bully, he acted somewhat similar to Chloé as both were scarred by the pain of the past and by letting it stir them in the present which led to actions in the future that caused nothing but trouble for everyone else including themselves. Although he hates oppressors, he has no qualms about depriving others of their freedom just to secure his own and that of those he valued, as demonstrated by his deal with Gabriel to obtain the Peacock Miraculous, turning fifteen Kwamis into slaves for Gabriel's future plans and betraying the heroes, something Chloé was close to doing before being defeated in "Miracle Queen". However, these situations may differ on the grounds that Chloé did it to "get revenge for herself" because Ladybug didn't give her the Bee Miraculous, while Felix did it "to avenge Strike Back (not only for himself but also for other Sentimonsters)".

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
Félix's intense hatred of being an outcast suggests that he himself may have felt like an excluded person his entire life. Yet upon gaining power, he failed to realize that he was doing the exact same thing to Ladybug and Cat Noir — betraying them. Ironically, once he obtained the power he had always lacked, he didn't notice how he had become the very thing he had always despised. In this, however, lies his key difference from Chloé Bourgeois: she had always been immersed in privilege and power, and merely deluded herself into believing she had been deprived of what was rightfully hers. Félix, who had never known power, unconsciously repeated the mistakes of others upon seizing it — and became an oppressor himself, the very thing he had hated his entire life.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
In "Emotion", underneath all the coldness and selfishness, he harbors great hate and resentment towards everyone who uses their authority to repress the freedom of others, something that stems from the very abuse he endured at his father's hands. This caused him to desire a world where everyone can be free and live as they want, and he goes to great lengths to achieve it, including betraying those who trusted him as he did with Ladybug in "Strikeback" or creating a Sentimonster that allowed him to destroy anyone he wanted, using that to blackmail the heroes of Paris to give him their Miraculous. However, despite his pure intentions of creating a free world, he did not perceive that, by using his powers vengefully, he acted like those he hated, something that Ladybug pointed out when she compared him to Monarch in doing what they thought was right, but causing much more trouble than needed.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
His vision of a world without oppressors also includes the ones he sympathizes with, as he spares Adrien and Kagami Tsurugi, seeing them as equals who also experienced the same pain as him. He is even willing to spare the ones they care about or that he considered to be worthy of his envisioned world, like Marinette, the girl Adrien loves and Kagami's best friend who was able to prove herself worthy by showing how much she cared for Adrien, even being willing to crash an exclusive event like the Diamond's Dance. After seeing how upset they were by his actions and how he couldn't find Marinette, believing he accidentally erased her and was unable to bring her back, unlike everyone he hates, he started to realize the error of his ways and bring everyone else back.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
His hatred towards oppressors also blinded him, as Félix didn't understand the difference between an oppressor and authoritative figures such as Ladybug. However, when he saw the error of his ways, Argos began to understand that not all people want to be independent at least not right away, and some of them need others to guide them — for example, his cousin Adrien, who prefers to first ask for the opinions of everyone he knows: friends, father, girlfriend, and Nathalie, and only then make a decision, usually based on someone else's judgment. It's funny that before 'Emotion,' he considered Adrien to be just like him — a slave forced to obey — not realizing that Adrien holds the exact opposite stance and is completely fine with relying on someone else; moreover, he doesn't even view his father as an abusive figure.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
However, even while recognizing the flaws in his vision, he still stood by its virtues when he later separated Kagami from her mother because he didn't like seeing her being controlled (since she, unlike Adrien, does not want an authoritarian figure to lean on), and he protected her despite her rejection of his help, even breaking his own weapon to prevent her akumatized mother from finding her. This shows that he can be selfless towards those he cares about. Furthermore, according to Kagami, the fact that Félix, in the guise of Argos, spied on her and kidnapped her just to talk to her, as well as due to his own status as excluded, led her to believe that he lacks social skills.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
Unlike the recent Peacock Miraculous holders before him, he's shown to care very deeply for the sentimonsters that are created by its power, including his own, as he felt sorry for Strikeback and its clones when Ladybug and her team sent them to the sun, and when he realized the error of creating the Red Moon to satisfy his selfish desires, it caused him to act like his predecessors, leading him to free it from reality in great grief. Nevertheless, he despises the idea of calling sentimonsters "monsters" and prefers "sentibeings" instead.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
By the time of "Pretension", his escapade in "Emotion" had left him deeply scarred, yet it also gave him the very understanding he needed. He had never viewed sentimonsters merely as creatures created to do their creator's bidding — however, in "Emotion", he began to carry out his vengeance in service of his principles, likely too blinded by his own trauma. Having cast aside his hatred for humankind and his desire for revenge, he returned to his original beliefs, making them his priority: the creator must care for every being they bring into this world and guide them. That is precisely why he refused to create sentimonsters only to ultimately take their lives in the end.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
From the moment he snapped his fingers and erased everyone from the face of the earth, he finally gained that one trait that made him not just a random holder of the Peacock Miraculous, but a worthy and conscious one: perspective. He finally understood the weight of his and his family's actions. He didn't realize that when Shadow Moth and Mayura created the sentimonsters, only they treated them badly and ordered them to sow chaos, while the residents, by default, couldn't treat them well because they were terrified and deceived by them.
Felix forgot that Adrien doesn't know that he is a sentimonster, so Adrien was used along with Kagami for a revenge none of them even asked for. Then, upon realizing the situation with the Red Moon and painfully revoking it, he realized it was the same with Strikeback where the others didn't destroy them out of cruelty but mercy because they were out of options and understood that the creature was too dangerous.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
When it came to freedom, Félix was blinded by anger over its absence. After his father's death, he gained physical freedom, but not psychological and emotional freedom. He still hadn't fully let go of the situation or freed himself from his father's influence, which, among other things, led him to act the way he did in this episode. Aside from Paris, hardly anyone else including Felix knew what it was like to be terrorized by evil Miraculous holders. Adrien probably thought he had been akumatized, when in reality Félix was simply succumbing to the influence of his trauma. When he joyfully shouted about freedom (likely freedom from the control of sentimonsters in general, since there were no people left at all) in a completely empty world, from Adrien and Kagami's perspective, it looked as if he had finally lost his mind.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
When he explained his reasoning towards sentimonsters, his description also matched a baby being cared for by its parents. Given that almost immediately after that phrase he said he was talking about himself and Kagami, it's likely that with this statement he was referring not only to his frustration about how sentimonsters are treated in general, but also to his pain regarding his father's treatment of him, a father who never loved him.
As of "Representation", Félix changed dramatically. He was finally able to let go of most of his trauma, stopped hating people and blaming them for his troubles, and gave up the revenge and envy that had consumed him throughout seasons 3 and 4. Moreover, considering that he decided to share very personal information about his past with Marinette, he also worked on his trust issues.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Personality
He helped Kagami escape her mother, and when she told him Ladybug's secret identity, Félix was skeptical that such a naïve girl could be the superheroine with whom he had a very complicated relationship (well he made it so), but he accepted the truth. He was also very sympathetic towards Marinette as she was in a vulnerable state. He felt bad seeing her heart being broken from being separated from Adrien, but gently assured Duusu, his Kwami, that they were only doing this so that everyone will have a happy ending. So they baited Marinette to the school, where Félix revealed his tragic past, along with Gabriel revealed to be Monarch. With this information, Marinette was able to defeat Monarch once and for all in "Re-creation".
However, Felix realized he had a long way to go after everything was done. He still harbors guilt over what happened, which can be seen in "Yaksi Gozen." This further confirms that his personality has changed significantly since seasons 3-4, when he was capable of hurting others and seeking revenge without any remorse.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Abilities
As a Civilian
Félix is a master of magic tricks and a skilled pickpocket. He is also good at basketball, being able to score a basket while facing away from the hoop. According to Adrien Agreste, he is also skilled in martial arts, as seen in his debut episode when he was able to fight with Lady Wifi, Princess Fragrance and Reflekta simultaneously, as well as when he easily kicked Lady Wifi's tablet right out of her hand.
Félix demonstrates ingenuity and psychological flexibility as he tends to come up with creative solutions and resist external pressure. In "Risk", Félix returns to Paris with various high-tech devices to expose his uncle, such as a jammer to disable security cameras and open safes. His most used item is an eyepiece, resembling a monocle, with a red lens; it is capable of x-ray vision and detecting hidden details on objects, such as fingerprints.
In "Multiplication" it is revealed that he is a triple kung fu medalist, horse riding medalist, chess prodigy, and England's youngest graduate.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Abilities
Felix is remarkably adept at pretense and concealing his emotions. In addition to a strong sense of self-control, he is perfectly capable of defending himself. Nevertheless, when he is with people he trusts, such as Kagami or his mother, he drops the pretense and shows a more genuine part of himself.
As Argos
Argos has enhanced capabilities such as speed, agility, and strength, making him almost invulnerable to physical damage and able to jump and leap several times his height and length. He showed considerable hand-to-hand combat skills against more experienced combatants.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Abilities
Argos is able to infuse a feather plucked from his hand fan with his power, transforming it into an amok, and send it out to possess an object owned by a chosen target, with whom he can communicate telepathically. While he is communicating, a blue curved peacock mask appears in front of him and his target's faces. His actions will then give an emotion from his target a physical form of that person's choosing, which would act as the target's ally until recalled via a snap of his fingers, which will release it from existence. Using his power would drain his Miraculous's energy, forcing him to detransform after five minutes. But, in "Revelator" it is shown that Argos has learned to control his adult powers, allowing him to not detransform back and to use Amokization as much as he wishes.
Even if he didn't create them, Argos can either bring back to life dormant sentimonsters, or dispel any sentimonster by revoking their amoks.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Etymology
Félix was the original name of the Cat Noir character in the PV, who was later replaced by Adrien.
This character was discarded as Thomas Astruc believed Félix was not purposeful to the series, as he came off as an anime cliché, and no one was convinced his dynamic with Ladybug as a couple of heroes to be appropriate.
For a while, Thomas considered bringing Félix back at some point, but since then, he did not have intentions to use him, eventually outright stating that PV Félix will never appear.
Despite the fact that Félix as Cat Noir was scrapped, his design and name were reused to create Félix Fathom, Adrien's cousin. The most notable differences between the two are PV Félix's eye color being steely grey instead of green and his hair being combed in the opposite direction.
Félix's name was inspired by the Latin word for happy/lucky.
Félix's last name, Fathom, is an English word that, as a verb, means "to understand/comprehend". This fits his character, as Félix is always trying to understand everything around him.
Despite using his father's last name, Félix does prefer his mother's much better, finding it to be as noble, pretty and elegant as her.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Etymology
His name Flairmidable is a combination of "Flair" (meaning style, poise or finesse) or the French word "flairer" (sniffing, smelling) and "Formidable" (meaning great, talented or mighty).
Félix having the Dog Miraculous and Adrien having the Cat Miraculous symbolize their counterpart dynamic with cats and dogs often being considered opposites.
Interestingly, both boys possess traits of the other's Miraculous animal, as Félix is shown to be solitary and self-centered (traits associated to cats), while Adrien is faithful and loves being with his friends (traits associated to dogs).
Argos is named after the Greek myth of Argus Panoptes, a hundred-eyed giant whose eyes were placed into the feathers of the peacock by Hera after his death.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Trivia
Miraculous Holder
Félix is the first occasional superhero to not return a Miraculous after a mission.
The third not wanting to return the Miraculous following Alya Césaire and Chloé Bourgeois.
The second to use it for selfish reasons following Chloé.
Thanks to Félix, Gabriel had access to almost all the Miraculous in the Chinese Miracle Box.
The only Miraculouses Félix didn't give to Gabriel in their exchange are the Peacock Miraculous (which Félix owns from the exchange), the Ladybug Miraculous, and the Cat Miraculous. However, Gabriel would end up having the Rabbit Miraculous taken from him by Canigirl in "Evolution".
According to Félix himself, despite he saw helping his uncle steal the Miraculous as a necessity to retrieve the Peacock Miraculous to secure his own existence and prevent its power from being abused, he does regret to have done it, as he knows how evil his uncle really is., which is shown in "Yaksi Gozen", when he regretfully points out to Marinette Dupain-Cheng that her previous loss of all the other Miraculouses wasn't her fault, while turning away in shame.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Trivia
This regret, together with his desire to free Adrien and Kagami Tsurugi, may have been the catalyst for his decision to create Red Moon and use it to either force Ladybug and Cat Noir to give him their Miraculous so he can have his wish for a free world granted or use his sentimonster to transform it.
Following Dark Grimalkin, his aunt and cousin, Félix is the fourth known person of English origins to wield a Miraculous.
Through his father, he is the eighth person from the Western Hemisphere to wield a Miraculous following Micazoyolin, Gilbert du Motier, La Mariquita, his father, Alya, Jessica Keynes and Zoé Lee.
Similar to Zoé due to his American origins, he is also the first known person from the Western Hemisphere to wield the Dog and the second known person to wield the Peacock Miraculous after his father.
He is the fourth known sentimonster to use a Miraculous, after Adrien, Kagami and Sentinino.
As of "Re-creation", He becomes the first member of the French Miraculous superhero team to use a Miraculous originally to be a supervillain and later use it to become a hero.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Trivia
He also becomes the seventh member of the French Miraculous superhero team to use another Miraculous. The first is Marinette with the Mouse, Fox, Cat, Dragon, Bee, Horse, Rabbit and Butterfly Miraculouses, the second is Adrien with the Ladybug, Snake and Rabbit Miraculouses, the third one is Master Fu with the Turtle and Peacock Miraculouses, the fourth one is Alya with the Ladybug Miraculous, the fifth one is Alix with the Dog Miraculous and the sixth one is Zoé with the Cat Miraculous.
He is also the only member of the French Miraculous superhero team who has not yet been officially akumatized/kamikotized. Since he rejected his akumatization in "Gabrel Agreste" before he had officially become an akumatized villain.
He is so far the most recent member of the French Miraculous superhero team to meet/interact with Lila/Cerise in "Strikeback".

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Trivia
Besides his need to secure his own existence and prevent its power from being abused, the other reason for Félix to want to possess the Peacock Miraculous is its importance to him due to its role in his family's history. The fact it was used by his father to create him and also was used by his aunt to create Adrien, he considers the Peacock Miraculous as part of the legacy of the Graham de Vanily family and, similar to his mother regarding the Graham de Vanily Twin Rings, couldn't just stand watching someone like his uncle use its power.
Currently, thirteen characters know Félix is Argos: Gabriel, Adrien, Marinette, André, Audrey, Chloé, Tomoe, Kagami, Ali, Soraya, Amélie, Nathalie and Cerise.
Gabriel always knew that Félix was now in possession of the Peacock Miraculous when they made an exchange in "Strikeback".
Adrien, Marinette, André, Audrey, Chloé, Tomoe, Kagami, Ali, Soraya and Amélie discovered or showed that they knew his identity in "Emotion".
Nathalie showed knowledge when she overheard Gabriel and Tomoe's conversation in the former's lair in "Pretension".
Cerise planned on using him as a spy in The Miraculers.

title: Félix Fathom
categories: Members of Graham de Vanily family
text:
Félix Fathom - Trivia
Many unidentified civilians were shown to have knowledge of his identity when he revealed himself in public in "Emotion". However, as Félix was posing as Adrien at that time, it is unknown if they know the full truth of what happened and if that is really Félix.
This makes Félix the third character to have the most characters knowing his superhero identity, following Chloé and Alix.
Due to the nature of his superpower, Amokization, allowing him to create a sentimonster that can last after he had detransformed, it's unknown if Félix, as Argos, managed to unlock his adult superpowers or if he, like the rest of the Miraculers in "Revelator", had to be taught by Ladybug and Cat Noir.
Considering he is not seen training with the others, it's very possible that he had already unlocked his adult powers, making him (possibly) the third of the Miraculers to do so, after Ladybug and Cat Noir.
However, if he had to train as well, it's unknown if he went to create a Sentimonster to start the countdown for his detransformation, considering his reservation to do so unless extremely necessary.

In the Season 6 opening, Argos briefly appears with blue eyes, it's unclear if this is an animation error.
Félix and Kagami are the second couple to learn each other's secret identities, after Alya and Nino in "Catalyst", and Marc and Nathaniel later in "The Ruler".
Félix is ​​the only member of the French Miraculous superhero team who has never been fully akumatized, but if alternative timelines don't count, the same can be said for Adrien.
Miscellaneous

He is the third person to resist akumatization, following Chloé and Alya.
He is the second person chronologically to discover Gabriel's identity as Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch, after Nathalie Sancoeur.

As seen when Ladybug reads his Wikipage in "Multiplication", Félix's birthday is either February 12th or December 2nd

Before "Representation", there've been hints suggesting that Félix is a Sentimonster:
Félix proved to be interested in the Graham de Vanily Twin Rings, which are later revealed to be containing Adrien's amok.
He was said to be after "a piece of jewelry" and was willing to make an exchange.

Félix Fathom - Trivia
In "Pretension", Félix claims that sentimonsters should not be called "monsters". Also, he said that whenever a living being is bring to Earth, the progenitor/creator is responsible to show the meaning of the life and their existence, and when asked by Kagami if he was talking about himself, he told her he was talking about both of them, hinting that Kagami is a sentibeing too.

title: Félix's ring
text:
Félix's ring - Intro
Félix's ring is a ring that Félix always carries on his right ring finger.
In "Emotion", Félix replaces temporarily his ring for another (a replica of his cousin's) which he uses as an amokized object to control Red Moon and receive its power and to pass unnoticed when he pretended to be Adrien during the Diamonds Dance.
In "Representation", this ring is revealed to contain the amok that was used to create Félix. At the time, the ring was in the possession of Colt Fathom. His brother-in-law Gabriel Agreste lent him the Peacock Miraculous in exchange for the employment of Placide I.T..
However, Colt fell ill, due to using the damaged Peacock Miraculous, causing Colt to use the ring to control his son like a puppet and passed away after roughly fourteen or fifteen years. After that, Félix took the ring, thus gaining his free will and has always carried it ever since.

title: Félix's ring
text:
Félix's ring - Intro
In "Yaksi Gozen", Félix considered giving his ring to Ladybug for safekeeping in her magical yo-yo to prevent it from being stolen or destroyed. However, due to Adrien briefly losing it after doing magic tricks on it and the titular villain's akumatization. Kagami picked it up and returned it to Félix, who decided to keep his amok.

title: Félix's ring
text:
Félix's ring - Appearance
Felix's ring is strikingly similar to the Cat Miraculous when worn by Adrien in its camouflage mode. Its silver color and shape are the same, and the only differences are that the center is a square and has three groove lines on each side.
In "Representation", it is revealed that there was once a crack on it.

title: Félix's ring
text:
Félix's ring - Trivia
As seen in "Representation", Félix's ring, when it used to belong to his father, got cracked when the latter hit it with too much force during a fit of rage, causing pain to the former. Because the ring is seen without a crack, it can be assumed that it was fixed later on.
In "Yaksi Gozen", Adrien briefly gets a hold of Félix's ring and unknowningly briefly controlled Félix with it, by first asking the latter to open up his hand to show Kagami's ring on it and later convincing Félix that there's nothing to worry about, which made an angry Félix to suddenly become relaxed and to agree with Adrien's statement.
Also, unknown to them, this also saved Félix from having his Amok stolen by Chrysalis, who along with Tomoe Tsurugi, wanted to use it to force Félix to become their spy among The Miraculers.

title: Fu's gramophone/Movie
text:
Fu's gramophone/Movie - Intro
Fu's gramophone is a gramophone that Wang Fu uses to hold the Chinese Miracle Box.

title: Fu's gramophone/Movie
text:
Fu's gramophone/Movie - Appearance
The gramophone is made out of dark brown wood with a bronze horn. The horn has floral designs carved inside it. The sides of the gramophone make in octagonal-shaped and has autumn trees and nature designs on all sides except for the front. The front side has 2 metal dragons facing each other with their teeth over a rectangle-shaped object with the words "奇迹" on it. The Miracle Box is likely to be held in the bottom part, which is dark brown with grass stuffed inside the space between wood. It stands on 8 small dark wood feet.

title: Fu's gramophone/Movie
text:
Fu's gramophone/Movie - Abilities
The gramophone used as a storage space to hold the Miracle Box when the guardian is not handing out the Miraculouses. In order to get to the Miracle Box, the person first must touch the dragons' eyes on the front of the gramophone. The dragons' eyes will turn red, the mouths will open wider, dropping the rectangle-shaped object, revealing a keypad. The person then must enter the code. When entered, the whole top part of the gramophone will turn. The part with the horn will then fall back, and 2 wooden doors will slide open, revealing the Miracle Box, as it rises. To close the gramophone, put the Miracle Box back in it, and either the person would close the lid and the gramophone will adjust back to the way it was, or the gramophone would close on its own.

title: Fu's gramophone/Movie
text:
Fu's gramophone/Movie - Trivia
On the gramophone, the word "奇迹" is Chinese for "Miracle".

The saddle had expanded and merged with a green fairing with two large frog eyes, one on each side in the back.

title: Gabriel's lair
text:
Gabriel's lair - Intro
was a room or observatory located inside the Agreste mansion. Here Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch used to stored many white butterflies that, once corrupted, would become akumas and megakumas, which he used to akumatize his victims.
In "The Collector", the lair is revealed to be connected to Gabriel's atelier in the Agreste mansion by a pathway. On the portrait of Émilie Agreste, there is a pattern of buttons Gabriel pressed to get to the lair.
In "Miraculous London", after Gabriel's death, Bug Noir and Nathalie destroyed all evidence linking Gabriel to his identity as a Monarch, and Bug Noir destroyed the access to the crypt, leaving the lair abandoned and inaccessible.

title: Gabriel's lair
text:
Gabriel's lair - Appearance
The room is large, dome-like, and dark when Gabriel Agreste as villain Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch is not using an akuma. It has a large window with a butterfly (or flower) design that opens whenever Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch plans to send an akuma to a person who feels strong negative emotions. In the back of the room, a circular shape is on the ground, which Gabriel stands on to travel between the Agreste mansion and his lair.
Once a villain gets defeated, the window closes, encasing the room in darkness once again.
Throughout the season 5, there were kwami cages which became a temporary home for Kwamis. In "Destruction", Gabriel installed a special device in the lair, which transported the Miraculouses to the Rings. In "Pretension", Gabriel installed a special healing couch with wires, absorbing the Kwamis' powers and restoring his health after the impact of Cataclysm on him. In "Conformation", during Monarch's final plan, he installed a control table with cables that were attached to the Kwamis cage. In "Miraculous London", after Natalie revealed all of Gabriel's secrets and released the Kwamis, Bug Noire destroyed the Kwami cage and the lair remained empty.

Gabriel's atelier - Intro
was one of the former offices of Gabriel Agreste and the office of Nathalie Sancoeur in the Agreste mansion.

title: Gabriel's atelier
text:
Gabriel's atelier - Appearance
Gabriel's atelier is a large room with black and white tile flooring in a diagonal checkerboard pattern. The room semi-funnels down to the center, where there is a large rectangular glass block that is purely architectural. On three sides there are magenta seats, with a very light yellow edge. The doors leading into the atelier have white grilles, with openings between them.
Right side
On the right side of the room, there is a large golden-framed collage of photos of Adrien Agreste. Each photo has a white frame, with six photos in all. At the left end of the wall, small doors enclose a set of storage shelves. The doors into the room are to the right of the gold frame. To the right of that, Nathalie's work desk sticks out of the wall; she sits behind it in the corner of the room when using it.
Back
The back wall has two large windows with a white grille. The windows have black drapes that are hung partially closed. Between the windows is a painted image of Émilie Agreste, done in the style of Gustav Klimt's Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I. Directly in front of the painting is a large touchscreen monitor, with a white backing and stand.
Left side

title: Gabriel's atelier
text:
Gabriel's atelier - Appearance
The left wall has three display alcoves lit from above from black semi-dome shaped overhangs. Each alcove houses a women's-fashion-related sculpture that is white with black adornments, with a matching white etched drawing on a black back wall. Vertical black and white stripe wall patterns separate the alcoves.
During security lockdown, as seen in "Simon Says", the three sculptures and back-wall drawings recede from view, downward and upward respectively, exposing eight security viewscreens on the wall in each alcove.
Front
On the front wall are two windows similarly styled to the back windows but without drapes. The wall also is black and white, with vertical stripes. There is an additional angled wall between the front and left sides of the room, with a large, unframed black-and-white photo of Adrien above four smaller color photos of him in golden frames.

title: Gabriel's atelier
text:
Gabriel's atelier - Trivia
Behind the painting of Émilie Agreste, Gabriel hides a safe in the wall. That box contains the Peacock Miraculous, a book about Tibet, a ticket to Tibet, rolled-up pieces of old paper, and the Grimoire, the latter being stolen by Adrien in "Volpina" and eventually ending up in Marinette's hands.
With that ticket it's likely Gabriel was referring to Tibet as his oversea trip mentioned in "The Collector".
In "Gabriel Agreste", it's revealed that he also keeps Adrien's drawing which he broke in "The Collector", although it's unknown why he started keeping it there, and not in the cabinet like he used to.
The touchscreen monitor in the room can control the security system, which sets the entire Agreste mansion on lockdown, as seen in "Simon Says".
The painting has a hidden mechanism that turns on a hidden lift that leads to Gabriel's lair when he presses specific buttons on the painting.
As seen in "Werepapas", after Gabriel's death, the room has become abandoned with its lights turned off and the furniture, monitor and sculptures are covered in white sheets and the painting of Émilie was removed. It is also the place where Milly Graham de Vanily was akumatized by Chrysalis.
