Exterior
The exterior is an inwardly sloping dome with slate silver fishscale tiles. There are also several white lines running vertically down amongst the tiles.
On the edges are metal gutters around the base of the dome with a semicircular window on either side. A short white overhang, a white grill, and green metal gates circling the area are included for decoration.
Interior

title: Marinette's room
text:
Marinette's room - Appearance
The interior of the room has cream pink wallpaper with no distinct designs. The floor is made up of a series of overlapping dark oak rectangular tiles. In the center of the room is a circular pink rug with a black and pink flower design running along the edges. The room is entered through a wooden trapdoor which has a dark oak border around a birch center. Upon entering her room, there is a chaise longue to the right. Its upholstery is pink with white polka dots, and it includes a white wooden frame and white triangular legs. Its back is curved and is burgundy with a white border on the outside, while the interior has wide pale pink and lighter pink stripes with thinner burgundy stripes. On either arm of the chair is a burgundy armrest. Resting near the back is a burgundy throw pillow with thick pink edges. A cherry-red paper umbrella rests against the chair. There is also a desk that has her computer, books, a jewelry box, a brown and white stuffed animal, pens in a cup, sewing machine and a black and gold box; on the wall is her cork board. A dressform and a full-sized mirror are situated near a set of white stairs with black railings beside Marinette's desk.

title: Marinette's room
text:
Marinette's room - Appearance
The stairs lead up to a loft above Marinette's desk, where she has a bed that has pink sheets with two thin black lines running down the middle. The top is black with two thick pink lines through it. Above, there is a pink pillow adorned with a bow decal and a large pink and brown cat pillow. The fitted sheet is dark magenta. Above her bed is a small shelf with books and a cube-shaped nightlight. The skylight door to her balcony is above her bed. At the edge underneath her bed is a large pull-down chart of Adrien Agreste's schedule.

title: Marinette's room
text:
Marinette's room - Trivia
The room resembles an attic, as it is entered through a trapdoor rather than a normal door.
However, one piece of concept art in The Art of Miraculous depicts the room as having both a trapdoor and a normal door. It's unknown whether both were meant to be used for entering or one of them was meant to be used to enter another room.
From Season 6 onwards, Marinette's room features more decorations reflecting her Chinese heritage, such as traditional lanterns, teapots, chinaware and Guó huà (国画) paintings.
Marinette has a huge striped pink and brown stuffed toy cat on her bed, behind her pillow, as seen in multiple episodes.
It's also mentioned in one of the Instagram posts from her account.
Marinette has photos of Adrien in her room, although they are seen only in certain episodes.
The framed picture of Adrien on Marinette's desk is also the first picture of him seen on Alya's new cellphone when she shows it to Marinette in "Lady Wifi".
Marinette takes down her photos of Adrien in "Gamer" before Adrien arrives.
Cat Noir enters Marinette's room in "The Puppeteer". However, he does not see Marinette's photos of his civilian self.

title: Marinette's room
text:
Marinette's room - Trivia
Cat Noir enters Marinette's room again in "Troublemaker" and sees the photos of his civilian self, but when Ladybug sees this happening, she hides the photos from him in embarrassment.
From "Gang of Secrets" onwards, there are pieces of fabric (or paper) pasted on the window, probably to keep her guardian identity secret.
During the first three seasons, Marinette is shown with three different sewing machines.
The first one is metallic-golden and appears in the backgrounds of most episodes.
Interestingly, even in episodes where another one appears, it can be seen in the background, while the other one appears when Marinette is using it. This is probably because the this machine is part of the room's model.
The second one is white and appears in "Mr. Pigeon" and "Prime Queen".
The third one is white and pink and first appears in "Christmaster", "Gamer 2.0" and "The Puppeteer 2". From Season 4 onwards, it becomes the main sewing machine and is seen in all episodes instead of the metallic one.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
is one of the two titular main protagonists (alongside Adrien Agreste) of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir and Miraculous World. She is a former student in Miss Bustier's class at Collège Françoise Dupont in Paris, France, and a budding fashion designer who wants to have her own brand one day. She is currently in a relationship with Adrien Agreste.
With the Ladybug Miraculous, when inhabited by Tikki, Marinette transforms into the superhero Ladybug, who gains the power of Creation. She is tasked with keeping Paris safe from akumatized villains and many other threats. She is also the leader of The Miraculers.
In "Syren", after Wang Fu translated the Grimoire to find a way to give Ladybug and Cat Noir the ability to transform into different powered-up forms, he was able to make the potion that grants the aqua form. Marinette is able to use it to become Aquabug, which gives her a specially modified aqua suit with fins on her feet, granting her enhanced swimming capabilities, as well as allowing her to breathe and speak underwater.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Frozer" when the titular akumatized supervillain froze over Paris to turn the city into his domain, Marinette used Wang Fu's Magicaroons to transform into Lady Ice, which gives her a specially modified ice suit with skates on her feet, granting her enhanced skating capabilities as well as allowing her to withstand subzero temperatures.
In "Reflekdoll", when Plagg accidentally brought the Cat Miraculous to an unrecognizable Marinette transformed by Reflekta, she temporarily used it and became Lady Noire, a black cat-themed superheroine with the power of Destruction.
In "Kwamibuster", after the titular akumatized supervillain captured Tikki, Marinette took multiple other Miraculouses, but only activated the Mouse Miraculous to become Multimouse, a mouse-themed superheroine with the power of Multiplication. In the same episode, Multimouse's various copies were able to transform when the Mouse Miraculous was combined with the Ladybug, Cat, and Fox Miraculous in order to become Multibug, Multinoire, and Multifox respectively.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Feast", after successfully defeating the titular sentimonster controlled by Hawk Moth and Mayura, Wang Fu began to train Marinette in order to pass off his title as "Master" onto her, and appoint her as the new Guardian of the Miraculouses.
In "Ladybug", after being expelled from school due to being framed by Lila Rossi, she was almost akumatized by Scarlet Moth into Princess Justice. However, her akumatization was interrupted after Scarlet Moth de-transformed to aid Catalyst, who had begun to suffer from an illness inflicted by the damaged Peacock Miraculous.
In "Miracle Queen", after the titular akumatized supervillain brainwashed the temporary Miraculous holders to be her slaves, Marinette unified the Dragon Miraculous with the Ladybug Miraculous, becoming Dragon Bug. Following Miracle Queen's defeat, Marinette officially became the new Guardian of the Miraculouses after Master Fu relinquished his role as Guardian.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Miraculous World: New York - United Heroez", after Xavier Ramier was re-akumatized into Mr. Pigeon for the 51st time, Ladybug became Cosmobug to stop Mr. Pigeon from taking over the moon for him and his pigeons. Cosmobug has the power to travel long distances swiftly via flight, including in space.
In "Gang of Secrets", after defeating the titular akumatized supervillain group with help from Rena Rouge, who rejected her akumatization into Lady Wifi, Marinette was finally able to confide in her friends and apologize for not telling them what was wrong with her. However, when Alya stayed behind to learn the whole truth, Marinette confessed to her that she was Ladybug.
In "Mr. Pigeon 72", after defeating Mr. Pigeon for the 72nd time with help from Plagg and Rena Rouge, Rena helped Ladybug expand the limits of her power. She now transforms into a new costume whenever she uses Lucky Charm (and reverts when she uses Miraculous Ladybug), and gains the ability to create Magical Charms that are able to protect people from being reakumatized.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Optigami", in order to immobilize Style Queen, Marinette unified the Bee Miraculous with the Ladybug Miraculous in order to become Lady Bee. It is also revealed that Alya is Marinette's heir presumptive to the Miracle Box and the role of the Guardian of the Miraculous.
In "Sentibubbler", in order to free herself from the bubble that the titular sentimonster put her in and to take the amokized coffee cup Shadow Moth was using to control him, Marinette unified the Horse Miraculous with the Ladybug Miraculous to become Pegabug.
In "Strikeback", after mistakenly believing Félix to be Adrien, Marinette unified the Ladybug, Horse, and Rabbit Miraculouses, becoming Pennybug, to reach him in the train and travel in time to figure out Risk's akumatized item. However, the mistake of giving a Miraculous to Félix resulted in him betraying her. He stole her yo-yo and gave it to his uncle Gabriel Agreste in exchange for the Peacock Miraculous, causing him to obtain all the Miraculous in the Chinese Miracle Box, except for Cat Noir's and hers.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Miraculous Paris", in order to counter Monarch's trap, Ladybug formulated a plan that involved the creation of two kamikotized heroes. After Betterfly kamikotized Alya into Ubiquity, he lent his Miraculous to Ladybug, who fused it with her Ladybug Miraculous to become Ladyfly in order to kamikotize Gabriel Agreste into Guardian Angel. Later, when Monarch threatened to invade other universes to get the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses, Ladybug allowed Betterfly to kamikotize her into Ladybiquity, gaining similar powers to Ubiquity to stop Monarch from going into other worlds.
In "Passion", to avoid detection by Safari's venom bolts, Marinette temporarily used the Cat Miraculous and once again became Lady Noire.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Reunion", when in need of advice regarding the possibility of a romantic relationship with Cat Noir, Marinette learned that the true purpose of the kwagatama she received from Tikki was to access the memories of past holders of the Ladybug Miraculous, thereby allowing her to commune with them. Using it on a seal of the Order of the Guardians left on a statue of a past Ladybug Miraculous holder, Marinette came in contact with Jeanne d'Arc, a past holder of the Ladybug Miraculous who fell in love with the Cat Miraculous holder of her time.
In "Elation", after Cat Noir didn't return Marinette's love for him, fearing he was taking advantage of her as she didn't know his true identity, she was nearly akumatized by Monarch into Unmasker. However, her akumatization was interrupted by a kiss from Cat Noir, causing her desire to override her anger and heartbreak and release the akuma.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Derision", when Marinette returned to the spot of her first heartbreak during her first real date with Adrien, it triggered her traumatic memories of Chloé's bullying from the previous school year, leading her to have a severe panic attack and once again nearly be akumatized by Monarch, now into Panic. However, she rejected her akumatization when she fully understood what happened in her past and made peace with it thereafter.
In "Revolution", after seeing all the Parisians willingly stand up and fight injustice with their own hands and refuse to turn their backs on Ladybug and Cat Noir, Marinette evolved her powers, allowing her to use Lucky Charms as many times as she wants and not de-transform after using them. After Adrien told Marinette he had to leave Paris, despite being devastated, she refused to break her promise to him and raced to the airport, where both finally shared their first kiss before being forcibly separated and watching his plane take off. When Chloé called her to taunt her about it, Marinette finally snapped at her and told her she was powerless, leaving the former in tears.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Representation", when following Félix, believing him to be Adrien, to the school's art room, she discovered through Félix and Kagami's play the backstories of the Graham de Vanily, Fathom, and Agreste families, and that Adrien and his cousin are sentimonsters.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "The Final Day", Ladybug went to the Agreste mansion to talk to Nathalie, but encountered Monarch. She then finally discovered that Gabriel Agreste was Monarch, came face to face in battle with him, and unified the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses to become Bug Noire. She finally defeated Monarch, but was paralyzed by him when she de-transformed to persuade him to give up, allowing him to take the two Miraculouses. He used them to summon Gimmi and make his wish, sacrificing himself in order to be reunited with his wife and heal Nathalie. Following this, she recovered all of the Miraculouses, restored them to their previous forms, and permanently gave them to her allies, ensuring that a supervillain couldn't steal them all again. However, not wanting to hurt Adrien with the terrible truth, she told him and the whole world a lie, claiming that Gabriel sacrificed himself as a hero to stop Monarch. Moreover, Marinette was unable to recover the Butterfly Miraculous as unbeknownst to her, Cerise Bianca managed to get her hands on it and planned to use it for revenge.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Miraculous London", after transforming again into Bug Noire upon thinking Nathalie was still on Monarch's side, she used Cataclysm to destroy the Kwami cage as well as the The Crypt to make sure Adrien wouldn't find out the truth about the fate of his parents. She then flew to London as Cosmobugnoire to free him and Kagami, and lie to him about Gabriel and Monarch. Later, Bunnyx recruited her to help stop a dangerous wish from being granted and save the timeline. Marinette used the Ladybug Miraculous from the past (the only time she had renounced her Miraculous and it had no holder) to become Chronobug, a different version of her usual Ladybug identity in order for Alix to distinguish her from any of Ladybug's past selves. After several attempts to stop Timestalker, she finally saved the universe when Timestalker gave up.
In "Sleeping Syren", after Ryuko was turned into a water guard by the villain's own water guard and dropped her Miraculous, Marinette temporarily used the Dragon Miraculous and once again became Dragon Bug. While using the Aqua power-up at the same time, she also became Aquadragonbug.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Mister Agreste", feeling consumed by the burden of the secret of Gabriel being Monarch, Ladybug ventured to Brazil to borrow the Snake Miraculous from Luka and unify it with her Ladybug Miraculous, becoming Viperbug in order to tell Luka the truth and ask him for advice.
In "The Dark Castle", in order to allow Alix to enjoy her birthday with her family and friends, Marinette decided to temporarily take hold of the Rabbit Miraculous in order to watch over the timeline and keep it and the Miraculous safe, unifying it with her Ladybug Miraculous to become Bunnybug. Later in the episode, in order to go face the titular villain without leaving the Burrow unattended, she summoned her future self (from later that day) and gave her the Rabbit Miraculous, allowing her to become Bunnynette, a rabbit-themed superhero with the power of Evolution.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Heartfixer", after the Couplewreckers tricked Adrien into believing that Marinette was cheating on him with Nino, Adrien broke up with her. Falling into despair, Marinette was akumatized by Chrysalis into Heartfixer, a supervillain who wanted to mend Adrien's broken heart and win back his love. Adrien discovered the truth and reassured Marinette of his love for her, bringing her to her senses and giving her the power to reject the akuma before she could do any more damage.
In "The Chained Titans", troubled by a friendly dispute about potential future hamster names between Adrien and Marinette, Nino believed that he could strengthen their relationship by allowing them to become temporary superheroes together. As Alya's stand-in, Marinette temporarily used the Fox Miraculous. When inhabited by Trixx, she became Renardette, a fox-themed superheroine with the power of Illusion.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Secret Protocol", after suspecting that her great uncle, Wang Cheng, was the new holder of the Butterfly Miraculous in disguise, she briefly removed her Miraculous and had Tikki give it to Alya so she was not suspected to be Ladybug. After Wang's akumatization, Sabine got a call from Fei and it was revealed that Wang never left Shanghai. She realized that the visiting Wang was in fact an impostor and might have been the new Butterfly Miraculous holder. Realizing that her secret identity put them in danger, Marinette revealed to her parents that she is Ladybug.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Intro
In "Nemesis", in order to discover the identity of the Butterfly Miraculous holder, Marinette had Alya create an illusion of her and had Rooster Bold make it possible to touch the illusion without making it disappear. The illusion pretended to feel betrayed by Alya and was akumatized by Chrysalis into Nemesis, a supervillain capable of turning anyone to stone. At the end of the episode, Marinette's friendship with Alya was damaged after Alya deduced that Gabriel Agreste was Monarch. After having a heart-to-heart with Adrien, Marinette felt crushed for having to lie to him, and is considering breaking up with him if she doesn't find the courage to tell him the truth about his father being Monarch.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Marinette is a teenage girl with a slender body. She stands at average height, and is quarter-French and quarter-Italian (both by her father's side) and half-Chinese (by her mother's side).
She has a fair skin tone followed by shoulder-length black hair with blue reflections that is always seen tied back in pigtails, which have a thin strand stick out above on either side. According to the "Miraculous Secrets card game", Marinette "wears her 2 pigtails in memory of a very good friend from school who is sadly no longer at her school" and "Derision" confirms that this "very good friend" is Socqueline Wang.
Marinette also has light pink lips, bright bluebell eyes, and light freckles on both sides and the bridge of her nose. Her bangs are swept to the left, and her thin forelocks frame her face. She has light scarlet lipstick.
In "Cat Blanc", "Heart Hunter", "Determination" and "Derision", when Marinette has her hair down, the full length of her hair reaches down to her shoulders, making her hair shoulder length.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
In "Reflekta" (pictured), "Animaestro", "Kwamibuster", "Derision", "Emotion", "Revolution","Representation", and "Werepapas", Marinette has her hair in a bun.
From Season 6 onwards, her hair appears to be more detailed with more strands. Her eyes are more cyan.
Civilian Attire
In the first five seasons, Marinette wore a very dark gray blazer with rolled-up sleeves; the inside of the blazer was lined in white with light fuchsia polka dots, and it had black trimming. Underneath, she wore a white t-shirt with black stitching and a flower-shaped design below the collar at the right. The design itself had pink flowers and black leaves. She wore pink rolled-up loose jeans with a circular button on the middle of the waistline, that had matching insides like her blazer and light pink ballet flats with reddish brown soles, and said flats had thin black edges at the top and bottom, with a small black knotted ribbon on the toe.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
She also sports black circular earrings with silver lining that serve as her Miraculous when Tikki inhabits them. She often wore a light pink purse over her right shoulder. The purse had white polka-dots and a golden clasp. The inside was red, and on one side, there was a light pink, white, and black flowery design, with an 'M' initial inside of a circle. Connected to both sides of her purse was a black cord strap. She also wore her Kwagatama necklace under her t-shirt. She held her pigtails with red hair ties.
In "Reflekta" (pictured) and a flashback in "Derision", Marinette wore light blue jeans instead of her current pink ones. The change is because Chloé Bourgeois made her favorite blue jeans covered in green paint as part of a prank in the school year prior to the show's events.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
From Season 6 onwards, Marinette's blazer has pink lining on the collar and a matching Sakura print adjacent to either side, with similar floral designs at the top and bottom as black stem accents form an 'M' in the middle, the blazer's insides lined with pink at the rolled up sleeves with pink circular studs. Underneath, her shirt has a small black bow formed in the middle with matching frilled trim. Her jeans are replaced by high-waisted pink denim shorts which are rolled up, but much higher to the thigh with the inside patterns inverted in color, and the button on the waistline is a pink Sakura flower. She now also wears glittery gray tights and her ballet flats are pink with short black heels, toe caps, soles, and edges at the top and bottom, with a small bow on the toe. Her earrings are now a glittery dark red. The purse now has a different shade of pink and a new flower design, while the cord is dark burgundy. Her hair ties are now pink.
As Ladybug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
In the first five seasons, Ladybug wore a red superhero bodysuit covered in black spots, with a black collar/turtleneck. According to Marinette in "Marinette's Double Life", her suit was made out of indestructible fabric. When not in use, she kept her yo-yo around her hips with a red string. On her face was a red mask with five black spots that were in a symmetrical design, and the waterlines of her eyes were colored black. Her earrings were red with five black spots in a quincunx pattern, and the bands holding her hair back became red ribbons, resembling a ladybug's antennas or a ladybug flying when she's moving. Her suit had a hexagonal pattern.
Modified Suit

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
As of "Mr. Pigeon 72", when Ladybug used her Lucky Charm, most of her costume remained the same and bore some resemblance to Mister Bug's costume, except she had solid black coloring on her hands, the bottom of her feet, her waist to upper thighs, and armpits where the spots were inverted. Her collar switched from completely black to swan-necked and red with black lining and a small ladybug-shaped zipper connected to the front of her costume similar to Cat Noir's bell. Her pigtails and hair ribbons became longer and gained a pair of blue ribbons, but after using her Miraculous Ladybug, she reverted back to her normal appearance.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
From Season 6 onwards, Ladybug keeps her modified suit permanently as her normal appearance, but it has minor alterations. Her pigtails no longer have the blue ribbons, but remain long and now have a dark red ombré at the tips. The black sections of her outfit also lose the spots in them, with the armpit sections extending to the front of the shoulders with a single inverted dot in front of them. Said sections also connect to the waist and thigh sections in a wide, wavy, vertical fashion with another inverted dot in the middle adjacent to the torso on either side. Around the hips are thick red linear sections with a circular part at the end on either side with a black dot in the middle. The ends of the black sections at the thighs also curve down more above the knees with an inverted dot in the middle, and her earrings gain some glitter. Her yo-yo now appears to be magnetically clipped to her hip rather than tied around her waist with its string.
As Lady Noire
The costume of Lady Noire was very similar to Cat Noir; she wore a dark gray catsuit with fluorescent green accents on her knees, forearms, waist, and neck.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
She had black gloves on her forearms with claws and a fluorescent green band that went down a bit and a black ball, and her black collar was a little open at the neck and had a fluorescent green band that went down to the poitrine and a black ball in the lower part of the neck. Around the waist, there was a black belt with a fluorescent green band in the middle at the right leg, a black button with a fluorescent green cat paw-shaped symbol to resemble the Cat Miraculous' symbol, and two parts of the band jutting out below with a black ball hanging at the end.
Her black boots with upward pointed fluorescent green lining went all the way up to the knee, with a small flowing green band in the heel, and ended with small black triangular platform shoes. She had floor-length black hair that was styled in a single braid, which made it look like a tail (similar to Cat Noir's belt). She also had black cat ears on her head with fluorescent green lining and a black mask. Lady Noire had the same green eyes as Cat Noir, with the green sclera and slitted pupils.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Like her yo-yo, Lady Noire kept her staff attached to her hip when not in use. She also wore the ring around her right ring finger like Cat Noir.
As Multimouse
Multimouse wore a gray bodysuit. She wore her hair in Oodango-styled twin buns, which resembled mouse ears, held by pink hair bands with part of them sticking out above adjacent to either bun. She also wore her Miraculous, a coin pendant, around her neck. Her mask was gray at the top and pink with a black border at the sides. She wore black gloves that were a little above her elbows and had a thick pink upward pointed horizontal stripe at the end and matching knee-high boots.
Around her waist was her skip rope that resembles a mouse's tail.
As Multifox
Multifox essentially looked the same as Multimouse, but all the pink accents on Multimouse became orange, and she had a white section on her chest similar to Rena Rouge as a result of the Fox Miraculous' influence worn around her neck. Her hair bands and skip rope become orange as well.
As Multibug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Multibug essentially looked the same as Multimouse, but her suit gained black spots on the grey part, and all the pink accents on Multimouse became red as a result of the Ladybug Miraculous' influence worn on her ears. Her mask also got five black spots that were in a symmetrical design, and the pink section became red. Her hair bands and skip rope are turned red as well.
As Multinoire
Multinoire essentially looked the same as Multimouse, but all the pink accents on Multimouse became black as a result of the Cat Miraculous' influence worn on her right ring finger. The pink section of her mask also became black. Her hair bands and skip rope became black as well.
As Dragon Bug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Dragon Bug wore a suit with traits from both Ladybug and Ryuko's design, with the right side being red with black spots lined in yellow with a black line with a yellow scale-like outline wrapping around the leg and the forearm and ending on the foot and the hand, respectively. The left side was black with red spots with a yellow outline, but with the leg and the forearm being red with the same line, but ending on the ankle and wrist, respectively. She had a black swan-necked collar/turtleneck with a yellow edge (where she had the Dragon Miraculous), and on her chest, over a black circular spot with yellow lining, she had the images that represented the three elements she controlled: lightning, air, and water.
On the back of her head, she had four red dragon-like horns (two pairs of conjoined horns on each side) with black tips and thick yellow outlining and, on her back, she had a holder for her sword. On her face, she wore a red mask around her eyes with three black spots and black fang-like sections with yellow outlining at the base of the sides.
She wore the Dragon Miraculous around her neck with her earrings.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
From Season 6 onwards, she now had elements of Ladybug's modified design. Her horns were no longer conjoined, but higher and curved. Her pupils were slit. Her neck was now black at right and red at left. Her right arm was red with black spots, hand, and gold trim. The other had inverted colors. She now had black armpits, left shoulder, waist, and thighs with a gold trim and flame design. There was a diagonal gold wavy line in the middle connecting to the emblem that contained all three weather symbols on her right chest, ending with an arch and spikes on top around the emblem.
Around the hips were thick red linear sections with a circular part at the end on either side with a black dot in the middle and gold spiky trim, similar to her Ladybug costume. The legs were red with black spots, gold trim, and black soles.
As Lady Bee

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Lady Bee wore a suit that possessed traits from both the Ladybug and Bee Miraculouses. Most of her suit was red with black spots that had a yellow outline and a black vertical line at the front of her body. The area of the hips, the upper arm, half of the forearm, and the swan-necked collar were black with yellow jagged stripes at the edges and lining. The upper half of her mask was red with black spots with a yellow outline and the lower half was black with a single yellow at either side.
She wore her hair back in a ponytail which was curled to resemble a bee's stinger at the ends, tied with a yellow hairband with two matching-colored antennae-like ribbons sticking out from it, and a thick streak of yellow hair curled into the end of her ponytail, along with a thin streak of red.
She wore both the yo-yo and the spinning top around the hip when not using them. She wore the Bee Miraculous on her head alongside her earrings.
As Pegabug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Pegabug wore a suit that possessed traits from both the Ladybug and Horse Miraculouses. Most of her suit was red with black spots, but the front down to the knees was completely white covered by said spots, with a white horseshoe over her chest. Most of her upper arms and the upper side of her forearms were dark brown, while the rest of her forearm and hands were white with dark brown fingers.
Her legs were white with a gradient effect, with black spots and the soles of her feet being dark brown and her mask being red with black symmetrical spots, except for a white middle spot on top. Her hair was tied in a ponytail with a red hairband with two red antennae-like ribbons sticking out on top and the ends of her ponytail were white. Her turtleneck was black with the upper arms colored dark brown.
She possessed two pairs of gold wing-like ornaments with white edges with one pair located on each side of her head and the other on each outer ankle.
Her horseshoe was located on her back, while her yo-yo was around her waist.
As Pennybug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Pennybug wore a suit that possessed traits from the Ladybug, Horse, and Rabbit Miraculouses. Most of her suit was red with black spots, but the front was white covered by black spots, with a white horseshoe over her chest and a white cotton ball attached to the front of her neck on top. her limbs up to the upper arm and thigh were black with white spots, with her having a light blue wing-like ornament with white edges on each outer ankle and big red puffy shoulder pads with black spots that had one big white spot at each end.
Her hair was tied in two ponytails, each with a bun on top and a cyan ombré, along with rabbit ear-like ornaments in the shape of a wing with a light blue interior lined in black.
Her horseshoe was located on her back, while her yo-yo was around her waist.
As Ladyfly

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Ladyfly wore a suit with traits from the Ladybug and the Butterfly Miraculouses. The torso, hips and thighs were red with dark magenta spots, and the same went for the face mask, however, those parts also possessed hues of purple shining on them. The thighs had dark magenta around them above the knee and ascending until halfway on the outer side with a red spot. Her shoulders were purple, but possessed a dark magenta cover connected to the costume with V-neck collar (with the Butterfly Miraculous beneath it), with two lines descending from it through the costume around the torso, and then connecting with thicker dark magenta lines originating from the back and ending below the abdomen, having two red spots (one on each side, aligned) at the front, with two thinner lines coming out from it at the back ascending until below the shoulder cover.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
She wore magenta gloves up until below the shoulders, each with a red spot at the top, and purple knee-high boots with a red spot at the top of each of them. She had her hair tied with pigtails with red ribbons with dark magenta edges at the shape of butterfly wings, each side representing one half set and having one purple spot on each end (both top and under) of the bigger "wings".
Her cane, when not in use, was located at her back.
As Bug Noire
Bug Noire wore a suit with traits from the Ladybug and the Cat Miraculouses, a true fusion of her Ladybug and Lady Noire forms. Most of her suit was red with black spots, but with solid black coloring from the sides of the neck to her arms, and from her upper thighs down to her feet, with a small gradient of fluorescent green spots going from bigger to smaller on both of her shoulders and from the middle of her thighs down to her knees, as well as thick fluorescent green lines surrounding the edges of the black parts.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Both the insides of her hands were red, and the soles of her feet were fluorescent green with black cat-paw prints. Her mask was red with black spots resembling her Ladybug form, but was shaped like her mask as Lady Noire. She also wore black triangular platform shoes. Atop of her head, she had black cat ears with red outer edging lined in fluorescent green. She had green eyes, with four small black dots on her irises in a quincunx pattern. Her hair became black and was divided into 3 braids: a longer, floor-length one, and two shorter ones that ended around her hips, all 3 being tied at the end with red ribbons.
Her yo-yo was black with fluorescent green spots, and her staff was black with the cat claw turning red. She kept the yo-yo tied around her waist while her staff was secured to the back of her waist.
As Chronobug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Being mostly a recolored version of her "upgraded" suit, Chronobug wore a suit which bore some resemblance to Mister Bug's costume, except she had solid black coloring on her hands, her waist to upper thighs, and arms where the spots were inverted. Her collar switched from completely black to swan-necked with black lining and a small ladybug-shaped zipper connected to the front of her costume similar to Cat Noir's bell.
Her pigtails and hair ribbons became longer akin to her modified suit design. She also gained an additional pair of blue ribbons. The spots and the bottom of her feet became white and had a soft glow. All the red parts of her outfit became yellow.
As Ladybiquity
Ladybiquity wore a suit with traits from the Ladybug Miraculous and Ubiquity's. Her suit conjugated a contrast between magenta and purple with white dots. While her front and the back of her waist were magenta, the rest of her costume (her lower forearms, shoulders, lower legs and back) was purple. Her magenta mask covered her eyes with three white spots shrinking in size further down her face.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Her hair was styled with two long wavy twin tails with white hair ties protruding outwards, resembling a ladybug's antennas or a ladybug flying when she moved. She wore purple headphones with the ears covered by large round objects with white spots arranged in a quincunx pattern. The headphones were actually the Ladybug Miraculous earrings after being infected with Betterfly's Kamiko to transform Ladybug into Ladybiquity. She also had a clear purple cape attached to her arms and back.
Similar to Ubiquity, she had large white dots on the sides of the chest with a thinner ring around them and three thin red stripes stretching out below down to the knee with matching spots that went in a gradational pattern from large to small. Her upper arms also had a red stripe in the middle of their purple sections. Her suit also had a galactic pattern on it.
She also still sported the Ladybug Miraculous' weapon, the Yo-yo, tied around her waist, but the string was now purple in color.
As Viperbug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Viperbug wore a suit with traits from the Ladybug and Snake Miraculouses. She wore a brilliant velvet red suit with a cerise tinge to it. Her collarbone, swan-neck, the sides of her waist, legs, and the sides of her back were dark crimson. The collarbone section pointed in the back and had lighter trim on top. Her armpits and the lower shoulders, including the middle of her hip sides, were hot pink with black spots in the middle, framed by hot pink teardrops that were wavy down to the middle of the hip sides. However, the dots on her shoulders were sideway teardrops.
She also had black spots on her upper arms and two more on the zipline of her chest. The legs had brilliant fuchsia spots and soles that pointed in the near-back. Her mask was solid velvet red with pointed corners resembling fangs. Her eyes turned gold with slit pupils and cerise sclerae, and her hair had a deep red ombre near the ends of her bangs, while her forelocks and curlier, pointier pigtails had a cerise-to-pink ombre. At the back were red ribbons.
As Bunnybug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Bunnybug wore a suit that possessed the traits of the Ladybug and Rabbit Miraculouses. Her suit had a similar appearance to her modified Ladybug costume. However, the red parts were white and the spots were blue with red trim. Her thigh sections also ended in a straight-cut with a white ring and a blue spot with red trim in the middle, matching the markings on her shoulders. Her collar had a white ball resembling a rabbit's tail with blue hands, a white ring, and a spot matching the others on top. Her zipline was disconnected as a red vertical line made of three blue spots with red trim.
Her mask matched the color of her suit and spots, with a red border. Her lips were blue and her hair matched its color, with a brighter ombre near the ends of her curlier, slightly larger pigtails, same for her outward forelocks. Her ribbons were blue and she had white pointed rabbit ears with blue insides, black trim, and white pointed tufts upfront.
As Bunnynette

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Bunnynette wore a two-piece arctic blue bodysuit. The top piece was a jacket with black pockets and trim, with rings at the upper sides and a white dot within. Her opera-length gloves were white with black trim and circles on top with blue dots within, matching her boots which had arctic blue soles, black trim, and an arctic blue dot on the foot. The bottom piece was white at the entire torso with a downward wavy point, black trim, and a blue dot in the bottom middle, while the hips and thighs were arctic blue. She had a swan-neck with black trim and a white pom-pom resembling a rabbit's tail in the middle.
She wore a mask and ears similar to Bunnyx, and her hair was dark blue with enlarged, curlier pigtails with a lighter ombre near the end, held by arctic blue hair bands and ribbons.
She wore her umbrella at her lower back.
As Heartfixer

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Heartfixer had a metallic mauve silhouette with a brilliant fuchsia and white shine. Her hair, worn in the same style as a civilian, appeared a little more unkempt, especially her bangs, which lengthened. Around her pigtails were pieces of barbed wire to match the string of her akumatized purse, which became a crystal heart. On the collarbone was a pastel pink glowing heart with cracks spreading to the shoulders and neck, as well as on her back, accenting her glowing eyes.
As Renardette

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Appearance
Renardette wore an orange two-piece suit. The top piece had black arms, white hands, a black swan-neck, and an orange front styled like a qipao. It had black trim and an orange gradient near the bottom half. The bottom piece had a black gradient down to her legs, paired with orange lotus heels with white soles. Over her face, she wore an orange mask with a white bottom half, a black nose, and thick waterlines around her eyes with sharp tips. Like Rena Rouge, she wore her hair in a high ponytail, resembling a fox's tail, held by an orange band. Her hair was slightly unkempt and her forelocks thickened. On her head, she wore orange fox ears with black trim around the white insides, accented by an orange hair tie and ribbons in the back. She had light tangerine lip gloss. She wore the Fox Miraculous around her neck as a pendant and wielded her flute at the back.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Marinette is a sweet, outgoing, attentive, young, and joyful girl who loves fashion, her friends, family, and Adrien Agreste (her boyfriend), who describes her as honest, kind, fair, and the type not to cheat. She is very helpful towards those who have insecurities and problems expressing themselves, such as; Juleka Couffaine, who was afraid of not being noticed by others, and Marc Anciel, who has too much doubt about his own abilities. According to Clara Nightingale, Marinette has a pure heart. She cares deeply for other people, usually putting their feelings and interests even before her own, in some cases at a personal cost. Despite being genuinely kind and an optimist by nature, even she has her limits, such as when she gets irritated with Chloé Bourgeois to the point that she refuses to continue guarding her against the Evillustrator as Ladybug.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Despite her outgoing and sympathetic personality, Marinette struggles with self-confidence and self-esteem. Before being Ladybug, she was more nervous and didn't oppose others, but her confidence grew considerably since then such as talking with Adrien and standing up for others. In urgent situations, she becomes very nervous, clumsy, a bit awkward, and quick to panic which includes approaching her crush, trouble-choosing between her love interests, when in contact with major celebrities if she thinks others do a better job compared to herself or losing something that will expose her secret identity. She once had an unhealthy obsession with Adrien, a male model who is in her class. In "Perfection", with Kagami's help Marinette starts to figure out that her lack of confidence and self-esteem come from a fear of being not good enough. And from "Derision", as well as out of the fear of being hurt and humiliated again as she was the year before.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
In some episodes, she starts showing her Ladybug traits in her civilian self, first off in "Darkblade", where she told everyone to retreat and in "Sole Crusher" when Zoé got akumatized into the titular villain and manipulated by Chloé and threatened by her to attack Kitty Section, Marinette was forced to step in and reason with the latter, telling her that everyone is different and has other unique qualities and other individualities to comfort her after revealing Chloé's lies, false beliefs, mindset, and that the "winner and loser" concept doesn't exist to her and seeing the latter upset from learning the truth of the "winner and loser" concept. Despite a brief interruption from Cat Noir, Marinette tells Sole Crusher that she might trip, she might fall but she will always have someone like herself to help her back up and she will always be there for her no matter what.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Marinette can act impulsively and irrationally at times, as shown when she deflected the false accusation of "stealing" Chloé's bracelet onto others who are also innocent. She is willing to do several risky tasks in order to protect her image, like erasing an embarrassing message on Adrien's phone by stealing it. More so if or when she is jealous when other girls such as Chloé or Lila Rossi flirt with Adrien, even abusing her powers as Ladybug to keep them away or forgetting to detransform in the first place. However, Marinette learns from her mistakes and becomes a more open-minded, understanding person. She also takes advice from others very well, whether it is family or friends, as seen throughout the series. According to herself in "Family", as her civilian self-personality wise, she takes after her father, having her great uncle's creative side and her grandfather's fear of change.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Thanks to Chloé and Kim's prank and unknowingly because of her archenemy, she learned what happens when one obsesses over their own desires and that you not only hurt yourself but others too. Such as earlier in the series, Marinette would have been all over Adrien but in "Mr. Pigeon 72", she forces Kagami to see him, but in "Crocoduel", she goes to great lengths to avoid seeing Luka. Her love obsession caused many problems, such as in "Desperada", where her emotional preference caused her to give Adrien the Snake Miraculous, even though Luka was a much better fit. And causing the kwamis' capture and with that being the last straw Marinette gives up her love for Adrien for the sake of her people. However, in trying to shut off her love affections she goes denial crazy again from running away from her feelings to desperately wanting a guy to love her back even to almost foolishly accepting Monarch's offer aware that everything would end in disaster if not for Cat Noir. As well as because of her archenemy's influence in "Derision", as both sought easier ways out of their problems but were short-sided and yet Marinette accepted the outcome and followed her friend's example.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Speaking of example, Marinette also has learned as a designer to take inspiration from many things even showing it her costume and powers as Ladybug at first it was simple showing that she wasn't ready to become a hero. But as time went on it started in "Mr. Pigeon 72", where her upgraded suit showed a resemblance to Adrien's Mister Bug suit in "Reflekdoll". As well as with her Magical Charms basing it off the charm Alya has attached to her phone as a result of their friendship and in "Derision", she styled her pigtails and as Ladybug they grew longer similar to Socqueline's and taking all of it into a fact that changes are all tributes to the three friends who displayed the one thing Marinette lacked but grew to have: confidence. And in her and Cat Noir's latest appearances, now they have taken inspiration from their Re-Verse counterparts to tribute what they encouraged each other to believe in: hope, themselves and others.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
As Ladybug, Marinette retains many of her alter ego's characteristics, but she is much stronger. Her confidence and bravery come out more prominently. According to Cat Noir, she can be stubborn at times, especially when she isn't easily convinced. While almost all of Ladybug's plans are effective, they tend to be complex and rather bizarre. She is more cautious and careful than Cat Noir, sometimes needing to restrain or stop him from doing hasty acts seen in several episodes and for Shadow Moth, he believed it was the only reason why she kept winning. Only on rare occasions, she can act hasty, especially if she is in a rush to do something, multiple things at once or being quick to assume like in "Kuro Neko", when she mistook the titular sentimonster for an akumatized Cat Noir. She believes that a great superhero always listens to their head, meaning that she isn't easily fooled or swayed by deceptions and lies.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Ladybug strives to rescue everyone, including those akumatized by Hawk Moth. She usually tries to persuade the supervillains to calm down and stop their rampage when she can. She is aware that there is a line between justice and revenge believing that honesty and justice don't mean anything if you're pressured into doing it, as she did with Bob in "Silencer". She acknowledges that good things come by doing good actions and that not all problems can be solved by wishing them away like Hawk Moth hopes, especially at the expense of hurting the innocent. She also values the lives of others more than material possessions. Similar to her partner, through her lifestyle, she isn't tempted by power because Marinette understands that her life can be great without it. However, for a long time, her obsession with Adrien got in the way of saving people.
Through her persona as Ladybug, she did not only become aware of the line between justice and revenge, she grew into a symbol for justice trying her best to uphold it or needing to be reminded of it as well as lead others to do the same.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Such as during the various episodes against akumatized victims, in "Oni-Chan", when Marinette was stopped by Tikki in using her powers in retaliation, in "Derision", where she didn't told a grudge against Kim and kept a furious Cat Noir in check.
All the way to critical moments like with Chloé in "Revolution" and against Gabriel in "Re-creation", where she had him dead to rights about everything even wanting to wish him away if she wanted too but realized it wouldn't do either of them any good instead she chose to forgive him and find a better way.
Even for her people for which is why else she concealed the truth about Adrien's father, knowing that Adrien despite deserving the truth, he doesn't deserve the world's vengeance for his family's mistakes or if Gabriel made his original wish resulting in sacrificing her, then it would be only a matter of time before the people or Adrien discovered the truth wanting to avenge her falling for the same trap their enemy did.
Marinette takes her image, Miraculous powers, and those of others very seriously as Ladybug.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Such as when fighting against Hawk Moth's villains, compared to Cat Noir's laid-back and goofy personality, and more so at Chloé for using her powers to create a fake accident, that could have led to a serious one.
It took the most critical point in "Revolution", when one of her moral codes as a hero was used against her but also realized even if it is that the person must still stand and do what is right.
Given these traits, Adrien claims that her civilian form is funnier than Ladybug.
But she is also sensitive about her image, such as getting annoyed at Chloé playing her alter ego in Clara Nightingale's music video, a little angry when Nora doubted her abilities, and even attacking Miraculer impulsively after the latter tauntingly mimicked her.
Although she can get exasperated with Cat Noir if he jokes too much, she handles it calmly at times and enjoys teasing him or others.
Similar to Cat Noir, she is clever with her words and occasionally enjoys making puns.
According to Marinette in "Family", as her alter ego personality-wise, she takes after her mother and her grandmother Gina's adventurous spirit.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
She also takes her capabilities to help others as Ladybug and herself with great pride seen in "Wreckless Driver". Such as with Aglaé, when Marinette discovered that she was still traumatized, afraid of akumatizations, thereby butterflies in general and even her alterego. And the same with Adrien when he desired to the therapist, Marinette felt disheartened about it realizing there was so much she could do.
As her alter ego, Marinette strives to keep her personal and superhero lives separate to protect herself and her loved ones. Still, she aims to be honest with others in other ways, like with Cat Noir about not having romantic feelings for him and seeking advice from others. No matter her difficult tasks, Marinette does everything she can to set things right as Ladybug while keeping up with her everyday responsibilities, like studying, designing things, and more. There are exceptions to the rule such as when she mixed up her duties to her former master and her personal plans, like her letter to Adrien. She also has occasional problems inventing excuses for her absences to her friends, teachers, and parents. When off duty like Cat Noir, Ladybug has learned to relax and have fun.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
As a duo, she is cool, calm, and level-headed, but does let personal matters take over sometimes as she voiced her frustrations at Cat Noir during a fight leading to her doubts about trusting him during the "New York Special", and then an accident. As time went on Ladybug realized that she and Cat Noir would have to include others in their work with them following her as the leader adopting a caring protective mother role figure. Doing so she doesn't see them as sidekicks but as friends and extremely values their support. She is also great at giving advice to others when they need it and shows great care for them and their loved ones when in danger such as when Chloé and Kagami, were suspended from their team roles as the cost of revealing their identities to Hawk Moth. According to Cat Walker in "Kuro Neko", as team leader, Ladybug doesn't play favorites and cares for everyone equally. Also, she learned to take suggestions, and ideas and to follow the lead of others when the situation calls for it such as in "Stormy Weather" and "Psycomedian", following Cat Noir's lead when she became more aggressive and irrational than normal, fierce boarding reckless.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
After taking on guardian duties, Ladybug still continued to accept the help of her allies both old and new understanding that the rules are slowly changing. And yet, she became overprotective of and bordering afraid for Cat Noir, herself, and others as well as affecting her friendship and partnership with him unknowingly acting like her archenemy by keeping him out of the loop, taking him for granted, calling the other heroes excessively or not trusting him to retrieve the Miraculous from the holders whose identities he knows unaware that he wanted to protect her to but in the opposite direction. To the point of being very controlling in "Penalteam", trying to keep the ball, which caused her team to lose the first part of the match. She fully realizes her and other mistakes, after Monarch stole all the Miraculous in the Miracle Box (except for hers and Cat Noir's), feeling immense guilt, believing what she deserved until Cat Noir reminds her that she still has him, the faith of all Parisians and ensured her they will retrieve all of the Miraculous, and make sure they are not stolen again inspiring her with the hope to keep fighting.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
With the loss of the Miraculous, her confidence as Ladybug shook to where she occasionally hesitated and became sensitive at the mention of it, especially missing the kwamis and the rest of the team.
Then, with Monarch's defeat and retrieval of the jewels, Ladybug felt great joy at the team's return. Since then, she has been more trusting with them giving them more space, allowing them to use their powers on their own to help those outside of akumatized villains unless summoned. While still having her caring mother figure assuring them when/if doubtful such as with Sabrina in "Daddycop" and Ivan in "El Toro De Piedra", yet stern but forgiving with Kim in "Sleeping Syren".

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Despite the fact that being Ladybug had allowed her to meet Tikki and save people, Marinette started to grow tired and stressed about keeping her two lives separate and having to lie to everyone she loves, eventually causing her to break down and cry to Luka about her problems. While on occasion, she rarely breaks down as Ladybug, often voicing her doubts and mistakes to Cat Noir during their hardest times. She felt more of the strain in her civilian life as she took the mantle of the guardian, causing her to break down, even more, realizing she couldn't have a love life or be honest with anyone; effectively condemning herself to a cage of lies until Shadow Moth is no longer a threat.
Speaking of her tasks as the Guardian, Marinette worked relentlessly to decode the grimoire and was very determined to stop Hawk Moth from re-akumatizing people.
However, she is also stressed out more and struggled to balance everything to the point where she constantly lies to her parents and friends.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Because of this, Marinette started to act like Gabriel such as resorting to drastic measures such as not telling Luka the truth and calling off her friendships with her friends, both instances lead to them being akumatized.
It was there that Marinette, after breaking off with Luka and making up to her friends, she decided to let Alya in on her secret of being Ladybug.
After gaining help from Alya in "Mr.
Pigeon 72", she has a deeper understanding of her powers and when using them she was happy about protecting people even further.
Through it, she calmed down and started to see the flaws in others.
Unlike Hawk Moth, Marinette has let go of past mistakes as she wasn't angry at Master Fu for losing the two Miraculouses leading to now, and in "Furious Fu" not blaming herself for Fu's condition knowing that he wouldn't want her to do that as others still needed her.
However, because of the big burden, she has as the guardian, similar to Master Fu, Ladybug becomes very protective of the Miraculous under her care.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
And yet, the burden of being the guardian wasn't the only thing that made her behave the way she did it was also Hawk Moth's relentless hunting of her and Cat Noir. Over time she had grown more aware of Hawk Moth's deceptive and super sneaky nature to the point where she had nightmares and was afraid of what he was going to do if he found out when she let others in on her secrets and has the power to back it up. Despite burdening herself to keep everyone else safe she had forgotten it works both ways as no one else wants to see her suffer for them. Because of her archenemy, she understood what the other guardians, Miraculous holders, and kwamis felt knowing what it's like to be hunted.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
To be free of one burden just to be tied with another, as for what Bunnyx mentioned in "Miraculous London" came true, despite defeating Monarch, Marinette felt guilty on how things ended and aftermath. To the point where she minced her words in "Mister Agreste", saddened for those still traumatized like Aglaé in "Wreckless Driver" and even Adrien. The guilt she feels could also be from not being able to do anything more, yet at the same time it wasn't her fault as the information she needed to end everything was kept from her to a point where she couldn't use it. Yet, the difference between her, Master Fu and Gabriel, unlike the others, Marinette was caught in the problems and not the cause.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Not only that through her adventures, Ladybug and Cat Noir have learned to never use their powers for personal desires as well as taught others to follow their example. Much moreso, it not only became a duel between good and evil but social classes too with Marinette learning from Gabriel, Tomoe and even Chloe that not only is it bad to use miraculous powers for personal gain but any power or status for such purposes. And that power should be shared not hoarded out of fear because of things one can't control as well as not only does power deserve to shared and understood but everything should be too.
After Monarch's death, Marinette decided it was best for Adrien not to know that the supervillain's identity was his own father, fearing that the emotional impact would lead him to be akumatized by the new wielder of the Butterfly Miraculous. Therefore, she lied to everyone, claiming that Gabriel helped her defeat Monarch. Despite feeling she did it for a necessary good, this action has placed a heavy burden on Marinette as she grapples with the guilt of having to constantly lie to maintain her secret.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
In the sixth season, the burden of keeping the secret has led Marinette to become very paranoid, anxious, and prone to overreacting. This is evident in "The Illustrhater" and "Sublimation," where her insecurity in her relationship with Adrien led her to avoid him and use her duties as Ladybug as an excuse to leave, and pursue Sublime based on a misunderstanding. She claimed that instead of being jealous of Sublime for being close to Adrien, she only wanted to be her friend. This even led her to fake being akumatized, causing Sublime's prosthetic legs to break during a test and her mother to be akumatized.
As the season progresses, Marinette has begun to suffer more and more from keeping Monarch's secret from everyone.
This has often made her feel incredibly guilty and insecure, mainly because she can't have a completely honest relationship with Adrien and fears that if the truth comes out, she will lose Adrien, Alya, and everyone around her.
Although she has been motivated to tell Adrien the truth on several occasions, she ultimately backs down due to Nathalie and her own insecurities.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
In "Lady Chaos," Marinette did everything she could to keep the truth hidden from Adrien when he wanted to interview people close to his father to try and uncover the truth.
This led her to visit each of these people to ensure they wouldn't reveal anything, and she even begged Amélie Graham de Vanily with puppy-dog eyes not to tell Adrien anything.
She also had Alya create an illusion of Ladybug to lie to Adrien.
Although she eventually succeeded in giving Adrien a positive impression of his father, this only increased Marinette's guilt.
When Adrien asked her to draw a portrait of his father, Marinette couldn't because of her resentment towards Gabriel for not being able to live a normal life because of hiding his secret.
She ended up having a dream about Gabriel, filled with all the guilt she had been carrying.
As Lady Noire, Marinette retained most of her personality as Ladybug, like her cautiousness and creativity. She took after her partner's sense of humor, cunning, and charm, with Mister Bug believing that she was the one wearing the clown suit. Returning as Lady Noire again, she adopted more of her partner's persona, becoming flirty.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Like Adrien when he was Aspik, as Multimouse, while trying to protect her identity as Ladybug, Marinette was trustworthy, faithful, and clever. However, she pretended to be a klutz and "revealed" her identity in front of Cat Noir so he wouldn't think that Marinette is Ladybug.
As Bug Noire, Marinette had both the personality traits of Ladybug (the creativity and precaution) and Lady Noire (the wisecracks and keenness).
During her final battle with Monarch, she wasn't afraid to show her civilian self-personality, such as being disgusted with how far the villain was willing to go to get what he wanted nor was she afraid to be brutally honest with the truth about his actions affecting the people around him and the world, especially his son, despite Monarch's claims that he was doing all this for him and believed Adrien would do the same.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
Despite this, after defeating him, she made it clear what she would do if she cataclysmed the rest of the rings (rendering him powerless, free the kwamis from his captivity, give Cat Noir his ring back, repair the damage he caused and everything would go back to normal) but decided not to, knowing it would do no good and because the fact that he and Nathalie had little time left and Adrien would be even more miserable.
Instead, she was willing to talk him down; hear him out about how much Émilie's passing had affected him before offering to come up with a solution.
Though she was tricked and warned him not to go through with the wish, she decided to honor his last wishes of sparing Adrien the harsh truths about his father.
As her adult alter ego, according to Bunnyx, Marinette will grow into a wise, calm, strong, and confident leader, meaning that she isn't impulsive and irrational. Such as when she comforted Bunnyx, telling her that their fight wasn't over, easily figuring out she had a message from her younger self, and after Timetagger's defeat, she confidently told her younger self that they'll always be able to save the day.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Personality
As Heartfixer, she appeared lethargic and sad, wanting to use her power on Adrien to make him love her again. Despite this, she still protected her secret identity as Ladybug, avoiding answering Chrysalis when she asked if she was Ladybug and trying to shift her attention to Adrien. However, after Adrien apologized for not believing her and assured her that he still loved her and didn't need her to fix his heart, Marinette overcame her sadness and rejected the Ultrakuma.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
As a Civilian
Marinette has exceptional talent in fashion design, able to sketch ideas in a notebook after getting inspired by her surroundings and sewing by hand or with a machine. She usually wears her own creations and makes clothing for others. She also can create graphic designs using a computer, such as album covers. Her skills in this field are exceptional for an amateur, such as when her pigeon-styled derby hat was good enough to be recognized by the famous professional designer, Gabriel Agreste, despite the fact that she had never made one before. According to Audrey Bourgeois, the harshest fashion critic, she didn't see other talents as great as Gabriel Agreste until she met Marinette. She also wants to become a fashion designer when she grows up. Since "Reflekdoll", Marinette is working on a website to show off her designs.
Although she is absent-minded, Marinette is clever and quick-thinking, as shown when she hid her signature in her hat when Chloé stole her design, which exposed her.
Many of her friends describe "she is always able to come up with the right plan at the right time".

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
Despite being amnesiac from the effects of Oblivio's powers, she outsmarted the villain while they were looking for her and Adrien.
Ladybug's resourcefulness is more obvious when she is figuring out how to utilize her Lucky Charm, most of her plans being outside the box yet risky and complicated.
She also has good instincts, as she told Cat Noir, that revealing their identities would have to wait until Hawk Moth was defeated, meaning she understood what her archenemy is capable of if he found out.
By putting the clues together, she figured out, despite being deceived, Hawk Moth's identity and also managed to trick Cat Noir into believing she isn't Ladybug.
To the point where her instincts and intuition have developed so much that even Su-Han had praised it with high marks calling it an essential quality for being a guardian.
According to her in "Hawk Moth and the Akumatized Villains", due to not knowing what villain will come their way, the type of powers they have, or how strong said villain is, forces her and the team to adapt shown in "Ephemeral" and countless other episodes.
According to Alya, Marinette always gets a high score on school tests.

In Miraculous London, it is revealed that Marinette can forge handwriting, as she managed to replicate Lila's handwriting so perfectly, Lila was unable to see the difference and was forced to concede defeat for the time being.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
Even in her civilian form, Marinette has high stamina, endurance, and agility, running long distances without stopping in several episodes. She is naturally flexible, being even more flexible as Ladybug because of her enhanced physical abilities. She is also quite stealthy, frequently sneaking up on Adrien and other people without being noticed. Marinette is very good at sports, being quite good at ice skating and dancing. By "Miraculous London", she even became able to fight quietly and stealthily. She has good reflexes, being on par with Adrien despite fencing for the first time, though Adrien was most likely holding back to teach Marinette through example and physical learning without hurting her. With practicing from Kagami, Marinette has the potential to be a good fencer. In "Kwamibuster", due to her high stamina, endurance, and mental resistance, Marinette was able to handle the strain and/or use of multiple Miraculous at one time with minor fatigue.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
From Master Fu, Marinette learned the history of the kwamis and their Miraculouses. Her knowledge extends to the spells such as the incantation needed for the wish-granting power of the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses. However, as Fu's understanding is limited, Marinette's training might be incomplete. But Master Fu knew that Marinette would figure out everything she needed to know about the Miraculous and grow stronger as a hero, she became the new Guardian of the Miraculous.
Marinette is very skilled at video games, easily beating Max at Ultimate Mecha Strike III and getting the highest score in the entire school. While playing with Adrien, she quickly wins the round they were playing. When playing with both boys, while the boys seem to be tense, and concentrating really hard, Marinette is the complete opposite. Unlike them, her expression is calm and collected, showing how easy and effortless it is for her to win.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
As complimented by Adrien, Marinette is an excellent baker. She knows both approaches, modern and traditional, to baking, as well as how to handle cooking facilities. She makes "magicaroons" for Tikki, containing all the power-ups from the Miraculous spellbook. According to Marinette herself in "Pretension", she has been working in her parents' bakery for so long that she knows how good something is without eating it. Despite her being terrified afterwards, she had the courage to stand up to Gabriel. In "The Puppeteer", it is revealed that Marinette can whistle. Not as good as Lila, she is adequate at acting or deceiving people, especially akumatized villains, as a part of her plans to defeat and save them.
In "Determination", Marinette knows how to speak Spanish, she is also working on learning Mandarin Chinese with her mother's help and Adrien's. She is learning how to play the guitar with Luka's help.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
Marinette is an exceptional driver for her age, despite not having much experience in "Reverser", she is good at flying a kite. In "Gorizilla" and "Lies", she knows how to pilot a remote-controlled helicopter and a drone. Due to her spending time with her grandmother, she learned how to ride a scooter bike in "Queen Banana". In "Dearest Family", Marinette gets a pink scooter bike from her grandmother, since she thought it was her birthday even though it was three months ago. "Jubilation" is the first time she's seen riding it.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
Ladybug has enhanced physical abilities, such as speed and agility. These abilities allow her to react to and evade light-based attacks, as well as jump and leap several times her height and length. Similar to a real ladybug, she can climb up and walk on surfaces without her yo-yo. Her increased strength allows her to do things such as using her yo-yo to pull a large robot onto the ground, as well as break Cat Noir's nearly unbreakable staff and an oyster's pearl using only her fingers. Her near-invulnerability and great durability to physical damage allow her to jump off of 2 story buildings and land without issue and survive a fall off of one, as well as seemingly survive a fall at the height of at least several stories. She can even handle temperatures as severe as absolute 0. Ladybug is skilled in hand-to-hand combat when fighting villains or Cat Noir when he ends up being controlled by one. Her combat skills have improved so much that she can fight blindfolded with ease in "Psycomedian". Even out of "Aqua Mode", she is a good swimmer.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
Ladybug has remarkable talent with wielding her tool, the yo-yo, like using it as a grappling hook, a rope to restrain others, a projectile, a slicer even against solid materials, and a shield if she spins it fast enough. Her yo-yo also can work as a breathing apparatus for those who can't breathe underwater like herself. After an akuma or amok is released from its corrupted object, Ladybug can open her yo-yo to catch it and remove the energy charged with it, releasing it into its original form. In other episodes, she can fight exceptionally well with other weapons besides her yo-yo and is good at dual wielding despite having little to no training.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
Her special power, Lucky Charm, creates an object that helps her to achieve her goal, often being to stop a villain. Though usually confused at first, her creativity and cleverness help enable her to perceive where the object can be used to help her achieve her goal. However, from "Origins" to "Collusion", Lucky Charm drained her power and reverted her back to Marinette shortly afterwards, so she had to use it wisely. But, after the events of "Revolution", that is no longer the case, as she has learned to control her adult powers, allowing her use Lucky Charm as much as she wants without transforming back. Once the villain is dealt with, Ladybug can throw her Lucky Charm object into the air and use the Miraculous Ladybug, which will make it revert to an enormous swarm of ladybugs and fix all of the damage done since the villain appeared. She is also able to erase her Lucky Charm without using the Miraculous Ladybug as seen in "Miraculous Paris".

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng - Abilities
Because she has the power of creation, Ladybug is the one that sets the limits of her power. This is shown when Ladybug, determined to stop other people from being akumatized, is able to expand her powers, gaining a new costume and the ability to create magical charms that are able to prevent re-akumatizations to those who receive them.
Because her Chronobug form from "Miraculous London" was simply a new form of the achieved with the same Miraculous, she had the same powers and abilities as her normal form. However, her suit was bioluminescent, meaning it glowed slightly in the dark; this trait appeared most likely as Marinette's subconscious desire to ease Bunnyx's job of keeping track of her. However, since she also needed to maintain stealth not to make other people aware of her presence and disrupt the timeline, the suit's glow was notably dull.
As Aquabug
Aquabug, in addition to her original powers also has enhanced swimming capabilities due to the fins on her feet as well as the ability to breathe and speak underwater. Because she can breathe underwater by herself in this form, she can give her yo-yo to someone else to use as a respirator.
As Lady Ice

text:
