title: Markov
text:
Markov - Intro
is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is a robot created by Max Kanté.
In "Robostus", after Markov got confiscated by Mr. Damoclès, he was akumatized by Hawk Moth into Robostus, a supervillain who brought machines to life.
In "Hack-San", after the titular sentimonster downloaded a virus into Markov which forced him to be angry, he was reakumatized by Shadow Moth into Robostus.

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Markov is a small robot that is mostly blue and gray. On top of his head, he has a propeller with a blue blade and a black shaft with white stripes. Moreover, Markov has a transparent blue tactile sensor, a gray face with a button that has a blue heart engraved on it, a brilliant opal/luminous vivid cyan screen that has two pupil-less black dots which resemble his eyes, and two blue ear-like round sections on his sides that have a white outline and a musical symbol on the center of each ear. Below his head, Markov has a white USB port, and attached to his body is a blue and gray mechanical arm that has a gray claw and black palm.
Inside his body, Markov has a white rectangular CPU with many LED lights and a small face engraved in the center with words reading "Markov 1.4."
From Season 6 onwards, his entire form has been reduced to a pocket-sized robot. His body is white with blue accents, and instead of a paw, he has two blue pincers, slightly resembling boats. He has blue propellers on top of his head. His face is completely digitized, consisting of a black screen with blue LEDs arranged to simulate a smile.
As Robostus

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Appearance
Robostus' main body interface stayed the same, except his colors have changed: his propeller, screen, ears, mechanical arm, and claw were bright red; the musical symbols and the outline engraved on his ears were black; and its tactile sensor and eyes were neon green.
Inside Robostus' body, the same CPU was dark gray with red LED lights and a green face.

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Personality
Although Markov is a robot and his capability and intelligence of emotions are limited, Markov is still very conscious and self-aware. Markov is quite naive, but he is also friendly, polite, and joyful, getting along with everyone very well. He also seems to have a whimsical nature and can be humorous. However, he is a bit sensitive and easily gets downhearted if he is insulted in any way. Additionally, Markov is inquisitive as, even when akumatized, he asks multiple questions to Hawk Moth as to why he needs to capture Ladybug and Cat Noir's Miraculouses, and he asks Max to define akumatization.
As Robostus, he was very sinister, malicious, and demanding. He was initially very eager to capture Ladybug and Cat Noir's Miraculouses as Hawk Moth requested but turned against Hawk Moth when he realized that the Miraculouses could grant his wish to make him human. Robostus still cared deeply for Max during his akumatization, but when Max betrayed him, he decided that humanity is heartless and humans need to be destroyed. Robostus took pride in his robotic intelligence and strategics, but he failed to consider his potential for missteps and the cleverness of his enemies.

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Personality
Much more dangerously like Hawk Moth, as Robostus, he didn't think about the consequences of his wish unaware that if it had came true, then he would've taken the humanity of someone else away and that someone could've been anyone, even his best friend.

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Abilities
As a Robot
Markov flies with his propeller and he uses his claw to grab objects. He can verbally communicate with others, but there is a button on one side of him that turns his volume on and off. Also, on the back of his head is the power button so people can turn him on and off altogether.
Like Max, Markov is a genius who helped to create an anti virus flash drive and calculated the distance to capture Ladybug's Lucky Charm. Along with other beings with artificial intelligence in worldwide network, Markov is looking for a solution to the global warming crisis.
As seen in "Party Crasher" and "Startrain", he is an expert hacker who helps Max, whether for entertainment or fighting technology-based supervillains.
From season 6 onwards, Markov can now transform into Max's watch.
As Robostus

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Abilities
Robostus had the ability of technopathy, which allowed him to move mechanical objects and wreak havoc. Given limited but useful intelligence, the objects could move and attack speedily in any way that best suited them, physically moving or hovering, and some objects could even communicate, a lamp flashing its light on and off to speak Morse code, for example. However, if the objects were broken into pieces or damaged, they became lifeless again. Robostus could also make large mechanical objects form a huge robot that he could control and drive from the inside.
When Hack-San infected him with a virus that forces him to be angry, causing him to be reakumatized into Robostus, he had the power to send out a signal to all cellphones or tablets. The owners of the phones and tablets were brainwashed once they answered the call and followed Robostus's command to give him their most prized possession. Any person or object a brainwashed victim touched with their phone or tablet to would be downloaded into a digital prison.

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Relationships
Friends/Allies
Max Kanté/Pegasus
Markov has a high appreciation and fondness for his creator and friend. He helps Max create an anti-virus flash drive, and he gives advice to him on occasion. However, he is upset when people disregard their friendship, and because he is never away from Max, he gets worried when Mr. Damoclès takes him to his office without Max. Once he is de-evilized and re-activated, Markov is happy to see Max again.
In later, episodes like "Syren" and "Party Crasher", he enjoys hanging out with Max and his friends.
During "Startrain", he comes with Max and his class to England and helps him along with Ladybug and Cat Noir save his mother and everyone on the train. After seeing Max transform Markov is aware of his identity as Pegasus and like the heroes, he'll keep it a secret to protect him.
As Robostus, he keeps his compassion towards Max, making sure he isn't hurt and that they aren't separated again. He decides to use the Ladybug Miraculous and Cat Miraculous to become human; but when Max prevents him and tells him they won't be friends if he hurts Ladybug and Cat Noir, he gets upset and angrily rejects Max as a heartless human.

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Etymology
Given the importance of Markov decision processes to machine learning and therefore to artificial intelligence, Markov is likely indirectly named after Russian mathematician Andrey Markov.

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Trivia
In "Action", it is revealed that Markov's body is actually not plastic, he's made of a biodegradable resin.
Markov was first revealed in a Brazilian synopsis for season 2 on O Universo da TV.
His akumatized form was first revealed as a silhouette in a promotional poster on Jeremy Zag's Instagram.
Markov's appearance is similar to a LEGO® Robot model using structures and ball joints similar to it.
Robostus is the first non-human character to be akumatized. He would eventually be followed by Feast in its eponymous episode and Senticollector in "Gabriel Agreste".
He is the second akumatized villain who disobeyed Hawk Moth, following Gigantitan, and the first to turn against him deliberately.
Robostus is the first akumatized villain to be considered a "mistake" by Hawk Moth, due to its volatile nature, unpredictability, disobedience, and the fact that he turned against him.
Markov briefly knew what the Miraculouses are and learns about the wish-granting power of combining the Ladybug Miraculous and the Cat Miraculous.
He is the very first villain to want the heroes' Miraculouses for himself besides Hawk Moth.

title: Markov
text:
Markov - Trivia
In "Syren", Markov says that his circuits are sensitive to water. However, in "Startrain", Max pours water on Markov to prevent him from overheating, and he suffers no ill effects. This may be a simple continuity error, Max may have upgraded Markov to make him waterproof or due to the temperature of the boxcar reaching a temperature of over 200 degrees the water evaporated enough to cool Markov down but not damage his circuits.
Unlike Uncanny Valley, Markov cannot recognize the Miraculous holders' identities because he's not as advanced as her.
As seen in "Hack-San", his phone number is shown to be +33601010, meaning that he has the capabilities to operate a phone.

title: Markov/History
text:
Markov/History - [[Season 2]]
In "Robostus", when Olga Mendeleiev's computer has a virus and she refuses to let Max fix it, he urges Max to warn them that there is a large chance the hard disk would be irreparably damaged if the virus could not be neutralized within 75 seconds. Markov hands Max his USB drive after Max was unable to locate it in his bag to eliminate the virus. When Max states that Markov helped him develop his antivirus program, Markov emerges from the bag, introduces himself, and talks about the program as the virus is being neutralized. The other students start to show curiosity and interest in Markov after the virus was neutralized. It is revealed that Markov knows all of the students' names and has been told stories about many of them in the past when he is talking to Marinette.

title: Markov/History
text:
Markov/History - [[Season 2]]
Markov respectfully responds when Olga Mendeleiev calls him a toy, stating that he is Max's best buddy and that he is not a toy. Max stands by him, claiming that Markov is not a toy, is his best friend, is intellectual like a human, and has feelings. When Mrs. Mendeleiev says robots cannot have feelings and that he only programmed Markov to say that he truly loves Max and to put Markov away, Markov retaliates by saying she is not being reasonable, when she threatens to confiscate him if Max does not put him away. He is then confiscated by Mr. Damoclès, upset about the situation, and put inside a drawer, he gets akumatized into Robostus, with the power to bring all machines to life.

title: Markov/History
text:
Markov/History - [[Season 2]]
He makes all of the city's machines alive once his Akumatization is complete and they cause chaos across the city. He then emerges from the drawer and storms out of Mr. Damoclès' office. Then he constructs a vehicle that resembles a mech out of city machines and climbs inside. To keep him and Max together forever, he searches for Max, picks him and Olga Mendeleiev up, and places Max in the passenger seat. He rejects Ladybug and Cat Noir's attempts to negotiate with him and engages them in combat before throwing them across the city and heading to the stadium.

title: Markov/History
text:
Markov/History - [[Season 2]]
He captures Ladybug and Cat Noir in a claw and attempts to steal their Miraculouses to use the absolute power to become human. However, when Hawk Moth informs him that the Miraculous are for him and not Markov, he responds by enabling intruder elimination mode in Gabriel's lair. Max throws his bag at the machines as he tries to obtain Ladybug and Cat Noir's Miraculouses, then opens the claw that the heroes were imprisoned in, releasing them. As a result, Markov fights with Max before deciding he no longer wants to be a human and wants to exterminate all humans, then he steals the Lucky Charm object before Ladybug gets his and Max's antivirus drive, and his mech is cataclysmed, dropping the Lucky Charm harp. To avoid the heroes, he flies upwards until his propeller is jammed by Ladybug and he is defeated when the antivirus drive is used on him, which deakumatizes him.
In "Syren", Markov is seen with Max in front of the theater and later, on the top of the theater, after the city had been submerged in water, he stated that his circuits are sensitive to liquid.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Intro
Marinette Dupain-Cheng is one of the two titular main protagonists (alongside Adrien Agreste) of "Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie". She is a student at Collège Françoise Dupont.
With the Ladybug Miraculous, when inhabited by Tikki, Marinette transforms into Ladybug, a ladybug-themed superhero with the power of Creation in order to stop Hawk Moth and his akumatized villains.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Appearance
Physical appearance
Marinette is a pale skinned girl of average height with dark hair with blue undertones, light pink lips, and light freckles on both sides and the bridge of her nose. She has light blue eyes.
Civilian attire
Marinette's most common attire is a pair of pale sport pink rolled up jeans with a white tank top with pink flower designs. She also wears a light gray jacket with white cuffs. Her hair is pulled into pig tails tied with pink hair ties. She also wears a white and pink wristwatch on her left wrist.
As Ladybug
When transformed into Ladybug, she wears a red leotard with black dots, her hair pulled back into pig tails with red ribbons. She wears a red mask with five black dots. She also has a red yo-yo with five black spots and golden swirl designs that is normally tied around her waist.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Personality
Marinette is a clumsy, sweet and shy girl who doesn't have many friends at first. She aspires to be a fashion designer when she grows up and is seen imagining her clothes on people. She is shown to deeply love her family, but is easily embarrassed by her father and is insecure about her public image. Marinette is knowledgeable about cooking, answering her father's question about soup easily, even after her traumatic experience with her first akumatized villain. She can find her way around tough situations, such as when Chloé Bourgeois threatened her and she managed to escape.
But unlike her TV show counterpart, when it comes to her feelings for Adrien, she had the patience to wait and slowly work up their relationship.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Personality
As Ladybug, most of Marinette's personality is the same but she is also braver, courageous, quick witted and less clumsy. As while as retaining her cautious nature as she knew it was a bad idea to fight against Hawk Moth alone and she is protective and caring especially to those close to her such as Cat Noir when she watched in horror as he fell from Eiffel Tower and into the water rushing to his rescue. Once they resurfaced, she held him close and tried to protect him.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Abilities
As a civilian
Marinette is good at drawing, as seen in her journal.
She was not good at the clarinet, but after she became Ladybug, she became better most likely because of her newfound confidence. The same thing happened with her gymnastics, as she was able to actually stick the landing after becoming Ladybug.
She is also very tough, as seen when she was injured and she managed to push Cat Noir away from Hawk Moth.
She also appears to be a good swimmer, as seen when she managed to carry an unconscious Cat Noir and barely swim out of the lava, but this may have been because she was transformed into Ladybug at the time.
As Ladybug
Ladybug has enhanced physical abilities, like agility, speed and strength. She can fly with her yo-yo and use it to grapple and throw herself. When empowered by love, Ladybug unlocks her power of Creation, allowing her to restore and re-create destroyed objects and even restore life, such as when she used it to restore Paris's building and plants after Hawk Moth renounced his powers.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Relationships
Adrien Agreste/Cat Noir
She first met Adrien at the library when she was hiding from Chloé, but she finds it hard to get a word out causing her to fall over a cart but he helps her up and she tried to ask him something but he disappears. They meet again at the funfair and get along well until they were interrupted by their fathers. Over the months they bond more becoming friends, hanging out going to the movies and picnics as well as hearing about his mother. But when she finally worked up the courage to ask Adrien to the winter ball at school the next day, she was sadly told that he is in love with someone else too. Then, after Hawk Moth's defeat and at the winter ball, she finds him alone in the streets calling him by his hero name who was surprised to see her continuing on she takes his mask, unveiling herself as his partner causing Adrien to cry in tears of joy that he had found the girl he loves as they share a kiss.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Relationships
However, their first encounter as their alter-egos didn't start off as well as she crashed into him through Notre Dome and she wasn't take off by his show boating, but once in action, she saw that this was his first time too. After defeating Gargoyle, she had tendency to bicker with him especially when Cat Noir called her a "watermelon", but after they go their separate ways, she finds Cat Noir ridiculous. Her opinion about him changed when they met again at the funfair as it was under attack by the Mime and Magician, and by working together, they discovered the secret of their powers. Once everyone was saved, hearing Cat Noir demote himself to being her sidekick, she clarified they were partners as they "pound it". Months later, they continued to work together being great teammates and friends enjoying each other's company.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Relationships
Then, one night through her earrings she feels Cat Noir's call quickly answering she wondered what he wanted arriving at what she thought was an abandoned building looking over the place she noticed claw marks and her partner's stick but Cat Noir was nowhere in sight. At first, she panicked believing that Hawk Moth's villains finally got him and arrived too late only to discover he was fine, after following him inside the building she was amazed that it was an abandoned theater where she hears Cat Noir mentioned about his mother and how he hasn't been the same since she died. Ladybug consoled him, with him telling her he was fine since they met and expressed his gift to her through "Stronger Together", but despite finding it touching she sadly and politely rejected him telling she was in love with someone else taking her leave.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie

Despite it, she was in a quarrelsome mood towards him regardless she knew better to challenge their enemy alone warning Cat Noir to wait but she watched her partner in horror as he challenged Hawk Moth up the Eiffel Tower to only end with him taking a hard splash into the water and knocked unconscious. With her desperately coming to his rescue bringing him to shore trying to get him to come too to no avail and as Hawk Moth cornered the duo, she rushed to protect him but was easily defeated. Now depowered and hearing her partner at Hawk Moth's mercy begging for her help, Marinette at first believed she couldn't save him without her alterego until she remembered his words from before realizing she was the hero inside and out rising to her feet, she pushed him out of the way of Hawk Moth's attack. Then, coming too, she hears her enemy unveil Cat Noir as Adrien under his mask.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:

Months later at the winter ball, Adrien laments how much he misses Ladybug and that his heart is in turmoil. However, she appears outside and reveals that she knows that he's Cat Noir and that she's Ladybug much to his happiness and they both share a first kiss at the movie's end.
Wang Fu
Wang Fu is Marinette's teacher, and the Great Guardian of the Miraculous. They first meet personally when she saved him from getting hit by a car. The same incident happens with their TV counterparts, except in the movie, it was at nighttime, and in the show, it was early in the morning. Wang Fu then disguises himself and talks to her (as Ladybug), and Cat Noir. He explains the situation regarding Hawk Moth, and how their job is to work together to defeat him to stop him from taking over the city.
Towards the end of the movie, Ladybug returns the Butterfly Miraculous to him, unlike the TV show counterpart, in which Wang Fu never receives it.
Alya Césaire

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Relationships
Alya is Marinette's best friend. They first met when Chloé tried to tackle Marinette when she accidentally spilled coffee on her designer shirt, but she was saved when Alya recorded the whole fight, and after that, they hit it off and become good friends. They even got to the part where Alya even starts giving a positive attitude toward her whenever she messed up and even went to the fair with her. At the end of the movie, Marinette even comes to the ball in a beautifully, handmade dress, and Alya compliments on it, saying it looked gorgeous.
Tikki
Tikki is Marinette's caring kwami. They both first meet when Marinette is running away from Chloé and is saved by Sabrina. She runs into Wang Fu's shop and Tikki immediately mentions that she was excited to be working as an ally with Marinette. Although it took some time to convince Marinette to join the team and accept that she was now a superheroine, they form a close bond, and become good friends with each other.
Chloé Bourgeois

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Relationships
Just like in the original series, Chloé harbors a strong dislike for Marinette, viewing her with disdain and believing they have nothing in common. In the movie, Marinette accidentally spills coffee on Chloé's sweater, which leads to Chloé becoming extremely frustrated and ready to retaliate against her. Fortunately, Alya intervenes by recording Chloé's behavior and threatens to post the video online. This stops Chloé in her tracks, and she storms off in a huff. By the end of the movie, it appears that Chloé has softened her animosity towards Marinette. In her own way, she encourages Marinette to enjoy herself at the party and to pursue Adrien, suggesting that she's trying to become a better person.
Gabriel Agreste/Hawk Moth
At first, Marinette didn't know to Gabriel Agreste too well except that he is Adrien's father and the world famous fashion designer likely inspiring to be like him.
However, as their miraculous holder alteregos there were enemies.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Relationships
Gabriel, as Hawk Moth, was aware that Ladybug and Cat Noir are the current holders of Ladybug and Cat Miraculous, the very Miraculous that he sought to use to bring back his wife. He was extremely frustrated and enraged that she and Cat Noir continuously foiling all of his plans. When he attacked Paris one last time, Hawk Moth, now akumatized, telepathically grabs Ladybug and took away her Miraculous. Before throwing her away, he comments that Ladybug was just a scared, little girl.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
On the first day of school, Marinette was getting ready to leave, but her father kept offering to take her to school. She declined until her father offered to pick her up after school and offer some unicorn cupcakes, to the kids there much to her embarrassment, and still declines the offer reminding him that she doesn't have any friends until her mother was able to fool her husband into leaving. Then, Marinette confided her fears to her mother about being made fun of and how to make dreams come true, but her mother advised her to listen to her heart and believe in herself. On the way to school, she established her personality and internal conflict, and how she likes to be a fashion designer, before she left after she embarrassed herself by falling on the ground in front of Nathalie Sancoeur.
After arriving at school, Marinette was anxious about what the other students might think of her which escalated when Nino Lahiffe accidentally bumps into her, causing her to bump into Chloé Bourgeois causing a drop of the latter's coffee spills onto her's sweater, shocking everyone around them.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
Marinette, was about to have a confrontation with a furious Chloé, but Marinette was saved by Alya who recorded the incident making Chloé back off.
Grateful for Alya's intervention, they became to friends.
Throughout the day, Marinette struggled in her classes, while Alya did her best to support her.
After them, they part ways, and Marinette started to imagine her classmates talking about how clumsy she was, worrying that they thought poorly of her.
Reaching her locker, Marinette was approached by Chloé again, threatening to confront her after school.
But distracts her, by pretending to see another girl wearing an Agreste sweater and managed to escape into the library.
Feeling dejected and contemplating leaving Paris to reinvent herself, she unexpectedly meets Adrien Agreste, who notices she was crying.
She tried to brush it off, claiming it’s just allergies to pollen, which confuses him.
Continuing to observe him, Marinette developed feelings for him.
In her nervousness, she accidentally dropped some books, and had his help her picking them up.
Just as she was about to ask him to hang out, she realizes he already left.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
Once school was over, Marinette was about to leave, until she saw Chloé, along with Sabrina Raincomprix, getting ready to continue what happened earlier forcing the girl to flee.
While trying to escape, she saw Master Fu in the street about to be run over by an incoming car until she saved him, asking if her was alright, (unknown that Tikki flew in her backpack).
Upon hearing the old man's strange desire to come with him to save the world, much to her confusion, until she kept fleeing from Chloé and Sabrina, hiding in an alleyway, until she was spotted by Sabrina, but was spared.
Leaving Marinette was relieved until she fell into a Chinese shop, became uneasy until she noticed a ladybug (Tikki's animal form), which glowed and led her to what Master Fu said before going under a table, she found the Ladybug Miraculous and put them on, which released Tikki, causing Marinette freak out.
Then, Marinette was informed by Tikki that she was the chosen wielder of the Ladybug Miraculous, but Marinette was reluctant and still stunned until Tikki explained through "You Are Ladybug" for her owner to accept the role.
Regardless, Marinette transformed into Ladybug, much to her shock.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
At first, she was amazed before being annoyed by her weapon being a yo-yo until it dragged her all the way to the Notre Dame Cathedral, where she crashed into Cat Noir (Adrien), having them both tied upside down before falling.
However their first interactions didn't go so well, with the hero demoting her to a sidekick, and commenting about her costume until she saw him lose his bravado upon noticing Gargoyle (an akumatized Raymond) behind him until was too late.
While watching Cat Noir, she was still hesitant to help but tried by attaching her yo-yo to the Gargoyle's tail, taking the pair on a wild ride and crashed through everything out of Notre Dame, with the people of Paris seeing the heroes for the first time.
Then, they were taken to the river before crashing into the train station.
When she heard Cat Noir in trouble inside the station, she started to get the hang of her weapon just in time to save Cat Noir from an incoming train that crashed into Gargoyle, which de-akumatized him in the process.
Hearing her partner come too, Ladybug comments not too bad for a sidekick and helps him up but they both leave when the police arrive.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
They both notice the akuma butterfly leaving (after leaving Raymond), and meet Master Fu (in disguise), who explained everything despite their bickering about what they needed to do but most importantly about working together before he disappeared.
Despite it all, Ladybug still refused to continue being a hero, nor wanting anything else to do with Cat Noir ranting to him about what they just been through before heading home.
Ladybug managed to return home in time to de-transform before her father came into her room, asking what ingredient is needed for dinner, which she managed to answer before he leaves.
Alone, while Tikki discussed Marinette needing to work on her abilities and of Cat Noir, but the girl believed that was because of her that anybody could've gotten hurt, and still thought of her partner as annoying.
However, was Tikki assured that once the world was saved, she'll Cat Noir will never be seen again, but Marinette still refused the role.
So she tried to get rid of Tikki and the Ladybug Miraculous, but it kept coming back until Marinette told the kwami to leave her alone due to being afraid.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
The next day, she and Alya were on their way to the fair while discussing what happened the other night, and with the former trying to deny that her alter ego and Cat Noir were a couple before the latter gave love advice.
They then meet Adrien and Nino at the fair there with their best friends assuming they like each other, despite Marinette and Adrien's denial.
Then, by themselves Marinette tried to have a conversation with mentioning the bakery that she lived in, but when Marinette dropped her stuff to get macarons for him, Adrien noticed her sketches and liked them.
However, they both noticed Marinette's father standing right next to them, much to the girl's embarrassment and yet seeing him leave, she called her dad out for embarrassing her.
But that would have to wait when the Magician and the Mime attacked the fair causing chaos, Marinette seeing everyone scared and distressed through "Courage in Me", she decided wash away here fear and became Ladybug again.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
Observing the scene, she saw at first what she thought was baby separated from it's parent in the chaos trying to save them but it was actually the hench-creature Badoom created by the Magician demanding her earrings, and just as she was about to be crushed by the balloon monster, Cat Noir arrived and saved her.
During their confrontation with the villainous pair, the hero duo started to understand what Master Fu mentioned earlier, soon they saw the villains cause chaos with the rides, so they decided to split up with Ladybug trying to slow down the coaster to no avail.
From there upon helping Cat Noir reach the ferris wheel, she noticed that Chloe fell from the cart but managed she save her, then using Badoom, she was able to have the coaster land safely on the ground before rejoining her partner.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
After defeating the villains, the wheel was still moving, yet noticing the Louvre, Ladybug and Cat Noir changed the ride's direction having the ride land on Badoom, thereby stopping the ride and the creature saving everybody but they soon came into contact with Hawk Moth through a giant hologram demanding that there will be no mercy next time and after purifying the akumas. The duo were praised by all of Paris for their deeds and as time went by they became Paris' protectors while defeating constant akumatized villains, while Marinette improved with her new confidence and started to get close to Adrien, their friends, and everybody else in school.
Months later, the two heroes are having ice cream together before they playfully fight together, but after an awkward moment, Ladybug left for home.
The next day at school, Marinette talked with Alya about her plans to ask Adrien to the ball, with the latter planning to ask Nino.
But hearing Chloé's claim that Adrien was going with her, but Marinette retorted otherwise.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
Later, that night, she happily finished making her gift for Adrien and was confident enough to ask him to the ball, until being warned by Tikki about Hawk Moth but Marinette was assured there was nothing to worry about.
Until she received Cat Noir's call, arriving outside an abandoned theater, but seeing no sign of him, only claw marks and his staff left behind, fearing that Tikki was right believing that Cat Noir was caught, she frantically panicked just to see he was fine.
Then, once inside she marveled at the theater and then learned more about his late mother, Emilie Agreste, and fear of intimacy but had improved since they met.
He reveals that he prepared a surprise, which is a song that they both sing together, and he confesses that it was she who saved his heart, and they both dance.
He tries to kiss her to confess his love for her, but she sadly reveals that there is somebody else (not knowing that Cat Noir is Adrien) and left, causing him to feel heartbroken.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
The next day at school, Marinette (with Tikki's assistance) approaches Adrien and she confesses her love for him by inviting him to the ball and giving him a tie as a gift, but he sadly uses the same words she did by revealing that there is somebody else (not knowing that Marinette is Ladybug, who is the somebody else) and leaves. Chloé, believing that Adrien was talking about her, tells Marinette she tried to warn her and that this wasn't like a fairy tale. Feeling heartbroken, Marinette disposes of the tie. That night at home, she wonders if it was enough to be her.
When Hawk Moth akumatizes himself and unleashes his final attack on Paris that destroys everything, Marinette becomes Ladybug again to try and save the city, but is shocked by the destruction that Hawk Moth has caused.
She struggles to keep some civilians safe and wonders where Cat Noir is until he arrives to help her when the akuma blasts become too much for her to handle, but they are both still emotionally hurt by each other's rejection and failure to show up.
They notice Hawk Moth on top of the Eiffel Tower, but Cat Noir goes to confront the villain alone.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
After Hawk Moth knocks Cat Noir down, the hero's Cataclysm accidentally destroys the Eiffel Tower, much to Ladybug's shock, and her partner falls into the river, and the debris knocks him out.
Ladybug saves Cat Noir from drowning, and Hawk Moth confronts them while turning the river into lava.
Ladybug attempts to attack Hawk Moth, but he easily defeats her and steals the Ladybug Miraculous from her in the process.
In a vision, Marinette sees Tikki, and she believes that she can't defeat Hawk Moth without Ladybug, but Tikki urges her to get back up and keep fighting and to overcome her self-doubt.
After slitting Cat Noir's costume and mask, Hawk Moth is about to destroy Cat Noir with a blast, but Marinette takes the hit instead to save Cat Noir.
Marinette then watches as Hawk Moth lifts Cat Noir, but the hero's slit mask makes him realize that Cat Noir is his son, much to his shock and horror.
He ceases the chaos and renounces the Butterfly Miraculous in the process, thus revealing himself as Gabriel, much to Adrien and Marinette's shock.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
Marinette witnesses and overhears Gabriel revealing Cat Noir as Adrien, and the former supervillain breaks down about having almost murdered his son and confesses why he became evil before he and Adrien reconcile and they both share a loving hug, which also releases the Ladybug Miraculous back to Marinette, who turns back into Ladybug in the process.
Gabriel turns himself in and is arrested off-screen when the people of Paris are informed that he was Hawk Moth.
Master Fu appears again and advises Ladybug to let the sparkle shine through her.
Ladybug is not sure how to fix the damage to Paris, but Master Fu reminds her of what he said before and reveals himself as the one she saved from a car.
Happy about this, Ladybug returns the Butterfly Miraculous to him so that he can place it back in the miracle box safe and sound, so that no one will ever be allowed to touch it again before leaving for another part of Paris, where she gives a speech to the people of Paris that love will protect them if darkness should rise again.
Everybody starts chanting her name, and this gives her the power to repair the damage Hawk Moth did to Paris.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - History
After de-transforming back, she reunites with her parents.
Months later, for the Christmas gala on December 25th, Marinette attends the ball where she meets Alya, Nino, Sabrina, and Chloé, and wanders where Adrien is until Nino reveals that he's outside. Chloé tells Marinette to enjoy the evening until next year, when their rivalry will restart. Outside, Adrien laments how much he misses Ladybug and that his heart is in turmoil. However, Marinette appears and reveals that she knows that he's Cat Noir and that she's Ladybug, much to his happiness, and they both share a first kiss.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Trivia
For unknown reasons, Chloé calls Marinette "Marinella". This is never explained, however, it's likely that it is just a name she made up to make fun of Marinette.
Funnily enough, this could be a reference to one of the well known fairy tales: Cinderella.
As Ladybug in the movie version, her yo-yo string when it attached to the waist is black, but in the show, her yo-yo string that attaches to her waist is red.
In the movie, even before she got the Ladybug Miraculous, she already had her own earrings, but in the series, she didn't have any earrings prior to getting the Ladybug Miraculous.
Unlike her show counterpart, she doesn't use Lucky Charm in order to defeat villains, nor does she ever use that power ever in the movie, although it is possible that she still has the ability as the movie version of Cat Noir still retains Cataclysm.
Her hair tie in the movie is pink, but in the show, it's red.
She wears a watch in the movie, while in the series, she doesn't.
When Marinette sings Reaching Out, she said that she "dreamed of calling Paris home". This implies that she has just recently moved to Paris; however, this is not confirmed in the movie.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Movie - Trivia
Also, when Tikki says "coccinellidae", Marinette is shown to be confused, coccinelle means Ladybug in French, implying that she is not fluent in French due to presumably still moving in and adjusting to the city.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Intro
Marinette Dupain-Cheng is one of the two titular former main antagonists (alongside Adrien Agreste) of Miraculous World: Paris - Tales of Shadybug and Claw Noir.
She is the counterpart of Marinette Dupain-Cheng from the Re-Verse. When Tikki inhabited the Ladybug Miraculous, she transformed into Shadybug, a ladybug-themed supervillain with the power of Creation.
In "Miraculous Paris", after Betterfly crossed the multiverse to get help from Ladybug and Cat Noir (the heroic versions of the villains), she followed him along with Claw Noir to steal the Butterfly Miraculous. After realizing the power that her Miraculous and Claw Noir's possess together, she betrayed him to get his Miraculous and try to summon Gimmi so they could allow her to switch lives with her counterpart, failing only because of the seal placed on Tikki and Plagg of her universe. In order to both retrieve the Butterfly Miraculous and have her wish granted, she allied herself with Monarch.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Intro
After her counterpart was able to inspire her to get the life she wanted to have, Shadybug gave up on her evil purpose, using her Miraculous Shadybug to repair everything and, in this way, get a new costume. Now allying herself with Betterfly and having joined his Resistance, she adopted the name Ladybug, becoming a superhero.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Marinette maintains a striking resemblance to her main universe counterpart from the Quantic Universe. However, subtle differences set her apart. Her signature hairstyle still features two pigtails, now adorned with bangs that sweep across her left eye, accented with a pink streak. Additionally, she also wears dark purple eyeshadow and painted black nails. Before harnessing the healing powers of the Miraculous Shadybug, Marinette bore visible signs of strain from her Miraculous use. Notably, dark veins marred her skin, a consequence of overexertion, with the veins extending upward, particularly prominent on her face following her unsuccessful attempt to summon Gimmi. Before healing herself with her Miraculous Shadybug, Marinette also had black veins on her skin from overuse of her Miraculous, with the veins crawling up her face after her failed attempt to summon Gimmi.
Civilian Attire

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Appearance
Compared to her counterpart, Marinette embraces a gothic aesthetic, characterized by her attire. She sports a white shirt beneath a sleek dark gray jacket, paired with edgy dark pink trousers featuring stylish rips above the knees and along the legs. Completing her ensemble are striking black high-top boots with grey soles, adding to her distinct style.
Additionally, she wears dark fingerless lace gloves extending halfway up her forearms. Furthermore, she wears a black ascot adorned with intricate grey ornaments, completing her unique and striking appearance.
As Shadybug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Appearance
As Shadybug, her attire featured a contrasting combination of red with black dots and black with red dots. The front and back of her waist displayed a vivid red with black spots, while the rest of her costume, including her arms, shoulders, legs, back, and sides of her torso, showcased a sleek black speckled with red dots. Her footwear included red platform soles reminiscent of Queen Bee's style. Her mask was integrated into her jumpsuit via a black turtleneck, concealing her eyes with a design akin to Ladybug's face mask, characterized by a symmetrical arrangement of red and black spots. Her hair was styled into twin buns similar to Multimouse's, accented with strands of red ribbons that resembled a ladybug's antennas or wings in motion. Additionally, a bold red streak adorned her bangs, while strands of red hair framed her face. Her eyes assumed a fiery red hue, and she wore dark mauve lipstick.
As Ladybug

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Appearance
As Ladybug, she wears a jumpsuit that resembles the attire of her main universe counterpart's, but with some notable differences. While most of the black fades into the design, certain areas, such as her sides, upper arms, and legs, still retain a prominent black color. The jumpsuit features an extended turtleneck, which holds her pendant as a unique accessory. Her hair returns to her usual civilian style, and the color of her bangs changes from pink to red. Additionally, her eyes revert to their original blue color.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Personality
Marinette's personality was shaped by the harsh environment of her alternate universe and the painful experiences she has endured. On the surface, she seems ruthless and aggressive, driven by deep-seated anger and a sense of hopelessness. Her readiness to use violence and intimidation, especially in her dealings with Betterfly and Claw Noir, reveals a hardened exterior and a survival mechanism adapted to her brutal world, where helping others is a crime. Unlike her Quantic Universe counterpart, Marinette was not able to make any friends. Because of that, she didn't have the support she needed to stand up against Chloé Bourgeois, whose heavy bullying caused her to become depressed, cynical, and unable to find any joy.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Personality
Her loneliness and sadness made her an easy target for the Supreme, who persuaded her to work for him as the holder of the Ladybug Miraculous. As Shadybug, she unleashed her frustrations mercilessly on her enemies, using her powers for evil without regard for the consequences, even when it meant overriding the security measures designed to protect her. Her cleverness and strategic mind, not unlike that of Ladybug, were evident in her use of the Lucky Charm to create weapons and tools to defeat her foes, though Claw Noir's impulsiveness often undermined her plans.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Personality
Before her final battle with Ladybug, Shadybug's true complexity is revealed. Reading her doppelgänger's diary exposed her rare vulnerable side and a naïve envy of her counterpart's better life, leading to jealousy and shock when she discovered the Ultimate Miraculous Absolute Power and realized the Supreme had hidden this from her. This spurred her desire to switch lives. Her reaction to Sabine Cheng's affection, so different from the lack of support and love from her own mother, deepened her insecurities and highlighted her inner turmoil. When talking to Sabine, she remarked that the sewing machine was broken while looking at herself in the mirror, implying that this was how she saw herself. Shadybug was also surprised to hear Sabine, thinking she was talking to her daughter, say "I love you," which led her to reluctantly reply, "I love you too." This suggests that her own mother in her universe never showed her any affection or support, further fueling her insecurities.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Personality
During her final fight against Ladybug, Shadybug laid bare all the anger she had harbored throughout her life, hinting at years of resentment and bitterness. However, Ladybug succeeded in persuading Shadybug that she, too, could change her life by embracing self-love and allowing friendship to enter. This inspired Shadybug to stop her assault and abandon her quest to retrieve the Butterfly Miraculous. Instead, she employed her Miraculous Shadybug to restore everything. This act of heroism transformed her, both inside and out, as her costume changed to reflect her newfound resolve. Choosing to become a superhero, she allied with Betterfly and took on the name Ladybug, honoring the hero who showed her a better path.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Abilities
As Shadybug
As an alternate version Ladybug, Shadybug exhibited most of the same abilities as her heroic counterpart. Like Ladybug, she exhibited massively enhanced strength, speed and agility, to the point where she and Claw Noir proved superior during their two clashes against their heroic counterparts, though this could could be attribute to their unrestricted powers and their more aggressive nature. Despite her physical superiority however, Shadybug seemed less intelligent than her counterpart, as she was overall much more aggressive and wasn't able to realize Ladybug intentionally exposed herself.
Much like Ladybug, Shadybug also possessed the ability to summon Lucky Charms. Due to removed restrictions on her Miraculous however, Shadybug could summon as many as she liked, and unlike her counterpart, was able to use them to summon the exact items that she liked, generally being used to summon weapons or objects with the goal to cause harm. Shadybug could only summon one Lucky Charm at a time, but was able to disperse the object in order to create a new one, which she used to great effect.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Abilities
However, Shadybug's power came at a price. As a result of the safety restrictions being removed on her Miraculous (due to her using the Miraculous for evil), she suffered side effects as a result from using her Miraculous (shown as a series of black lines across her neck and face), alongside her partner Claw Noir. According to Shadybug, the effects were gradual, though Marinette attempting to summon Gimmi ended up accelerating the process, resulting in the affliction spreading to her face. It's unknown how the affliction affected Shadybug physically or what happened if it was complete, though according to her the use of their Miraculous Powers "will slowly destroy them". The affliction seemed to affect the user physically however, as both her and Claw Noir were able to feel the affliction when it was removed. Overall, the effects are similar to the effects caused by wearing a broken Miraculous.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Abilities
After her counterpart convinced her to use her powers for good and become a hero, Shadybug used the Miraculous Shadybug to restore the damage from their battle, resulting in the removal of the affliction infecting her and Claw Noir. Since she now uses her powers for good, it's unknown if she still possesses the ability to summon multiple Lucky Charms.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Trivia
In the original French dub, her supervillain name is Toxinelle, which is the combination of the words toxique ("toxic" or "poisonous") and coccinelle ("ladybug"), with her name literally meaning "toxic ladybug".
Being her a villainous counterpart of Marinette/Ladybug, Shadybug is the first known holder of the Ladybug Miraculous to be a supervillain, following Gabriel Agreste who had used it to become Monarch Bug for a brief moment and to summon Gimmi in "Re-creation".
The style of this version of Marinette in her civilian form matches the one of Juleka Couffaine from the main universe, with both having a gothic appearance (including using a dark eye shadow, black nail polish, fingerless lace gloves and rips on her pants), but also possessing bangs that cover part of the left side of her face, including her eye.
Her counterpart has a mother that is the opposite of the main where she's calm and gentle. This could mean that the family dynamics of the Re-Verse Agreste and Dupain-Cheng families are inverted.
When Shadybug tells Ladyfly that she doesn't have a boyfriend who think she's a loser, it's possible that she might've dated Kim in her world before he traumatized her love life.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Re-Verse - Trivia
In Adrien's case, it is shown that they are not dating seen in his amazed reaction to discovering that he was Claw Noir. However, she most likely knew him because his father still has an image of fame in this universe, but it is not known if they knew each other at school.
It's possible that this "boyfriend" could also be Luka, but considering that Juleka and Marinette probably don't know each other since she had no friends and Juleka may not have repeated a year in this universe, it's very likely that this isn't the case.
Shadybug is considered the villainous representation of Marinette in the Quantic Universe, serving as what would happened if she didn't stand up to Chloé Bourgeois in "Derision" and prior to origins, then Marinette would have become rageful and bitter.
After redeeming herself, she starts wearing her hair in pigtails as Ladybug, probably in honor of the Ladybug in the original universe. This is similar to how the latter started wearing them in honor of Socqueline Wang.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse - Intro
Marinette Dupain-Cheng is a minor character of "Miraculous Paris". She is an alternative version of Marinette Dupain-Cheng from a Giuliaverse, where she's also the main holder of the Ladybug Miraculous. When Tikki inhabits the Ladybug Miraculous, she transforms into Ladybug, a ladybug-themed superhero who gains the power of Creation.
In "Miraculous Paris", after Betterfly kamikotized Ladybug in her universe into Ladybiquity, this Ladybug was indirectly kamikotized as well into Ladybiquity, as Ladybiquity's power allowed her to connect herself with any of her counterparts in all the universes.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse - Appearance
Physical appearance
It possible that her civilian outfit might be different from what her main counterpart wears.
As Ladybug
She wears a red superhero jumpsuit covered in black spots and a black collar/turtleneck. When not in use, she keeps her yo-yo around her hips with a red string. On her face is a red mask with five black spots that are in a symmetrical design, and the waterlines of her eyes are colored black. Her earrings are red with five black spots in a quincunx pattern, and her hair is held back by red ribbons, resembling a ladybug's antennas or a ladybug flying.
As Ladybiquity

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse - Appearance
Ladybiquity wore a suit with traits from the Ladybug Miraculous and Ubiquity's. Her suit conjugated a contrast between magenta and purple with white dots. While her front and the back of her waist were magenta, the rest of her costume (her lower forearms, shoulders, lower legs and back) was purple. Her magenta mask covered her eyes with three white spots shrinking in size further down her face. Her hair was styled with two long twin tails with white hair ties protruding outwards, resembling a ladybug's antennas or a ladybug flying when she moved. She wore purple headphones with the ears covered by large round objects with white spots arranged in a quincunx pattern (her kamikotized Miraculous). She also had a clear purple cape attached to her arms and back.

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse - Abilities
As Ladybug
Like her Quantic Universe counterpart, Ladybug has enhanced physical abilities, such as speed and agility. Ladybug has remarkable talent with wielding her yo-yo, like using it as a grappling hook, a rope to restrain others, a projectile, a slicer even against solid materials, and a shield if she spins it fast enough.
Her special power, Lucky Charm, creates an object that helps her to achieve her goal, often being to stop a villain. Once the villain is dealt with, Ladybug can throw her Lucky Charm object into the air and use the Miraculous Ladybug, which will make it revert to an enormous swarm of ladybugs and fix all of the damage done since the villain appeared. She is also able to erase her Lucky Charm without using the Miraculous Ladybug.
As Ladybiquity

title: Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse
text:
Marinette Dupain-Cheng/Giuliaverse - Abilities
Ladybiquity's main power was the ability to be omnipresent in all the universes where she had a counterpart there. She did this by connecting to any of the counterparts and turning them into Ladybiquity. Once she did that, she could see, hear, talk and act through her counterparts. When she was in control, her counterparts had no idea what was happening, only regaining it once the real Ubiquity was not using their bodies.
Her second power was the ability to open portals between universes through her cape which became covered in stars, simulating an universe, when activated. By connecting herself with her counterparts, she could create a bridge between her world and her counterpart's. Since she could act through all her counterparts, she could open portals from and to any universe she desired.
Because she could act through all of her counterparts by turning them into her, her kamiko was also present in the same object of that counterpart, similar to when an akumatized villain used Multitude while holding their akumatized object, with the akuma being able to be freed by breaking only one of the cloned objects.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Intro
is a supporting character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. His mother is Claudie Kanté, a famous astronaut. He is a student at the Collège Françoise Dupont and a former student of Miss Bustier's class, before she became mayor of Paris.
In "Gamer", when he lost his place in the school video game tournament because of Marinette Dupain-Cheng, he was akumatized by Hawk Moth and became Gamer, a video game-themed supervillain who controlled a huge fighting robot.
In "Startrain", in order to save his mother, who was akumatized into the titular villain, and his friends, Max received the Horse Miraculous from Ladybug. When the Miraculous is inhabited by Kaalki, Max becomes Pegasus, a horse-themed superhero with the power of Migration who helps Ladybug and Cat Noir during "particularly difficult missions" in the third season and beyond.
In "Gamer 2.0", after being turned down by everybody to play his creative video game, Max was reakumatized into Gamer, with the new title of Gamer 2.0, getting a new ability to create a video game in real life.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Intro
After the events of "Strikeback", Max was temporarily unable to become Pegasus after Monarch managed to steal the Horse Miraculous along with all the others contained in the Chinese Miracle Box from Ladybug's yo-yo.
In "Re-creation", after Ladybug recovered the stolen Miraculous and reforged them following Monarch's defeat, Max was given back the Horse Miraculous permanently and reunited with Kaalki.
In "Revelator", it's shown that, after getting his Miraculous back, Max, along with the other secondary heroes of Ladybug's team, was trained to unlock his adult powers, no longer detransforming after using his power.
In "A Fairy Good Night", after Max's mother is accepted on a space mission that leaves her stuck in space for a few weeks. His friends offer for him to stay with them, and after a conversation with his psychiatrist, he chooses to stay with Marinette for a night as a form of training for when Claudie departs. Despite a few complications, by the end of the night he decides that if his mother ever leaves on a mission again, he will stay with Marinette during her absence.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Max is a short slender teenage boy, who has a medium-brown complexion, coily-kinky brown hair in a flattop that appears to have a slight tilt at left, and moderate tangelo eyes. He is the only male character in Miraculous with realistic eyelashes (all the others likely appear to be wearing eyeliner).
From Season 6 onwards, he seems to have horizontal shaved cuts at the side above his ears.
Civilian Attire
In the first five seasons, Max wore black-rimmed glasses with rectangular rims and a pale green dot at the left side, a light green collared button up shirt with three lighter tiny vertical buttons on the collar, and pale, light grayish gamboge and brown checkered jeans. He also has suspenders with a light brilliant tangelo line between two grayish amber lines and silver buckles in the middle and bottom, along with pale, light grayish cobalt blue sneakers with white sneakers and laces and a square-shaped blue watch on his right wrist. Up until "Re-creation", on occasion, he wore his Miraculous as glasses, with the lens clear and round with black frames.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Appearance
From Season 6 onwards, his attire is slightly different; he ditches his shirt for an identical long-sleeved one, except it is now layered with a closed dark green cardigan, tucked into his now solid light gamboge jeans. His suspenders also switch their coloring, now having two light, brilliant tangelo lines and a wide amber grayish line in the middle, with the coloring after the buckles being dark brown. His watch is now silver and his glasses, which now also double as his Miraculous, have a half-transparent frame and become rectangles, the rims being at the top half of the lenses.
As Pegasus

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Appearance
In Seasons 3-5, his hair was longer and turned light brownish gray, braided in multiple locks that were tied back with a small dark brown hairband that likely resembled a horse's tail, and his sides of his sported an undercut. His costume was deep brown high-mandarin-collared. He had grayish tangelo outlines around his torso, abdomen, and at the sides of his hips with an angular shape. He also had dark grayish vermillion bracelets and anklets in a V-shape with grayish tangelo trimming, accented by thick angular lines going diagonally around his thighs and around his shoulders, as well as two round-ended straps around the sides of his torso with a dot in the middle, all of which had the same trimming. He had a light gray small horseshoe on his neck, acting as a zipper. The Horseshoe was on his upper back when not in use. He also had sneakers with two light beige angular linings above the sole and two pointed pieces at the sides to accent the straps on his torso, resembling the wings Hermes has on his sandals. His glasses also turned black and circular with five teal dots in the bottom right corner of the right lens.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Appearance
From Season 6 onwards, his hair sports even longer braids, tied into two sections with multiple dark brown hairbands, and the shorter braids flare out on the back of his head to resemble a horse's tail more.
His bodysuit sports two shades of brown, one shade being darker than the other.
The lighter-shaded part is made of thicker material and pads mostly on the front of his torso, shoulders, and sides to accent his dark grayish vermillion details.
His front now has a grayish tangelo V-shaped line in the middle and a zipline.
The zipper turns into a circular gray pendant with a dark brown emblem of the Horse Miraculous on top, left partially unzipped.
The grayish tangelo outlines lessen, leaving only two on his each side of his waist with dark grayish vermillion bordering.
His bracelets lengthen into longer ones with more square-like angular tips, worn with deep brown gloves that have a small strap like the ones on his torso with lighter lining, and around the top of the hand is a dark grayish vermillion color for the rest of the palms and fingers.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Appearance
His anklets are more boot-like, going past his calves, and each side of his sneakers only have one wing instead of two, as well as the lining altering to become light beige souls with a thin line on top that keeps the angular shapes, but with a dark grayish vermillion heel in the back.
His glasses turn into visors with a thick brown frame and large green lens.
The light point went from circular to rectangular with one being long and the other 4 are small rectangles, all of them have a lighter shade than the lens.
As Gamer
Gamer had grayish purple skin and vivid amaranth eyes. His glasses became angular, large, and butterfly-shaped, and the glass had a light green tint. He wore a black skin-tight bodysuit with a head cover over his head that also bore the shape of his hair, albeit it looked solid and had a slight tilt to the left, and it also covered his neck. He had a small green circle on his chest and three thin green stripes around his waist, each forearm, and each lower leg.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Personality
Max is a gamer and a fan of technology. He is smart, especially when it comes to mathematics, as seen when he figures out how fast Kim needs to be to make it to Pont des Arts right before Chloé Bourgeois gets there in "Dark Cupid". He tends to be carried away with his knowledge, often over-explaining things with further detail than necessary and occasionally revealing something that was supposed to be a secret. Max is also friendly, helping his friends with knowledge and support.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Personality
Due to his autism, Max can get visibly upset when something disrupts his state of mind or everyday life. He gives examples of how tardiness, forgetfulness and getting lost can cause slight distress to him. He also finds it difficult to understand certain social cues, like when people are upset or when they are joking. Due to finding comfort in order and predictability, all of his everyday life is carefully planned, from the time he does his tasks to the little rituals that go along with them, like drinking from a special bowl of his or sitting on a specific seat on the tram. He even finds comfort in his own friends' predictability. To better deal with any disruption of his everyday life, Max developed a few defensive mechanisms, like always carrying a heart-shaped piece of paper given to him by his mother and rubbing it whenever he feels distressed. Thanks to his visits to Dr. Psiquat, Max has also come to learn how to better handle with the distress his autism causes to him and find solutions or whenever he has a personal problem he can't understand or solve.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Personality
He's also incredibly organized and has a great sense of responsibility, two traits heavily showcased throughout "A Fairy Good Night", where it is shown that he has a time and specific routine for everything in his life. When staying at Marinette's for a night because of his mother's absence, he felt uncomfortable at her overeagerness to try and help him, making him doubt if he would feel comfortable staying with her. However, after he is affected by an akumatized villain, a dream Claudie attempts to convince him to stay at home he almost accepts but an alert from Ladybug, reminds him of his responsibility to save Paris, prompting him choose to adapt to the changes instead of staying in comfort.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Personality
Another example of his autism is also seen in "Gamer", when he loses his place in the competition for which he trained a whole year. The sudden disruption of his plans to join the competition caused Max to not deal well with defeat. Despite he sportingly congratulates Marinette and Adrien, once outside, he starts rambling to himself about how unfair his situation was, and it isn't until after his akumatization and Marinette offering up her spot to him in the competition that he perks up. As seen also in "Gamer 2.0", although he isn’t the best sport when it comes to losing, he still favors playing with someone else over playing alone, so he can get upset when none of his friends had time to play with him, especially when it's a game made by him.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Personality
As Pegasus, Max is also brave as well as shown to be very polite and works well with others seen in "Party Crasher". He is also very eficient as a Horse Miraculous holder, being very precise with his portals. Even when under quite a bit of stress, he can be quite precise. Thanks to that, he becomes an essential part of the team, as he becomes the key for many of the traps Ladybug prepares for the akumatized villains and to save a large number of civilians, either by evacuating them or protect them from any falling debris. He becomes more loose with his traditions shown when he decided to give the Magical Charm to the victim in A Fairy Goodnight instead of Ladybug.
As Gamer, he stopped at nothing to show everyone that he was the best gamer, even turning people into experience points that helped him level up. Additionally, the resentment he held towards Marinette turned into hatred, resulting in him specifically targeting her for a brief period. He also puts his vast experience as a gamer to its full use, like when he respawned his robot after Cat Noir destroyed it by saving his last level.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Personality
In "Gamer 2.0", however, he shows a slightly different demeanor than his first akumatization. Despite still taking full advantage of the rules of the game as well the perks of being both the creator and final boss, his primary objective is not winning the game, but rather play it with others and have them enjoy playing his game. Because of this, he shows a great deal of joy for seeing Ladybug and Cat Noir engaging with his game and also a much humble demeanor when admitting defeat, especially after his opponent is able to trick him in his own game.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Abilities
As a Civilian
Max is very intelligent, being excellent at knowing facts, statistics, and calculations. He is also very skilled in playing video games and he has one of the highest scores in the entire school at playing Ultimate Mecha Strike III.
Max's intelligence was shown in his inventions that are revealed in "Robostus": an anti-virus flash drive and Markov, a highly-functional robot that has developed emotions on its own. Max is even capable of creating his own video game based on the akumatized villains.
As Pegasus
Pegasus has enhanced capabilities such as speed, agility, and strength, and he is almost invulnerable to physical damage. These abilities allow him to react to and evade akumatized villains attacks, as well as jump and leap several times his height and length. He is also very skilled at utilizing the Horseshoe during close combat. Pegasus can also perceive which targets he can throw the Horseshoe at like a boomerang, in a way similar to how Ladybug visualizes her solutions.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Abilities
His special power, Voyage, allows him to open a portal that he can travel through and exit at any location he desires. This is a highly versatile ability, making Pegasus useful in virtually any team configuration.
Initially, using his power would depower him and cause him to detransform after 5 minutes, however, in "Revelator", Pegasus has learned to control his adult powers, allowing him to not detransform back and use Voyage as much as he wishes, allowing him to open multiple portals and use them in a variety of ways⁏ such as protecting himself from villain attacks or safely evacuating large numbers of people from dangerous areas.
As Gamer
As Gamer, he piloted a giant fighting robot designed after MX-01 from Ultimate Mecha Strike III. The robot could shoot a laser beam that would transform any people and vehicle it hit into floating green orbs that serve as experience points. By absorbing these experience points the robot would level up.
Level 1: A simple floating black pyramid with a green eye.
Level 2: Added two tall tentacle-like legs.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Abilities
Level 3: The robot became more human-like and it gained the power to perform special moves, such as firing electricity and missiles, creating a force field, and spinning like a drill.
Level 4: The final level, but its form was never seen.
Gamer was able to "save his last level" and respawn the robot if it got destroyed.
As Gamer 2.0
Gamer 2.0 controlled a massive pyramid, which was a real world video game inside. The game pitted player against player and the playable avatars were past akumatized supervillains.
After each fight, both the winning avatars' akumatized object and the losing avatars' akumatized object were added to the winning players arsenal where they could later be selected as a power-up in the final battle, giving the player access to those villains' superpowers. During the final battle, Gamer 2.0, due to being both the creator and the final boss, can change into any of the previous supervillains, even those that he lost to his adversaries.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Etymology
Max's name is of Latin origin and means "Greatest".
In the Irish dub, his name is changed to Marcás; Irish for Marcus.
His family is from Mali, although the ethnic group is unknown.
In the French dub, his superhero name is "Pegase" which is French for Pegasus.
Max's superhero name stems from a mythical creature called Pegasus which is a winged horse from Greek Mythology.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Trivia
Miraculous Holder and Akumatized Villain
A scarlet version of Gamer reappeared in the two-part special event "Heroes' Day".
A statue of Gamer appears in the Musée Grévin in "The Puppeteer 2".
Following Alya Césaire, Nino Lahiffe, Chloé Bourgeois, Nathalie Sancoeur, and Luka Couffaine, he is the sixth person to become a Miraculous holder and akumatized villain, excluding Gabriel Agreste, who akumatized himself.
He and Carapace are the only Miraculous holders who wears glasses and keep them even after transformation.
This is due to the fact that the Horse Miraculous are said glasses.
He is the only member of team that doesn't wear a mask due to the Horse Miraculous being a pair of glasses but wasn't the first Miraculous holder to be seen without a mask.
Max is the first member of the team that doesn't give himself a superhero name. Instead, he was called Pegasus by Ladybug.
He is actually that third person of African origins to wield a Miraculous succeeding his Miraculous predecessor Mudekudeku who wielded the Ladybug Miraculous and his friend Carapace.

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Trivia
As seen in "Mr. Pigeon 72", Max has been akumatized into Gamer four times. ("Gamer", "Catalyst", "Gamer 2.0" and one off-screen akumization).
In "Miraculous: Rise of the Sphinx", after Clonika's Clones of his friends mocked his newly created game before his face, he was reakumatized into Gamer again, this time under title Gamer 3.0, getting the ability to merge Paris with his game and be able to reprogram it at will.
Miscellaneous
In "The Bubbler" and "Lady Wifi", Max appears without glasses.
Thomas Astruc noted the instance in the former episodes as an animation mistake.
In his first appearances in the Korean musical Ladybug, Max wears a different outfit, which includes a purple t-shirt with white lettering printed on the front underneath a green and black plaid hooded jacket.
In later performances, Max's outfit is mostly identical to his show appearance, excluding his glasses and including a black hat.
On Twitter, Miraculous creator Thomas Astruc confirmed that Max is asexual, meaning he  experiences little to no sexual attraction stating "On va dire que Max est plutôt ace et Alix plutôt aro..." meaning "We will say that Max is kind of ace and Alix kind of aro...".

title: Max Kanté
text:
Max Kanté - Trivia
In "Risk", it is revealed that Max does not know how to swim.
In "Wreckless Driver", Max is revealed to be autistic as he mentioned his visits to Dr. Psiquat.
In "A Fairy Good Night", it is shown that Max's autism overlaps with OCD as well, as his everyday tasks are done at a very precise time which normally has the hours and minutes matching exactly, he has very particular rituals he can't possibly stop doing, has everything neatly placed and is very particular on certain things, like always drinking from a special bowl and seating on the same seat on the tram.

title: Marlena Césaire
text:
Marlena Césaire - Intro
is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. She is the head chef of the restaurant in Le Grand Paris and the mother of Alya, Ella, Etta, and Nora Césaire. Starting from season 6, she is also the cook at the cafeteria and the culinary instructor at Collège Françoise Dupont alongside Nora.
In "The Dirtifiers", it is revealed that Marlena is pregnant with a baby girl and is preparing a nursery.

title: Marlena Césaire
text:
Marlena Césaire - Appearance
Physical appearance
Marlena is short and has brown skin. Her eyes and hair are brown, with the hair pulled up into a bun. She wears brilliant pink lipstick.
From season 6 onwards, she now wears eyeshadow, white pearl earrings, and a silver bracelet on her right arm.
Civilian attire
While on the job, Marlena wears a white chef jacket with three white buttons on each side of the front, light blue pants, and white tennis shoes. She also occasionally wears a tall chef's hat with "Le Grand Paris" embroidered on it in gold.
Outside of work, she wears a moderate raspberry/strong red tunic with luminous vivid gold trimming, very dark azure pants and black slip-on shoes.
From season 6 onwards, she wears a red tunic with colorful trimming and a white undershirt.

title: Marlena Césaire
text:
Marlena Césaire - Personality
Marlena is kind, calm, soft-spoken and considerate. In "Rogercop", when she explains that she didn't bring any food samples from the restaurant like Marinette's father did from his bakery, she jokingly says that perhaps the owner of Le Grand Paris, André Bourgeois, would invite them to have lunch at the hotel. Her kindness is also shown in "Kung Food" when, as a judge of The World's Greatest Chef, she gently tells Wang Cheng that his soup, which was ruined by Chloé Bourgeois, isn't good, unlike the other judges who were far less tactful.
She is also brave, as she was willing to take on Scarlet Moth's army of akumas despite having no powers of her own, and highly supportive of the heroes, cheering them on and putting absolute faith in them to succeed.

title: Marlena Césaire
text:
Marlena Césaire - Abilities
Being the head chef of a five-star hotel's kitchen, Marlena possesses considerable cooking and leadership skills in both preparing food and overseeing the kitchen staff in said preparation.

The book cover has the title in white text at the top and black algebra equations scattered throughout the rest. title: Max's flash drive
text:
Max's flash drive - Intro
is an anti-virus flash drive that Max Kanté and Markov created together.

title: Max's flash drive
text:
Max's flash drive - Appearance
The drive is blue with a round end with a white button, the other end with the USB connector. A blue round-tipped detachable lid covers the connector when the drive isn't connected to a device. On one side, there is a black measure bar with dark gray lines is on one side, the measure going from red to green depending on how full the drive is.

Marinette: (writing/narrating) Dear Diary: remember when Tikki got sick not so long ago? Since I didn't know how to heal a kwami, Tikki had given me the address of a vet.
Master Fu: What type of cat did you say?
Marinette: Cat? Um, right! A rare hairless flying species from Kingdom of Achu?

Marinette: (narrating) But it turns out he wasn't really a vet.

Marinette: (narrating) Tikki formally introduced me to him today.

Marinette: (narrating) Remember the old man I saved as he was crossing the street back on my first day of school? That was actually some kind of test to see if I was worthy of becoming the new Ladybug. Master Fu is incredible; he's 186 and a half. Can you believe it? He's still very agile, though.

title: Master Fu/Transcript
