title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Intro
is one of the four deuteragonists (alongside Tikki, Plagg and Alya Césaire) of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is a former student in Miss Bustier's class at Collège Françoise Dupont and Adrien Agreste's best friend. He is currently in a relationship with Alya Césaire. He is also a DJ and the head of the school radio.
In "The Bubbler", when Nino became frustrated with adults after failing to convince Gabriel Agreste to allow Adrien to have a birthday party, he was akumatized into the Bubbler, a bubble-wielding supervillain.
In "Anansi", after Alya and Cat Noir were captured by the titular villain, Nino received the Turtle Miraculous from Ladybug. When the Miraculous is inhabited by Wayzz, Nino becomes Carapace, a turtle-themed superhero with the power of Protection who helps Ladybug and Cat Noir "during particularly difficult missions" in the second season and beyond.
In "Mayura", during the fight with Scarlet Moth, Rena Rouge was akumatized while protecting Carapace. In his grief, he was akumatized into Shell Shock, a turtle-themed supervillain.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Intro
In "Oblivio", due to his and Alya's embarrassment at being caught playing the Super Penguino video game together, he was akumatized alongside her into Oblivio, a single entity and a memory-erasing supervillain.
In "Rocketear", after coming to believe that Alya was cheating on him with Cat Noir, Nino was akumatized into Rocketear, a supervillain with the power to cry exploding tears. He also revealed to Adrien that he is Carapace, and received a Magical Charm from Ladybug that prevented him from being reakumatized.
After the events of "Strikeback", Nino was temporarily unable to become Carapace after Monarch managed to steal the Turtle Miraculous along with all the others contained in the Chinese Miracle Box from Ladybug's yo-yo.
In "Illusion", in order to continue helping Ladybug and Cat Noir fight Monarch following the loss of his Miraculous, Nino formed the Resistance, a group of inactive Miraculous holders with the mission to support the main heroes however possible, even without superpowers.
In "Re-creation", after Ladybug recovered the stolen Miraculous and reforged them following Monarch's defeat, Nino was given back the Turtle Miraculous permanently and reunited with Wayzz.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Intro
In "Revelator", it's shown that, after getting his Miraculous back, Nino, along with the other secondary heroes of Ladybug's team, was trained to unlock his adult powers, no longer detransforming after using his power.
In "The Chained Titans", it is revealed that Nino has a difficult home life because of his parents' constant arguing. After being troubled by a friendly dispute between Marinette and Adrien, he suggests that he and Alya lend them their Miraculous temporarily to strengthen their relationship. However, when his parents are akumatized, Marinette and Adrien are forced to return the Miraculous. After his parents are deakumatized, they decide on an amicable divorce.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Nino is a tall, slender Moroccan-African teenage boy with short dark brown hair, light rakuda tan skin, and moderate orange eyes. He lacked bangs in the first five seasons.
From Season 6 onwards, Nino's hair is slightly longer and has now gained curls at the front. He appears to have gained some muscle.
Civilian Attire
In the first five seasons, Nino wore a plain red cap, used black-rimmed wayfarer glasses, and often had a pair of black headphones with orange ear cushions, vivid azure lining at the sides, and matching-colored zigzags with duplicated orange ones on top of them on the speakers hung around his neck.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
He typically wore a vivid azure t-shirt with an eye design on the front (a design involving a black pupil, white sclera, a dark gray upper eyelid with three lashes, the adjacent ones diagonal and the center one straight, and a light blue lower lid). Around his moderate azure jeans was a brown belt, and while most of it was hidden by his shirt, one tip stuck out a little bit below the hem. Additionally, he wore lime green, pink, red, blue, and yellow wristbands around his right wrist, and white high collar sneakers with intricate red accents, tongues, and toe caps, as well as white laces and a white knight design on the tongues that are lined in white.
On occasion, up until "Re-creation", he wore the Turtle Miraculous around his right wrist, which was the same model as its charged mode in a light mint color.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
From Season 6 onwards, Nino wears a white shirt underneath a blue hoodie, which has short white drawstrings and the same eye design in the middle of the torso as his past shirt, and his hoodie is similar to his re-verse counterpart. His sleeves are rolled up to just below the upper arms. His headphones are now white at the headband, with black circular tabs in the middle at the sides, and the speakers are now a solid black lined by a tangerine ring, as well as a small tangerine bar in front of the outer black border, and the ear cushions remain the same. At the front is a black strap crossing at the left where a dark blue backpack rests behind Nino's back.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
His wristbands now consist of plain yellow, beaded black-and-blue, beaded white-and-pink with Alya's name carved on it, red zigzag-striped with a silver strap, and green shiny ones on the right. At the left are beaded yellow-tangerine-and-sky blue, white polka dotted teal-yellow, purple and lilac wavy-patterned, and beaded green-and-forest green ones. His jeans are now charcoal gray with large pockets at the sides, as well as more simplified sneakers that remain white, but with a red upside-down triangle on the tongue's top, a red strap in the middle, and red lining at the bottom with a rectangular section at the side, and white soles with additional black accents connecting to the straps and around the back of the foot. His cap and glasses are retained.
His Miraculous also alters in its camouflage mode; it is now made of beaded patchwork consisting of a thick black line in the middle with a pattern consisting of white diamonds and dots, the diamonds' insides being lime with a red ring and yellow circle in the middle, and white lining at the top and bottom of the wristband, with a bronze hexagon on top lined in silver.
As Carapace

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
In Seasons 2-5, Carapace had a deep green jumpsuit with a hood over his head, the suit itself made with tiny hexagonal patterns resembling those on the Turtle Miraculous. The hood had a dark olive half at the bottom, thick curved forest green triangular stripes at the sides with yellow lining, two pale dullish green curved designs at their front that straightened at the tip and connected to vermillion arrow-shaped accents at the back, and two small light green ovals below the bottom of the hood's opening with a gray round segment on top of the opening.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
Over his eyes, Carapace wore black goggles with yellow-green lenses, and underneath the suit, he had a black collar. On said suit, he had five hexagon-shaped light green circles on his chest, which had two lined horizontally stacked on top of one another below, and another horizontal pair followed by one last triangular point at the bottom, all of which were lined in dark olive. He had dark olive hexagon-shaped protective pads on his shoulders, elbows, hips, and knees with two dots in each of their centers. He also had dark olive accents on his wrists consisting of a V-shaped line on his left wrist, and a short, handless glove where the Turtle Miraculous, which was dark mint with very light shell designs, was on his right wrist.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
Around his hip armor were dark olive lines consisting of a V-shaped one at the top just below the abdomen, and the bottom lines angularly reached down to the thighs vertically, then wrapped around the back diagonally. Also, Carapace wore deep green boots with an indent between his big toe and other toes, dark gray outsoles, and scalloped trimming on top of the tongue and sides, and bright green linear accents consisting of a hexagonal-like one circling the foot, one angular one reaching the top vertically at the back, and another stripe following it behind. On his back, he carried a turtle-like shield that was dark green on one side and light green on the other.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
From Season 6 onwards, Carapace's costume undergoes some changes. Statically, the costume remains the same, with it being still a jumpsuit with a hood (which keeps the ovals at the bottom on the front below the bottom of the opening, but they are now orange holes with a silver border and forest green inside, the accents on the sides turning orange with a thick tangerine stripe in the middle and black lining at the top and bottom, and the bottom half of the hood becomes shorter into a wide hexagonal section with a lime trapezoidal tab on top, and the accent on the top of the hood's opening now has lining connecting to the bottom half of the hood) and retaining the hexagon-shaped protective pads on his shoulders, elbows, hips, and knees, changing mostly only on the color scheme.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
The suit is dark green on most of the torso, the bottom side of the hood, on his forearms, front side of his upper-arms, outer sides of the thighs and legs, and hands, and is green on the fingers, the ventral area, the rest of the hood, the back side of his upper-arms and the inner sides of the thighs, all of which are done in a hexagonal-like fashion. Both shades are divided by an outlined lighter shade of green. His boots also get a dark shade of green at their downward-pointing tips and the back heel and a bright green circular detail on the middle of the sole, as well as matching rectangular lining at the sides and on top of the now split, sharper soles with a rectangular part in the middle of the tongue trimmed with bright green. He now has a thick green line in the middle of his wrists lined with bright green and a hexagonal point on top where an embossed light green hexagon is, as well as where his altered Miraculous is on the right wrist, which is now secured in a dark green hexagonal tab beneath the hexagon, the symbol of the Miraculous placed on top in a mint color with a head and legs to resemble its animal more.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
He no longer has goggles, having instead a dark green hood-like mask that covers his chin with a tiny rectangular part on top and the top half of his face with orange tinged lenses over his eyes. The circles on his chest are now embossed. His hip armor also turns into metallic dark green pieces that coil around the hips with hexagonal tips and a green line in the middle. On his back, he has the symbol of the Turtle Miraculous.
As the Bubbler
The Bubbler had light brilliant arctic blue skin, dark amaranth eyes with shrunken irises, and black circles around his eyes, along with a black spot above his left eye and another spot below his right eye. He wore a luminous vivid red, arctic blue, and yellow elbow-length sleeved tunic with many parts of the suit being rounded like attached bubbles, which matched his leg warmers. Around his head, he had a red hood-like thing that featured an antenna on top with a sphere. Also, he wore black boots, black elbow-length gloves with luminous vivid red knuckles, and black pants.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
On his chest, he had an eye-like design composed of a white circle with a black pupil and thick dark red bordering around the eyelid with two dark gray tubes attached. The tubes connected to the Bubbler's yellow bubble container that had a red stripe at the top with black lining and a blue lid, where he put his bubble wand when he wasn't using it. His bubble wand had a blue handle and a yellow head with a long, oval-shaped hole.
As Shell Shock
In "Mayura", Shell Shock had the same appearance as his superhero counterpart except for being red all over, as well as the lenses of his goggles and shield owing to him having been taken over by a Scarlet Akuma. His appearance resulting from a normal akuma is unknown.
As Oblivio

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
Oblivio was a purple faceless silhouette with an orchid glowing outline, standing at a tall height with a muscular build. They had a light silver laser cannon with light lavender highlights and a pale purple rectangular light on top with dark purple energy inside in their left hand that shot memory-erasing beams, and a gray glove on their right hand with orchid markings across the wrist down to the palm vertically with a black oval-shaped pad on top, and orchid tips at the index and middle fingers, and on the palm.
As Rocketear

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Appearance
As Rocketear, Nino's entire skin tone became a light cornflower blue tint. His head (which may also have been a helmet) was shaped like a teardrop, with a pale, light grayish azure front and black back, with the black part curling over his cheek onto the front of his face. On the pale, light grayish cerulean part of his helmet was a blue teardrop lined in white. Over his eyes, replacing his glasses, were blue visors with white lining, and his eyes were brilliant cerulean. Rocketear seemed to be wearing what looked like a light cerulean supervillain jumpsuit with pale, light grayish cerulean hands to match his feet. His costume was swan-necked with the black part covering his neck beneath. On his shoulders, waist, thighs, hands, feet, and elbows were black teardrops with a light blue outline, with a bigger one on the chest. There was a black square on each of his gloves. There was also very thin white lines circling above the chest, around the muscles down to the sides of the waist, and down past the thighs to the back of the body.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
Nino is a fun-loving, enthusiastic, charismatic, sociable, and compassionate boy whose friendly attitude allows him to get along well with others. He's quite informal when interacting with people, including those of certain social standing. He has proven to be one of the most sociable members of his social circle and can make friends easily. True to how Marinette Dupain-Cheng's description in the webisode of the same name, Nino is a music lover who listens to music everywhere he goes with his headphones on. He enjoys being a DJ at parties and television events, being a a fun-loving by organizing events to have fun with his friends. He's a film buff, directing his class's film projects and aspiring to become a film director when he grows up. Nino also seems to be very attached to his fashion sense, as seen in "Chameleon", when he gets flustered because the titular villain steals his signature red cap.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
When it comes to his loved ones, Nino is brave and loyal, being very affectionate and attentive to them. He has a strong protective instinct towards those he cares about and refuses to leave them in dangerous situations, even if it means putting himself at risk, which leads Ladybug to choose him as the holder of the Turtle Miraculous. He is a source of support and comfort to his friends, especially Adrien Agreste, who, attending school for the first time and becoming his best friend, he guides through school life and does what he can to comfort or encourage him through the problems he has with his distant father. Nino doesn't tolerate anyone threatening his girlfriend Alya Césaire, willing to confront akumatized villains for her well-being, as shown in "Anansi", where despite being outmatched by the fighting skills of the titular villain, he fought against her to save Alya. He also has a close relationship with his younger brother Chris and cares deeply for him, running all over the city to find him in "Christmaster".

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
Although Nino usually appears self-confident, sometimes he can be very insecure and worried about disappointing others. In "Guilttrip", it is revealed that Nino feels guilty for not being able to help Adrien confront his father, with the implication that he considers himself a horrible friend for it. He's afraid of ruining his relationship with Alya, feeling the need to prove himself to his girlfriend and fearing that she will leave him. In "Rocketear", after noticing that Alya was evasive and kept secrets, not to mention her apparent attention to Cat Noir, combined with a scene from a film where Rena Rouge is seduced by Cat Noir's flirtatious behavior, Nino comes to suspect that there may be something between them and follows Alya to confirm his suspicions. This insecurity on his part leads him to misunderstand the situation and to believe that they are together, resulting in him being akumatized into the titular villain.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
His insecurities around relationships are expanded upon in "The Chained Titans". Wherein it is revealed that his own parents have an extremely tumultuous and toxic relationship, constantly arguing over the simplest decisions. A situation that created an extreme avoidance of conflict in him; he often uses his music to block the sound of their arguing. Not only that, but his parents have also affected the way his relationships work, demonstrated when he hid his dislike for strawberries to avoid disagreeing with Alya. His fear of romantic conflicts can escalate so much that even witnessing a discussion between a couple could make him extremely anxious. Shown when he recklessly suggested he and Alya lend their Miraculouses to Marinette and Adrien over a small disagreement the latter had.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
He freely expresses his thoughts and values ​​sincerity, especially in his relationships. Nino hates secrets and hiding things from his loved ones or them hiding things from him, becoming visibly upset when he realizes that his friends are not sincere. If Nino has a vision for something, he stays dedicated to it, sometimes rather stubbornly, becoming exasperated or annoyed if things don't go in the fashion he wants them to. He's more than willing to argue his points to defend his opinions, which can make him impulsive and cause him to make mistakes while trying to prove he's right, though he is able to change his opinions on situations or particular people. While he has good intentions, his methods for achieving his goals can sometimes make him insensitive, as seen in "Illusion", where he chooses to humiliate Gabriel in the middle of a parent-teacher meeting in order to akumatize him and discover how Monarch transfers the Miraculous powers to the akumatized villains. But he refuses to cross the line and hurt others, being willing to stop and apologize if things get out of control, demonstrating that he has no qualms about apologizing when he's wrong.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
Nino has a powerful sense of justice, becoming frustrated if he sees something he considers unfair or wrong. He has a strong aversion to bullies and abusers, refusing to let them get away with their bad actions. He detests the distant way Adrien's father treats him and doesn't hide his displeasure with Gabriel's behavior toward his son, as shown in "The Bubbler" where he criticizes Gabriel for not allowing Adrien a birthday party. He doesn't hesitate to reprimand Chloé Bourgeois, and later Raymond Pugnant, Loïc Stompet and Nelson de Glusset, for tormenting and hurting other students for fun or out of indifference. With and without his powers as Carapace, Nino retains his loyalty and willingness to help the heroes of Pars, creating the Resistance in season five to help Ladybug and Cat Noir fight against Monarch, demonstrating some leadership ability by guiding the Resistance to fight against Chloé's tyranny in "Revolution", and in the battle against the Miraculized army in  "Conformation" and "Re-creation".

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
As Carapace, most of Nino's personality remains the same, leading Alya to recognize him as Nino when she meets him as a superhero. Similar to his civilian self, he is informal in his way of speaking and always willing to help others, being a team player during missions. Like a turtle, Carapace is calm and focused, following Ladybug's instructions flawlessly and using his powers quickly and ingeniously to ensure the safety of his teammates and the citizens. However, knowing that his girlfriend is Rena Rouge (temporarily Rena Furtive), he can become impulsive during battles when she is in danger. He is also somewhat open about his identity as Carapace, revealing it to Adrien and Marinette as they are his best friends, without knowing that the latter is actually Ladybug.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
As the Bubbler, he became less caring and more aggressive, being much wilder and louder than normal. Although one of his intentions was to let Adrien have the birthday party that he never got, he also despised adults and used his powers to get rid of them, ignoring the fact that Hawk Moth was an adult himself. His hatred could extend to his peers if they defied his orders. If anyone didn't listen to him, they got trapped in a bubble. His rage even proved to be an issue for Hawk Moth when he trapped Ladybug and Cat Noir and sent them into the sky instead of taking their Miraculouses.
As Shell Shock, his personality as Carapace seemed to inverse, making him cruel and aggressive.
As Oblivio, he and Alya became incredibly arrogant and conceited in their own abilities, erasing people's memories on a whim and taunting Ladybug and Cat Noir constantly after doing the same thing to them. However, they were easily frustrated as well, growing angrier and angrier while trying and failing to track down Ladybug and Cat Noir after they detransformed.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Personality
As Rocketear, he was vengeful towards Cat Noir for what he believed was Alya cheating on him with Cat Noir. He also cared about others who cared about him such as Adrien and Alya, who weren't considered his enemies. He tried to destroy Cat Noir mainly, rather than get the Miraculouses or destroy Ladybug. However, when Ladybug stopped him from causing any more harm to Cat Noir, he then aimed to destroy her as well until he saw the video he recorded being projected with the audio being added by Rena Furtive without him knowing. This caused him to let go of his vengeance and reject Shadow Moth's akumatization.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Abilities
As a Civilian
Nino is a skilled DJ, competing with his abilities and making it to the second round of The Challenge. He quickly developed great acrobatic skills even in his civilian form, demonstrating decent fighting abilities and good coordination while dancing with Alya. Aspiring to become a film director, he leads the film projects in his class. He is also knowledgeable in film tropes and film crew, noting how cell phones don't usually work in horror movies and mentioning Hollywood director Steven Basielberg.
In season five, Nino has shown to have skilled leadership: he built The Resistance against Monarch from the ground up, from finding Monarch's true identity, to helping the civilians from the effects of the akumatized villains. Nino came up with very thorough but risky plans, but they ended with great results.
As Carapace

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Abilities
Carapace has enhanced capabilities such as speed, agility, and strength, and he is almost invulnerable to physical damage. These abilities allow him to react to and evade akumatized villains attacks, as well as jump and leap several times his height and length. His tool is a shield that can easily be thrown and used to fight and is strong enough to endure hits from powerful villains. It also functions as a communication device and a skateboard for transportation.
His special power, Shell-ter, is executed through his shield, and allows him to create a giant green shell-like spherical barrier/force field to protect himself and others, and is also able to damage particular surfaces, as well as trapping his opponents. In "Revelator" it is shown that Carapace has learned to control his adult powers, allowing him to not detransform back and use Shell-ter as much as he wishes.
As the Bubbler
With his bubble wand weapon, the Bubbler could create giant impenetrable bubbles with various powers and colors.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Abilities
Purple bubbles could be used to chase and capture people, turning green. Additionally, the Bubbler could use them to project his face and give a message, and he could stand on them to levitate.
Red bubbles were his offensive attack: he could throw them at his enemies, causing a fiery explosion on impact. Additionally, the Bubbler could turn existing red bubbles into swarming green ones that attached to people and morphed into a giant green bubble. This was used to catch both Ladybug and Cat Noir in one go.
He was unable to levitate in mid-air without standing on a bubble, but he could jump very high and can fly from one place to another leaving a trail of purple bubbles.
His bubbles couldn't be penetrated by limbs or by Ladybug's yo-yo. However, the shields Ladybug and Cat Noir created by rotating their weapons did offer some protection. Additionally, the bubbles could be blown away by air currents and could be burst by Cataclysm and the Miraculous Ladybug.
As Shell Shock
Shell Shock still had enhanced skills and wielded the same weapon as Carapace. However, any further abilities as Shell Shock are currently unknown.
As Oblivio

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Abilities
Oblivio had super strength and wielded a laser cannon that could fire a blast of purple energy that caused whoever it hit to lose their memories. Oblivio was invulnerable to physical attacks, which phased right through them.
As Rocketear
Rocketear was able to create tears from his visors and shoot them at his opponent. Once the person aimed for was touched by the tears, they will immediately be pushed to a far-off distance. However, if his tears touched an object, they would cause a massive explosion around its area. He was also able to charge a short beam of energy, which had the same affect as his tears.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Etymology
Nino's name is a wordplay on "No life" - or rather, Nolife - a French TV network about pop culture, self-described as "for geeks, nerds and otakus". This refers to his geeky personality.
Carapace means a "protective shell", which is an apt description of his special power when using the Turtle Miraculous.
It is also the technical name for a turtle's backshell.
In the Serbian dub, his superhero name Carapace is changed to Karapaks.
Shell Shock is a terminology used for psychologically traumatized soldiers from World War I, although it's most likely a pun on the words "shell", due to him using the Turtle Miraculous, and "shock", due to how shocked Carapace was when Rena Rouge was akumatized.
In the Italian dub, Shell Shock's name is changed to Caraguerra. It's a pun on his superhero name "Carapace" and "guerra", which means "war", as "pace" means "peace" in Italian, the exact opposite of war, hence the wordplay.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Etymology
In the Brazillian Portuguese dub, Shell Shock's name was changed to Casca Grossa, which means literally "tough shell". The term can mean "a person who's very resilient", refering to the idea of Carapace being the Hero of Protection, but can also mean "someone who's rude and poorly-mannered", refering to his brutal, mean nature as an akumatized villain.
When Nino and Alya become Oblivio, their supervillain name is a pun on the word oblivious.
Alternatively, it might come from the word 'oblivion' in reference of their power of erasing memories.
The word "tear" from "Rocketear" may be a reference to Nino using his explosive powers through his tears. However, the name is also a reference to the superhero Rocketeer from the eponymous 1982 movie,

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Trivia
Revealed by the Staff
An earlier concept design for Nino involved a white shirt with red color included in the eye logo and dark gray headphones.
At Comic-Con 2019, Marinette, Adrien, Alya and Chloé were announced to have real-world Instagram accounts that fans could follow. In the video showing the accounts, Nino was shown to be tagged in a picture with a supposed account of his own, under the account name "@djnino" – currently, however, there exists an inactive account under that same nickname. While it is currently unknown if Nino will get an Instagram account in the future, Alya started the trending hashtag #ninoneedsaninstagram, which the accounts use to "tag" him in posts.
In a post where Chloé mentions her distaste for being paired up with Nino for an art assignment (one that also saw Adrien with Alya and Marinette with Nathaniel), she commented, "#ninodoesntneedaninstagram".
Both Carapace and his civilian identity were revealed on August 31, 2017, in a press release video from French Miraculous distributor TFOU.
Miraculous Holder and Akumatized Villain

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Trivia
Nino and his family comes from the country, Morocco. It was previously assumed his family came from Réunion based on a series of tweets.
But it's unknown if the African side off his family comes from his mother's or father's side.
Nino is actually that second person of African origins to wield a Miraculous succeeding his Miraculous predecessor Mudekudeku who wielded the Ladybug Miraculous.
But unlike Khepri, Mudekudeku and LadyLion, Nino doesn't live in Africa.
Following Alya Césaire and Chloé Bourgeois, Nino is the third person to become a Miraculous holder and an Akumatized villain, excluding Gabriel, who Akumatized himself.
In "Gamer 2.0", Bubbler returns as a playable akumatized villain as part of the Gamer 2.0's powers.
A statue of the Bubbler appears in the Musée Grévin in "The Puppeteer 2".
Alongside Chloé Bourgeois and Alya Césaire, he is the third person to break free from an Akuma's control, and is the first male person to do so. Coincidentally, the three of them are Miraculous holders.
However, given that Chloé wasn't akumatized when she broke free, he is technically the second person to break free from an Akuma's control while akumatized.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Trivia
As seen in "Mayura", Carapace is the third person to break an akumatized object, instead of Ladybug and Cat Noir, following Queen Bee and Rena Rouge in "Mayura".
Nino, alongside Zoé Lee, Juleka Couffaine, Kagami Tsurugi, Lê Chiến Kim, and Sabrina Raincomprix, are the only current members of the Miraculers to whom Ladybug gave a Magical Charm.
Rocketear is the third villain that doesn't abandon their civilian identity, after Truth and Sole Crusher as he doesn't correct Ladybug when she calls him by his civilian name, and Sole Crusher, who also doesn't correct Marinette or Chloé, when the both of them call her by her civilian name.
Nino is currently the fourth person in having the most akumatized identities, having four (Bubbler, Shell Shock, Oblivio and Rocketear), with Chloé being the first with her having seven akumatized identities (Antibug, Queen Wasp, Miracle Queen, Queen Banana, Penalty, Sole Destroyer and Queen Mayor), and Kagami and Lila/Cerise being the second and third, with them being tied for having five akumatized identities (Riposte, Oni-Chan, Lies, Ryukomuri and Riposte Prime for Kagami; Volpina, Chameleon, Hoaxer, Spectral Looter and Timestalker for Lila/Cerise).

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Trivia
Unlike the aforementioned characters, Nino has never been akumatized into one of his identities twice, becoming a new identity every time he was akumatized (in the show itself, as he was re-akumatized into the Bubbler in the videogame "Miraculous: Paris Under Siege").
In "Miraculous: Paris Under Siege", after André Bourgeois cancelled the Aset exhibition due to the centerpiece being broken, due to the anger at his hard work going to waste he was reakumatized into the Bubbler alongside Lady Wifi, Truth, and Sole Crusher, working with Stormy Weather to take over Paris using Aset's power.
Miscellaneous
Nino aspires to be a film director, as hinted in "Horrificator", as well as "Volpina" when he says "Lila knows all of the Hollywood directors, she promised she'd mention me to Steven Basielberg himself!". He also directs the Creatica film in "Queen Banana". It is also mentioned as his future career in "Confrontation".
Nino is a DJ during his spare time, and he manages the school radio station.
According to one of Alya's Instagram photos, Nino as Carapace, is a bit camera shy.
In "The Bubbler", Nino has black hair but in all episodes afterward, he has brown hair.

title: Nino Lahiffe
text:
Nino Lahiffe - Trivia
In "Sentibubbler", it is revealed that Nino is afraid of tarantulas. However when he is near Alya, he tries to pretend to not be scared of tarantulas.
In "Rocketear", it is revealed that Nino always wanted a mustache.
In the cardboard game Miraculous Secrets, it's revealed that Nino's headphones are a special gift from his favourite DJ after a concert and starts carrying with him before Season 1.
In "Confrontation", it is revealed that Nino wants to be a film director when he grows up.

title: New York City
text:
New York City - Trivia
Geographically, the neighborhood where Miss Bustier's class took their field trip in "Miraculous New York" was Manhattan, but more specifically somewhere in midtown Manhattan. This is because it featured Times Square and had the Empire State Building and Central Park in the background. The New-York Historical Society that the class visited, however, is located on the Upper West Side of Manhattan.
Additionally, Gabriel Agreste stayed in a apartment he owned after stealing the Eagle Miraculous from the museum.
Coincidentally, another ZAG Heroez shows, Ghostforce take place prominently in the borough of Manhattan.
Both Ghostforce and Miraculous have previously cross-referenced each other's franchises in their respective shows.
Some of the background sets from the "Miraculous New York" special were reused from "Ghostforce". For example, when the police were arresting Techno-Pirate for endangering everyone on the plane, there is a basketball court with graffiti on the walls that is also used for "Ghostforce". The graffiti, in particular, was drawn by Jérôme Cointre.
In Ghostforce, Ladybug appeared on both a poster in an alley and a billboard near the same basketball court.

title: New York City
text:
New York City - Trivia
In Miraculous Adventures, Ladybug and Cat Noir arrived in New York through a portal created by Doorman to help the American heroes fight the Trash Krakken.
In the official concept art, it appears that Ladybug is standing on the Chrysler Building but the view is actually a commonly used one from the attraction "The Top of The Rock" at The Comcast Building, otherwise known as 30 Rockefeller Plaza.
New York is home to the American branch of the Style Queen Magazine, a fashion magazine created by Audrey Bourgeois.
In "Queen Wasp", Audrey offered Marinette to join her and study fashion under her in New York, but Tikki told her that this would mean giving up her Miraculous.
Zoé originally lived in New York City before moving to Paris. However, it is unknown what neighborhood she resided in there.
In the season 5 finale called "The Final Day", New York City was one of the cities Nightormentor traveled through in the making of the Operation: Perfect Alliance.

title: Nathaniel Kurtzberg/History
text:
Nathaniel Kurtzberg/History - Intro
Nathaniel Kurtzberg is a skilled artist who enjoys drawing in his sketchbook, especially during class time. He is a student at the Collège Françoise Dupont and a former student of Caline's class, before she became mayor of Paris. He is also the current holder of the Goat Miraculous, which he uses to transform into Caprikid.

title: Nathaniel Kurtzberg/History
text:
Nathaniel Kurtzberg/History - [[Season 1]]
In "Ladybug & Cat Noir", Nathaniel was one of the new students in Miss Bustier's class. After class was over, he went to the library.
In "Stoneheart", Nathaniel was seen in the classroom when Miss Bustier takes attendance until Stoneheart bursts in and captured Mylène. Later in the library, he and most of his classmates listen to Hawk Moth on live TV as he demands that Ladybug and Cat Noir surrender their Miraculouses. At first, he appears frightened, but when Ladybug refuses and promises to always protect the Parisians, Nathaniel happily cheers. The next day at school, he is amused when Marinette stands up to Chloé.
In "The Bubbler", Nathaniel was one of the many kids Bubbler forced into attending a surprise birthday party for Adrien. Though he dances at the party, he was as miserable as everyone else. Therefore, he was delighted when Ladybug and Cat Noir show up to stop Bubbler, though cheering for the duo caused him and the other partygoers to be trapped inside floating bubbles. Fortunately, he was freed after Ladybug and Cat Noir defeat Bubbler.

title: Nathaniel Kurtzberg/History
text:
Nathaniel Kurtzberg/History - [[Season 1]]
In "Mr. Pigeon", he was sitting in the back of Miss Bustier's class listening to Mr. Damocles' announcement about the derby hat designing contest.
In "Timebreaker", Nathaniel went with the rest of his classmates to Trocadéro in order to watch the bet between Alix and Kim. He cheers Alix on as he wants to be done with Kim's constant dares. However, when Alix's one-of-a-kind pocket watch was destroyed, she's akumatized as a result, Nathaniel was horrified as Timebreaker rollerblades towards him and his classmates. In a new timeline, he fled to safety with the other students.
In "Copycat", he was sitting in the back of Miss Bustier's class.
In "Lady Wifi", Nathaniel was in Miss Bustier's class until Lady Wifi appeared causing him and everyone to flee the school.

title: New Heroes/Transcript
text:

Scene: Marinette writes in her diary.
Marinette: Dear diary, for a long time, Cat Noir and I thought there would only be the two of us fighting against Hawk Moth.
Scene: The Lucky Charm materializes. It is a teapot.
Marinette: Until the day I got a very strange Lucky Charm.

Scene: Master Fu sits calmly, sipping from a cup. He presents Marinette with the Miracle Box.
Marinette: Instead of helping me to defeat the villain, my power was telling me to go to the Guardian of the Miraculous.
Marinette: Hello, Master Fu.

Scene: Fu opens the box. Marinette contemplates which Miraculous to take.
Marinette: That was a signal to let me know that I had to choose a new hero to help us with our mission.

title: Native American Miracle Box
text:
Native American Miracle Box - Intro
The  is a jewelry box used to store Miraculouses when they are not in use.
This Miracle Box is currently owned by Monk.

title: Native American Miracle Box
text:
Native American Miracle Box - Appearance
Exterior
The box is made out of a light brown wood and is shaped like a hexagon. The box contains six sides with each side having two dark colored buttons with an animal symbol in the center vertically aligned. The lid of the box has a dark brown design with the symbol of the Order of the Guardians surrounded by patterns in the middle with Native American designs at the edges. The box includes twelve drawers where more Miraculouses are being stored.
Top level
Inside the box, on the top level, there is a square divided into four sections with a circular center and a gold outline. In each section of the square and the circle is a Miraculous: wolf, bear, bison, eagle and Thunderbird.
Each section has a different color with a darker-shaded circled symbol in the center. The section opposite of the lid's hinge is red with a darker eagle symbol, which is where the Eagle Miraculous is placed. The left section is black with a dark symbol. The right section is yellow with a dark symbol. The upper section is white with a dark symbol. The central section is turquoise with a dark thunderbird symbol, which is where the Thunderbird Miraculous is placed.

title: Native American Miracle Box
text:
Native American Miracle Box - Access
Magic World
Just like the Chinese Miracle Box, it's possible that, within the Miracle Box, there is a pocket dimension where the kwamis can gather.
When gathered in this magic world, kwamis can communicate with other, non-present kwamis on their cycle, or birthday. There is no way to contact the kwamis while they are inside their magic world.

title: Native American Miracle Box
text:
Native American Miracle Box - Trivia
This is the second Miracle Box to appear, after the Chinese Miracle Box that is currently in Marinette Dupain-Cheng's possession.
The exterior design of the box strongly resembles the previous design of the Chinese Miracle Box.
The four outer sections of the top compartment are based on the Native American medicine circle and correspond to the four sacred mountains of Navajo culture, themselves responding to the cardinal directions (North, South, East, and West).
These mountains, and other similar sacred quartets in various Native American cultures, are typically assigned one of four colors: Black, White, Yellow, and Blue (which has been replaced by Red).
The center's color likely refers to the extensive use of turquoise stone in Native American jewelry.

title: Native American Miracle Box
text:
Native American Miracle Box - Trivia
Thomas Astruc has confirmed that the five Miraculous in the box's top drawer are the Wolf, Bear, Bison, and Eagle (bottom) Miraculous, with the Thunderbird Miraculous in the center. The four Miraculous surrounding the Thunderbird, he claims, correspond to the four cardinal directions of the Native American medicine circle, but did not clarify which Miraculous corresponds to the remaining three directions. Further, which animals correspond to which direction varies greatly by the source.
The unspecified Miraculous in the East/yellow compartment includes feathers, despite only the Thunderbird and Eagle Miraculous corresponding to birds. Further, it appears to reuse the same feather model used for the Thunderbird Miraculous. This may indicate an error in designing this Miraculous, an error in which animal it may be assigned, or that feathers are used in this box's Miraculous irrespective of which animal it corresponds to.

title: Native American Miracle Box
text:
Native American Miracle Box - Trivia
Most of the Miraculous are based on the 12 animals of the unofficial Native American Astrological Zodiac (unofficially confirmed to be the Bear, Wolf, Falcon, Otter, Deer, Beaver, Salmon, Woodpecker, Raven, Owl, Goose and Snake). These animals are seen in the opening of Miraculous New York.
This box features the second known Snake Miraculous, different from the one in the Chinese Miracle Box.
Because the Bear and the Wolf Miraculous are part of the Native American medicine circle at the top of the box instead, it's possible their are replaced in the Native American Zodiac with other animals.
Since in some versions of the Native American Zodiac, the Wolf is replaced by the Cougar, it's possible that there's a Cougar Miraculous.
A total of seven of the jewels and kwamis in the Miracle Box are based off a type of bird.

title: New-York Historical Society
text:
New-York Historical Society - Intro
The  is an American history museum and library that's located in the Upper West Side of the Manhattan borough in New York City. It presents exhibitions, public programs, and research that explore the rich history of New York and the nation.

title: New-York Historical Society
text:
New-York Historical Society - Description
Exterior
Located across from Central Park and the American Museum of Natural History, at the corner of Central Park West (8th Avenue) and 77th Street, the New York Historical Museum is in neoclassical style. Its façade is white, with a stepped portico, a colonnade on the first floor behind which are windows. Between the columns, the museum installs posters to promote an ongoing exhibition. The museum has a green tile roof.
Interior
The museum has a large hall whose predominant color is white. This has two staircases that join to form a balcony.
On the floor we find a black round pattern on a white background and objects on display protected by transparent cubes.
The rooms are quite large and house numerous works, including a room reserved for temporary exhibitions, such as the one on Franco-American friendship, in particular that of Gilbert du Mottier de Lafayette and Gustave Eiffel.

title: New-York Historical Society
text:
New-York Historical Society - Trivia
Historically, it was founded in 1804 as New York City's first museum.
However, this is from real world history. The museum's history may be different in the Quantic Universe.
As seen in the special, the front entrance of the museum was decorated for French-American Friendship Week. There are two banners depicting Gilbert du Motier and there's one in the middle depicting Gustave Eiffel in front of two national monuments he built: the Eiffel Tower and the Statue of Liberty.
The lost Eagle Miraculous was previously on display in the Lafayette room at the New-York Historical Society before Hawk Moth stole it.
The museum has been part of an akumatized villain attack. When Hawk Moth akumatized Techno-Pirate into Techlonizer, the akumatized villain breaks into the museum to steal Lafayette's saber so that when the heroes went after him, they forgot about the museum, thinking the saber was the target, allowing Hawk Moth sneak in after they left and steal the Eagle Miraculous.
Nadja Chamack refers to the New-York Historical Society as the "New York Museum".

title: New York Bay
text:
New York Bay - Intro
The  is a body of water formed by the mouth of the Hudson at New York City and its flow into the Atlantic Ocean.

title: New York Bay
text:
New York Bay - Description
Upper New York Bay
This is the northern part of the bay above the Narrows. This part is at the confluence of the mouth of the Hudson and the East River.
In New York City, this bay borders the southern tip of Manhattan, the western shore of Brooklyn, and the northeastern shore of Staten Island. The bay has many islands, the main ones being Governors Island, Ellis Island, and Liberty Island.
This bay is also called New York Harbor, as it is the port of New York where many ships of all types sail, from container ships to tourist excursion boats to the Statue of Liberty.
Lower New York Bay
This is the southern part of the bay below the Narrows. This part borders the southeastern shore of Staten Island and the southwestern shore of Brooklyn and opens onto the Atlantic Ocean.

title: New York Bay
text:
New York Bay - Trivia
The bay was discovered by Europeans in 1524 by Giovanni da Verrazzano on a mission for Francis I in 1524 and named "New Angoulême" because the king was also Count of Angoulême.
In the series, the Upper New York Bay hides a nuclear warhead launcher beneath its waters.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Intro
"" is a season 6 episode of the series, Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. As based on the series' production order specifically, "" is the 26th written, produced and final episode of season 6. It is also the 157th written and produced episode of the series, overall.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Synopsis
As Marinette feels Alya getting closer and closer to her secrets, Ladybug comes up with a plan to flush out the new Butterfly holder.
Disney Channel
While Marinette sees Alya get increasingly closer to uncovering her secrets, Ladybug comes up with a plan to flush the new holder of the Butterfly Miraculous out.
Disney+
Ladybug tries to flush the new Miraculous holder out.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
In the cold opening, Alya, as Rena Rouge, is still going through simulation after simulation regarding Bug Noire's final clash with Monarch with her Mirage, but nothing seems to work. As her mother and younger twin siblings call her down for dinner, Alya powers down after dispelling her latest attempt, just as Gabriel and Monarch appear to merge in a glitch. However, this triggers a revelation in Alya. She powers up again into Rena Rouge and runs one last simulation. This one has Monarch disarming a badly injured Bug Noire of the Ladybug and Cat Miraculous. As she reverts back to Marinette, Monarch reverts back into Gabriel Agreste, thus causing Rena to realize that could actually be a plausible solution and the actual truth to what Ladybug told the world about Gabriel and Monarch.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
After returning from a mission, Marinette de-transforms in her room. Her parents check on her, expressing relief and offering help, but Marinette is visibly stressed. Although they know she is Ladybug, their anxiety over her safety as a superhero weighs heavily on her. Furthermore, Marinette is suffering from severe psychological pressure because she is hiding a massive secret: Gabriel Agreste was Monarch. To spare Adrien from devastation, Marinette lied and claimed Gabriel made a heroic sacrifice. Consequently, she is now trapped in a web of lies with both her boyfriend Adrien and her best friend Alya, avoiding their calls because she can no longer bear talking to them without lying.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
Adrien calls Marinette and shares his latest project. Having found peace with his father's memory through the "truth" Marinette provided, he plans to turn parts of the mansion into a museum honoring Gabriel and displaying his jewelry designs. He asks Marinette to draw a portrait of his father for the official poster. Marinette flatly refuses, unable to suppress her disgust for Gabriel's past abuse and control. Adrien is baffled and hurt by her reaction, pointing out that she previously encouraged him to move forward. They part ways on tense and awkward terms.
Alya arrives and confronts Marinette, using a Mirage illusion to recreate the scenario. She figures out the missing link: Gabriel Agreste was Monarch, and Marinette kept it a secret to protect Adrien. Marinette confesses, explaining that telling Adrien the truth would destroy him, and involving Alya would force her to lie to him too. Faced with a new Butterfly Miraculous holder who attacked her family and remains entirely anonymous due to her failure to secure the Butterfly Miraculous from Gabriel as the original Hawk Moth, Marinette proposes a high-stakes sting operation.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
At his house, Adrien is speaking to Plagg about Marinette's behavior lately, but before they can go further into discussion about it, Adrien gets Ladybug's summon through the Miraculous Call.
Putting aside Plagg's suggested trip to the cheese museum, they transform into Cat Noir.
Ladybug gathers the team (Cat Noir, Rena Rouge, Pegasus, Ryuko, Polymouse, Miss Hound and Rooster Bold) to execute the plan: Rooster Bold uses Sublimation to give himself a power that wraps an illusion of Marinette in a layer of air, allowing the illusion to be touched without vanishing.
Rena creates the illusion of Marinette.
The plan: the fake Marinette will experience severe emotional distress (simulating a betrayal by Alya) to attract the new Butterfly holder's Ultrakuma.
Ladybug will pretend to be defeated and let the akumatized illusion take her real Miraculous earrings.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
The tracking: the illusion will deliver the earrings to the villain (after which they would be brought back by Miss Hound using her Fetch), allowing Ryuko and Polymouse to trace the villain's hiding place and report back to Pegasus, who will portal the rest of the team in, as Minotaurox, Carapace, Purple Tigress, Vesperia, Pigella, and Caprikid are ready and waiting at the Miracle Station.
Before the plan goes into effect, Ladybug activates her Lucky Charm, getting a caterpillar keychain that she entrusts to Rena for safety in case anything happens to her.
A second Marinette illusion will remain at the Dupain-Cheng house to serve as the "authentic" one that agrees to the Miraculers' plan to protect her from being hunted by the new Butterfly holder anymore once they convince the new Butterfly holder that Marinette and Ladybug are NOT the same person.
The plan goes into motion.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
Chrysalis falls for the decoy Marinette's emotional meltdown that she detects with Empathy, and akumatizes Marinette's illusion into Nemesis, a villain driven by the pain of a broken friendship, with the appearance of a winged stone angel with a sword and shield, symbolic of the namesake Greek goddess of retribution.
Nemesis hunts down Alya.
Cat Noir and Ladybug attempt to stop Nemesis.
As planned, Ladybug "loses" the fight as she is petrified by Nemesis' Medusa Gorgon Eyes attack from her eyes and mouth, alongside Pigella and Caprikid, while Cat Noir is incapacitated by an Antikuma, and Nemesis seizes the Miraculous earrings, taking them to the Fontaine de Trocadero on the villain's orders.
At the fountain, Nemesis drops the earrings into the fountain to be picked up later, where Ryuko is waiting to tail them in her Water Dragon form.
Chrysalis then orders Nemesis to go back and secure Cat Noir's Cat Miraculous so she has both to summon Gimmi.
Ryuko and Polymouse track the person who retrieves the earrings and places them in a candy wrapper, but the object is rapidly passed from a child to a firefighter, and then lost in the crowd.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
Rena tells Ryuko to disengage after losing the firefighter at the fire station, as Polymouse has it from there.
The earrings soon end up in the possession of a pregnant woman who then makes her way into the catacombs.
Once sure she's safe, the pregnant woman, revealed to be Chrysalis in disguise, contacts Nemesis and requests that she undo Ladybug's petrification so she can confirm the Ladybug Miraculous are genuine.
Nemesis complies and reverses Ladybug's petrification, causing her to revert back to Marinette.
This in turn also returns the Ladybug Miraculous to normal, causing Tikki to emerge, who gasps in horror upon realizing she's with Chrysalis, who gloats that she has one-half of the Miraculous she needs now to summon Gimmi.
Unknown to her, one of Polymouse's clones from Multitude had been hiding on the Miraculous, and signals Rena.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
Miss Hound activates her Fetch, and her ball takes back the Ladybug Miraculous, causing them to vanish from Chrysalis' hand, along with Tikki, much to her shock and horror that she's been tricked and denied summoning Gimmi again, before, on Rena's command, the Miraculers storm into the Parisian Catacombs using Pegasus' Voyage, catching her by surprise.
Realizing she's fallen into their trap, Chrysalis flees in a panic.
Meanwhile, upon getting the Ladybug Miraculous back, Marinette transforms into Ladybug again and joins the raid.
However, as the Miraculers struggle to find Chrysalis, Ladybug hears a door slam, and notices a glow and heavy smoke coming from one area.
Going to check, she finds that Chrysalis, realizing she's been made, has set fire to her lair and sealed the door, destroying all her equipment to deny the Miraculers any evidence they can use against her.
Despite the Miraculers' best efforts, it appears that Chrysalis slipped through their fingers and escaped.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
With little else to go on, they turn their attention back to Nemesis to avoid raising suspicion, and "convince" her to de-akumatize herself, allowing Ladybug to use her Miraculous Ladybug to fix everything, including de-petrifying Pigella and Caprikid.
Returning to Marinette's house, Rooster Bold dispels his power, and Rena dispels the two Marinette illusions before Ladybug and Rena power back down into Marinette and Alya. Following the incident, Alya tells Marinette that while she won't tell Adrien the truth, she refuses to participate in Marinette's ongoing lie anymore since she wants Marinette to tell Adrien the truth herself when the time comes. Before leaving, Alya tells Marinette that she will stay her stand-in as Ladybug, alongside being Deputy Guardian and Rena Rouge, but tells her to promise that she will never lie to her anymore if she wants them to remain best friends.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
At the Miracle Station, as the Miraculers discuss how their trap was only partially successful, when Ladybug questions King Monkey regarding his part in the raid, it soon dawns on the team, after Ladybug recalls her Lucky Charm she summoned earlier, much to their own horror, that Chrysalis is a shapeshifter, having evolved her powers with the Butterfly Miraculous to be able to disguise herself as anyone, including the Miraculers as their civilian or superhero identities. Realizing they need to step up their game more than ever now, Ladybug and the Miraculers vow that their war with Chrysalis has only just begun...

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot
Later, Marinette visits Adrien at his house to clear the air, with Adrien expressing how much he values their relationship built on absolute honesty and trust. Hearing this crushes Marinette, as her entire relationship with him is now built on a foundation of deception. After she leaves Adrien's house to head home, Marinette talks to Tikki, realizing she cannot continue dating Adrien while keeping the truth about his father hidden, but also unable to tell him. With no other choice left, a heartbroken Marinette wonders if she should end their relationship if she doesn't find the courage to tell Adrien the truth, leaving her crying on the steps in the nighttime as it begins to rain...

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot Developments
The episode continues where "Secret Protocol" left off, with Marinette's parents being aware of her being Ladybug.
Alya discovers Gabriel is Monarch after the illusions of his and Marinette’s final battle briefly merge. Like in "Revelator", she becomes upset and distant from Marinette, though less angrily. She chooses to keep Marinette's secret, wanting her to tell Adrien herself, and reassures her that she will stay as Rena Rouge, Deputy Guardian, and Ladybug's stand-in. However, she told Marinette to never lie to her again if she wants them to remain best friends.
Alya realized Marinette had a big secret she couldn't tell her at the end of "Revelator" and by "Sadnansi" Alya realized that secret had to do with the final battle against Monarch and started manifesting scenarios of the final battle against him.
Marinette, when caught, first tries to gaslight Alya in feeling guilty for thinking such a thing of Marinette, but eventually breaks down from all the secrets and trauma she gathered from the Final Day and through season 6, including the Butterfly Holder infiltrating her house and attacking her family, which happened in "Secret Protocol".

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot Developments
Marinette is shown struggling with trauma through hallucinations in "Sadnansi" and paranoia in "Secret Protocol", both of which happen shortly before this episode, suggesting she is nearing a mental and emotional breakdown. She even tells Alya that the Miraculers must stop the new Butterfly holder before "[Marinette] can't go on anymore."
Marinette's parents are revealed to be supportive of their daughter as Ladybug, even offering her baked goods to keep her in form and offering to wash her suit. However, despite attempting to be calm, Tom and Sabine are naturally worried for their daughter and the double life she leads.
Adrien, following his documentary on and change of view of his father from "Lady Chaos", now wishes to transform parts of the mansion, like Gabriel's study, into a museum in honor his father.
He also changed his mind about Gabriel's statue made by Théo Barbot from "Mister Agreste", deciding to let city hall built it after all, wanting to place it at the front garden of the Agreste mansion.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot Developments
Marinette, finally overwhelmed, lets out how she can't forgive Gabriel Agreste for all he did, though she only brings up his misdeeds as a father and still keeps secret the identity of Monarch; this also causes her to disapprove of Adrien building his life in his father's shadow.
Adrien, in turn, is naturally confused on this "sudden change of heart" and now tries to reassure Marinette that Gabriel was a good person using part of the documentary from "Lady Chaos", where Marinette reassured (lied to) Adrien about Gabriel's goodness.
Marinette, at the end of the call, says 'I'm sorry I'm not acting like you'd want me to.' This implies that Marinette still believes she needs to act in a certain way around Adrien to keep him happy, part of it being because of keeping Monarch's secret.
It is revealed in this episode that with some assistance with keeping it from vanishing (like Rooster Bold's Sublimation), an illusion can get akumatized.
However, they would still be under the control of the Fox Miraculous holder, meaning the emotions must come from them. Despite that, the Butterfly holder cannot sense the Fox holder's presence and mistakes the illusion for a genuine victim.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot Developments
After putting her parents in danger, Ladybug comes up with a counter-plan to uncover the Butterfly Miraculous holder by letting Chrysalis take her Miraculous while concealing Ladybug's identity by akumatizing an illusion of Marinette. The plan works, allowing the Miraculers to locate her lair in the Parisian Catacombs, but she manages to escape.
Due to the Miraculers finding her lair, Cerise sets it on fire to prevent them from finding anything connected to her.
To execute her plan, Ladybug deploys all available Miraculers except Argos, Viperion, and Bunnyx. Rena Rouge, Ryuko, Polymouse, Rooster Bold, and Miss Hound work as the key players to set the trap and the rest as reinforcements to raid Chrysalis' lair.
This also marks the very first direct confrontation between Chrysalis and the Miraculers. Although in the end, they still haven't managed to discover her name and her true appearance.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Plot Developments
This episode reveals that Cerise somehow has the ability to seemingly shapeshift, explaining how she has remained so elusive. She even used King Monkey's form to trick Ladybug and escape the Miraculers. This also explains the mysterious individuals seen observing Marinette and her friends throughout season 6, as well as the fake Wang Cheng in "Secret Protocol".
Cerise was able to shapeshift while Marinette was akumatized and telepathically communicate with her while in other people's forms, suggesting she either used the Butterfly Miraculous, upgraded its powers to allow her to akumatize two people at once, or has found another method.
Her shapeshifting was foreshadowed at the end of "The Illustrhater", when she compared herself to a chameleon, referencing her former Chameleon identity.
Since Chameleon could use the powers of those she impersonated, Cerise may now be able to do the same, explaining how she used Kung Food's powers in "Secret Protocol".

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Trivia
Despite the second illusion of Marinette serving to trick the other Miraculers so they wouldn't discover Ladybug's identity, Ryuko is the only one to be aware, besides Ladybug and Rena Rouge, of the existence of a second Marinette illusion, due to already knowing she is Ladybug.
It's unknown if this confirms Kagami is aware that Rena Rouge is Alya and that she knows Ladybug's identity. However, considering she discovered Marinette was Ladybug when eavesdropping a conversation between the two of them in "Perfection", it's very likely that she is aware of it.
The fact that Chrysalis was able to sense the negative emotions from the Marinette illusion was either from feeling those negative emotions from Alya feeling the emotions of her best friend not being honest with her or that unlike hallucinations or mirages, an illusion can affect a person's eyes, senses and mind, allowing Chrysalis to sense the false negative emotions from the illusion itself.
The errors in Bug Noire's and Marinette's models from Rena Rouge's illusions of the final battle have been fixed - she wears the Cat and Turtle rings on the correct fingers and doesn't have her Season 6 leggings as a civilian.

title: Nemesis
text:
Nemesis - Trivia
Not counting the flashbacks from "Intuition", this is the third episode where fire is shown after "Elation" and "The Illustrhater".
References
With the illusion of Marinette being akumatized into the titular villain, this marks the second time a clone became an akumatized villain after the sentimonster version of Gabriel Agreste in the episode of the same name.
The reason the Miraculers used a "solid" illusion as bait for akumatization instead of a sentimonster is because neither Marinette nor Félix would create a sentimonster just to use them for a bit and them snap them out of existence when they served their purpose.
Like in season 4, Marinette proves herself incapable of sharing secrets that need to be told without a major threat making it necessary, as despite Alya's warnings, in both "Revelator" and "Sadnansi" as well as this episode, Marinette couldn't tell Adrien the truth.
Overwhelmed from all the secrets that she keeps from him, for good or bad, Marinette wonders if she should end her relationship with Adrien because she still can't bring herself to tell him the truth.
Without Marinette knowing, her secret will hurt the exact same person as in season 4: Adrien/Cat Noir.
