text:
Qilin - Plot Developments
Sabine is fully akumatized for the first time, after her transformation into Verity Queen in "Ladybug" was not completed.
As of this episode, Marinette is the only member of her family to not get fully akumatized until "Heartfixer" since her transformation into Princess Justice in "Ladybug" was not completed because of Nathalie Sancoeur's illness.
It is revealed that Sabine had been marking Marinette's growth for the last five years (sometime after Marinette's 8th birthday), which is a reference from "Ladybug & Cat Noir" (4 years in the same class with Chloe).
This episode marks the final appearance of the normal akumas, because starting from the next episode "Dearest Family" onwards, Shadow Moth/Monarch uses megakumas to break the Magical Charms' protective barriers and would even later on send a megakuma to anyone who is not even wearing a magical charm and he would now only occasionally send out megakumas to akumatize anyone who either has a magical charm or not.

title: Qilin
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Qilin - Trivia
Internationally, this episode first premiered in the USA on Disney Channel.
Additionally, this is the sixth time Miraculous-related content premiered in the US, following "Captain Hardrock", "Ikari Gozen", "Miraculous New York", "Wishmaker", and "Ladybug Saves Christmas", later being followed by "Risk", and "Daddycop".
The lollipop sentimonster is revealed to be named Lollipop Boy.
This episode is of many seconds involving:
Where Cat Noir uses the umbrella feature of his staff following "Glaciator 2" and before "Ephemeral" but this is the first time he uses it in combat.
Marinette spilling milk on the table, after "Ladybug & Cat Noir".
Ladybug ties herself down to something so she does not get blown away, after "Stormy Weather".
An episode of Season 4 where the other kwamis from the Miracle Box don't appear following "Psycomedian".
Where Cat Noir gets tossed into the river following "Princess Fragrance".
Following "Malediktator", despite the ray gun being a weapon of science fiction Ladybug gets a weapon as a Lucky Charm.
This episode takes place on Saturday the 14th of an unknown month.

title: Qilin
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Qilin - Trivia
There is no Saturday 14th except that before Mother's Day in 2016, the year in which it is assumed the episode takes place. The only possible days are November 14th 2015, January or October 14th 2017, all of which are too far from late May.
Mother's Day is celebrated on the second Sunday (in China and North America) or last Sunday (in France) of May. This difference, however, does not affect the error.
Since Marinette mentions she is over a month late for Mother's Day, which takes place in May, the episode would most likely take place in June or July.
This would be impossible, as each episode happens during the same school year, and as seen in future episodes, the school year still has not ended.
The following episode, "Dearest Family", takes place in early January.
It is revealed that Sabine teaches Chinese painting classes at Marinette's school.
Some of her students include Nadja Chamack and Lila Rossi.
When TF1 aired the episode in France, they cut out the scene of the ticket inspector harassing Sabine on the bus, and her being arrested and akumatized, making the episode only 18 minutes long. The exact reason for this is unknown.

title: Qilin
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Qilin - Trivia
Although TF1 has stated that the cut was due to them believing the episode's theme was too mature for young children, several have believed it was politically-motivated censorship, as it very clearly portrays police officers and state officials as aggressors.
However, according to Thomas Astruc, the episode was sent in its original form to TF1, so all other broadcasters which air the show in French aired the episode fully (RTS, Disney Channel France and Belgium, Disney+ and Télé-Québec).
When Shadow Moth was talking to Sabine about him being misunderstood that isn't completely true if he had explained his problem in the first place, then the people would understand his problem but not agree with Gabriel on how he is handling it.
What is also interesting is that Ladybug could've used the ray gun to blast the cuffs off of Qilin but instead she handled the problem with diplomacy.
This is the only time Clara Contard is seen in the studio, instead of reporting from outside.
References
This is the fifth episode in Season 4 where a character is fully akumatized for the first time, following "Psycomedian", "Furious Fu", "Sole Crusher" and "Wishmaker".

text:

This is also the third episode in season 4 where a character from season 1 is akumatized for the first time after "Furious Fu" and "Wishmaker".
This is the twelfth episode where the thinking pattern of someone who is not Ladybug is seen, following Fei's in "Miraculous Shanghai", Adrien's in "Oblivio", Marinette's in "Oblivio", "Ladybug", "Heart Hunter", "Hack-San", and "Simpleman", Pegasus' in "Startrain", Félix's in "Félix", Cat Noir's in "Psycomedian", Master Fu's in "Furious Fu" and Alya's in "Sentibubbler".
Sabine is one of the few akumatized victims who at first tries to resist Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth's control.
She is the third person to break free from Shadow Moth's control while akumatized following Alya in "Gang of Secrets" and Nino in "Rocketear".
When Nino broke free, the akuma expelled from his glasses, however, when Sabine broke free the akuma had to be released when Ladybug destroyed her handcuffs.
This makes her the fifth character who is a visual artist, following Marinette, Nathaniel, Master Fu, and Kagami.
This is also one of the few times someone has seen the akuma before it hits its target.

title: Qilin

text:
Qilin - Trivia
This is the fourth time Cat Noir runs up a wall, following "Stormy Weather", "Frightningale" and "Lies".

title: Qilin
categories: Episodes where Adrien is a minor character
text:
Qilin - Trivia
This is the seventh time where Ladybug's Lucky Charm resembles an akumatized villain's object from before it got akumatized following the handcuffs in "Frightningale".
This is the sixteenth time where Ladybug's Lucky Charm is an object from a previous episode.
Allusions
In Chinese mythology, Qilins, also known in Japanese as Kirins, are East Asian creatures that resemble a unicorn, being one of a great number of East Asian creatures to have one horn. That makes this episode the sixth one where the titular villain is named after a mythological creature, after "Dark Cupid", "Befana", "Sapotis", "Anansi", and "Oni-Chan".
Thomas Astruc has stated on Twitter that this episode would have themes of racism.
This is one of the few episodes with obvious sociopolitical themes. It deals with themes of racism and police aggression. This makes it one of the few episodes confirmed to have mature themes, after "Reverser" and "Mega Leech".
The episode was written during the Yellow Vests movement in 2018, which explains the political themes.
Qilin is similar to Starfire from the Teen Titans episode "Go!" where she was berserk before she met Robin.

title: Quantic Comics
text:
Quantic Comics - Trivia
The company is based on one of the well-known American comic book publishing companies: DC Comics.
The Quantic Comics logo is only seen on the cover of Majestia #56.
A concept art reveals a cover for an unseen Super Comics #1 featuring Majestia. Super Comics is a parody of Action Comics, which is a comic book/magazine series published by National Allied Publications (the original name for DC Comics).
In "The Dark Owl", Denis Damoclès owns five comic book issues from different series that feature Knightowl. Each of the series' titles is a parody of an actual comic series.
Justice Comics is a parody of the Detective Comics series which was published by Detective Comics, Inc., before the company would eventually later rebrand itself as DC Comics. "Justice" might also be a reference to DC's superhero team Justice League.
There's a concept art that revealed that the title was originally going to be Super Comics, just like Super Comics #1 featuring Majestia. However, Detective Comics and Action Comics are separate comic book series.

title: Quantic Comics
text:
Quantic Comics - Trivia
It's likely that the concept art for Super Comics #10 has its title name changed to Justice Comics #27 later in production to match the actual comic book cover it parodies.
World's Finest Team-Up is a parody of the World's Finest Comics which was a crossover anthology series from 1941 to 1986 featuring two or more DC heroes teaming up.
The Untold Story of Knightowl is a parody of The Untold Legend of the Batman, a three-issue miniseries published in 1980.
A concept art revealed that the title was originally going to be The Untold Legend of the Knightowl.
All New, All Different, All Mystery is a parody of All-New, All-Different Marvel, a 2015-2016 branding for Marvel Comics. This makes this comic series the only one that isn't based on a DC Comics cover.
Three of the comic issues Mr. Damoclès owns feature the Comic Code Authority seal on the cover.
In real life, the Comic Code Authority only applied to the United States from 1954 to 2011. Because Mr. Damoclès is from France and the covers are in English, it's likely he bought the three issues from the States.
The in-universe comic book covers featured throughout the show are parodies of actual DC comic book covers.

title: Quantic Comics
text:
Quantic Comics - Trivia
Super Comics #1 is based on Action Comics #1, which marks the debut of several comic-book characters, with the most notable being Superman.
The cover date for Super Comics #1 is different than the actual Action Comics #1 it parodies. According to the concept art, the cover date for Super Comics #1 is June 1930, while the cover date for Action Comics #1 is June 1938.
Super Comics #10/Justice Comics #27 is based on Detective Comics #27, which marks the debut of Batman.
While Justice Comics #27 doesn't feature the cover date, both Detective Comics #27 and the Super Comics #10 concept art have the cover dated May 1939.
The Adventures of Knightowl #1 is based on Batman #1.
While the cover date for The Adventures of Knightowl #1 is unknown, the cover date for Batman #1 is March 1940.
The Adventures of Knightowl has a logo that said "Owl Publication", which is based on DC's logo from 1940 to 1942. Because of this, it's unknown if Owl Publication was a previous name of Quantic Comics when the issue was first published.
The cover of the volume mentioned it is a "Spring Issue", indicating that The Adventures of Knightowl #1 was published during the spring season.

title: Quantic Comics
text:
Quantic Comics - Trivia
World's Finest Team-Up #289 is based on the World's Finest Comics #289.
The cover date for World's Finest Team-Up #289 is different than the actual World's Finest Comics #289 it parodies. The cover date for the former is November at an unknown year, while the cover date for the latter is March 1983.
The Untold Story of Knightowl #5 is based on the paperback edition of the The Untold Legend of Batman.
Interestingly, the cover art reveals that it is the fifth issue of the series. However, the series it parodied only has three issues.
Knightowl #505 is based on the second printing of Batman #608.
The cover date for Knightowl #505 is different than the actual Batman #608 it parodies. The cover date for Knightowl #505 is December 2005, while the cover date for the second printing of Batman #608 is December 2002.
Majestia #56 featured Majestia's posing similar to Wonder Woman #3 from its third volume.
It's unknown what real-life comic book cover All-New, All-Different, All Mystery: Knightowl is based on.
Assuming the cover dates from the Super Comics #1 concept art is canon, Quantic Comics must have been found between the late 1920s to June 1930.

title: Quantic Comics
text:
Quantic Comics - Trivia
And assuming Majestia in the cover is Olympia Hill, that would also mean she has been around since the late 1920s.
Alya Césaire and Mr. Damoclès are the only known characters who are revealed to read Quantic Comics. Alya is a fan of Majestia and owns a poster that is similar to Majestia #56 in her bedroom. Whereas Mr. Damoclès is a huge fan of Knightowl and owns five issues in his principal's office.
While Marinette Dupain-Cheng isn't an avid reader of Quantic Comics, she did once read a copy of the first volume of The Adventures of Knightowl solo series which was created as a Lucky Charm object to figure out how to defeat Dark Owl.
Since the United Heroez superheroes are actual people and not in-universe fictional characters, it's likely Quantic Comics published stories based on their heroic endeavors.
Majestia, a predecessor of Knightowl, and a predecessor of Sparrow are the only known members of the United Heroez to appear in the comic books.
It's unknown if other members of the United Heroez, such as Doorman and Uncanny Valley, have their own comic series.

title: Quantic Comics
text:
Quantic Comics - Trivia
Because a majority of the United Heroez members don't have a secret identity, it's likely that Quantic Comics publishes stories that feature the heroes' actual civilian identity.
One of Knightowl's predecessor(s) has a butler who appeared in The Adventures of Knightowl #1. The butler is based on Alfred Pennyworth.
The design of an unknown villain who appeared on the cover of All New, All Different, All Mystery seems to be based on a Marvel supervillain Thanos.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Intro
"" is a season 6 episode of the series, Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. As based on the series' production order specifically, "" is the 24th written and produced episode of season 6. It is also the 155th written and produced episode of the series overall.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Synopsis
Upon learning that Chloé is back in Paris, Marinette fears the worst… Quite the opposite of Sabrina, who is convinced that Chloé has changed and become a good person. Who is right?
Disney Channel
When she hears that Chloé is back in Paris, Marinette fears for the worst.
Disney+
Chloé is back in Paris.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
Chrysalis watches a live stream of Chloé Bourgeois announcing her return to Paris. She places an Ultrakuma into a lovely, pearl-adorned box. Chloé mentions that her stay in Paris might be extended if her autobiographical film proves successful. Chrysalis reverts to her civilian form, closes the box, and dons a blonde wig, transforming into a new persona. At the post office, she buys stamps featuring the Eiffel Tower and affixes one to the box. The scene shifts to Cerise—using a false identity—smiling mysteriously at her phone, which is displaying Chloé’s stream, while aboard an airplane.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
Adrien and Plagg go down the stairs in the former's room, still sleepy, only to find the large window covered by a poster announcing Chloé's arrival. The same thing is happening at Zoé's and Marinette's homes; the former is angry, while the latter is terrified. A crowd of Chloé's fans has gathered around Collège Françoise Dupont, trying to get inside—a sight that surprises both Adrien and Marinette. A group of their friends stands outside the school, furious. Max tells Marinette that the school is closed until further notice, and Nino adds that it is due to the filming of Chloé's movie. Sublime asks what the deal is with Chloé. Marinette tries to explain but freezes up. Rose and Zoé explain that Chloé used to be Marinette's chief tormentor. When Sublime asks why the adults didn't do anything about it, Alya replies that even they were afraid of her. Mylène finishes the story by recounting how Chloé fled to London after a confrontation with everyone. Adrien reassures Marinette that she has nothing to fear.
The girl's panic is interrupted by Sabrina, who suggests that Chloé has changed.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
When asked what gave her that idea, she admitted that she was Chloé's helper in bullying the others, but they forgave her and consider her a friend.
While the others didn't deny her point, Zoé points out that unlike Chloé, Sabrina had a change of heart because she understood how she was hurting people.
Sabrina shows a letter she received "from Chloé," containing an apology for the terrible way she had been treated.
Marinette does not believe the letter is actually from Chloé, a view shared by her best friend, Alya, who points out that Chloé would have written something completely different than that.
Sabrina once again suggests that the bully has changed, but before the group can respond, the roar of a helicopter interrupts the conversation.
Inside the vehicle, Chloé remarks that her fans are ridiculous, crumpling up one of the many love letters and tossing it out the window.
She opens another box, finding a lovely pearl-adorned jewelry case inside; she grows frustrated when she is unable to open it.
She steps out of the helicopter holding the case.
The holder of the Butterfly Miraculous continues to watch the broadcast.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
The girl enters the school; Sabrina tries to follow, but Marinette stops her.
Sabrina insists that Chloé has no hold over her, clutching the pin she received from her.
She tells the security guard she is Chloé's best friend, but he retorts that Chloé has no friends.
Marinette steps in and lies to the guard, claiming that she and Sabrina are part of the Paris Youth Council.
Zoé sighs and approaches, adding that Chloé's sister wants to speak with her.
The guard calls another guard, asking him to notify Chloé.
Chloé emerges from the nurse's office wearing her Queen Bee mask, frustrated that she cannot open a mysterious pearlescent box.
She spots a tree in the middle of the campus and orders it cut down, citing the fact that the tree wasn't there when she attended the school.
Audrey tells her to stop, but Noé urges her to let Chloé express herself.
The girl continues to struggle with opening the box.
A security guard approaches her unexpectedly and says her sister wants to meet.
Chloé asks if she is alone, and the guard replies that two other girls are with her.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
She contemplates a perfect plan to torment the trio, but Audrey forbids it, saying they have more important matters to attend to.
Noé again tells his mother to give Chloé more freedom, noting that she is such a caricature that people forget how absurd and terrible her behavior actually is—which drives up her social media following.
The guard lets Zoé, Sabrina, and Marinette into the school.
Chloé orders the guard to film, while Marinette spots Audrey and Noé in the corner.
Suddenly, Chloé orders them to fire at the newcomers, but her staff do not understand her commands.
Eventually, they fire nets at the trio but miss.
Sabrina looks disappointed, and Zoé asks her sister what she had planned.
Chloé explains her scheme to torment the girls by shooting tennis balls at them.
Sabrina approaches her and tells her she should show everyone her new, true self, referencing the letter.
Chloé doesn't understand what she's getting at and mocks her in front of everyone, then tears the letter to pieces.
Cerise watches the broadcast with a sinister smile.
Sabrina mysteriously thanks Chloé and walks away, delighting Marinette and Zoé.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
Chloé makes a pathetic attempt to salvage her image, but the only response she gets is laughter from Marinette.
When Chloé demands an explanation from "Baker Girl", Marinette turns around and tells Chloé to remember one thing from the end of "Revolution" in Season 5 after she was removed from power as Interim Mayoress and kicked out of Paris and Marinette told her off with how she couldn't bully Marinette anymore: that *she* is the ridiculous, utterly ridiculous, one, showing that Marinette was no longer afraid of her upon seeing Chloé hasn't changed one bit and is still the same shallow bully and brat from before her exile, having learned nothing, enraging Chloé.
Seizing the moment, Cerise remotely opens the box containing the Ultrakuma, and it flies into Chloé’s purse.
While akumatized, she mutters to herself, vowing to make the three girls the laughingstock they made of her.
She chooses the name "Dread Queen" for herself and then undergoes her transformation.
She uses a fake spinning top to create a golden zone around herself.
As she approaches Zoé, Sabrina, and Marinette, the girls are overcome by irrational fear and flee in a panic, splitting up.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
She decides to go after Marinette Dupain-Cheng first.
Adrien hides in a dark alley, where Plagg remarks that he hasn't been this afraid since they ran out of cheese.
Despite their fear, they transform into Cat Noir; meanwhile, the akumatized villain searches for Marinette, who is hiding behind a dumpster.
Terrified, Marinette huddles down, not making a sound.
Dread Queen moves on silently, believing the alley is empty.
Tikki remarks that this akumatization of Chloé is far more terrifying than the previous ones.
Marinette agrees before having Tikki transform her into Ladybug, her voice trembling.
Cat Noir finds Dread Queen in the Place des Vosges and moves to confront her, but the villain's golden sphere causes him to cower in fear and apologize for his threats.
He hides inside the carousel, but before the villain can take his Miraculous, Ladybug rescues her partner using her yo-yo.
Dread Queen flies toward the heroes, causing them to cower once more.
The supervillain aims her spinning top at them, but Ladybug manages to escape.
They are fleeing from her, but she has given chase.
It turns out they cannot escape the bubble created by her spinning top.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
They flee across a series of rooftops, and on one of them, Ladybug and Cat Noir lose sight of Dread Queen.
They discuss their observations.
Ladybug uses her Lucky Charm and conjures a zip tie.
Cat Noir asks what she intends to do with it, but Ladybug has an idea; she opens her yo-yo and presses the Dog and Bee symbols.
Zoé is watching the akumatized villain from hiding when she suddenly receives a signal from the Guardian.
Pollen emerges from her pocket, telling her to join the action, and she transforms into Vesperia.
Sabrina is trembling with fear, hiding behind some bushes.
Sensing a signal from Ladybug, Barkk appears and tells her to transform, which his holder does.
Dread Queen destroys Marinette’s balcony but is startled by a familiar voice.
Vesperia calls out to her, mocking her fake Bee Miraculous costume as embarrassing.
A confrontation ensues, with the akumatized villain chasing Vesperia.
Unfortunately, Vesperia corners herself in a dead end, and Dread Queen’s power leaves her defenseless.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
Just as the villain is about to grab the Bee Miraculous, due to Chloé wanting to be Queen Bee again after Ladybug kicked her off the team for her betrayal back during events with Hawk Moth and Mayura, her purse is struck by Miss Hound's ball; the power "Fetch" is activated, teleporting the akumatized spinning top back to the user.
Cat Noir destroys the spinning top with Cataclysm, and Ladybug catches the Ultrakuma and purifies it in her yo-yo; she then throws the previously conjured zip tie and uses Miraculous Ladybug, repairing all the damage caused by the akumatized villain.
Vesperia exhales calmly, while a furious Chloé yells at Ladybug, demanding to know why the heroine is always getting in her way.
Ladybug tries to give her a Magical Charm, but Chloé slaps her hand away and tells her to leave.
Before she can finish her rant, Lieutenant Raincomprix and Caline step out of a police car; Caline informs her that the contract signed by Noé Luxus is worthless, as there was no mention of closing the school for filming, let alone remodeling it.
Roger warns that if she doesn't order the film crew to clear out of the school grounds, he will have to cite and fine them.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
Seeing even her ex-teacher and Sabrina's father no longer afraid of her like when Andre was still Mayor, Chloé furiously declares she is heading back to London, and Ladybug discreetly slips the amulet into her handbag.
The heroes share a celebratory fist-bump.
Aboard a private gold-colored jet, Chloé receives a notification on her phone.
She opens her handbag to retrieve the device but spots the amulet instead.
She calls her bodyguard over and orders him to throw it away, but as he heads toward the service area, Noé asks him to hand it over.
The brother smiles sinisterly and clenches his fist for the next operation of The Kingdom.
Back at the school, the friends clean up the mess Chloé left behind.
Sabrina tosses the brooch from her former friend into a dumpster; Zoé then approaches her and asks what she had thanked Chloé for earlier.
Sabrina explains that she thanked her for allowing her to close that chapter of her life, adding that she now has more room in her heart for new friends.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot
Marinette notices the letter Sabrina had shown her earlier and intends to throw it away, but she realizes that the stamp of the Eiffel Tower on the package containing the Ultrakuma is identical to the one on the letter to Sabrina and the final war will soon be ready.
At Wang Cheng's restaurant, Fei is serving dishes to customers. She is beckoned by a female customer she doesn't recognize, who asks if she might personally congratulate the chef. Fei asks if she is French; the woman confirms this but notes that she has been living in Shanghai for a few months. The customer turns out to be Cerise Bianca, operating under a new identity. Fei invites her to meet Wang Cheng. Cerise smiles ominously when she spots Marinette in one of the photos displayed in the restaurant.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot developments
After being seen via Zoo in "Climatiqueen" and "Daddycop", Chloé Bourgeois briefly returns to Paris in this episode, for the first time since being driven away by the people after her brief, but tyrannical rule as Mayor of Paris in "Collusion" and "Revolution". Despite her downfall, Chloé is still shown to have not changed her ways, being just as arrogant and mean-spirited as when she left, having learned nothing from her failures.
Chloé was revealed by Sabrina to have moved to London after her fall from grace in "Revolution".
She is accompanied by her mother, Audrey Bourgeois and her half-brother, Noé Luxus, revealing that she knows him as her brother. It is unknown if Zoé knows Noé is her half-brother due to being estranged from her family.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot developments
Despite Audrey saying she's gonna "take control of Chloé's life again" at the end of "Revolution", she is shown in this episode to have let her son Noé control his sister. Instead of a direct attempt at managing her, Noé is using a more subtle version of control, manipulating her into being and doing what he wants, much like Cerise did in "Collusion" and "Revolution". Using her diva-like personality to his advantage, Noé turned Chloé into a successful influencer, an area Audrey herself admits she doesn't understand.
Despite being driven away from Paris, Chloé is shown to have many fans from her Zoo posts in this episode. Noé explains to Audrey this is because Chloé's caricatural character-like personality makes it easy for people to forget how unacceptable her actions are and making evil look like a fun trend.
In addition to not learning her lesson, Chloé is delusional and still obsessed with her former Queen Bee persona, still seeing Vesperia as an unworthy copy and the Bee Miraculous as rightfully hers, thinking that Ladybug "stole" it from her.
Like in "Queen Banana", Chloé is akumatized into a variation of her Queen Bee design and is baited by Vesperia.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot developments
Like she did with Armand in the first five seasons, Chloé names her staff names that start with "Jean", which cause confusion as to whom she's speaking to.
Both Marinette and Sabrina, despite mostly moving on from Chloé Bourgeois, are still affected in opposite ways by her brief return to Paris, but both find closure in this episode:
Sabrina, despite reforming and largely moving on from Chloé, was revealed to not have discarded the trash bin in which she threw her Queen Bee merchandise in "Daddycop" or the brooch Chloé gave her in "Antibug" and, due to a forged letter sent by Cerise, still thought that Chloé could reform. However, when she sees that wasn't the case, she finally gets some closure regarding her "friendship" with Chloé and accepts that Chloé was not only never her friend but that she won't change, symbolizing her acceptance by throwing away the brooch. It was later revealed that Sabrina knew that Marinette was right when she said that people like Chloé will never change their ways.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot developments
Marinette, upon seeing that Chloé had returned to Paris, was revealed to have not completely gotten over the trauma that Chloé's bullying and actions in the flashback in "Derision" had caused her, starting to tremble and even apparently shying away from Adrien's touch like in "Derision" while catastrophizing about Chloé's return. However, much like Sabrina, after seeing how Chloé continued to stay the same childish bully, she completely let go of her fear of her. Marinette shut Chloé down using her own "Ridiculous! Utterly ridiculous!" catchphrase against her, much like she did in "Revolution" when she was exiled from Paris.
Similar to Marinette and Sabrina, Adrien made good on his promise of severing ties with Chloé if she refused to change, not even bothering to try and speak to her. He first threatened to cut ties with her in "Despair Bear" and again in "Queen Banana", before ultimately going through with it and letting go of Chloé in "Derision" after learning what she did to Marinette and refusing to apologize to her.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot developments
Like the others, Mayor Bustier learned from her mistake of being too lenient with Chloé after the events of "Collusion" and "Revolution", which inspired her to be Paris' mayor in the first place, and took action to forbid Chloé from shooting her film and ruining Collège Françoise Dupont.
Mayor Bustier's vigilance may also result from Noé's actions almost forcing her out of office in "Noe".
Cerise is properly shown in her lair among her diaries, as well as one of the many wigs she wears as a disguise.
She uses the same disguise she used in "Miraculous London" to buy stamps to deliver a box with an Ultrakuma to Chloé, showing she is still aware of how impulsive and easy to akumatize or drive someone else to akumatization she is.
Cerise is revealed to have written a letter to Sabrina pretending to be Chloé sometime after "Daddycop", probably knowing or anticipating Chloé's return, and delivered an Ultrakuma to Chloé so it would be near when she emotionally hurt Sabrina, but because Sabrina by this point mostly moved on from Chloé, she decided to completely let go of Chloé, making Cerise fail in her plans.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot developments
This is the second time Cerise sent a letter to further her plans, after sending one to Max in "A Fairy Good Night".
Because of the matching stamps, Marinette makes the connection that the same person that sent the box with the Ultrakuma, also gave Sabrina the fake letter saying Chloé had changed. She is unsure if it's the holder of the Butterfly Miraculous, but stays cautious.
It is revealed that Cerise is a member of the Butterfly community on Zoo.
Dread Queen's dome being immune to Cataclysm was most likely the result of Chloé remembering Cat Noir getting his adult powers from when she had trapped him in a similar Cataclysm-immune dome by using Shell-ter combined with Resistance in "Revolution".
Noé currently takes the Magical Charm meant for Chloé after taking it from Chloé's employee to be discarded.
Cerise heads to Shanghai and meets Fei Wu at Uncle Wang's restaurant while learning about Marinette's family, possibly as part of investigating her life due to her suspicion of Marinette being Ladybug from "Vampigami" and "Heartfixer".

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Plot developments
Among Wang's family photos on his wall, there is a new picture of him, Fei with his accordion, Bastille and Marinette and Adrien right after the events of "Miraculous Shanghai".
She sent her Ultrakuma to Chloé through a package because she was seemingly aware of not being able to influence Chloé due to being outside of range, which was first revealed in "Startrain". As a result, Chloé doesn't have a conversation with Chrysalis, but a brief monologue of her darkest thoughts, which the Ultrakuma amplified, much like it happened to Claudie Kanté before transforming into Startrain in the eponymous episode.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Trivia
An alternate Lucky Charm is seen where Ladybug is noticeably scared.
This marks the second time someone is infected by an akuma and transformed into a villain without the Butterfly Miraculous holder speaking to them, after Claudie Kanté's akumatization into Startrain during the episode of the same name.
References
Chloé's akumatized form of Dread Queen, as an allusion to her former identity as Queen Bee, is similar to her akumatizations as Queen Wasp in the eponymous episode and "Mayura", and Queen Banana in the eponymous episode.
Her Dreadzone dome is similar to her power as Penalty from "Penalteam".
Allusions
Dread Queen looks similar to the Pokémon Vespiquen from the Pokémon franchise.
Errors
Chloé's necklace is fully yellow in the end card.
Despite Adrien standing next to Marinette, when Marinette reads the letter, Adrien is nowhere to be seen, until she's done reading.
The position of the merry-go-round changes while Dread Queen is in the park.
Marinette's school bag disappears after she hides behind a bin from Dread Queen before transforming.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone - Trivia
As the camera focuses on Adrien and Marinette walking towards the school, the people who walk by are not in the same line as shown in the previous shot.
As Chrysalis detransforms into Cerise, her height decreases.
In the wide shot of the entrance of Collège Françoise Dupont, when Zoé, Sabrina, and Marinette are leaving, Zoé's shadow does not anchor with her feet, creating a noticeable detachment.
As Dread Queen's dome is shown covering the school, the background isn't fully loaded, so a black area with yellow text can be seen in the top right corner.
Cat Noir mispronounces "ultrakuma" as "ultra akuma".
This error was also present in "Yaksi Gozen" and "The Chained Titans".

title: Raincomprix apartment
text:
Raincomprix apartment - Intro
The  is the residence of Roger and Sabrina, located near the Canal Saint-Martin.

title: Raincomprix apartment
text:
Raincomprix apartment - Appearance
Exterior
The Raincomprix apartment is located inside a rather modern building, which is accessed through a small courtyard delimited by a pedestrian gate and characterized by a small flowerbed and a rose bush.
Interior
The interior of the apartment is characterized by white walls and parquet floors.
Sabrina's room
Sabrina's room is relatively simple, with white-gray walls and a wooden floor. It features a built-in closet with a pink door and a simple bed with white sheets and a pink blanket. The bed has a large mattress and is accompanied by a storage chest, next to which lies a small black and orange rug.
On the opposite side of the bed, there's a simple, modern white and brown computer desk with a few drawers. Sabrina's computer sits atop the desk, flanked by two filing cabinets. Above the desk, various diplomas and certificates are framed. Nearby, there's a wastebasket completing the tidy setup

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Chloé: Bonjour, Paris! I know you've missed me. Well, dry those tears. You're being ridiculous, utterly ridiculous!
(Chrysalis opens up a pearl-adorned box.)
Chloé: I, Chloé Bourgeois, have returned to grace you with my presence! (gestures towards Eiffel Tower) How long will I be staying? That depends on you, Paris! And on the success of my upcoming movie! That's right! Big news—I'm here to produce my first masterpiece!
(Chrysalis evilizes a butterfly and puts it in the box before sealing it. She then detransforms and locks the box with an app on her phone.)
Chloé: A motion picture—obviously written by me, composed by me, produced by me, directed by me, and most importantly, starring your favorite actress of all time—duh, me! (laughs)
(Cerise puts the pearly box into a small cardboard box and puts on her blonde wig.)
Postal worker: I have some commemorative stamps, if you'd like.
Cerise: Yes, thank you. They're beautiful.
(Cerise takes the stamps, which have a design of the Eiffel Tower on them.)
Chloé: Spoiler alert: my movie will be a musical about my life as a superhero. Get ready for Queen Bee: The Super Chloé Bourgeois!

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
(In the video, a blimp displays a poster for the movie. Cerise smirks at her phone.)
[ Theme Song ]
Marinette: What's going on?
Max: School's closed indefinitely.
Nino: They're building sets for the shooting of Chloé's movie.
Marinette: A film shoot with Chloé at our school means something's up!
Juleka: Probably a lot worse than just something.
Sublime: So what's the deal with this, uh, Chloé girl?
Marinette: She... she...
Rose: She bullied all of us for years.
Zoé: Marinette more than anyone else!
Marinette: She undermined my self-confidence so badly that I couldn't even hold Adrien's hand!
Sublime: But didn't the adults do anything about it?
Alya: Even they were scared of her. No one would dare punish her.
Mylène: Until everyone fought back and she fled to London.
(Marinette's hand trembles.)
Adrien: Don't worry, Marinette. There's nothing Chloé can do to us anymore. (reaches for her hand)
Marinette: I'm sure she's come back to get revenge!
Sabrina: Or not.
(Everyone looks at her.)
Everyone: Huh?
Sabrina: I mean, maybe she's changed!
Marinette: Huh? Are you serious?
Sabrina: Why not? I hurt you guys too. I was Chloé's accomplice, but you forgave me, and now we're friends!

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Zoé: Yes, but unlike my sister, you understood how you were hurting people and you decided to change.
Marinette: Chloé has never wanted to change. Have you seen her videos? You know why she's here today! She's keeping us from going to school!
Sabrina: I know, but... she wrote me this!
(She hands a letter over to Marinette.)
Marinette: (reading) "Dear Sabrina, I hope you're well. Since you've been out of my life, I've taken some time to reflect on all the harm that I caused you, and I'm sorry. I miss you. No one knows this, but the movie is just an excuse. I'm only coming back to Paris because I hope you will talk to me, and perhaps, forgive me." (puts the letter down) I'm sure it's a trap.
Alya: Obviously. The real Chloé would've written something like "Sabrina, I've run out of people to bully! I'm coming back to Paris because you're no longer here to think for me, which gives me utterly ridiculous headaches!"
Sabrina: Or... she's actually changed!
(A helicopter flies down, causing the crowd to clamor. Chloé is shown inside looking at fan mail.)
Chloé: A love letter? Ugh! (crumples up letter and tosses it) Those fans are ridiculous, utterly ridiculous!

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
(She then opens the box from Cerise, picking up the pearl-adorned box inside.)
Chloé: Ooh! Finally, something interesting.
(She tosses the cardboard box to her worker, or "Jean," and tries to open the pearl-adorned box, which remains shut.)
Chloé: Ugh, who's dumb enough to send me a gift that's too hard to open!
Jean 1: (looking at cardboard box) There's no sender's name or address—just a stamp. A beautiful one.
Chloé: You're so useless, Jean-Régis!
(Two "Jeans" help Chloé out of the helicopter while the Jean in the helicopter steps out clumsily with the fan mail and a selfie stick in hand. The crowd tries to barge in while another Jean keeps them at bay. Chloé waves at her fans and then talks into the camera Jean 1 is holding.)
Chloé: (from livestream) Hello, Paris! Now's your chance to snap a photo of me! Enjoy!
Cerise: (to herself) Hello, Chloé.
Chloé: Cut, Jean-Régis! Ugh, these losers really busted my eardrums!
(After they enter the building, Sabrina stares at them assuredly.)
Sabrina: I'm going in!
Marinette: (grabs her hand) No, don't! I'm sorry, Sabrina. Do you... do you really believe what she wrote?

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Sabrina: Of course not. I just want to make sure. Don't worry—she has no control over me anymore!
(Marinette lets go of her hand and nods. Sabrina starts marching towards the entrance, and then clutches her chest, where her brooch is.)
Roger: Here, Sweetie! You got a letter!
(Sabrina takes the letter and looks it over. As she reads it, she gasps and clutches it happily. She then opens her closet and takes the brooch out of the trash, where several other things relating to Chloé are thrown away. She clutches the brooch to her heart.)
Sabrina: (to the guard at the front of the school) Hello, I'd like to see Chloé. (whispering) I'm her best friend.
Jean 2: (laughs) Nice try, but Miss Bourgeois doesn't have any friends.
(Sabrina looks down, dejected.)
Marinette: I'm gonna go help her.
Adrien: Are you sure, Marinette?
Marinette: Yes, yeah, don't worry. (walks to the guard) Hello, sir. As a member of the Paris City Youth Council, I am requesting to speak with Chloé Bourgeois.
Jean 2: That's nothing. Miss Bourgeois doesn't have time.
Marinette: But, I mean, youth with Paris City Hall—that's not nothing!
(Zoé sighs and joins them.)
Zoé: Tell Chloé that her sister wants to see her.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Jean 2: (talking through earpiece) Hello, Jean-Régis? It's Jean-Régis. Do you copy?
Jean 3: (over earpiece) Yes, Jean-Régis.
Jean 2: No, I meant the other Jean-Régis.
Jean 4: (over earpiece) I'm listening, Jean-Régis.
Jean 2: Right. I've got family at the door.
Chloé: Ugh, this box has to open sooner or later! (to Jean 1) And you, hurry up, already! (takes off mask and looks at the large tree in the courtyard) Ew! What is that thing?
Jean 5: Uh, that's a tree, ma'am!
Chloé: (tosses mask) Ugh, who cares. It wasn't there when I went to this school. Chop it down, right now!
(The camera pans to Audrey and Noé in the corner, with a Jean holding a parasol over Audrey.)
Audrey: Chloé!
Noé: Let her express herself, Mother! (to Chloé) Chopping down a tree is a brilliant idea! You're incredible, Chloé!
Chloé: Duh, of course I'm incredible!
(She continues to try to open the box while Jean 4 walks up to her.)
Chloé: What?!
Jean 4: Uh, Ma'am Bourgeois, there's a family member asking to see you.
Chloé: A family member? Who is it?
Jean 4: Your sister, or so she says.
Chloé: (stops struggling with the box) My sister? Does she have weird colored hair?

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Jean 4: It's blonde, with red and blue highlights.
Chloé: Is she alone?
Jean 4: No, she's with two other girls. One has pigtails, and the other one wears glasses.
(As he describes them, chibi forms of them pop up.)
Chloé: My underling, my punching bag, and my half of a sister, all at the same time!
(In the background, chibi versions of the three are tied to the tree while Chloé shoots tennis balls at them.)
Chloé: Aw, a little entertainment like the good old days! Jean-William!
(She tosses the pearl box, which Jean 1 catches.)
Jean 4: Who's Jean-William?
Chloé: You are, you dummy!
Jean 4: But I thought I was Jean-Régis!
Chloé: Who cares! Bring them in! And bring me three onesies, a tennis ball machine, and some chalk!
Audrey: Chloé, no! We have other plans!
Noé: Let her be, Mother.
(He nods at Jean 4, who nods back and walks towards the entrance.)
Noé: This won't change our plans. If anything, it will earn her even more fans! Two million more, and she'll be the world's number-one influencer!
(He shows Audrey his tablet, which has her Zoo analytics.)
Audrey: Oh, I'm so relieved that she's finally serving a purpose, even though I don't get any of this stuff.

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Noé: It's quite simple. Chloé is such a caricature that she manages to make people forget how unacceptable her actions are. With her, evil becomes fun. Evil becomes cool. Evil becomes aspirational.
(As he says this, Chloé blows a kiss to the camera and then sniffs a coffee cup and tosses it away.)
Audrey: Hm, evil becomes the trend! That, I understand.
Jean 4: Okay, Jean-Jean, let them in.
(Jean 2 steps out of their way, and the three start walking in.)
Sabrina: We're about to meet the new Chloé! I mean, if she's changed.
Marinette: And if she hasn't, at least we'll be together to face her.
(They enter the school.)
Chloé: Ah, my favorite victims. I can already smell their fear. (to Jean 1) Jean-whatever, film this! (to Marinette, Sabrina, and Zoé) Come closer, I'm not gonna bite you!
(Marinette looks at Audrey, and then sees the tennis ball launcher. The three of them start coming closer and step on a red "X" on the ground.)
Chloé: Jean-Patrick, now!
(Nothing happens.)
Chloé: Hm? What are you waiting for? Fire! Fire, fire, fire!
(The three girls look down and see the X, and then quickly step back.)
Jean 6: (from second floor, holding a net launcher) Does Jean-Patrick mean us?

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Jean 7: (from higher up) No, we're Jean-Régis!
Jean 8: Nope, we go by Jean-William now. She changed it earlier.
(The three Jeans launch nets. Chloé laughs before the nets hit the "X", capturing no one.)
Chloé: (to Jean 6, 7, and 8) Ugh, come on, you're such losers! Utter losers!
Zoé: What were you planning to do to us, Chloé?
Chloé: Duh, I just wanted to capture you and hang you from the tree so I could fire tennis balls at you!
(The same chibi visual appears again.)
Marinette: See, she hasn't changed at all.
Sabrina: But Chloé, I thought... your letter said...
Chloé: My letter? What are you talking about, Little Miss Traitor?
Sabrina: I get that you're scared of showing your new face, Chloé, especially in front of Marinette and Zoé, but I know you can do it, just like you found the courage to write to me and tell me that you decided to change—to become the beautiful person I always knew you could be! To become our friend!
(Chloé stares at her before laughing.)
Chloé: You're ridiculous, utterly ridiculous! (continues laughing) I never wrote you anything! (laughs some more)
(The ultrakuma perks up from inside the box.)

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Marinette: We know very well you had one of your assistants write it. You should be ashamed of yourself for being so cruel!
Chloé: Thanks for the compliment, but I still have no idea what you're blabbering about. The last time I ever wrote something was to Santa when I was six, and I didn't even write it—I dictated it!
(She takes the letter from Sabrina and tears it to shreds.)
Marinette: Okay, Chloé, hold it off! You can stop now! (to Sabrina) Come on. Let's go.
Cerise: Just a little more. Come on, Chloé.
Chloé: You should see your faces! You really look like three losers!
Marinette: I'm sorry, Sabrina.
Sabrina: Don't be, Marinette. Chloé has no idea what she just did. (to Chloé) Thank you, Chloé.
(The three of them walk away.)
Chloé: What do you mean, "thank you"? Are you kidding me? Where do you think you're going? Stay here. Heel! Ugh, I don't care if you leave anyway. I'll be putting you losers in my film, and the actresses I'll pick to play you will be just like you—ridiculous, utterly ridiculous! And—and... during the film shoot I'll destroy your school, and it won't be rebuilt! You'll no longer exist, in my film or in real life!

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
(Audrey and Noé give each other a look. The three girls begin to leave before Marinette steps in her tracks, laughing.)
Chloé: What's so funny, Baker Girl? I meant what I said. You should be shaking with fear!
Marinette: Earlier, when I saw you were back, I was afraid. I remembered all those years of your bullying. But hearing your absolute nonsense just now, I don't even know how I could ever be afraid of you. I'm laughing because you're" the one who's ridiculous, Chloé. Utterly ridiculous.(The three leave and Chloé seethes. Audrey and Noé share another look.)''
Jean 1: Uhh, should I stop filming?
Cerise: Evil always finds a way.
(She unlocks the box through her phone.)
Chloé: Oh really? I no longer scare you? I've been too nice—too weak—and now you're making fun of me?! Ooh, but I'm about to reverse the trend! You'll be everybody's fools! And believe me, you'll be terrified like never before in your entire lives! Fear Dread Queen!
Dread Queen: Bow to the Queen of the Dreadzone!
(She tosses a spinning top similar to the one she had as Queen Wasp. It creates a field encasing a large area around her. Chloé fans run and drop their signs, as Marinette's class runs as well.)

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Jean 1: Please, don't hurt me! (falls to the ground)
Dread Queen: You can't even get up on your feet, can you? (to Marinette, Zoé, and Sabrina) Girls, it's your turn to be afraid!
Sabrina: She's coming for us!
Zoé: We better run!
Marinette: Let's split up so she can't follow us all at once!
(The girls run away in different directions.)
Dread Queen: (laughs) Run, you scaredy-cats! You can't escape my magic dome anyway! I'm gonna get you one after the other! The only question is, who will be first? Eeny, meeny, Marinette Dupain-Cheng! Ooh, perfect!
Plagg: The last time I was this fearful, we were all out of cheese!
Adrien: I feel afraid too, but the people of Paris are counting on us. Plagg, claws out! (transforms into Cat Noir)
Dread Queen: (sing-song) Oh Marinette! Where are you hiding, Baker Girl?
(Dread Queen gets closer and Marinette starts hyperventilating, covering her mouth. Right as Dread Queen gets very close to her, she turns and walks away. Marinette somewhat calms down, and Tikki pops up.)
Tikki: This new akumatization of Chloé has me more frightened than usual!
Marinette: Yes, me too, but... we still have to get out there, right? Tikki, spots on!

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
(She transforms into Ladybug and zips away with her yo-yo.)
Dread Queen: (sing-song) Oh Marinette!
(Cat Noir drops down on a lamppost.)
Dread Queen: Ah, here comes the cavalry!
Cat Noir: Don't you mean the cat-valry?!
Dread Queen: Didn't anyone ever tell you puns are for losers, Loser Cat?
Cat Noir: Didn't anyone ever tell you to mind your own buzz-ness?
(Cat Noir runs towards her, but once he gets close, he falls to the ground.)
Cat Noir: No, no, I didn't really mean that! Forget it!
Dread Queen: Oh, that's more like it! Feeling a little fear brings you down a peg or two, doesn't it?
Cat Noir: Leave me alone! (runs to the carousel) Don't come any closer! Please!
Dread Queen: (laughs) Looks like I tamed you, cat!
(The camera quickly cuts to Cerise watching the livestream.)
Dread Queen: And now I'm gonna take your Miraculous! Because I like pretty magic jewels.
(Ladybug quickly hooks her yo-yo onto Cat Noir and yanks him towards her.)
Ladybug: Are you alright, Kitty Cat?
Cat Noir: There was nothing I could do, M'lady! I was a scaredy-cat for real!
Ladybug: Now that we're together, we're gonna be okay!
(Cat Noir nods.)

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Dread Queen: You are not calling the shots in the Dreadzone, Loserbug!
(She jumps up towards them, and Ladybug swings her yo-yo around as a shield.)
Cat Noir: Here we go again!
Ladybug: It's impossible to resist!
Dread Queen: That's right! I'm just irresistible, aren't I?
(Ladybug stops swinging her yo-yo and hides behind Cat Noir.)
Dread Queen: Not so clever now, super-losers! Give Dread Queen your Miraculous, and I'll let you get back to your ridiculous lives!
Ladybug: Never! (to Cat Noir) We're powerless against her!
(She flings herself and Cat Noir away from Dread Queen. They start running on the rooftops.)
Ladybug: I don't know about you, but I certainly didn't miss Chloé Bourgeois!
Cat Noir: Neither did I! Do you think the ultrakuma's in her top?
Ladybug: Maybe. I just can't think clearly right now!
Dread Queen: (in the distance, catching up) From now on, everyone will make fun of you two super scaredy-cats, because you're ridiculous, utterly ridiculous!
(Ladybug and Cat Noir hit the end of the Dreadzone.)
Ladybug: We're trapped!
Cat Noir: Cataclysm!
(He cataclysms the Dreadzone, but it has no effect.)
Dread Queen: No one can leave the Dreadzone! You two are at my mercy!

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Cat Noir: We need a hiding place!
(Dread Queen starts getting closer, before Ladybug swings herself and Cat Noir away again.)
Dread Queen: I'm not interested in playing hide-and-seek with you. I'll deal with you both later. In the meantime, I'm gonna have some fun with Dupain-Cheng! Get ready, Baker Girl. Dread Queen is coming!
(She hops away while Ladybug and Cat Noir calm down behind the wall.)
Cat Noir: I'm feeling better!
Ladybug: So am I. The fear seems to subside when she moves away!
Cat Noir: Yes, and it's a relief.
Ladybug: But the closer we get to Dread Queen, the more she frightens us. (gasps) That must be her superpower!
Cat Noir: As insightful as ever, M'lady. Wait a minute, how are we supposed to break the akumatized object if we can't get close to her?
Ladybug: There must be a solution. Lucky Charm!
(A small cable tie forms.)
Cat Noir: A cable tie? There's no way we can tie her up without getting too close!
Ladybug: Unless we don't use it on Dread Queen!
(Ladybug uses her Miraculous Call system to summon Vesperia and Miss Hound.)
Dread Queen: (sing-song) Oh Marinette!
(Zoé is shown hiding behind the corner before Ladybug summons her.)

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Pollen: Looks like Ladybug needs help, Your Majesty!
Zoé: Let's go remind Chloé that she doesn't call the shots around here! Pollen, buzz on!
(She transforms into Vesperia and jumps away. Dread Queen keeps searching.)
Dread Queen: Yoo-hoo, Marinette! Come to your queen!
(Sabrina hides behind a hedge as Ladybug summons her.)
Barkk: Is it time to go hunting?
Sabrina: Hunting for supervillains, yes, since Chloé will never change. Barkk, on the hunt! (transforms into Miss Hound)
Dread Queen: Hiding from me, are you, Dupain-Cheng? Oh, you must be trembling with fear already. But this is only the be—
Vesperia: Yoo-hoo, Dread Queen! Your fake Vesperia suit looks kinda weak. Nothing beats the real one that belongs to the real holder of the Bee Miraculous, don't you think?
Dread Queen: Well, since you're foolish enough to show yourself, I can finally take back what should have never been stolen from me in the first place!
(Dread Queen chases Vesperia and eventually corners her in an alley.)
Dread Queen: You really don't deserve that jewel, Ves-pathetic! First, I'll make you kneel.
(Vesperia falls to the ground in fear.)
Dread Queen: Next, you'll give me back my property yourself!

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
(Dread Queen reaches for the Bee Miraculous, but suddenly Miss Hound's ball is shot out of the tennis ball shooter, hitting Dread Queen's top. Dread Queen looks back to see the ball is connected to the cable tie and Ladybug's yo-yo.)
Miss Hound: Fetch!
(The ball travels back to the top and collects it.)
Dread Queen: Noooo!
Cat Noir: No scaredy-cats here.
(He cataclysms the top, turning Dread Queen back to Chloé and removing Vesperia's fear.)
Ladybug: No more evildoing for you, ultrakuma! (She opens up her yo-yo.) Time to de-evilize! (She catches the ultrakuma.) Gotcha! Bye-bye, little butterfly! (She tosses the cable tie into the air.) Miraculous Ladybug!
(The Dreadzone disappears and everyone's fear is removed.)
Chloé: Ugh, why do you always stand in my way!?
(Ladybug hesitantly pulls out a Magical Charm.)
Ladybug: Chloé Bourgeois, this—
Chloé: Drop it, Loserbug! I don't want your magical thingy! I'm shooting my movie anyway, and everyone will find out that you're ridiculous, utterly ridiculous!
Caline: If I may, Chloé.
(Mayor Caline Bustier is shown exiting Roger's police car.)

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Caline: That's not going to happen. The permits requested by Mr. Noé Luxus didn't mention your intentions of having some work done in the school, which renders the contract null and void.
Chloé: "Null and void"? What's that supposed to mean?
Caline: It means you no longer have any power here, and as mayor of Paris I'll never let you turn this city upside-down!
Chloé: (seethes; to her phone) Noé!
Roger: There's no one you can call. It's the law. You heard the mayor; remove your crew from the school right now or I'll start issuing tickets!
Chloé: (scoffs) If that's the way it is, then I'm going back to London! Paris doesn't deserve me!
(Ladybug slips the Magical Charm into Chloé's bag.)
Vesperia: It sure doesn't.
(Chloé huffs away.)
Miss Hound: Why did you give her the Magical Charm when she didn't want it?
Ladybug: So that she will remember that if she ever tries to terrorize people again, things will always end up exactly the way they did today.
The Miraculers: Pound it!
Chloé: Ugh, that Loserbug is such a pain. Jean-Régis, throw this thing away!
(She tosses it behind her and Jean 1 catches it.)
Noé: (to Jean 1) May I?
(Jean 1 gives him the charm, which he smirks at.)

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Noé: So much talent.
Mylène: All this trash... what a lack of respect!
Ivan: I think that was Chloé's last evil act for good!
(Sabrina sadly looks at the brooch Chloé got her before tossing it away.)
Zoé: Why did you thank Chloé earlier?
Sabrina: Because by being malicious one last time, she gave me what I needed to get her out of my heart for good. And now, there's a lot of room in it!
(Zoé smiles. Meanwhile, while sweeping, the envelope Sabrina received flies over to Marinette. She looks at it, and then looks in the bin to see the cardboard box the jewel box came in. She compares the stamps.)
Tikki: Is something wrong, Marinette?
Marinette: The stamps... the stamps are identical! Which means whoever sent the ultrakuma to Chloé is the same person who sent the letter to Sabrina!
Tikki: The same person? Do you mean the new holder of the Butterfly Miraculous?
Marinette: I don't know who they are, Tikki, but based on what they did today, I'm afraid of what they're planning next.
Cerise: Excusez-moi ?
(Fei comes over.)
Cerise: That was incredibly delicious. Could I meet the chef? I'd like to congratulate him.
Fei: Are you French?

title: Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript
text:
Queen of the Dreadzone/Transcript - Intro
Cerise: Yes, but I've been living here for a few months now and this is my first time coming to your restaurant. The food really is excellent.
Fei: Follow me. I'll introduce you to Uncle Wang! He has family in France.
Cerise: He does? The 8-hour time difference must make phone calls a bit complicated, right?
Fei: Uncle Wang always gets the time wrong.
(Cerise looks at a photo of Wang, Fei, Adrien, Marinette, and Bastille. She smirks.)
Cerise: Whenever I wanna talk to my family and friends, I always call before dinner. That way I'm sure I won't wake them in the middle of the night.
Fei: Clever!
Cerise: Right?
(She evilly glares as the episode fades to black.)

title: Pyramid of Khafre
text:
Pyramid of Khafre - Intro
The , also known as Pyramid of Chephren, is the second largest pyramid among the Pyramids of Giza and Egypt. Built during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom, it is located in the heart of Khafre's funerary complex.

title: Pyramid of Khafre
text:
Pyramid of Khafre - Description
Built around 2530 BC, the Pyramid of Khafre is the second pyramid built within the Giza Necropolis, southwest of the Pyramid of Khufu.
It is a square-based pyramid with sides of approximately 215.16 meters, the maximum error of which, to obtain a perfect square, is plus or minus eight centimeters. It currently measures 136.4 meters in height, having lost more than 7 meters since its construction due to erosion.
Despite being smaller than the Great Pyramid of Giza , it appears larger due to its construction on higher ground and the fact that it has retained some of its limestone casing over its last 45 meters in height.
The Pyramid of Khafre is a tomb forming part of the Khafre funerary complex. It is believed to be the final resting place of Pharaoh Khafre, son of Pharaoh Khufu. It is surrounded by a well-preserved satellite pyramid and mortuary temple. A long funerary causeway connects the mortuary temple to the Valley Temple of Khafre, which adjoins the Sphinx Temple and the Great Sphinx of Giza.

title: Pyramid of Khafre
text:
Pyramid of Khafre - Trivia
The Pyramid of Khafre has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979 under the title "Memphis and its necropolis – the pyramid areas from Giza to Dahshur".
The Pyramid's ancient name was Wer Khafre (Khafre is Great).

title: Pyramid of Menkaure
text:
Pyramid of Menkaure - Intro
The  is the third great pyramid of the Pyramids of Giza. Built during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom, it is located at the heart of the funerary complex of Menkaure.

title: Pyramid of Menkaure
text:
Pyramid of Menkaure - Description
Built around 2515 BC at the request of the Pharaoh Menkaure, the Pyramid is the third pyramid built within the funerary necropolis of Giza, southwest of the ]]Pyramid of Khafre]].
It is a square pyramid measuring 105 meters on each side and 65.5 meters high. It is the only one of the three great pyramids of Giza to be unfinished.
The Pyramid of Menkaure is a tomb that is part of the funerary complex of Menkaure. It is presumed to be the final resting place of Pharaoh Menkaure and is surrounded by three satellite pyramids, the pyramids of the queens, the ruins of a funerary temple, and a necropolis of priests of the king's cult in the quarry used for the construction of the monuments. A 605-meter funerary road connects the complex to the Valley Temple of Mykerinos and another pyramid necropolis for Queen Khentkaous I.

title: Pyramid of Menkaure
text:
Pyramid of Menkaure - Trivia
The Pyramid of Menkaure has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979 under the title "Memphis and its necropolis – the pyramid areas from Giza to Dahshur".
The Pyramid's ancient name was Netjeri Menkaure (Menkaure is Divine).

title: Rainbow Bridge
text:
Rainbow Bridge - Intro
The  (レインボーブリッジ, reinbō burijji), officially Tōkyō Kō Renrakukyō (東京港連絡橋), is a suspension bridge which crosses the Tokyo Bay between the Shibaura Pier and the Odaiba wavefront, in Minato, Tokyo.

title: Rainbow Bridge
text:
Rainbow Bridge - Description
Built in 1993 by Kawasaki Heavy Industries, the Rainbow Bridge is a 798-meter-long steel suspension bridge with a 49-meter-wide deck and two 127-meter-high white support towers.
The bridge deck has two platforms. The upper platform is dedicated to highway traffic, including the Shuto Expressway No. 11, while the lower platform supports the Rinko Duro and an automated subway line.
There are also two pedestrian walkways, north and south, offering magnificent views of Tokyo Harbor and Tokyo Tower to the north, and Tokyo Bay and occasionally Mount Fuji to the south.
Lamps are placed on the wires supporting the bridge, and are illuminated at night by three different colors, red, white and green, using solar energy stored during the day.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Intro
"" is a season 1 episode of the series, Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. As based on the series' production order specifically, "" is the 21st written and produced episode of season 1. It is also the 21st written and produced episode of the series, overall.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Synopsis
Nickelodeon
When Juleka is excluded from the class picture, she is akumatized into Reflekta and threatens to turn everyone into a reflection of herself.
Netflix
Excluded from a class photo, dejected Juleka akumatizes into the villain Reflekta, who turns everyone, including Cat Noir, into copies of herself.
Disney Channel
A picture-day curse takes a sinister turn when Juleka is excluded from a class picture and transforms into Reflekta, a villain who wants to turn everybody into a reflection of herself.
Disney+
Ladybug and Cat Noir face Reflekta, alias Juleka.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
Ms. Mendeleiev's class is taking a class photograph in the courtyard of Collège Françoise Dupont. Waiting on the steps in the courtyard is Miss Bustier's class. Marinette is freaking out about how she's going to be in the picture with Adrien, since they're all in the same class. Standing behind them are Rose and Juleka, overhearing Marinette's conversation with Alya.
Juleka doubts that she will be in the photograph, given her history of things going wrong in photos. Rose tells Juleka that she isn't cursed, but Juleka doubts it. Ever since Juleka was a little girl, whenever someone tried to take a picture of her, something would get in the way. Rose and Marinette reassure her that this year will be different and that she will definitely be seen.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
Finished with Ms. Mendeleiev's class, Vincent begins adjusting his set for Miss Bustier's class using two rows of benches. Vincent makes the shorter people sit on the bench in front, those being Max, Alix, Rose, Marinette, and Mylène. For the back row, he picks Nathaniel, Alya, Sabrina, and Chloé to stand on benches. Chloé protests, stating that she must stand next to Adrien since they're the same height, using her hand to emphasize that their foreheads are at the same level. But he disagrees, prompting Chloé to bring up her father as a threat. Since Vincent has no idea who her father is, he shoots her down and waves her off, threatening to make her sit in the front row.
The rest of the students file in between the two rows, at least, all except for one. Marinette spots Juleka staying on the steps and makes Vincent halt in order to include her. He apologizes and tells Juleka that she can stand between Nino and Adrien. When she takes her place, Marinette comments that Juleka will be in the center of the photo, completely visible, and she'll destroy her "curse."

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
Vincent is about to take the picture but groans, finding he isn't satisfied with the seating arrangement. He starts moving Ivan around, prompting Mr. Damoclès to ask what is wrong. Chloé states that she is in the wrong spot, even after hearing him say that Ivan is throwing off the picture's harmony. She then goes as far as to try to push Juleka out of the way. Both Miss Bustier and Adrien scold her, and Vincent continues moving students around. Chloé continues her protests, saying that she is too far away from Adrien, but she is shot down again by Mr. Damoclès.
Right as Vincent clicks the shutter button on his camera, the battery flashes, dead. He leaves to go get a new battery, telling the students to stay in their places. Meanwhile, Juleka asks Miss Bustier if she can use the bathroom, receiving permission. Chloé tells Sabrina to make sure Juleka doesn't come back. Sabrina runs off to the bathroom, grabs a nearby chair, and props it under the door handle of the stall Juleka's in, trapping her inside. Sabrina returns just as the photographer puts a new battery in the camera.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
Chloé jumps down from the bench and stands next to Adrien, swinging an arm around him. Both Adrien and Marinette question Chloé about what she's doing there, but Vincent gets the class's attention again. Before Marinette can stop him, he takes the picture, the eyes of the students all on Chloé, except for Marinette, who is holding out an arm to stop the camera, and Adrien, whose face is directed at the camera lens by Chloé's hand.
Vincent thanks them for their time, stating that the photo is perfect, to which Marinette protests that they need to take it again and tells Mr. Damoclès about Juleka, whom he does not appear to realize is anyone, let alone a student at his school. When Marinette describes her, the rest of the class realizes she is missing and wonders where she is. Adrien states that she went to the bathroom. Seeing that if they manage to get Juleka back, she would lose her spot in the picture, Chloé redirects Mr. Damoclès into thinking about lunch and the other classes left to photograph, resulting in Mr. Damoclès refusing to retake the picture.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
During the lunch break, Rose searches for Juleka, finding her trapped in the bathroom. Freed, the first thing Juleka asks about is the photo. Rose mentions that she missed it, but it was Chloé's fault. Juleka says that she was foolish to believe that she could ever be in a decent photograph, lamenting that she is invisible and that no one ever listens to her. Rose protests, but Juleka runs out of the school to the Place des Vosges, sits on a bench and starts crying. Hawk Moth senses Juleka's sadness, and sends an Akuma after her.
At Collège Françoise Dupont, Rose explains to Marinette and Alya what happened. Marinette stands up, coming up with the idea to delete the picture so that Vincent will be forced to take another picture with Juleka in it. Sabrina and Chloé stand off to the side, overhearing their plan and vowing that Marinette will not get away with it.
Back at the Place des Vosges, the Akuma possesses Juleka's wrist mirror. Hawk Moth greets her as Reflekta, telling her that he'll make it so she'll be the only one that people see and will never be ignored again so long as she helps him in return. Juleka agrees and is akumatized.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
Meanwhile, Marinette sneaks inside Denis Damoclès's office to delete the photo, but Sabrina and Chloé are searching for her. Reflekta goes back inside the school and starts turning everyone into physically identical copies of herself, including poor Rose. Adrien quickly transforms himself into Cat Noir so he can stop Reflekta. Narrowly avoiding Reflekta's beam, he traps her in a basketball hoop. Cat Noir is about to use his Cataclysm on some lockers that are blocking the school's entrance. Before he can touch the lockers, Reflekta zaps him with one of her lasers, which also leads to Cat Noir losing his Miraculous.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
At the same time, Marinette gets herself caught on purpose by Sabrina and Chloé. When Chloé shows her the video of her breaking into the office, Marinette gives her an ultimatum: give her Chloé's phone so she can delete the video or she'll erase the class photo instead. Knowing she'll lose the picture of her and Adrien together, Chloé gives Marinette her phone. However, once the phone is in Marinette's hands, Sabrina takes out the camera's memory card. Marinette then gives Chloé another ultimatum: give her the card or she'll keep her phone. Suddenly they hear Reflekta's voice calling Chloé's name, and Marinette grabs the card from her running off to hide.
When Chloé steps out of the office after Sabrina runs to get Marinette, Reflekta finds her and turns her into Reflekta's mirror image. Marinette sees everything and runs to hide in the library, transforming into Ladybug. Ladybug realizes that Reflekta is Juleka, and she jumps in-between Chloé and Reflekta. Ladybug then flees when Reflekta is about to zap her into her mirror image. Cat Noir watches them and begins gathering up the transformed students so they can help stop Reflekta.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
Ladybug soon realizes that using her yo-yo is useless against the akumatized villain. However, before Reflekta can get Ladybug's earrings, Cat Noir and the transformed students surround them. They're about to get Reflekta, but she escapes and runs off to turn more people into her mirror image. Cat Noir takes Ladybug away from the group to talk in private. While Ladybug makes fun of his looks, Cat Noir tells her that attacking Reflekta from the front isn't the best solution, unless Ladybug changes her look, which gives Ladybug an idea. Using her yo-yo, both she and Cat Noir head to the TVi Tower.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
While Reflekta turns many citizens of Paris into her mirror image, Ladybug is at the TVi Tower, broadcasting to everyone that they need to wear a costume so she could tell which is the real Reflekta in order to stop her. While this is happening, Reflekta corners the Mayor in his office and tells him that Ladybug is not coming to save him. Now knowing where Ladybug is, Reflekta heads for the TV studio. As "Reflekta" walks into the studio recording room, Ladybug uses her yo-yo and ties "her" up. Cat Noir quickly takes off "her" wrist mirror and tosses it to Ladybug so she can get the Akuma. After she smashes it, they find the Akuma isn't in it. Both Cat Noir and Ladybug then realize that they have been tricked and learn the imposter Reflekta is actually the Mayor.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
The real Reflekta shows up and is about to zap Ladybug, but Cat Noir shields her taking the attack. The ray doesn't affect him since he's already been changed. Ladybug summons her Lucky Charm, and a camera appears. Ladybug tells Cat Noir to turn off the lights, and she uses the camera's flashes to temporarily blind Reflekta in order to evade her blasts. She manages to grab Reflekta's wrist mirror and breaks it, revealing the Akuma. Ladybug catches the Akuma and purifies it. She then tosses the camera into the air and cleanses the city, returning everyone, including Juleka and Cat Noir, back to normal.
As Marinette goes back to Collège Françoise Dupont, she tells Tikki that she has another idea to end Juleka's "curse". After returning Chloé's phone to her, as well as the memory card to Vincent, Marinette explains to him about Juleka not being in the picture earlier and suggests taking another picture with her in it.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot
When school's over, he once again takes the class picture, this time at the park. Chloé and Sabrina decide not to be in a "ridiculous" photo again, and Juleka thanks Marinette for ending her photo "curse", because she appeared in the center of every picture Vincent takes of her.

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot Developments
When Chloé records Marinette entering the Principal's office, Tikki isn't seen in the video. This further proves Plagg's point in "The Collector" when he states kwamis cannot be filmed or photographed.
It is revealed that Chloé, Sabrina, Nathaniel, Rose, Juleka, Max, Kim, Marinette, and three extras were all in Miss Bustier's class the previous year. The characters' attire and hairstyles are also different in "Derision":
Marinette wears her hair in a bun. Instead of pink, her pants are blue.
Sabrina's outfit is green instead of purple and teal. Her headband is also green instead of white.
Nathaniel's shirt is blue.
Rose's hair is longer.
Max's hair is round and circular and his shirt is blue with green edges.
Kim wears the same style of hoodie that he normally wears, but the majority of it is yellow with the sleeves being red.
Miss Bustier's outfit is lime green.
Interestingly, Chloé's, Juleka's and Denis Damoclès's outfits do not change.
This is the first time we see that if a Miraculous holder gets struck by an akumatized villain while attempting to summon their powers, said powers will be cancelled out or nullified, which is followed by "Sandboy" and "Malediktator".

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Plot Developments
Juleka says she doesn't like cats. This turns out to be ironic since she would receive the Tiger Miraculous which is foreshadowed in "Crocoduel".

title: Reflekta
text:
Reflekta - Trivia
Internationally, this episode first premiered in France.
In this episode, it is revealed that Aurore and Mireille are in the same class.
In this episode, it is revealed that Juleka hates cats.
Strange enough she didn't need Hawk Moth to give her powers when all she really needed was confidence training to be seen and heard.
Also this is the first time we see that an akumatized villain's powers are ineffective.
References
This is the second time where Ladybug's Lucky Charm resembles an akumatized villain's object both before it got akumatized following "Pixelator".
Allusions
The curse that is mentioned has been prominent before this episode aired; Juleka's face is blocked by Nino's hand in the title sequence.
When actually it's called a "photo day jinx", that usually when someone has a recent mishap before a photograph is taken.
During one of the final pictures, Adrien, Nino, Kim, and Juleka make a pose, referencing the "Charlie's Angels" franchise.
Chloé calls her classmates "Rugrats", referencing the 1991 Nickelodeon cartoon series centered around babies, being followed by Cat Noir in "Gigantitan".

When Reflekta confronts Chloé, a door can be seen behind them. When Chloé runs away, the door is replaced by a wall.
When Ladybug spun her yo-yo and said, "Thanks but I prefer the one I’ve got," her hair can be seen and not transparent through the yo-yo. In the next scene, her hair can be seen through the yo-yo.

title: Reflekta

Right before Marinette transforms, Tikki appears with a double white circle in her left eye.
Despite having photo shoots with him, Vincent referred to Adrien as "blond hair boy" as if he didn't know him.
When Reflekta attacks the students in the locker room, the girl with blonde hair is mirrored.
