In Paris again, Nightormentor is watching the fireworks, asking himself who Adrien is, where once again Cat Noir attacks him, 'suggesting' that Adrien is avoiding him, as he isn't a nice father. They engage in a brief fight, Cat Noir saying that he should leave the girl and boy alone, before Nightormentor once again uses Voyage, this time Cat Noir is unable to follow him, and falls off the building into the road, calling Nightormentor, and effectively Gabriel as a whole, a coward.
Continuing the play, 'Adrien' explains that the two twins grew up, both quite different.
The "firstborn": Émilie was more curious, escaping the life at court at every opportunity she could, meanwhile the "younger sister": Amelie wanted to please her family, becoming well-behaved and staying in the castle.
The king and queen wonder if they entrusted their legacy to the right princess, believing she will be better behaved eventually.
Due to this belief, Émilie was allowed to leave the castle, where she studied overseas in another kingdom.
Here is where she fell in love with a "humble tailor": Gabriel.
Marinette realizes who this is referring to.

title: Representation
categories: Episodes where Marinette is a minor character
text:
Representation - Plot
Gabriel made magnificent clothes that revealed the beauty of anyone who wore them.
Despite her parents' anger, Émilie gave up her legacy and luxury to be with the tailor.
She takes her ring off, splits it into two, and gives one half to Gabriel, while she keeps the other half herself.
Émilie concludes that the only thing left to have a truly happy life is for them to have a child.
Meanwhile, to please her parents, Amélie marries a man described to be "a wealthy, yet heartless Lord of War": Colt.
They also dreamed for a child, to be the heir to their kingdom.

title: Representation
categories: Episodes where Marinette is a minor character
text:
Representation - Plot
Going back to Paris yet again, Nightormentor is calling out for Adrien, when Cat Noir catches up with him, once again ridiculing him, saying he would not want a father like him. Nightormentor fights Cat Noir, saying he would teach him some manners if he was his son. Cat Noir tells him he would say that he couldn't always make decisions for people, that his responsibility for having a child is to allow them to blossom and be free. Just when Nightormentor is cornered and Cat Noir is about to cataclysm his blowpipe, he remarks on how sorry he feels for his son. Nightormentor says his son is very happy, putting Cat Noir in shock. This allows Nightormentor to kick Cat Noir back and finally hit him with the magic dust, awakening his nightmare, while Nightormentor tells him to learn some respect.
In the play, time passes, and neither couple were able to have a child.
After some time, Émilie resigned herself to the court, to be able to benefit from the remedies her sister did.
But this didn't work, until one day, the curious princess was expecting.
During this scene, peacock feathers appear behind the couple, shocking Marinette, as she realizes the truth.

title: Representation
categories: Episodes where Marinette is a minor character
text:
Representation - Plot
Colt is furious at this, believing he and his wife deserved a child more than Émilie who abandoned her kingdom.
Colt confronts Gabriel and says how it's unfair, whereas Gabriel suggests it's a miracle.
Émilie feels bad for her sister and brother in-law, and asks Gabriel if he can let them have a child as well.
Gabriel confronts Colt and says that he has found a solution for him and his wife, but he will have to pay a price: to give his best knight to guard their future child.
For this exchange a magic amulet will be lent, one that is able to give life to creations and dreams, and allows the creator to control them: the Peacock Miraculous.
Colt refuses to use sorcery; Gabriel says it ultimately up to him whether he decides to use it, but the former accepts and takes the 'amulet,' using the miraculous to create an amok and inserting it into his ring.
The jealously he uses comes to life, allowing his wife to become pregnant, once again showing peacock feathers in the background, though unlike Gabriel, Colt is reluctant to touch the belly.
A few months after this, both sons were born from their mothers.

title: Representation
categories: Episodes where Marinette is a minor character
text:
Representation - Plot
Cat Noir wakes up in his nightmare, where Paris is in ruins, the moon is destroyed similar to Cat Blanc, the sky is orange and everyone is destroyed, encased in fragile statues. His suit is white, while his hair, skin and eyes are blue. Cat Noir questions everything in horror while Nightormentor comments this is what happens to ill-mannered children who can't control their anger. Cat Noir realizes he is holding a destroyed Ladybug, denying that he did this, before the Ladybug crumbles to dust. He kneels down and sobs, while Nightormentor says that if he hands over his Miraculous, the nightmare will end, which the distraught Cat Noir agrees to. The villain grins.
In the play, Colt has fallen ill some time after his son was born, believing he was paying the price for using magic the weaker he became.
This made his fear morph into hatred for his creation, his son, constantly mistreating and calling him a monster.
His son did not understand why his father didn't love him, which is said as 'Adrien' takes off his mask and faces Marinette.
Marinette realizes he and the son in the play are Félix, feeling sympathy for him.

title: Representation
categories: Episodes where Marinette is a minor character
text:
Representation - Plot
Félix also did not understand why he felt like he needed to obey his father at every command he gave, even if these commands were hurtful to him.
If he became fond of anything his father did not approve of, his father would then destroy it.
The lord of war continued to call his son a monster through all this time, partially damaging his ring at some point, causing the child to collapse.
Félix soon realized that his life was linked to the very ring that caused him to obey his father.
He could only recover the ring, and therefore his freedom, when his father passed away.
Félix realizes that 'amulet' that allow his mother to gave him life could also take away it.
He went to the tailor's house - who had become a prince - in order to steal the amulet.
But this prince was powerful, and the only thing he would trade the amulet for, were other amulets that he desired.
Marinette recognizes it as "The day she lost the Chinese Zodiac Miraculouses".

title: Representation

Nightormentor is just about to take Cat Noir's ring, when Nino's log is thrown at him, by none other than Nino, who is with Alya and Kim, asking him why he's so mean to people. They throw balls and other objects at him, distracting him long enough for Ivan to use a bunting banner to tie him up and get him away from Cat Noir. Nino sends Kim to check on Cat Noir, who slowly starts to come to his senses. Kim and later Max say that they need Cat Noir at 100%, as Ladybug is nowhere to be seen. In the play, the son then met a girl like him, which is narrated while both Félix and Kagami take off their masks, the two fell in love, exactly like the curious princess and the tailor, both of the couples just wanted to be free and love each other, but the tailor is trying to stop them, to which they could use someone's help: the help of Ladybug, the only one able to face the tailor, and the only one who can fix things.

title: Representation

text:

The play ends as Marinette turns on the light, still hearing narration in her head, telling her she knows how the son and girl feel, not being able to be with the one you love, having to fight to save the one you love, having to lie all the time, never been able to say who you are.
As this last line is said, Marinette unrolls a curtain to see a statue of her alter ego, Ladybug, startling her enough to wake up on the floor, in the exact position she started the play in, revealing that whole sequence to be a dream.

She closes the curtain, with a determined expression, and looks out the window, accepting to help them, as the feather flies out.

They share another kiss before they part ways.

title: Representation

text:
Representation - Plot Development
Nathalie is shown suffering further effects of using the damaged Peacock Miraculous. She has once again become bedridden, the red highlights in her hair have turned gray and she has visible bags under her eyes.
As of "Re-creation", this is the last akuma battle where Gabriel is Monarch.
The mysteries surrounding the Agreste and Graham de Vanily families are uncovered:
Émilie and Amélie are the only children of two aristocrats of the British nobility, though they were originally expecting a boy, with the former being the older twin and the one their parents have entrusted with their legacy, including the Graham de Vanily Twin Rings.
Growing up, Émilie was bold, adventurous, and escaped the nobility whenever she had the chance to, worrying her parents and made them wonder if they were right to entrust her with their legacy. Amélie was docile, obedient, and stayed indoors, doing whatever she could to please her parents.
Émilie went to study abroad, possibly to Paris, where she met, fell in love with and married Gabriel Agreste. Meanwhile, to satisfy her parents' will, Amélie married Colt Fathom.

title: Representation
categories: Episodes where Marinette is a minor character
text:
Representation - Plot Development
Amélie may be implied to have also been abused by her husband, due to the fact that the narrating says that "if he became a fond of anyone who displeases his father", and it shows an arm of a stuffed bunny being ripped and in "Gabriel Agreste", Amélie also wore a bunny mask in the party.
Both sisters had trouble getting pregnant, much to their despair. However, after finding the Peacock Miraculous, Emile used its power to get pregnant.
This confirms the theory that Adrien is a Sentimonster.
In order to placate his wife's sadness over her sister's inability to get pregnant, Gabriel strikes a deal with Colt, allowing him to use the power of the Peacock Miraculous to make Amélie pregnant as well, in exchange for the services of one of the latter's bodyguards to protect the former's son.
Colt used the Peacock Miraculous to get Amélie pregnant, giving life to his jealousy that became Félix. As Félix grew up, his father would control him heavily and never show him any love, especially after realizing that his creation had led him to start losing his life force. After Colt died, Félix got hold of his amokized object and, in this way, gained control over his own existence.

title: Representation

text:
Representation - Plot Development
This confirms that all the episodes from season 1 to season 4 are either named after akumatized villains (or group of akumatized villains), sentimonsters, or Miraculous holders.
That also confirms that Félix is younger than Adrien.
Both Émilie and Colt died due to have used the Peacock Miraculous to bring their respective sons to life.
Félix betrayed Ladybug so he could trade all the other Miraculous for the one thing that could end his own existence: the Peacock Miraculous.
Through Kagami and Félix's play, Marinette learns of the latter's reason to betray her and (only partially) that Gabriel Agreste is Monarch.
It is revealed by Adrien that the magical effects caused by an akumatized villain are cast on a person, they will remain until they are restored by the Miraculous Ladybug superpower.

Also as seen in "Timebreaker" and "Miraculous Shanghai", sentimonsters can be killed temporarily, but restored by the Miraculous Ladybug if their Amoks are still active somewhere.

The popular fan theory that Adrien and Félix were sentimonsters, which had been hinted at in many previous episodes, is finally confirmed in the episode.

title: Representation
categories: Episodes where Marinette is a minor character
text:
Representation - Trivia
This is the seventh season 5 episode that is not named after the concept of a Miraculous.
The concept is applied in the episode, showing how people put on a show for others:
Marinette tried to pretend everything was fine in front of her friends to not spoil the end of the year party with her sadness over Adrien's departure.
Félix disguised himself as Adrien to lure Marinette to Collège Françoise Dupont's art room.
He and Kagami used the power of their sentimonster, Once Upon a Time, to put on a play about Félix's life (and by extension, Adrien's) to tell Marinette why he betrayed Ladybug and why they need her help.
The concept is also applied through the powers/nature of some characters:
Gabriel akumatized himself into Nightormentor, a villain with the ability to manifest one's nightmares.
Argos gives life to his and Kagami's thirst for truth to create Once Upon a Time, a sentimonster capable of projecting scenarios and special effects for a play.
The revelation of Adrien and Félix's nature as sentimonsters shows how the emotions accompanying his, and possibly Adrien's, creation are reflected in their personalities.

title: Representation
categories: Episodes where Marinette is a minor character
text:
Representation - Trivia
Adrien is the representation of his parents' love for each other, a feeling that defined his kind nature.
Félix is the representation of the jealousy of his father towards Gabriel and Émilie, an emotion that, combined with his father's mistreatment, defined his cold nature, inability to properly interact with his peers and need to succeed at everything.
The concept of representation was applied in other episodes:
In "Despair Bear", when Chloé tried to put on a show of being nice to everyone else.
In "Miracle Queen" and "Protection", despite being happy for the other, neither Kagami nor Marinette couldn't contain their sadness over losing Adrien's love.
From "Multiplication", Gabriel and Tomoe have begun using holograms of Adrien and Kagami to convince the public their children are a couple.
Since her debut in "Volpina", Lila constantly put on a show with her lies fooling people into believing her to be someone she isn't.
Representation also means acting or speaking on the behalf of someone which is shown in other episodes:
In "Gamer", where Max and Marinette represented their school for the gaming tournament.

title: Representation

text:

In "Darkblade", where Chloé and Sabrina represented their class grade then the role was passed onto Marinette and Alya.
In "Hack-San", where Scarabella represented as Ladybug's replacement for the weekend.
In "Ephemeral", where Adrien represented as his father's replacement for the celebration of the 100th collection of his father's brand.
Ladybug and Cat Noir representing Paris' hope and light.
This also alludes to the Miraculers problem with Monarch, as long as they didn't know what the latter's problem was there wasn't much they could do to help unless Monarch speaks up himself, he messes up revealing or someone else does on his behalf.
A person's actions are also used to represent something:
Like Ladybug in Season 4, where her actions of pushing Cat Noir away and Shadow Moth's obsession represented her fear of Cat Noir being akumatized and being held responsible for it, like in "Cat Blanc".
And the fear she had for all her allies despite trusting them with the jewels and their powers, her getting them back after each mission shows her distrust in Monarch, but it came out of her care and love for others as she refused to let her allies get to used anymore than they already have.

title: Representation

text:

Gabriel's actions in trying to reunite his family represents his confidence, independence, dedication and passion but also his obsession, selfishness, desperation, lack of trust towards others and fear of the truth.
Adrien's and Félix's hesitant actions were the same as it represented their fear of being hurt again or hurting others.
Monarch remade the Miraculouses in "Multiplication" so only he, the people he akumatized, and the Miraculized can use them, therefore remaking their magic represents his selfishness, fear and greed.
The kwamis are the physical representation or embodiments of all the abstract concepts that came into the universe.
At first, Ladybug seeing her partner in white represented her fear but as of "Miraculous Paris" and "Jubilation", seeing Cat Noir in white represented freedom and love.
Representation can also be found in various objects as well:
How the Miraculouses were made to represent the greater good, but when used for evil purposes, then they represent danger and fear and the abstract concepts and the Kwamis they represent.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Intro
"" is a season 5 episode of the series Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. Based on the series' production order specifically, "" is the 23rd written and produced episode of season 5. It is also the 127th written and produced episode of the series overall.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Synopsis
Chloé is now more powerful than ever and, thanks to her, so is Monarch. Ladybug and Cat Noir wonder about their superpowers, unaware that they have just fallen into an evil trap. As for Marinette and Adrien, their lives are about to change forever.
Disney+
Ladybug and Cat Noir unknowingly face Queen Mayor.
Netflix
When Paris descends into chaos under her reign of a tyrannical teenage mayor, Ladybug will need all her power to defeat the villain and restore order.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
The episode begins with Chloé, now interim mayor of Paris, speaking to Nadja Chamack in a TV interview. She restates her first decree as mayor — Ladybug, Cat Noir and Monarch are outlawed. Seeming concerned, Nadja asks her if this is going to last long, which Chloé affirms. Advised by Cerise through the earpiece she is still wearing, she retracts her statements and promises to elaborate in a meeting. She finishes by announcing the start of "Chloé's Law", which will be enforced by her police robots.
Ladybug and Cat Noir finish watching the broadcast on a rooftop and stare at the robots traversing the streets of the city.
Cat Noir is determined to take action, but Ladybug is hesitant, pointing out that Chloé has not been akumatized and it would be immoral to attack a civilian.
With no further ideas, the two heroes hope for authority figures to resolve the situation as they focus on fighting Monarch, and split up.
Ladybug returns home and de-transforms into Marinette.
Upon entering her room, she turns on the news on her computer, where multiple Parisians are interviewed.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
Some see Chloé as a representative of young people, others express their distrust towards Ladybug and Cat Noir, yet others are clearly disapproving of the idea of a teenager in such a high position of power.
Back in his room, Adrien hesitates to call Marinette, hoping to convince his father not to send him away to London himself.
Plagg reassures him that since Marinette is the girl he loves and trusts, they can always find a solution together.
Suddenly, the phone rings — it is Marinette.
Adrien answers and tries to break the news to her, but she quickly interjects and asks about the news.
Adrien turns on the TV to see more interviews with citizens.
Marinette promises to call their classmates to brainstorm a solution before hanging up.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
In the restaurant of Le Grand Paris, Chloé is sitting at a table with her mother - who is evidently proud of her new position - Gabriel and Tomoe. She expresses great satisfaction with her new robots, using an opportunity to replace her butler with one of them to bring her drinks. Gabriel congratulates her on successfully banning Miraculous holders. A close-up of Chloé's Alliance ring reveals its camera function is turned on. In her Catacombs hideout, Cerise rewatches the recorded video, taking note of the briefcase used to control the robots. She praises Chloé for her performance, which Chloé uses as an opportunity to gloat. Behind her, two workers are repainting her office gold and one of them thinks the girl is talking to him. He gets immediately yelled at, fired on the spot, and removed from the room by one of the robots.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
In his lair, Monarch calls Mrs. Tsurugi. They discuss their plan to exploit Chloé's new position. Monarch absorbs Pollen, Orikko, Stompp, Wayzz and Kaalki's powers, while Tomoe prepares her control briefcase. Monarch teleports to the mayor's office, where he is immediately stopped by the police robots. Tomoe, in her lab, discreetly deactivates the bots' defense mechanisms. Monarch offers Chloé an alliance, which she initially rejects, but changes her mind because of Cerise's directive. Monarch proposes to grant her superpowers in a discreet way, meaning nobody would know that she is akumatized. Pleased with the idea of defeating Ladybug and Cat Noir while keeping a good public image, Chloé accepts the offer. Monarch sends out a Megakuma from his cane, which lodges itself in the mayoral sash. Chloé is transformed into Queen Mayor, and her robots receive the superpowers of the five Kwamis — Venom, Shell-ter, Resistance, Sublimation and Voyage. Upon completing the deal, Monarch makes his exit.
Standing in front of the school, Adrien is determined to tell Marinette the truth.
He makes his way to the entrance, but is surprised to see the students holding up signs in front of him.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
Nino tells him that it was Marinette, Alya and Mylène's plan, and the two boys praise Marinette for her skills.
Not long after, Queen Mayor arrives in her limousine.
She walks into school flanked by news reporters, who are entirely unaware of her being akumatized.
She then encounters the event planned by the three girls — a protest to reinstate Miss Bustier and Mr.
Damoclès, in which all the members of the Resistance are participating.
Queen Mayor tries to smear her classmates and she disavows Zoé as "the girl who is pretending to be her sister" as if she does not know her and the students as holding the school hostage, campaigning for the return of teachers who are a bad influence, with no regard for democracy.
Sabrina states that they're not taking the school hostage, and Ivan and Mylene demand elections be held, to which Chloé states that people who threaten the mayor go to "detention".
Caline tries to reason with Chloé to come to her senses, but she refuses to listen.
Seeing Marinette and Adrien holding hands, Chloé tries to reveal Adrien's secret, but puts it off for later at Cerise's instruction.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
In class, Olga Mendeleiev teaches a made-up history lesson about how ancestors of the Bourgeois family discovered gold, enabling the creation for every important human invention. Queen Mayor, the only student in attendance, is not paying attention, preferring to play with her briefcase. The remaining students are gathered outside the classroom, watching furiously. Suddenly, Marinette notices that Mylène and Ivan have disappeared, leaving behind their protest signs.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
As the sun sets, Ladybug and Cat Noir meet up near the Arc de Triomphe, on top of which an enormous golden statue of Chloé has been erected. Cat Noir still wants to act, but Ladybug deters him, believing Monarch is not involved with it. The next day, Adrien meets up with Marinette and Nino on the Pont des Arts for André's ice cream, still hoping to tell his girlfriend about his upcoming departure. Marinette instead asks the boy to speak to his father, hoping he'll be able to convince Chloé to step down. Their conversation is interrupted when Queen Mayor's helicopter descends on the bridge. She informs the ice cream seller that he'll need a permit to continue his business or he'll be sent to "detention" if he does not comply. André hands Marinette and Adrien their dessert, concerned that it might be his last. Nino is also worried, since Alya promised to meet up with them, but has not shown up nor answered any calls.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
Marinette returns home on her scooter, but to her surprise, she finds Queen Mayor lying on the bakery counter, eating chouquettes. The supervillain reveals Tom and Sabine had been sent to "detention" for trying to make her pay for the treats. Marinette frantically calls out for her parents when one of the police robots appears behind her. It stuns her using Venom, then teleports her away with Voyage. In his room, Adrien worries about his calls to Marinette going unanswered. He makes his way to the Dupain-Cheng bakery, but only finds Marinette's pink helmet on one of the counters. Outside, he also spots André's bike rolling along the street without the man driving it. A flyer for Chloé's mayoral candidacy is carried by the wind into his hand, and he deduces she is behind all of this.
Adrien bursts into the mayor's office, determined to find answers.
Queen Mayor mocks his concern for Marinette, then threatens to reveal to her the secret he has been keeping if he refuses to become deputy mayor.
Adrien remains undaunted.
A police robot appears behind him, Venoms him, then teleports him away.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
The place Adrien is taken to is revealed to be the "detention" Queen Mayor often mentioned — a large maze-like corridor with rounded edges set up in the Stade des Princes.
There are numerous large screens set up in it, which switch from a white display of Queen Mayor offering comforting words, to a red one with her being scornful.
Prisoners are followed and monitored by the police robots, who promise that anyone who finds a corner to stand in will be allowed to leave, despite there not being one.
Adrien and Marinette call out to each other.
On their own, they both come up with the same plan: they pretend to try to destroy one of the screens to cause the robots to shoot projectiles at them, which rip the screens off the walls.
Underneath the destroyed screens, they transform into Ladybug and Cat Noir.
Cat Noir uses his Cataclysm to create a hole in the floor, through which he and other prisoners can escape into the sewers.
Ladybug escapes by yo-yo swinging out of the arena.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
Meanwhile, Queen Mayor hosts a meeting in front of the Louvre. She announces that, since she has performed so well as the new mayor, an election will not be necessary. Both arrive at the scene and call upon their powers to prepare. Ladybug's Lucky Charm gives her a pair of panties. They interrupt Queen Mayor's speech and promise to bring an end to her reign. In the distance, from behind a building, Cerise dictates every word Queen Mayor says; the villain accuses Ladybug and Cat Noir of not respecting democracy, yet the vast majority of the attendees agree with Cat Noir that they don't want Chloé as the mayor. The heroes jump into action, but are taken by surprise and trapped in two Shell-ters. Ladybug's Lucky Charm touches the barrier and disappears. Cat Noir tries to break out using Cataclysm, but its effects are nullified, revealing the spheres have been enhanced with the power of Resistance. Queen Mayor gloats over her victory, reveals her invisible robots, and exposes herself as being akumatized. In the audience, Gabriel and Tomoe prepare to take control of the situation to seize the heroes' Miraculous.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
Ladybug and Cat Noir's de-transformation timers run out — they begin reverting back to their civilian selves, though they discover the process is occurring much slower this time and realize they can resist it.
Ladybug takes this time to speak to everyone gathered, thanking them for their support and encouraging them to remain resilient in the fight against Monarch.
Feeling empowered by the speech, the Resistance gathers the courage to act.
Right as Ladybug and Cat Noir thank each other for their time together, the Resistance get on the stage, and prepare to attack Queen Mayor.
The other Parisians in the crowd soon join, breaking the barriers and running into action.
In the process, the control briefcase is knocked out of Tomoe's lap.
She, Audrey, and Gabriel make their escape, leaving Chloé behind, while Cerise watches from a distance.
Parisians fight against Queen Mayor's robot army, some getting imprisoned.
Ladybug and Cat Noir, determined not to give up, boost their powers and overcome their time limit, unlocking their adult powers much to Gabriel's displeasure and asks Nooroo about this.
Gabriel and Tomoe then flee the scene and into their cars.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
They can use their powers many times without having to feed their kwamis.
Queen Mayor is surrounded by the Resistance. Miss Bustier snatches her sash and tears it, releasing the Megakuma, which causes all of the Shell-ters to break. Cat Noir destroys the de-akumatized robots one by one, while Ladybug purifies the Megakuma. Queen Mayor loses her powers and de-transforms back into Chloé. On her knees, she looks up in defeat, and sees all those who once had hope that she would change for the better look down at her furiously, fed up with her antics for the very last time. Ladybug takes a deep breath, a little hesitation on her face hinting whether she should give her a Magical Charm, and proceeds to open her yo-yo shortly after to do so, only to be stopped by André Bourgeois, who promises to rectify his mistakes. He forcibly drags his daughter away despite her protests, leaving Chloé completely unaware that she was used as a pawn in her own plan. Meanwhile, Cerise, still hidden behind a nearby building, seizes the opportunity to grab the briefcase that Tomoe dropped.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
Fireworks light up Paris as the students celebrate the end of Chloé's reign. They propose Miss Bustier to run in the upcoming elections. Zoé then informs them that the end-of-the-school-year party is about to begin. Marinette runs off to change. Adrien, upset at how he still does not get to tell Marinette about his departure, also leaves to prepare.
In their private jet bound for London, Audrey angrily reprimands her daughter for losing all her power and ruining the family's reputation and vows to take control of her life again, starting with her education. Chloé, seething that she even lost her mother's love and respect for her failure, stomps off to the back of the plane, where she looks through the contact list on her Alliance. She looks remorseful when she sees Sabrina on the screen, but quickly changes her mind and scrolls to Marinette, smiling deviously.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
Adrien runs back home. Upon entering, Gabriel tells him to pack his bags and refuses to listen to his son's protests. As Adrien packs, Plagg tries to cheer his holder up by pointing out his power upgrade, but it does not work. On the way out, Nathalie tells him that he cannot disobey his father, but also not to allow anyone to control his love life. As they drive to the airport, Adrien attempts to reason with his father one last time and even jump out the car, yet nothing works. Gabriel remains unfazed. Defeated and in tears, he calls Marinette, reveals the truth about his departure to London and apologizes. Marinette is heartbroken, and tears fall on the charm Adrien gifted her in her hand. She decides she will not leave him, grabs her helmet and runs off.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
At the airport, Adrien is lead by his bodyguard to the Agreste's private jet. Back in the car, Gabriel and Tomoe talk about their plan to launch "Operation Perfect Alliance" once their children arrive in London. Suddenly, Adrien notices Marinette on her scooter, getting chased by an airport employee. Fortunately, Placide I.T. allows him to leave the aircraft. They run to each other and share a passionate kiss on the staircase to the plane before being forcibly separated. The plane then departs as Marinette watches on.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot
In the post-end card scene, Marinette arrives at the end-of-year party at the Eiffel Tower, her mascara smeared from crying. She receives a call from Chloé, who tries to torment Marinette by mentioning Adrien's departure from Paris. However, Marinette cuts her off, stating that she is already aware of Adrien's departure but still knows that he loves her. She then firmly tells Chloé off, without raising her voice, emphasizing that Chloé has lost lost any and all power over everyone in Paris. Marinette ends the call by calling Chloé "ridiculous, utterly ridiculous" and sarcastically telling her to "enjoy her trip." Shocked, Chloé begins to cry as she realizes she has truly lost everything. Meanwhile, back in her lair, Cerise places the stolen briefcase on top of a drawn map, with the Agreste mansion marked as the target. She grabs a screwdriver and begins to work on it.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot Development
This episode begins directly after the events of "Collusion". This is the first non-special episode to do so.
"Collusion" and "Revolution" join "Origins", "Volpina" and "The Collector", "Queen's Battle", "Heroes' Day", "The Battle of the Miraculous", "Truth" and "Lies", "Shadow Moth's Final Attack", "Evolution" along with "Multiplication" and "Destruction", and "The Kwamis' Choice" as episodes that take place during the same day.
It is also confirmed that Marinette does not get expelled as she is seen on school grounds with her classmates, meaning Cerise & Chloé's plan was null and void.
It is revealed that Monarch is still able to use the Miraculous powers even after transferring them to other people, as after transferring the power of Horse Miraculous, Voyage, to Queen Mayor's robots, Monarch was still able to teleport away to his lair. This ability would be seen again during the events of "The Final Day".
A new effect of Resistance and, by extension, a new weakness of Lucky Charm, is revealed: if a Lucky Charm is touched by the effect of Resistance, then the Lucky Charm will disintegrate.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot Development
Ladybug and Cat Noir evolve their powers further by unlocking the ability to use their superpowers more than once and remain transformed. This is shown when Cat Noir uses Cataclysm repeatedly to destroy the police robots without transforming back.
With this scene, it is revealed that a minor doesn't have to be 18+ in order to unlock this ability but it is enough that they attain the maturity and wisdom of a normal adult and learn what it truly means to be a hero.
Interestingly, this is the third time where the de-transformation of an underage Miraculous holder happens slowly following "The Dark Owl" and "Troublemaker", but they were a result of Ladybug's Miraculous being multiple pieces.
It is revealed that Gabriel and Tomoe are planning "Operation Perfect Alliance", which involves some amount of Alliance rings being sold everywhere in the world, and all people wearing them are at their mercy. This operation won't start until they make sure their children are "safe" in London.
Adrien finally tells Marinette, he is going to London, ending a mini story arc that started back in "Pretension".
In this episode, Chloé finally faces the consequences of her actions:

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot Development
After spending years abusing her power, influence and privileges, she finally loses all of them, moving to London with her mother and having all her freedom taken from her.
Ironically, Chloé made multiple attempts to have her half-sister, Zoé, move back to New York over the past two seasons, but ultimately ended up leaving Paris herself instead. Her last attempt was in "Adoration" but she gave up altogether.
It is also possible that Chloé still has power, influence and privileges, as her mother is still a successful businesswoman in the fashion industry and a big name in New York.
However since Audrey is controlling Chloé’s life, her power will be limited.
Audrey's line foreshadows "Miraculous London".

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot Development
After spending years treating people as inferior and oppressing them, Chloé is left without any friends and any type of respect or compassion from the adults that had any hope for her, like Miss Bustier and her father. Even Audrey loses the little bit of love she had acquired for her older daughter back in "Queen Wasp". She is even abandoned (and betrayed) by Gabriel, Tomoe, and Cerise, whom she considered her allies and had brought her to power to begin with, after having served her purpose for them.
After relentlessly bullying Marinette for years, Chloé attempts to torment her one last time by revealing the secret Adrien had kept from her, only to have Marinette beat her to it. As a last confrontation between them, Marinette chastises Chloé, citing that she has lost all power over her and everyone else, and calls her "utterly ridiculous". Seeing Marinette stand up to and shut her down so harshly finally shatters Chloé's pride and spirit as she breaks down in tears, realizing that she has truly lost everything and hit rock-bottom.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Plot Development
This mirrors "Strikeback (Shadow Moth's Final Attack - Part 2)" in how Marinette/Ladybug reacted after Gabriel obtained every Miraculous from the Miracle Box.
This is also interpreted how Marinette and Chloé did this to each other, starting with Ladybug indefinitely suspending Chloé from having the Bee Miraculous, which caused her to team up with Hawk Moth, which consequently led to her expulsion from the team, losing her respect and admiration for the heroine she use to idolize, and her behavior getting worse.
In retrospect, Chloé lost her Miraculous and hero status because of Ladybug's need to protect her and her family, but then threw away everything else she had out of anger, greed, and a thirst for power, whereas while Marinette lost the Miraculous because of Felix's deal with Monarch, she still retained her friends, family, and Cat Noir due to her love, selflessness, and compassion.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
According to Wilfried Pain, the episode was officially ready at the time of May 21, 2023.
This is the sixth season 5 episode that is not named after the concept of a Miraculous.
The concept of revolution is applied in three specific events:
Chloé makes a revolution by forcibly taking over as an interim mayor and using the position to impose her will and selfish rules on Paris. After making an alliance with Monarch and getting akumatized by him, she takes her tyranny to an all-new level by "punishing" those who do not obey her rules.
Marinette and her friends hold a strike, refusing to attend classes until Miss Bustier and Mr. Damoclès are reinstated as their teacher and principal respectively.
Inspired by Ladybug and Cat Noir, the Parisians rise up against Chloé and her tyranny by fighting against her and her robots. Their actions not only corner Chloé, allowing Miss Bustier to de-akumatize her, but also inspire the duo to finally overcome the detransformation time limit of their Miraculous and achieve the same level of power as a grown Miraculous holder.
As well as other events where revolutions or revolts took part in other episodes:

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
"Mayura", as Ladybug and Cat Noir inspired the citizens of Paris to fight back against Scarlet Moth's army.
From various episodes, Adrien began to revolt against his father's rule.
In "Mega Leech", where Marinette and the school stood against Project Oxygen.
"Reunion", when Scarlet Fate and Dark Grimalkin revolted against their kings.
From "Miraculous Shanghai", "Gigantitan" and "Cat Blanc", where the akumatized victims revolted against their creator.
When in control of the amokized object or when not known the sentimonsters can revolt against the Peacock Miraculous holder.
"Miraculous Paris", where Betterfly revolted against the Supreme.
A scene where Monarch uses Voyage to leave his lair is reused from "Deflagration".
During the scene in Chloé's office, when she's talking with Cerise and the wall is being painted behind her, Chloé seemingly looks briefly at the camera.
This is the second time someone reuses a power previously summoned through the use of Sublimation, But unlike "Illusion" and "Deflagration", the power of invisibility is used in an akumatization.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
This is the second time people think the akumatized villain is not akumatized, following Risk in "Shadow Moth's Final Attack".
Because of that, Queen Mayor is the fourth akumatized villain not to change her civilian physical appearance when akumatized, following Vanisher, Glaciator and Chameleon (Despite being a sentimonster, she would be the fifth if we include Feast).
This is the second time Marinette is seen wearing a dress following "Emotion".
This is the third time Adrien and Marinette's lucky charms appear together in the same episode, following "Befana" and "Collusion".
This episode takes place in July on Bastille Day.
This episode takes the record the for the most uses of Cataclysm by a Miraculous holder (in the permanent timeline), with a total of six times, tying it with "Miraculer" for the most uses in a single episode being second to "Cat Blanc".
Although Chloé is the one akumatized and controlling the police robots, this is the first time the Miraculous superpowers are used by an object.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
Technically, Queen Mayor is Chloé's overall weakest akumatized form and the most powerless of any akumatized villain thus far, because she alone was powerless and the robots already had the capabilities to receive the Miraculous superpowers. The akumatization itself was just an excuse and cover-up for Monarch, so Chloé wouldn't figure out how he transferred the superpowers or suspect why her robots were capable of harnessing them.
When Queen Mayor arrives in her limousine, the news van's license plate is called "ZAG-100-UG" and Zag is the last name of Jeremy Zag.
This is one of the many times where both heroes transform off-screen.
This is the only episode of Season 5 in which Nooroo speaks.
This is the second time Marinette and Adrien was affected by Venom, with the former following "Passion" and the latter following "Illusion".
Caline borrows Ladybug's "No more evil-doing for you" line upon ripping up Chloé's mayoral sash.
Similarly, Marinette borrows Chloé's "Ridiculous, utterly ridiculous" line to retaliate against the latter.
This episode marks the second time Adrien and Marinette kiss each other in their civilian form and the first time they kiss as a couple.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
Technically speaking (and in the permanent timeline), this is the fifth time they kiss.
Their first kiss was in "Dark Cupid", when Ladybug kissed Cat Noir to free him from the titular villain's influence.
The second kiss was in "Oblivio", when Ladybug and Cat Noir kissed before the former went to repair the damages caused by the titular villain and the duo regain their memories and lose the ones they made during their amnesic state.
The third kiss was in "The Puppeteer 2", where Marinette kisses Adrien who was pretending to be a wax statue.
The fourth kiss was in "Elation", where Marinette and Cat Noir share a kiss during the time they were "in love" for one another.
Counting the alternate timeline in "Cat Blanc", where Adrien discovers Ladybug's identity and declares his feelings to Marinette and the dream Ladybug and Cat Noir had in "Jubilation", where they defeat Monarch and retrieve all the Miraculous, and later both get married and form a family with children of their own, they have kissed seven times.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
Despite being a sad moment for both, this episode also ends another mini story arc started in "Adoration" and continued in "Emotion" and "Collusion", where Marinette and Adrien can't get a good moment to have their first kiss after becoming a couple.
As of now, and in the permanent timeline and in an official way, Ladrien (Ladybug + Adrien) is the only ship of the love square not to have gotten a kiss as a couple. Because Adrien and Marinette are officially a couple, that may never happen, unless they reveal their secret identities to one another.
References
Chloé uses the quote "Revenge is a dish best served cold", a common quote used in most media but the actual pun/idiom is a pastry and is a reference to The Godfather. This is because the Dupain-Chengs work at a bakery. Hawk Moth uses this quote in "Kung Food", "Glaciator", "Frozer", and "Feast" after his akumatized villains have been defeated.
This is the tenth time Chloé gets akumatized, following "Antibug", "Queen Wasp", "Mayura", "Miracle Queen", "Queen Banana", "Penalteam", "Deflagration" and 2 off-screen akumatizations that were revealed in "Mr. Pigeon 72".

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
This time, she gets akumatized into Queen Mayor, her seventh akumatized form overall.
Chronologically, Queen Mayor was the penultimate akumatized villain of season 5 just as Penalty was the penultimate akumatized villain of season 4, although Miracle Queen was the final villain of season 3.
Chloé also becomes the last victim chosen by Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch to be akumatized.
Queen Mayor holds the record for being the longest akumatized villain in terms of duration of Chloé and overall every akumatized villains in the show so far in the permanent timeline, as she remained akumatized for days.
If alternative timelines are taken into consideration, then this record goes to Cat Blanc, who remained akumatized for several months before being de-akumatized by the present Ladybug.
This is the third time Lila (directly or indirectly) makes Chloé prompts to get akumatized following "Miraculer" and "Deflagration", and this is the second time she succeeds in getting Chloé akumatized after "Deflagration".
This is also the second time Chloé voluntarily allies herself to Monarch, with the first time being when the latter was still Hawk Moth in "Heart Hunter".

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
This is also the fifth time that Chloé has been voluntarily akumatized, following "Miracle Queen", "Queen Banana", "Penalteam" and "Deflagration".
This is the third time Monarch transfers multiple Miraculous powers, following "Transmission" and "Pretension".
For the first time, Monarch transfers powers to objects controlled by his akumatized villain instead of the villain themselves.
This is the seventh time when the Miraculous Ladybug superpower isn't used following "Ladybug and Cat Noir", "Catalyst", "Destruction", "Illusion", "Intuition" and "Emotion".
This is the seventeenth time where the Magical Charms don't appear since their introduction following "Sentibubbler", "Hack-San", "Ephemeral", "Kuro Neko", "Risk", "Evolution", "Destruction", "Illusion", "Passion", "Reunion", "Transmission", "Deflagration", "Intuition", "Emotion", "Revelation" and "Collusion".
However when Chloé was de-akumatized, Ladybug hesitated to give her a Magical Charm, but André got involved and took the responsibility to correct his errors.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
This is the nineteenth episode that features a post-credit scene, following "Miracle Queen", "Gabriel Agreste", "Optigami", "Sentibubbler", "Dearest Family", "Multiplication", "Jubilation", "Illusion", "Transmission", "Perfection", "Derision", "Intuition", "Protection", "Emotion", "Pretension", "Revelation", "Confrontation", and "Collusion".
This is the eleventh not to feature Gabriel Agreste, following "Multiplication", "Jubilation", "Derision", "Intuition", "Protection", "Emotion", "Pretension", "Revelation", "Confrontation" and "Collusion".
The end card is similar to "Miracle Queen" but with Marinette and Adrien with a sad expression instead of a happy sad face with Ladybug and Adrien.
When talking to Marinette on the phone, Adrien recited the same line as his father in "Risk", about not being worthy of someone else's love.
Chloé gets akumatized into a ruler-themed villain, just like her father in "Malediktator". Curiously, they share an akumatized object — the mayoral sash.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
This is the tenth episode in which someone other than Ladybug and Cat Noir breaks an akumatized or amokized object, following "Mayura", "Lies", "Furious Fu", "Mega Leech", "Crocoduel", "Kuro Neko", "Transmission" and "Pretension".
This is the tenth time where a Lucky Charm object breaks (excluding the broken plate in "Troublemaker") followed by "Robostus", "Weredad", "Miraculer", "Psycomedian", "Hack-San", "Miraculous Paris", "Derision", "Protection" and "Adoration".
This is the fifth time Marinette's hair is seen in a bun following "Animaestro", "Kwamibuster", "Derision" and "Emotion".
This is the sixth time that Adrien is seen crying, following "Cat Blanc", "Miraculous New York", "Glaciator 2", "Jubilation" and "Transmission".
Like "Miracle Queen" and "Kuro Neko", this episode also shows another parallel between Adrien and Chloé: this time, it is with their statuses and how they're disciplined.
Chloé constantly used her status and power to get what she wanted as well as due to her father constantly trying to please her, he didn't discipline her enough and let things get so bad that even he admitted his daughter was out of control.

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
While Adrien, on the other hand, didn't do such a thing as Chloé called him out for it in "Derision" and as well as calling her former friend "his daddy's little puppet". On top of that, Chloé had the freedom to go and do what she pleased while Adrien didn't. While she was constantly around others, he was kept away from them so there was no one he could pull his status on.
Even if he wanted to, Adrien still wouldn't do it because he is far too kind and would probably eventually realize he could be nothing like his father as he said that in "Glaciator 2".
Unknown to Chloé, as of "Representation", she really had no idea how right her comment was as she, like almost everyone else, didn't know that Adrien is a sentibeing.
Outside of that, Chloé, Gabriel, and Tomoe not only took advantage of their statuses, but also Ladybug and Cat Noir's too; more specifically, their moral code by akumatizing Chloé and making her appear normal, allowing her to slip under their radar.
Chloé becoming the mayor callbacks to what Marinette said about her in "Darkblade".

title: Revolution
text:
Revolution - Trivia
Upon discovering that Ladybug and Cat Noir finally have their adult powers and what Gabriel said about it, it is a callback to "Timetagger" about him refusing to wait until they were adults to get the jewels, but they are now.
Just like in "Miraculer", Chloé was a part of Ladybug and Cat Noir's test this time to see if they could stand up to those who fight under any condition.
Like in "Passion", it's a bit of a flip as the heroes rise in power, Chloé loses the last of hers.
Allusions

Kim calling himself "Super Underpants" is a reference to an American comic book hero Captain Underpants.
When Gabriel and Tomoe are running, abandoning Chloé, their running animation is similar to Fred "Freddy" Jones from Scooby-Doo!.
Whenever a police robot appears by Sublimation, they make a sound effect resembles where a Swoopin' Stu/Gooble jumps in "Super Mario Sunshine" (albeit the pitch is higher).

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Intro
"" is a season 5 episode of the series Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. Based on the series' production order specifically, "" is the 20th written and produced episode of season 5. It is also the 124th written and produced episode of the series overall.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Synopsis
Lila is an accomplished liar. This evil talent has allowed her to be loved by all, and even to be hired by Gabriel Agreste. But Marinette and Adrien's growing closer pushes the boy's father to name Kagami as the new face of his brand, enraging Lila. She uses an incident in class to call for new elections in order to replace Marinette as class representative. But the campaign goes wrong, much to Monarch's delight. Tread lightly, for with Lila, things are more than often not what they seem…
Disney+
Ladybug and Cat Noir face Hoaxer.
Netflix
After losing her job, Lila takes it out on Marinette by running her class representative, but her campaign turns dangerous when Monarch steps in.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
The episode starts with Lila apologizing to her supposed mom, saying that due to the internet in the savannah, she has to go and save a baby rhino and she will call her later and hangs up. Just then, another one of Lila's mothers who is deaf walks into the room and asks Lila who she was talking to with sign language. Lila replies that it was her agent and goes to Sabine's art class. She gets on a bus and uses her acting skills and the fact that her face and voice are used on Alliance rings to get a free ride. She uses this opportunity to lie and make herself look better to the other passengers. She arrives in front of the school and picks up a coin from the ground and puts it in her purse.
At the art class, all of the Alliance rings update as Lila is replaced by Kagami. At first Lila, is angry but decides to take advantage of the situation. She then uses the fact that she is no longer the female model on Alliance rings to impress the other people at the class and say that she decided to quit to spend more time with Sabine. She also tells the other people that Marintte is not.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
Meanwhile, at the Agreste mansion, Gabriel takes off his left glove and sees most of his hand is completely black and that Cat Noir's cataclysm has spread there. Nathalie walks in his office and tells to Gabriel that someone is waiting for him at the gate. Gabriel uses his computer and sees Lila at the gate, telling him that she believes the update was part of their agreement and the face of his brand. However, Gabriel tells Lila she was only the face of the Gabriel brand in exchange for the mission in which she had to keep Adrien away from bad company and that she failed at it. Gabriel tells Lila she will remain as nothing as the camera retracts back into the wall and the conversation ends. At the outside of the Agreste mansion, Lila is extremely angry at what happened with the new update and with what she has just heard. Gabriel is tempted to use Lila's anger but resists, deciding that akumatizing a person who hates him is not a good idea. Lila walks off.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
At school, Marinette and Adrien are walking through school, holding hands as they notice everyone is adoring the image and idea of Adrien and Kagami together as a couple on their Alliance rings. When Marinette asks Adrien whether or not he was aware about the recent update, he replies with no. When Marinette's friends rush over and Rose asks Adrien about whether or not his father knows that he and Kagami broke up. Adrien answers with they are just images and that his father can do nothing to force his truth on them as Lila listens in on the conversation as the bell rings and class starts.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
In class, Miss Bustier is giving back the students their test results. When she gives back Chloé and Sabrina's result, she points out that both papers have Sabrina's name. Chloé is surprised and angry at Sabrina who apologizes and says it was due to her not sleeping for several nights as she was preparing the end-of-year exam cheats. Miss Bustier is shocked as she asks Sabrina whether or not she has been doing Chloé's homework the whole time only for Chloé to tell her that Sabrina forged Chloé's handwriting and finds out that this has been going on ever since Sabrina became literate and that Chloé doesn't know how to write. Miss Bustier decides to give Sabrina's real grade and that she must not waste her energy for Chloé and she needs some for herself as well. Miss Bustier then deduces that it must have been a very long time since Chloé did any of her own work, she is falling behind and she is going to need help.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
Marinette objects, saying that it is unfair that the only punishment that Chloé will receive is just her getting help. Miss Bustier then tells Marinette that Chloé being behind is already enough of a punishment and she is just like everyone else at the school. Chloé disagrees with the idea of her being like the other students as she has wealth and that there is no need for her to learn because she will never need to work. Lila sends a text to Chloé saying she will handle it and she has got it. Lila tells Marinette that she must have discussed Chloé's difficulties to the other teachers as the class representative. Marinette is confused as she points out Chloé has no difficulties but instead just privileges. Lila uses her acting skills to lie that Marinette's relationship with Adrien means she does not have time for her class rep duties. Lila goes on to say she quit as being the female face for the Gabriel brand to make time with her classmates and tells everyone that due to her being absent the day when class elections were held, it was not fair and she could be the new class rep. Miss Bustier then decides to consider about Lila's proposition at lunch.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
At lunch, Marinette tells Lila is always up to trouble but Alya steps in and says Marinette disliked her from her first day and that there has been no evidence of Lila doing anything wrong. Adrien agrees with Marinette by also saying Lila is a lair. Alya and Nino aww, saying that it is adorable how Adrien is willing to agree with Marinette. At a different lunch table, Lila and Chloé agree that they both want to get rid of Marinette and make her lose all that she has. Lila tells Chloé that if she does everything she says, Chloé will get what wants at the end as Sabrina listens in.
Class resumes as Miss Bustier announces she has decide to take on Lila's suggestion and hold an election as to whether or not Lila should become the new class representative. Lila gives a speech and makes Chloé her deputy as the class wonders if Lila can make Chloé change for the better as Marinette is infuriated. Marinette and Alya give their own speech of their own. Just when the class is about to vote, Lila decides to quit the election, saying that Marinette was right to insult her and that Gabriel Agreste fired her as she loved helping people. Lila runs out of the classroom, pretending to be crying.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
In the locker room, she places her phone in her locker and tries to get Monarch to sense her anger in a bathroom stall. Monarch in his lair, senses some powerful hatred. Shocked that the emotion is Lila's, he considers for a few seconds whether or not to grant her powers and the consequences that may happen. He decides that the anger is no longer directed at him and creates a megakuma and uses Kaalki to teleport it to her. The megakuma arrives in the bathroom stall and enters Lila's Alliance ring. Monarch gives Lila the power of the Fox Miraculous as Lila is akumatized into Hoaxer.
Monarch takes off his Alliance ring in his lair and destroys it so Lila can't control him. Hoaxer walks out of the bathroom stall and enters everyone's Alliance rings. She then hypnotizes everyone who is wearing an Alliance ring. Marinette transforms into Ladybug in a bathroom stall as Hoaxer tells everyone of a fake revelation that makes everyone believe Marinette is Monarch and that she wants to akumatize Lila. Everyone in the classroom that wears Alliance rings believes Hoaxer's fake news as they walk out of the classroom and ignore Adrien's warning. The classmates run and search for Marinette.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
Adrien splits up from Ivan and Mylène and transforms into Cat Noir in the classroom. The people of Paris hunt down Marinette as Ladybug and Cat Noir meet up. They capture officer Roger and takes off his Alliance ring as he reverts back to normal. The Parisians stop looking for Marinette before Hoaxer tells her victims who are under her control that Ladybug and Cat Noir have taken off their ring. She makes up a new story that Ladybug and Cat Noir are from outer space and tells them where Ladybug Cat Noir, at City Hall. The people of Paris run after Hoaxer tells them to capture Ladybug and Cat Noir's Miraculous and bring them back to her. The people surround the heroes as they give officer Roger's ring back to him and tell him to not put the ring on. They run off and hide as Ladybug uses her Lucky Charm and receives a sewing machine. She runs off while Cat Noir distracts the hypnotized Parisians.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
Back in her room, Ladybug figures out that the sewing machine brought her here as Alya jumps out of nowhere and as her Alliance ring is removed. Ladybug and Alya are on a rooftop as Ladybug detransforms back into Marinette. She gives the Ladybug Miraculous to Alya as Hoaxer appears and tries to take Cat Noir's Miraculous who is captured.
In her room, Nathalie receives a revelation from Hoaxer that tells her that Gabriel Agreste is an alien and that he must have other secrets that he is hiding. Nathalie gets out of her bed and uses her phone and not her Alliance ring just like how Hoaxer ordered her to. Nathalie takes pictures of Gabriel Agreste's fry shop, a menu at the shop, one of Gabriel Agreste's old passports, a picture of the fry costume designed by him from in "Psychomedian", a picture of André Bourgeois, Audrey Bourgeois, Gabriel Agreste and Émilie together in their younger days and a picture of Nathalie, Gabriel Agreste who is holding the Peacock Miraculous and Émilie on the Tibetan mountains where they dug up and found it and the Butterfly Miraculous.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
Cat Noir is fighting the other people of Paris while Nathalie sends Hoaxer a picture of a document in the safe behind the painting of Émilie signed by Gabriel Agreste about his brand and Tomoe Tsurugi's company. Nathalie also takes pictures of pages in the Grimoire. Marinette appears and presents herself to Hoaxer. Meanwhile, Nathalie uses the elevator and arrives at the Crypt. She takes a picture of Émilie in her coffin and a picture of her wearing one of the Graham de Vanily Twin rings. Scarabella, who is hiding, texts Cat Noir about her plan to defeat Hoaxer. In her room, Nathalie then sends Hoaxer all of the photos that she requested, puts it back into her safe and returns to her bed. Hoaxer rejects the megakuma and is deakumatized back into Lila as she smiles deviously. Scarabella throws the Lucky Charm into the air as it puts everyone where they belong and turns people back to normal.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot
Monarch detransforms in his lair and turns back into Gabriel and angrily yells it's always Marinette's fault and that she will pay. At school, Adrien apologizes to Marinette for being too kind to Lila and that giving people like Lila chances will just make them take advantage of it and that disasters will occur. Marinette takes his hand and swears they'll expose Lila of her lies one day. In class, Lila is unanimously elected the new class representatives along with Chloé. Marinette tells Alya she did not trust Lila by quitting the election but did it so she can eventually prove to the class who Lila really is deep down. Lila destroys her Alliance ring by stepping on it and receives the pictures that Nathalie sent to her when she was under her control. Lila goes to her locker and swears that she will get the Butterfly Miraculous from Monarch as the episode ends.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot Developments
Many revelations are shown throughout the whole episode:
Lila is revealed to have at least 3 moms who she keeps away from one another by using different identities and lies that prevent them from ever meeting or learning the truth. Besides Mrs. Rossi (an Italian ambassador), she has an unknown mother who thinks she is in Africa helping endangered animals and also a deaf-mute mother who communicates through sign language who thinks Lila is an actress who needs to travel a lot.
Miss Bustier discovers that Sabrina has been doing all of Chloé's schoolwork for her and that has been happening ever since both of them learned how to write, with Sabrina even learning how to forge Chloé's handwriting.
More about Gabriel's past is revealed:
Gabriel's family used to own a French fry shop, and his birth name is Gabi Grassette.
His height according to his old ID is 1.79 m.
He and Émilie have known Audrey and André Bourgeois since their youth.
He, Émilie and Nathalie discovered the Peacock Miraculous (and possibly the Butterfly Miraculous) in the snow of the mountains of Tibet (possibly near where Master Fu lost it).

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot Developments
Lila gets to know about all of Gabriel's secrets, starting from his past, how he discovered the Butterfly and Peacock Miraculous, his deals with Tomoe Tsurugi, pictures of the Miraculous spellbook, ending with Émilie's body and the importance of the Graham de Vanily Twin Rings for him.
Adrien realizes his error in his approach to people like Chloé and Lila – they can take advantage of the kindness they're shown and second chances they're given.
With Chloé, he gave her too many chances to change her behavior, evidenced in "Despair Bear" and "Queen Banana", which always ended with her not changing at all. After his pleas to apologize to Marinette falling on deaf ears in "Derision", Adrien officially ends his friendship with her.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot Developments
With Lila, he didn't warn his friends about her lying and manipulative nature, thinking that way she would only get angry and want to lie even more without learning anything, as shown in "Chameleon". However, because he waited too long to tell his friends about her, they didn't believe him, as they think he is only supporting Marinette (who hates Lila) because she is his girlfriend. If he had warned them about Lila sooner, she wouldn't have that much control over their classmates.
It could also be that he was afraid that his friends wouldn't believe him even if he did tell them the truth sooner.
And looking at the state of the photos in the safe concludes they were burned but how they were can lead to these possible outcomes:
Because of his in-laws and Colt, Gabriel decided to burn them as to not be reminded of his past until Émilie or Nathalie convinced him to save them.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot Developments
It could be before, he and Émilie lived in the Agreste Mansion, they lived somewhere else in Paris, likely Gabriel's place or since they were friends, with Audrey and André, it could be that they were staying at the Grand Paris Hotel until they could find a place of their own but either building caught on fire and they were able to save the pictures.
Before Adrien was born, it could be the Mansion caught on fire but the couple were able to get out, save the pictures and rebuild it.
Lila continues to keep her word to make Marinette end up alone. This time, she decides to take Marinette's role as class representative by manipulating Miss Bustier to hold elections. She claims Marinette's love life was preventing her from carrying out her duty, such as helping Chloé become a better person, and that she would love to take that responsibility away from her (indirectly painting Marinette as a selfish girl). She emphasizes that by having Chloé act as her deputy to show she can actually change. Lila later withdraws her candidacy, pretending it was because Marinette made her feel useless and stupid for believing Chloé could change.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Plot Developments
While akumatized as Hoaxer, she makes everyone believe Marinette is Monarch, causing her to become a target to all of Paris.
Eventually, Lila and Chloé win the re-election, becoming the new class representatives.
It's revealed that it's only two weeks until the end of the school year.
Though Ladybug detransformed after summoning her Lucky Charm, Scarabella later uses the same one to call upon Miraculous Ladybug, meaning she either used the power herself and received the same object, or Ladybug's detransformation didn't cause it to disappear in the first place.
If the second option is true, this gives further insight on "Sandboy", where lucky charms can be used by other Ladybugs even if they aren't the original summoners.
Overall this is the third time this happened following "Hack-San", and "Sandboy".
Lila decides to destroy her Alliance ring to symbolically cut her ties with Gabriel Agreste.
When asked about how long Sabrina had been doing her homework, Chloé responds "Oh, since we learned to write— I mean, since Sabrina did", which could imply that she is illiterate.
Despite this, she wrote her name on her gift for Miss Bustier in "Zombizou".

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Trivia
As of April 28, 2022, the animation for this episode was completed.
This does not (necessarily) include lighting, 2D effects, or other post-production work.
This is the third season 5 episode that is not named after the concept of a Miraculous.
There have also been revelations in other episodes and the characters too:
During Adrien's character development, he was originally supposed to be disabled, and use a crutch. However, the producers and the broadcasters didn't trust themselves to write him well, so the idea was scrapped and it later became Cat Noir's staff.
At first, Félix was only suppose to exist in the PV Version only but that wasn't until "Felix" and his version of him as Cat Noir was apart of in-universe movies.
In "Heroes' Day", Team Miraculous discovered that Hawk Moth also had the Peacock Miraculous in his possession.
In "Chrismaster", as Ladybug; Marinette was surprised that the story she made up about Santa's rules, making an exception to the most well behaved kid in the world and her being said kid was actually true.

title: Revelation
text:
Revelation - Trivia
In "Miraculous Shanghai", when Marinette was told the truth about Fei's betrayal it's likely she figured out that Lian, Kang and Jiao saw Fei stealing her in the first place and tried to stop her.
Nor that kwamis can automatically speak any language in the world.

title: Revelation
text:

References
This is the seventh time Lila gets akumatized following "Volpina", "Catalyst", "Mayura", "Chameleon" and 2 off-screen akumatizations into Volpina as seen in "Mr. Pigeon 72". This time, however, she gets akumatized into Hoaxer, her third overall akumatized form and second fox-themed identity.

title: Revelation
text:

This is the thirteenth time when a Miraculous has its ownership transferred in the show following "Anansi", "Reflekdoll", "Desperada", "Kwamibuster", "Miracle Queen", "Queen Banana", "Mega Leech", "Penalteam", "Strikeback", "Evolution", "Passion" and "Transmission".
This episode also shares some similarities to "Hack-San".
Both akumatized villains (Hoaxer and Robostus) have a red color scheme with some black and white in their costume, as well as the fact that their names are not the episode title.
Both akumatized villains hypnotize people that are in possession of technological devices, with their eyes glowing red as well. However, in Hoaxer's case, the victims eyes' glow red continuously and can be un-hypnotized by removing their alliance ring, whilst with Robostus, the victims eyes' temporarily glow red and there was no known way of restoring them without defeating him.
Nathalie contributes to the plot in some capacity; where in this episode she delivers Gabriel's private information to Hoaxer, while in "Hack-San", she uses the titular sentimonster to infect Markov and allow Shadow Moth to akumatize him.
Both episodes feature Alya as Scarabella.

title: Revelation
text:

Allusions
The end card is similar to the 2016 Marvel Studios film "Captain America: Civil War".
This episode shares some resemblance to the MCU movie "Black Widow":
In Black Widow, the Widows are controlled by Red Dust, with a chip inside of them. Here, the Paris citizens are under control through their alliance rings by Hoaxer.
In Black Widow, Yelena takes out the chip that was inserted inside of her and Dreykov finds out. Here, Ladybug removes the alliance ring from Roger and Hoaxer finds out; she later removes Alya's as well.
The only difference is that in Black Widow, vials are destroyed in front of the Widows to free them from Dreykov's control, which does not happen here.
The phrase "A fake photo is worth a thousand lies", said by Monarch while akumatizing Lila, is an allusion to a quote from the Canadian writer Claude Jasmin ("Une photo vaut mille mensonges = A photo is worth a thousand lies")
