Adrien: Don't worry about me!
Marinette: (runs into the elevator, the doors closing behind her) Tikki, spots on! (A glow emanates from the closed doors as she transforms. The Hawk Moth statue knocks Adrien down, and tries to stab Adrien, but Ladybug saves him.)
Ladybug: (sets him down) Go and find a safe place to hide, I'll handle this. (attacks the statue, Adrien runs off)
Adrien: (closes the elevator doors) Plagg, claws out! (Another glow emanates from the doors. Ladybug ties up the Hawk Moth with her yo-yo.)
Cat Noir: (jumping in) Whoa! You've captured Hawk Moth!
Ladybug: I wish! (pulls on her yo-yo, cutting the wax statue into pieces)
Cat Noir: Ohh, a wax statue.
Ladybug: The Puppeteer is back! She must be here somewhere!
Cat Noir: We gotta find and save her!
Ladybug: The Hero's Room! That's where she found Hawk Moth's statue!
Cat Noir: After you, m'lady. (They run down to the Hero's Room.)

title: The Puppeteer 2/Transcript
text:
The Puppeteer 2/Transcript - Intro
Ladybug: Look out! (They jump through the entrance, dodging the attacks of the Lady WiFi and Bubbler statues, who hit and trap each other. Ladybug wraps up a Puppeteer statue with her yo-yo, then lets it go.) It's not her, it's a statue! Look, (points) the real Puppeteer had a wand, remember?
Cat Noir: Then this Puppeteer must've taken it. That's where the akuma must be! (The statues start moving, and surround them.) Okay, who wants to play red light, green light? ("Guitar Villain" and "Dark Cupid" attack Ladybug. Cat Noir fights a "mummy" from The Pharaoh.) Nobody's up for hopscotch, either?
Ladybug: Enough jokes, Kitty— There's a little girl at stake! (Cat Noir hits "Rogercop", Ladybug slices "Darkblade.")
Cat Noir: (decapitates "Timebreaker") You know, M'lady, the worse the situation, the more I realize how amazing you are.
Ladybug: How do you do that...? Ah! (dodges an attack from "Pixelator")
Cat Noir: (fending an attack from "Rogercop") Do what?
Ladybug: (fighting "Pixelator") I mean so much to you, how is it so easy for you to say these nice things to me, even in the worse situations? (slices the "mummy") The really important things are the hardest to say, aren't they?

title: The Puppeteer 2/Transcript
text:
The Puppeteer 2/Transcript - Intro
Cat Noir: (breaks "Rogercop's" visor) It's precisely when something is important, that it's important to say it, no matter what.
Ladybug: (smiles, then sees "Thomas Astruc's" head, some eyeballs, and couple hands coming down the stairs) The workshop— She's gotta be there! (takes off)
Cat Noir: (kicks "The Mime") Got it! (Ladybug jumps over "Astruc's" head, and exits. "The Mime" lassos Cat Noir who trips and falls. He is pinned down by "Darkblade," "Reflekta," and "Evillustrator." "Astruc" sucks on his finger, trying to get Cat Noir's ring.) Ahh, that's so gross! Ah! ("Kung Food", "Princess Fragrence," and "Volpina" land on top of him.)
Ladybug: (breaks the door handle) That should hold them for a bit. (They run up to the door of the workshop) Wait up! We don't know what we're gonna find behind this door, let's stack the odds in our favor! Lucky Charm! (catches it) A cardboard tube? What am I gonna do with this? (looks around, to no avail) I'll figure it out. Let's go! (kicks open the door, rolls in)

title: The Puppeteer 2/Transcript
text:
The Puppeteer 2/Transcript - Intro
Puppeteer: (floating alongside statues of Philippe, Audrey Bourgeois, Clara Nightingale, and Aurore Beauréal) Neener, neener, neeener! I've got tons of friends, but you? No one wants to play with you, Ladybug!
Ladybug: You forget I always have my partner with me— Cat Noir!
Puppeteer: Really? Cat Noir, capture Ladybug! ("Cat Noir" grabs and throws her to the ground.)
Ladybug: Ah! What's wrong with you!? (realizes) It's a statue!
Cat Noir: (puts away his staff) Cleaning done! It deserves a little scratch under the chin before going up, right? (He offers his cheek to a statue of Ladybug. It grabs his hands, and leans in for a kiss, so he doesn't see that it's taking off his ring.) Is that a new perfume, m'lady? This one smells like... wax? Cataclysm! ("Ladybug" crumbles apart, Cat Noir runs out)
Ladybug: (the other statues corner her) We're done playing games! (knocks Puppeteer's wand out of her hands) Gimme that! (jumps for it)

title: The Puppeteer 2/Transcript
text:
The Puppeteer 2/Transcript - Intro
Puppeteer: Noo! (They all jump for it. A wax hand grabs it, Puppeteer grabs it.) You lose, Ladybug! (flies away) Now you won't be able to steal my wand again, meanie! (the statues surround her) Take her miraculous! (Shuts herself in the wax room. Ladybug gets pinned down by "Clara Nightingale" and "Cat Noir," a wax hand tries grabbing her earring.)
Cat Noir: (pins down the hand) Hands off, you pale imitation! Hah! (hits the statues against a wall, where they fall limp) Only one cat is allowed to have her hand.
Ladybug: (stands) Thanks, Kitty.
Cat Noir: (sees her Lucky Charm) Have you found out what to do with your Lucky Charm? (fights "Audrey Bourgeois")
Ladybug: (spots a tub of glue, some paint brushes, paints, and cardboard stars) I do now!
Ladybug: Let go, you fake! (pretends to struggle)
Puppeteer: (evil laugh) I've almost beat you, Ladybug! Cat Noir, give me her earrings! (Cat Noir reaches for the earrings, then freezes) Cat Noir, give me her earrings!
Hawk Moth: (through his telepathic connection) What's happening, Puppeteer?
Puppeteer: I don't know, my wand stopped working!
Ladybug: Surprise! (holds up a fake version of the wand) I swapped them earlier. You lose, Puppeteer!

title: The Puppeteer 2/Transcript
text:
The Puppeteer 2/Transcript - Intro
Puppeteer: Heh! I don't care! If you break my wand, I'll just turn them into real wax statues! (reveals Véronique and Théo tied up above the molten wax)
Ladybug: No! Don't do that! Fine, I'll give you your wand back.
Puppeteer: (giggles, and grabs the fake wand. Hears Cat Noir's ring beeping) Huh? What is that? Hey! (gets the wands mixed up) If you're the real one, then that means that—! Ah! (Ladybug grabs the real wand from her.)
Ladybug: Too late! (breaks it)
Puppeteer: No!
Ladybug: (an akuma flies out of the wand) No more evil-doing for you, little akuma. Time to de-evilize! (captures the akuma) Gotcha! (releases a white butterfly) Bye-bye, little butterfly! Miraculous Ladybug! (throws up the Lucky Charm, everything turns back to normal)
Ladybug & Cat Noir: (fist bump) Pound it!
Hawk Moth: Soon, I'm the one who'll pulling the strings, Ladybug, and that day will come sooner than you think! (the lair's window closes)
Véronique: There we are. All back together again. (chuckles)
Marinette: (playfully) Hey, wait, Manon has to see this! Oh, but where is she?
Alya: (playing along) Maybe she's behind that weird statue over there! (The friends walk over to Manon, who poses on a podium)

title: The Puppeteer 2/Transcript
text:
The Puppeteer 2/Transcript - Intro
Manon: Boo! (They scream, Manon laughs.) Gotcha! (They all laugh.)
Adrien: (to his bodyguard) To Manon's place, please! (Cut to Marinette hugging Manon goodbye. Manon hugs her mom and they wave goodbye as Adrien and Marinette get back in the car.) To Marinette's?
Adrien & Marinette: I'm sorr—!
Marinette: You go first.
Adrien: No, please, you.
Marinette: (rapidly) I'm sorry, I shouldn't have kissed the statue, but I didn't know it was you, and if I had, it wouldn't have been a prank because I—
Adrien: No, no... It's my fault. When you left the workshop, I was so worried that you were mad at me...? It made me do the stupid prank, and...
Marinette: Of course I wasn't mad at you! I'm sorry that I made you believe that.
Adrien: Is that true? We're still friends, you and me?
Marinette: Of course! But, to be safe, maybe we should stop playing pranks on each other.
Adrien: (laughs) I know, I'm not good with jokes. The girl I'm in love with doesn't like them either.
Marinette: The girl that you—? You're... you're in love with...?
Adrien: Are you okay, Marinette?
Marinette: Yeah, yeah. I'm glad we're friends. (They arrive at her house, and she gets out of the car.)

title: The Puppeteer 2/Transcript
text:
The Puppeteer 2/Transcript - Intro
Adrien: See you tomorrow at school?
Marinette: Yeah... (She loses the car door, and it leaves.)
Marinette: (reaching to take down a picture of Adrien) You heard him. Adrien's in love with another girl, and me? I'm just a friend.
Tikki: Oh, I'm sure life has many surprises in store for you, Marinette!
Marinette: (leaves the picture up, falls onto her bed) Yeah... (smiles) That would've been one very silly first kiss, anyways.
(The end card shows the Grévin Wax Museum in the background, with Marinette embracing Adrien, Manon and the Puppeteer above them, and Ladybug and Cat Noir at their sides.)

title: The Resistance
text:
The Resistance - Intro
The Resistance was a group formed by the former students of Miss Bustier's class, except Chloé Bourgeois and Lila Rossi. Unbeknownst to the school, the group are members of the French Miraculous superhero team who were left inactive after Félix Fathom stole their Miraculouses to Monarch.
Their mission was to assist Ladybug and Cat Noir in any way they can by trying to find out how Monarch is able to transfer and give the Miraculous superpowers to his akumatized villains without giving them the actual Miraculouses.
In "Illusion", the Resistance is formed with Nino, Adrien, Alya, and Marinette being the founding members. It is then followed by Max, Kim, Rose, Juleka, Ivan, Mylène, and Lila.
In "Deflagration", it is revealed that Nathaniel, Marc and Zoé are part of the Resistance. They managed to fight against Monarch Bug and find out that he reforged the Miraculouses into rings.

title: The Resistance
text:
The Resistance - Intro
In "Confrontation", Lila, along with Chloé, frames Marinette for forging her classmates' study option forms in order to get them to turn against her. Her plan backfires when she falls into a trap set up by Marinette and Sabrina and accidentally exposes her true nature in front of her entire class and the school faculty, leading to her expulsion from the school and the Resistance, Sabrina becomes a member of the group, replacing Lila since she was expelled from the school, meanwhile Chloé received special attention from Miss Bustier as punishment.
In "Action", the Resistance begin a campaign against plastic users, causing the attention of Bertrand King.
In "Revolution", Damoclès joins the Resistance during a protest and they began to stop Chloé's reign of terror and Caline Bustier rips her sash, and subsequently being forced to leave Paris for London with her mother.
In "Representation", they noticed Gabriel Agreste is akumatized into Nightormentor, as he was trying to find Marinette after Adrien ran away from him. Following his defeat, he was no longer a member of the Resistance.

title: The Resistance
text:
The Resistance - Intro
In "Conformation", the Resistance was into the Perfect Alliance app due to the nightmares caused by Gabriel Agreste as Nightormentor until the news of Ladybug and Cat Noir being falsely accused of kidnapping Adrien and Kagami. Ivan is the first to transform into a Miraculized, along with many innocent citizens. They are almost tempted to join until Alya urges them to resist since they know the two superheroes would never do that to anyone and to disposed of their rings.
In "Re-creation", they fought against the Miraculized army with the United Heroez, the Order of the Guardians, Ladydragon, and many citizens. The group is officially disbanded as its members receive and keep their Miraculouses from Ladybug permanently, thus becoming full-time superheroes of the French Miraculous superhero team, later known as the Miraculers.

title: The Resistance
text:
The Resistance - System
Each member of the Resistance has a code name based on a sauce, seasoning, or culinary side dish.
When necessary, a Resistance council is held, particularly to decide on the implementation of actions aimed at helping Paris' superheroes.
Central headquarters
The headquarters is located in the basement of Collège Françoise Dupont, more precisely inside the boiler room.

title: The Resistance
text:
The Resistance - Trivia
All the members of the Resistance have a codename named after sauces. Incidentally, those are their main weapon, using them in "Deflagration" and "Re-creation".
In the European Portuguese dub, Alya's codename is Camarada Béchamel Chefe de Mesa (Béchamel Maître d'Hôtel), while Marinette's is Camarada Hollandaise.
The only members of the Miraculers who aren't in the Resistance are Alix Kubdel, Luka Couffaine, Kagami Tsurugi and Félix Fathom.
Lila Rossi was the only member of the Resistance who is not a part of the Miraculers. Unbeknownst to the group, she was a spy working for Monarch.
Zoé Lee and Marc Anciel are the only members of the Resistance who are not in of Miss Bustier's class.
"Action" is the only episode where the Resistance doesn't fight against Monarch, but rather against the global pandemic that is plastic waste.

title: The Resistance (Re-Verse)
text:
The Resistance (Re-Verse) - Intro
The Resistance is a clandestine group formed by Gabriel Agreste with the purpose of opposing the dictatorial rule of the Supreme over the world. It exists in the Re-Verse, an alternative reality to the Quantic Universe.

title: The Resistance (Re-Verse)
text:
The Resistance (Re-Verse) - History
At some point in the past, an evil being known as the Supreme came into possession of the Mother Box and used its Miraculous to become the ruler of the world. He kept the existence of the magical jewels a secret from the general public, and established a regime in which any form of mutual aid is considered a crime (so as to prevent rebellions). However, sometimes he entrusts Miraculous to a few select people of the world whom he considers powerful. Gabriel Agreste, a successful and world-famous fashion designer, was once one of the Supreme's allies, but in order to obtain something he wanted more than anything, he stole the Miraculous of the Butterfly and the Peacock from the Supreme. He then entrusted the Peacock Miraculous to his wife, Emilie Agreste.

title: The Resistance (Re-Verse)
text:
The Resistance (Re-Verse) - History
However, Gabriel and Emilie misused the Miraculous, which somehow resulted in Emilie's death. Realizing the wrong in their actions and wishing to redeem himself, Gabriel used the Miraculous of the Butterfly and became the superhero Betterfly, with the goal of freeing the world from the tyranny of the Supreme by showing people that if they work together, they can revolt, that a better world than theirs is possible. Later, at some point, a couple of teenagers, Alya Césaire and Nino Lahiffe, along with an AI called Maxkov, joined Betterfly to support his cause, and so the Resistance was born.

title: The Resistance (Re-Verse)
text:
The Resistance (Re-Verse) - History
Meanwhile, in order to retrieve the Miraculous he had lost, The Supreme recruited two teenagers, Marinette Dupain-Cheng and Adrien Agreste (Gabriel and Emilie's son). He took advantage of their suffering to lure them to the side of evil, as Marinette's life was a constant nightmare due to Chloé Bourgeois's bullying, while Adrien was still deeply hurt by his mother's death and unable to move on. He entrusted them with the Miraculous of the Ladybug and the Cat respectively, and gave them the mission to find and defeat Betterfly, and return the stolen Miraculous to him. They became the supervillains Shadybug and Claw Noir.

title: The Resistance (Re-Verse)
text:
The Resistance (Re-Verse) - History
After some time, Shadybug and Claw Noir managed to find the secret headquarters of the Resistance and broke in to defeat Betterfly once and for all. Fortunately, the Resistance was already aware that the villains were onto them and had devised a last-resort plan: they would travel to a parallel universe where the Ladybug and Cat Miraculous are used for good and seek help from their holders. To accomplish this, Betterfly used his superpowers to kamikotize Alya into Ubiquity, a superhero with the ability to exist in all universes simultaneously. She had the power to take control of any version of Alya Césaire from any universe, as well as using her body as a portal between any two universes. She connected herself to the Alya from Ladybug and Cat Noir's universe and opened a portal to allow Betterfly to reach them. However, Betterfly was not the only one to cross it, as Shadybug and Claw Noir were able to force Ubiquity into opening the portal for them as well and followed Betterfly through it.

title: The Resistance (Re-Verse)
text:
The Resistance (Re-Verse) - History
Shadybug and Claw Noir managed to hunt Betterfly down and almost defeated him, but Ladybug and Cat Noir intervened and the three heroes managed to escape. Shadybug and Claw Noir later allied themselves with Monarch in an attempt to seize all three of their Miraculous, but the heroes managed to evade Monarch's attacks and convince Shadybug and Claw Noir to renounce evil and try other ways of dealing with their problems. Shadybug and Claw Noir then became the superheroes Ladybug and Furry Paw. They returned with Betterfly to their universe and joined the Resistance in the fight against the Supreme.

title: The Resistance (Re-Verse)
text:
The Resistance (Re-Verse) - Trivia
Interestingly, all members of the Resistance have counterparts in Ladybug and Cat Noir's universe who were also members of the group of the same name created by Nino to help the two superheroes in their mission to defeat Monarch (although Gabriel Agreste was only an honorary member, and was secretly Monarch himself).
While the Supreme owns most of the Miraculous of the Mother Box, the Resistance holds the two most powerful ones (the ones of the Ladybug and the Cat, the only ones that would allow the Supreme to win instantly by making a wish), along with the one that allows them to act from a distance (the one of the Butterfly).
The current fate of the Miraculous of the Peacock is unknown, as Shadybug and Claw Noir only ever mentioned their mission to recover the Butterfly Miraculous. Therefore, it might still be in Gabriel's possession, or the Supreme may have already recovered it.
It's also unknown if the Supreme possesses the Miraculous of the Rabbit and if so why he hasn't used it to retrieve the others (unlike Ladybug and Fu, he wouldn't be afraid to alter the past, just like Monarch).

The Resistance (Re-Verse) - Trivia
On the other hand, it could be that the Supreme is afraid to alter the past as a result of possible creating a paradox that could result in erasing his own existence.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Intro
"" is a season 6 episode of the series, Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. Based on the series' production order specifically, "" is the 15th written and produced episode of season 6. It is also the 146th written and produced episode of the series, overall.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Synopsis
While trying desperately to hide her seasonal cold from Adrien, Marinette tries to help Nathaniel assert himself so he can illustrate the comic Marc wrote for him.
TFOU
While trying to hide her seasonal cold from Adrien, Marinette tries to help Nathaniel assert himself so that he can draw the next strip of the comic book that Marc has written for him.
Gloob
While desperately trying to hide from Adrien that she is ill, Marinette helps Nathaniel illustrate the comic written by Marc.
Disney+
A villain wants to get Ladybug straightened out.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
In the opening scene, we are provided in the morning an insight on Nathaniel and Marc after they show the next issue of their comic, 'The Adventures of Sun-Heart & Rain-Piercer', to their parents. With the Kurtzbergs, Aton is shown to be rather supportive, thinking the comic is lovely but only lacking genuine sentiment (after receiving a few nudging looks from Shirel). Shirel, however, disapproves of the art and her son's comic, even thinking it lacks seriousness. Seeing this, Nathaniel is disheartened by his parents' lack of approval as he was looking for positive support. The Anciels, on the other hand, fully support and love the comic and express that they're proud of Marc from writing from the heart. They even give Marc a warm hug as they are excited to see how Nathaniel draws the story.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Meanwhile, Marinette discovers that she is very ill with a cold, and her nose can't stop sneezing. As she blows her nose, she worries that Adrien will think she was disgusting if he sees her like this. However, Tikki reassures her that Adrien loves her just the way she is. Just then, Sabine calls out to Marinette, reminding her that she will be late. Unfortunately, Marinette still has to go to school or else she'll try to get a doctor by force.
At school, students we know like Max, Alya, Rose, Mylène and Adrien are in awe as Diane explains how she accidentally dropped a paint can on the canvas in front of them, creating a portrait of Jagged Stone.
Marinette retreats considering her nose runs again.
Elsewhere, Nathaniel is about to voice his opinion on their comic to Marc, but the ground shakes again, since Marinette blew her nose.
Resuming their talk, Nathaniel vents his worries about the script.
He is unsure if the final reveal scene will meet people's standards, and how everyone will read the comic such as their friends, teachers, and parents.
While Marc reassures him, he remarks how his parents even cried while reading.
Because of this, Marinette stirs in between them, worried.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Marc assures Marinette it's only about the storyline of their next issue.
However, as Marinette exclaims out loud how they have written the next issue, every student such as Juleka, Kagami and Nino stop their activities and gather around them, showing just how amazing the comic actually is.
Even so, Marc confesses how Nathaniel isn't sure everyone will like it, and suggests their friends to review it.
Marinette gladly accepts.
The script is a success, as they all leave positive reviews.
In spite of all this, Nathaniel is still in doubt.
Marc, Marinette, and the others provide some comfort.
Seeing this, Nathaniel finally decides to illustrate the issue, then almost all of them share a group hug.
After that, Marinette's nose starts running again.
Adrien sees something is wrong, but she excuses herself of 'something that smells awful', additionally saved by the bell.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
As the students start swarming out of school, Nathaniel seems to be bothered by his decision. Marc asserts that it's ok if he changes his mind, as it won't change anything between them. Nathaniel reluctantly gives the script back to Marc, and they exchange small reassuring smiles. They begin to part ways from each other. However, Nathaniel stops in his tracks and changes his mind. He dashes back to Marc, silently stating he will do it. A heartwarming hug follows between them.
Later at Nathaniel's residence, Ziggy is touched out of the perfection in the final scene of the script.
She understands the pressure given to Nathaniel, as what he draws may not be as powerful as the text.
Nathaniel agrees, it will be challenging, but he gives it a shot anyway.
After drawing a few scenes, he pauses.
He is unhappy with the ending, with the heroes losing their powers.
A lightbulb activates in his mind, and then, with unfiltered passion, he starts drawing a new ending to the story.
Fast forward to next day, Marc praises Nathaniel's new resolution to the story.
At that moment, Shirel barges in, and seeing the comic sheets spread out on her son's desk, deplores of it.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Luckily, Marc defends Nathaniel by making up an excuse; it's only schoolwork, a group assignment due.
Hearing this, Shirel appreciates their seriousness and excuses herself.
After that, Marc believes that Shirel will never like comics and that they should keep the issue to themselves.
Nathaniel disproves his idea, reminding him that this is the best thing they've ever made, and they should print it.
Marc is dumbfounded.
Nathaniel believes that once his mom reads their comic, she will see how beautiful and important it actually is.
At the College Francoise Dupont art room, as the proofs are being printed, Adrien asks Marinette if she is still smelling something awful, then she pretends to fan away the bad smell that she believed smelled like dirty socks and cheese.
She excuses herself when she sees that the proofs are done.
Adrien, looking confused, smells his jacket, then walks away to the men's room.
Marc and Nathaniel were pleased with the results of their comic book.
Jean was pleased with it as well and said that they can start the final printing of their comic book.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Marinette saw that Nathaniel was about throw away the proofs, but then stopped him and ask if she can keep them in her room and then asked if the both of them could sign it.
Jean announced that now with the proofs complete, he will distribute the comic book everywhere.
Everyone cheered.
In the men's room, Adrien lets Plagg out of his jacket, asking if snuck camembert into school as he already knows how smelly it is.
Plagg offended by the question as Adrien crosses his arms at him.
Plagg admitted that it might have happened in the past, but not this time.
Adrien asked Plagg if he smelled like camembert, only for him to say that he wished Adrien did, as Adrien stares angrily at Plagg for his petty remark.
Back at the Kurtzberg household, Nathaniel was in shock to find that his mother found the script to his and Marc's comic book.
She furiously asked him if he was planning to illustrate it, to which Nathaniel falsely denies.
She then asked if his friend wrote the story, to which Nathaniel says yes.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Asking if that was what she wanted and if the sentimental value was genuine, as well as feeling displeased with the comic book, Shirel tells him that Marc can imagine anything he wants, but Nathaniel shouldn't waste his time on comics.
She tells him that there are a lot of serious arts, such as architecture, industrial design, scenography and that his comic book days are over.
After this, Shirel goes as far as to say that if he rebels against her, he'll never see Marc ever again.
Shirel shreds the script right in front of him and leaves the room, saying that she's doing this for his own good.
Aton, while remorseful, tells Nathaniel that he told him that that's not what people want to see and leaves the room as well.
Distraught by her harsh words, Nathaniel runs away crying to the school.
At school, he transforms into Caprikid and creates a big shredder that destroys all the comics but remembers that Marinette still has the proofs.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
In the Dupain-Cheng household, at Marinette's bedroom, she questions Nathaniel about why he wants to destroy the proofs, and he says that he is done with comic books, but when she tried to stop him, her nose starts to run again and then blows her nose and the whole building shaking around.  She asks Nathaniel to not tell Adrien that she is sick with a cold. As she was going to say, that comic books are a big part of who he is. Which he believed she was only saying that because it's the only thing he has only done in his life and thinks that if he does something else he can become someone else but unfortunately it's not how it works. Pleading to Marinette to respect his decision, she reluctantly does but then is concerned that he will regret that decision one day and that he will be saddened with the choice that he made in the future. They hug and she asks Nathaniel what he’s going to tell Marc, making Nathaniel wonder.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
In front of the Francoise Dupont High School's lake, Nathaniel tells Marc about his decision to give up being an illustrator for comic books. Marc points out that even if Nathaniel stops drawing comic books, he will still be coming up with ideas to draw in his head. Nathaniel insists that he wouldn't and that it would be his problem and, in that case, they can still be friends. Marc also reminds him that he draws from the heart and doesn't hide who he truly is inside or gives up on his passions. Nathaniel reluctantly says that he hopes Marc finds another illustrator and then leaves, leaving Marc heartbroken.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
At the high school's rooftop garden, Marinette cuts a tomato then hears someone crying and questioned to herself "tomato plants cry when you cut them". Her nose starts running again and she runs into the garden shed to blow her nose again, causing the camera to shake again. Max asks "another jet plane". Marinette looks up to find that it was Marc and walks up to him, asking if he's crying because of Nathaniel. Marinette reassures him that Nathaniel will change his mind when he is ready. Unfortunately for Nathaniel, he would have to change parents, or his parents are the ones who need to change their perspective.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Marinette stops Nathaniel, asking him since he isn't drawing comic books anymore if he didn't mind if she did it herself, but then his mom answers for him and asked if she's illustrated comics before. Marinette says she has, but it wouldn't be the same as if Nathaniel did it though. His mom believes that comic books have no future and, in her eyes, if they were serious, they would be in the Louvre and calls her son's comic book art "nonsense" and "graffiti with meaningless stories" as some of the students, even Marc, watched the conversation. Marinette tells her that she wouldn't say that if she actually read the ending of her son's comic, and she says that they'll never know since Nathaniel never drew the ending. When she asked Nathaniel, he gives her a death stare, making her realize that the comic book has already been drawn out and printed after she told him not to. She grabs her son's arm in a fit of rage, dragging him off to "straighten him out" as he pleas her to let go of him.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Marc walked in, asking what was going on. Marinette tells him that she wanted to make the situation better but instead made it worse. Then an ultrakuma flies into Shirel's earring and gets akumatized into The Ruler. Marinette runs into the women's restroom, letting Tikki out of her pocket. Tikki pointing that Nathaniel's mom looked really, really angry. Marinette sneezes and her nose run again then transforms into Ladybug.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Nathaniel was struggling to break free and was about to get hypnotized by The Ruler, but then Marc jumped on her to free Nathaniel. She went after Marc instead, and was hit by The Ruler's sword, which she then ordered Marc to never get near her son again. Nathaniel gasps, taking it out on him is one thing, but on his partner, she really shouldn't have done that. Getting ready to strike, Ladybug swings in at just the right time and tells Nathaniel that if he wants to help her, he should go somewhere and hide. Nathaniel goes into the closet to transform into Caprikid to help Ladybug in the battle. The Ruler and Ladybug continue to fight, and Ladybug tells her to think about what she is doing and if she wants her son to be happy, but she believes that she is doing this for his own good and so that he wouldn't suffer in the future. Caprikid arrives and says that her son is already suffering now because of her actions, and uses Genesis and gets a bag of crayons, throwing them at her. Caprikid tells Ladybug that the Ultrakuma is in her earrings under her helmet. he continues to throw crayons at her but then runs out of crayons.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
As Ladybug engages Ruler, Caprikid uses his Genesis power to conjure a giant pencil and throws it at her, but she slices it in half. They realize they'll have to dismantle all of her gear piece by piece. Fortunately, Cat Noir arrives just in time to use his Cataclysm ability to destroy her equipment. However, he gets hit by Ruler's sword, then she orders the human-sentimonster to retrieve Ladybug's Miraculous. Ladybug takes the opportunity to escape. In a dazed trance, Cat Noir attempts to use his Cataclysm on Ladybug. She tells him that she prefers it when he was making jokes. Ladybug finds a hiding spot, but her nose starts to run, and she feels a sneeze coming on. To avoid revealing her position, she pinches her nose. Cat Noir jumps away, and Ladybug cautiously comes out of hiding. She leaps onto the roof where Caprikid and Ruler are located. Summoning her Lucky Charm, she uses a stuffy-nosed voice to call forth a rope. With her Ladybug vision, she devises a plan to defeat Ruler.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
The Ruler demands her son and thinks that she is doing this for his own good, but in reality, she is making him unhappy. She strikes again, but Ladybug swings in to catch him. Caprikid uses his Genesis to make a carabiner clip, then Ladybug goes ahead to make a diversion, but just when she was about to do her plan, Cat Noir sneaks up behind, tripping her, making her fall, and gets hit by The Ruler. Ladybug and Cat Noir are getting ready to hand over their Miraculous. Caprikid uses the rope and carabiner to take Ruler's sword and uses it against her. Caprikid orders Ruler to take off her helmet and break her earrings, and Ladybug to throw her lucky charm into the air and say "Miraculous Ladybug". Everything goes back to normal after Ladybug de-evilizes the Ultrakuma. Ladybug gives Shirel a magical charm to remember that children must follow their own path, not one that is planned for them. Caprikid, Ladybug, and Cat Noir pound it.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
On Marinette's balcony, she is seen writing in her diary, then Adrien comes upstairs to the balcony with a pink, flowery effect, telling Marinette that the good news is that she won't be bothered by the bad smell again. Marinette questions what happened to him. He says that he put three bottles of perfume on himself because he thinks that the reason Marinette has been avoiding him is that he smells like cheese. But then Marinette finally tells him the truth that she has been sick with a cold and was afraid to blow her nose in front of him because it was very loud. Luckily, he doesn't care that it's loud and that she can blow her nose anytime that she has to. Marinette blows her nose in front of Adrien, blowing him away. She goes over to check on him to see if he's okay and if he still loves her. Adrien teases her and tells her that he loves her just the way she is and to not change into someone else. Especially with someone who has a quieter nose, then share a laugh.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
Meanwhile, Cerise writes in her journal and wonders about Nathaniel's true face. At the Kurtzberg apartment, Aton and Shirel were reading Marc and Nathaniel's comic book as Marc held Nathaniel's hand for support. When they finished reading their comic book, Aton gives his support by saying that he wouldn't change anything in the story. Marc and Nathaniel turn towards Shirel, waiting for her response. As she thought about Ladybug's words earlier and the magical charm she received, Shirel reconciles with Nathaniel by finally accepting who he is and apologizes to him by saying that she loves him. Nathaniel walks up to his parents as they share a hug, and Aton allows Marc to join in too.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot
In the post-ending, Nathaniel and Marc are seen sitting close together on Nathaniel's bed as they discuss their comic. Nathaniel tells Marc that power or no power, he'll always be there to protect him and affectionately touches his cheek, and Marc says he'll do the same for Nathaniel and warmly takes his hand. Marc tells him to promise him that he wouldn't put himself in danger for him, saying that he isn't a superhero. Moved by Marc's deep concern, Nathaniel thinks about his words and reluctantly transforms into Caprikid, revealing his superhero identity to Marc. Shocked that Nathaniel trusted him enough by transforming in front of him and revealing his identity to him, Marc gasped silently and covers his mouth with his hands. After silently staring at each other for a brief moment, Caprikid, while a little flustered, asks Marc to say something. Marc, heartwarmingly touched by this revelation, smiles and then transforms into Rooster Bold, showing Caprikid that he's also a superhero. The episode ends with Caprikid smiling at this revelation and that Rooster Bold reciprocated the same level of trust.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot Developments
More about Nathaniel is revealed in this episode, including his family:
His father is an artist.
His mother is a famous architect. She hates comic books and wants him to become a "serious" artist.
His parents are the root of Nathaniel's insecurity about his art, with his father thinking he should comply with what people want/expect from his creations (only because of the nudging looks he received from Shirel) and his mother disapproving of his inclination towards illustration to focus on more serious forms of art, such as architecture.
The scene where Nathaniel's mother reprimands him may instead imply his father is influenced by his wife's domineering personality and that the "people" he says Nathaniel should be more compliant to are actually his wife. This is because while Shirel shouts at Nathaniel, his father looks sad/guilty and says again in a small voice that Nathaniel should be more "compliant to the people".

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot Developments
Shirel being unsupportive and having very little respect for Nathaniel's passion for drawing comics is also a metaphor for homophobia. After she gets de-akumatized, she learns that Nathaniel should make his own decisions and choose his own path after receiving a magical charm from Ladybug.
The Kurtzberg family lives in fancy apartment, as their home is first shown in this episode. The view from Nathaniel's bedroom window shows Notre-Dame relatively close in the distance, indicating that Nathaniel lives close to Collège Françoise Dupont and Marinette's bakery/home.
Marc's parents also appear for the first time, and they are shown to fully support their son's writing aspirations and his relationship with Nathaniel.
Cerise wonders about Nathaniel's true face, possibly thinking that he is Caprikid, though she can't prove it.
Nathaniel and Marc reveal their identities as Caprikid and Rooster Bold to each other.
They are the third couple to reveal their hero identities to each other, after Alya and Nino in "Catalyst" and Kagami and Félix in "Miraculous Tokyo".

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Plot Developments
Them revealing their respective superhero identities match the final scene of their comic, where the two knights reveal their identities to each other.
The transformation phrases of the Goat and Rooster Miraculouses are revealed to be "Bleat it" and "Sunrise", respectively.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Trivia
Marinette is shown as being with a cold for the duration of this episode, as she is shown blowing her nose very loudly, something that causes her to get self-conscious about and tries very hard to hide from everyone else, especially Adrien.
Her cold is included in the de-evilization sequence, where she has a stuffy nose voice.
Her Lucky Charm and Magical Charm Sequence also has her nose being red added due to her having a cold.
This is the second time an akumatized villain breaks their own akumatized object, even if The Ruler did it while under control of her own power and Caprikid told her to. The first akumatized villain that breaks their own akumatized object is Penalty, who broke hers when breaking free from her megakuma.
This may be because Caprikid knew where the Ultrakuma was despite Nathaniel being the only one near his mother when she was akumatized.
The knights' story is extremely similar to Marinette and Adrien's.
This is the first time Ladybug and Cat Noir have been mind-controlled by a villain in the same episode.

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Trivia
This is also the second time Ladybug was put under the control of the akumatized villain after "Miracle Queen" and the first and only time this occurs in the permanent timeline.
This is the most times Genesis was used in an episode on screen, having been used six times in one episode.
When the episode was aired in Russia, most of the queer aspects were censored:
All of Mylène's badges were blurred, despite only one being a pride flag, and it not being censored in other episodes.
The rainbow bolt on Marc's jacket was blurred.
The end card was zoomed in, not showing Sun-Heart and Rain-Piercer's kiss.
Multiple scenes were cut, making the episode significantly shorter.
References
In Nathaniel's room, it's possible to see two drawings belonging to the fairytale he and Marc created in the episode "Gabriel Agreste" depicting Marinette and Adrien's romance and the obstacles they are facing, showing Marinette as a knight, Adrien as a princess and Gabriel as a witch.
Nathaniel's comic pages were drawn by Gaëlle Geniller, known under the username avril_circus.
As Marinette transforms in the boiler room, a part of her transformation theme from seasons 4 and 5 can be heard.
Allusions

title: The Ruler
text:
The Ruler - Trivia
Cat Noir saying "Must cataclysm Ladybug" three times while under the villain's control is similar to the Kim Possible episode "The Twin Factor" when a brainwashed Kim says "Must capture Ron Stoppable" three times.
Errors
In the version aired on TF1, Gine Jinet's right eye is miscolored. This was fixed when the episode was aired on Gloob.
In the beginning scene where Marc shows the script to his parents, his dad's nose vibrates weirdly when they all hug.
For a split second, Marc is already back to his original self before the magical ladybugs go over him.
The Rooster, Tiger and Dragon Miraculous have their textures missing.
In one scene, the pink and blue dye on Zoé's hair are missing.
Sometimes, a few of the glowing parts on The Ruler's armor are not glowing.
Caprikid, using Genesis, launches an enlarged pencil at The Ruler, although the titular villain slices it in half because of her stamp-like sword. In the next scene, the pieces are nowhere to be found.
In one scene, Kagami's hair loses some of it's lighting and hair texture.
Sometimes the goat miraculous does not have the segmented curved lines in its charged mode.
In one shot, the nurse's sleeve clips into her body.

title: The Ruler

At one point during Nathaniel and Marc's heart-to-heart at the end of the episode, a weird tangled texture is present on the back of Marc's head.

When she opens her yo-yo and it drops to the ground, it is briefly closed.
Before she captures the Ultrakuma, the lighting on the yo-yo is missing for a second.
When she says "Gotcha", her left earring is black and her hair has two different renders masked over each other.

title: The New Holder of the Butterfly Miraculous/Transcript
text:
The New Holder of the Butterfly Miraculous/Transcript - Intro
Narrator: To try and ruin Marinette's life, she came up with many schemes.
Lila: We're going to make fake forms. And we'll pin it all on Marinette!
Narrator: And manipulated many people.
Lila: I've really tried to be her friend, but she keeps calling me a liar, getting the others to gang up against me.
(Marinette sticks the broken toilet sign outside the girls' restroom door. Now inside, she removes the mirror and replaces it with a remote-controlled two-way mirror and puts a small hidden microphone underneath the sink.)
Narrator: But in the end, Marinette was the one who successfully tricked her into revealing her lies.
Lila: I had everyone believing that Marinette pushed me down the stairs. I had everyone believing that I was halfway around the world so I wouldn't have to go to school.
(Sabrina brings out a button remote and presses it, revealing that the temporary restroom was a trap set for Lila and Chloé, showing everyone their true motive. The mirror now shows the other side of the wall, where the whole class and faculty are seen to be standing just right outside the temporary restroom.)
Marinette: You've just told everyone who you really are, Lila.

id: The New Holder of the Butterfly Miraculous/Transcript::Intro::2
title: The New Holder of the Butterfly Miraculous/Transcript
text:
The New Holder of the Butterfly Miraculous/Transcript - Intro
Narrator: What Marinette doesn't know is that in reality that girl has many faces.
Narrator: And that we haven't seen the last of her.
Cerise: Mr. Damoclès? Hello! My family and I just moved to Paris. Is it still possible to register at your new school for the upcoming year?
Mr. Damoclès: Of course! I'll see you at the start of the school year.
(The scene switches to La Plage.)
Cerise: I look forward to seeing you again, Marinette Dupain-Cheng.
Narrator: Today, no one knows where she is.
Cerise: (Writes in her notebook, with only her hands and legs visible.) Nothing. Nothing! You'll know nothing about me, about us, about them. (She closes the notebook and walks away, just like any normal civilian.)
Narrator: And yet, I can assure you that she's still here.
Narrator: Like a chameleon, when using the Butterfly Miraculous, she makes sure to leave no trace.
(Marinette complains that they know absolutely nothing about the new Butterfly Miraculous holder, while they know almost everything about Hawk Moth/Shadow Moth/Monarch.)
Narrator: Even Marinette, a.k.a Ladybug, doesn't know what the new supervillain looks like.

id: The New Holder of the Butterfly Miraculous/Transcript::Intro::3
title: The New Holder of the Butterfly Miraculous/Transcript
text:
The New Holder of the Butterfly Miraculous/Transcript - Intro
(Cerise as Spectral Looter steals the Ladybug and the Cat Miraculous and makes a wish.)
Narrator: The only thing she knows for sure is that they want to seize the Miraculous of the Ladybug and the Black Cat to make a wish. But what wish?
Marinette: Someone's making a wish.
Cerise: I too have secrets. Everyone has secrets.
Narrator: (Chrysalis blows on top of her purple open palm, releasing an antikuma.) I know what you're wondering. What does she want? Where does she come from?
[Transformation Sequence](Cerise transforms into Chrysalis.)'''
Narrator: Truth be told, she might not even know herself.
Narrator: In fact, I'm the only one who knows. I know you're wondering who I am, but that's a secret, too.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Intro
is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is an artist and a sculptor.
In "Copycat", when Ladybug didn't attend the unveiling of his statue of her and Cat Noir, he became frustrated. When Cat Noir claimed to "have a thing" with Ladybug, Théo also became jealous and got akumatized by Hawk Moth into Copycat, a doppelgänger of Cat Noir.
In "Mister Agreste", after having his proposal for a statue of Gabriel Agreste being rejected by Adrien, Théo was akumatized by Chrysalis into Mister Agreste, a giant statue-themed supervillain in the likeness of Gabriel Agreste. He also received a Magical Charm from Ladybug that prevented him from being akumatized again.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Appearance
Physical Appearance
Théo is a tan-skinned young man who appears to be a bit taller with long chocolate-brown hair tied up in a bun at the back of his head, moderate tangelo colored eyes, and a soul patch and he has a matching goatee in his chin.
From season 6 onwards, his eyebrows are thinner.
Civilian Attire
He wears a purple shirt with a two button-up top, which he keeps unbuttoned underneath a black dress jacket, dark gray, almost black dress pants, and black laced-up work boots with buckles around the knees.
From Season 6 onwards, his shirt now has three buttons.
As Copycat

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Appearance
Copycat resembled Cat Noir in every detail, sharing the same physical features. He had cat-like eyes with green sclerae, dark green irises, and slitted pupils. His hair was similar to Cat Noir's, honey blond and slightly messy. Copycat wore a textured, black, skin-tight catsuit adorned with metal accents. His matching gloves featured claws on the fingertips, and his boots had hidden wedges, silver toes, and paw-shaped treads. Around his neck, he wore a golden bell attached to a zipper on the front of his costume. Additionally, a long belt wrapped around his waist and hung down from the back like a tail. He completed his look with black cat ears and a black mask that covered his face.
As Mister Agreste
Mister Agreste was a giant clay statue made of regenerative stone, resembling Gabriel Agreste himself, but he was a lot more gigantic in size.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Personality
Théo is creative and gracious. He appreciates Ladybug for protecting Paris; he's sure they have a lot in common. Though more on the quiet side, he has a lot of passion for his work and the things he cares about. He has feelings for Ladybug and he takes it hard when she doesn't show up for the reveal of his statue. He also gets easily jealous when Cat Noir brags about he and Ladybug being a couple, claiming that Cat Noir isn't good enough for her. However, after he is reverted back to his normal self, he gets over his frustration and jealousy, appreciating Ladybug signing his photo of her and being at peace about Cat Noir and Ladybug being together not knowing that it isn't the case.
Being an artist and having worked with Gabriel Agreste in many occasions, Théo developed an immense admiration for him, both as a fashion designer and, after Monarch's defeat, for saving the world. However, his admiration caused him to disregard the feelings of those who knew Gabriel closely, like Adrien. After being de-akumatized and being advised by Ladybug not to put people on a pedestal, Théo managed to simmer down that admiration.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Personality
As Copycat, he was overcome by his jealousy of Cat Noir and admiration of Ladybug. He made a bad name for Cat Noir by stealing the Mona Lisa from the Louvre and he captured Cat Noir and attempted to trick Ladybug into thinking that he was the real Cat Noir, in hopes of achieving her affection. When he was unable to fool Ladybug, he shouted that no one would have her and attacked Cat Noir. While cunning and determined, he fell for Ladybug's trick of asking him about their secret promise that they never made, which he thought they had.
As Mister Agreste, he attempted to emulate Gabriel Agreste completely, behaving like him to the point of assuming his identity. His main objective was to pursue Adrien and "discipline" him so that he would allow the construction of the statue. However, after Adrien vented his frustrations about his father, revealing to Mister Agreste how his father used to treat him, this new perspective caused the villain to start hardening and his physical form crumbled away.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Abilities
As a Civilian
Théo is a very skilled artist, being able to make a very realistic bronze statue of Ladybug and Cat Noir (although, according to the latter, he should be taller). Also, Théo is able to do a wide variety of jobs, such as being a furniture mover and a boom operator, as seen in multiple cameos.
As Copycat
Being Cat Noir's doppelgänger, Copycat possessed supernatural strength and agility. He wielded a replica of Cat Noir's staff and had the ability to use Cataclysm. Additionally, he could not lose his powers unless he chose to do so. Copycat could also mimic Cat Noir's voice.
As Mister Agreste
As a giant clay statue of Gabriel Agreste, he possessed immense strength and size, and his voice even began to resemble that of the real Gabriel. However, his true power stemmed from his invincibility, which allowed him to regenerate his body when damaged—even from a Cataclysm. This ability enabled him to project pieces of himself as projectiles. He could also morph parts of his body, such as the tips of his fingers, into smaller hands to grasp objects, including Miraculouses.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Abilities
It became evident that his invincibility was linked to his admiration for the real Gabriel Agreste. However, when Adrien began expressing his frustrations and emotions about his father to Mister Agreste, the statue started to harden and eventually crumbled away.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Relationships
Friends/Allies
Ladybug
Théo has a crush on Ladybug, inspired by her heroism and admiring her greatly. However, he is upset when Ladybug doesn't show up to the reveal of the statue he designed, and he became determined to win her over after becoming akumatized as Copycat. He attempted to trick Ladybug into thinking he was Cat Noir, but his trickery was figured out, and, upset that Ladybug wouldn't take him over the real Cat Noir, he declared that if he couldn't have her, no one would. After he is returned to normal, Théo is happy by Ladybug's compliments on his statue and accepts her apology. Also recovering from his heartbreak, he admits he has come to peace about her and Cat Noir's relationship, not knowing that it was a lie.
Cat Noir
Théo appreciates Cat Noir's work for Paris, but he becomes jealous and disgusted of him when Cat Noir implies that he and Ladybug are close. While being Copycat, he sought revenge on Cat Noir by framing him for a crime and stealing his place as Ladybug's lover. Later, once no longer Copycat, Théo gets over his crush on Ladybug and accepts Cat Noir's relationship with Ladybug.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Trivia
In an early concept, Théo's full name was Théo Camiel.
In the original French version, Théo's supervillain name is L'Imposteur (The Impostor).
As Copycat, when he is imitating Cat Noir, he is voiced by Bryce Papenbrook, the voice actor who actually portrays Adrien/Cat Noir.
He makes various brief cameo appearances doing random jobs:
In "Dark Cupid", he is a furniture mover, helping to carry a large picture frame into Le Grand Paris for Chloé.
In "The Mime", he helps advertise the mime show by holding a sign.
In "Guitar Villain", he works as a DJ for XY.
In "Kung Food", he is a boom operator for the World's Greatest Chef contest.
In "Gigantitan" and "Sapotis", he is a rickshaw driver.
In "The Puppeteer 2" and "Lies", he is an employee at Musée Grévin.
In "Ladybug", he sells Eiffel Tower keychains at the Place des Vosges.
In "Heart Hunter", he works as a waiter for André and Audrey Bourgeois' wedding anniversary at the Le Grand Paris.
In "Collusion", he works as a waiter in the Café Crème on the Place de la Sorbonne.
This also makes him the character with the most known jobs in the city.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Trivia
Théo is one of three characters to be akumatized into a supervillain version of a Miraculous superhero, with the others being Lila and Chloé, but he is the only one to look exactly like the Miraculous superhero.
Unlike Volpina but like Antibug, Copycat can only use his power once, while Volpina can use hers as many times as she wishes.
It is unknown what would have happened had Copycat's time limit ran out after using his Cataclysm, but it can be assumed that it would have transformed him back to normal, like the real Cat Noir.
In "Animan", he is seen in the restroom of Collège Françoise Dupont, suggesting he goes there.
In "Gamer 2.0", Copycat returns as a playable akumatized villain as part of the Gamer 2.0's powers.
He's one of the four characters who impersonate Adrien Agreste/Cat Noir along with Chameleon, Gamer 2.0, and Félix.
In "Mister Agreste", he became the first akumatized villain created by Chrysalis to almost have an absolute victory over Ladybug and Cat Noir, having seized the latter's Miraculous and almost succeeding in getting the former's.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Trivia
Both of his akumatized forms were based on imitations: Copycat was based on Cat Noir, and Mister Agreste was based on Gabriel Agreste. Both also had the voice of the person they impersonated, and not Théo's usual voice, and both identities were based on members of the Agreste family.
In the Russian dub, however, Théo's voice doesn't change as Copycat, instead being voiced by his usual voice actor. Coincidentally, Gabriel and Théo share a VA, so despite having Gabriel's voice, Mister Agreste is also voiced by Théo's civilian actor.
Mister Agreste has some similarities to the DC character, Clayface: both have clay-like bodies that they can manipulate to their own liking, and can mimic the voice of another person. But Mister Agreste's shapeshifting abilities aren't as advanced as Clayface's.

title: Théo Barbot
text:
Théo Barbot - Trivia
Mister Agreste has some similarities to Zoé Lee's akumatized form, Sole Crusher: both are giants that resemble villainous characters (Zoé's half-sister Chloé Bourgeois for Sole Crusher, Gabriel Agreste for Mister Agreste), and captured Marinette/Ladybug (although civilian for Sole Crusher and Ladybug for Mister Agreste). However, unlike Mister Agreste, Sole Crusher doesn't become giant initially until she absorbs people with her shoes to grow larger and stronger. This makes Mister Agreste one of the few villains that their appearance is based on a civilian.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - Intro
The  is a panjas bracelet that, whenever Roaar inhabits it, transforms the wearer into a tiger-themed superhero with the power of Elation.
To activate the panjas bracelet, the user must speak the transformation phrase: "Stripes On". To deactivate the panjas bracelet, the user must speak the detransformation phrase, which is currently unknown.
The panjas bracelet is currently owned by Juleka Couffaine, who uses it to transform into Purple Tigress. It was previously stored in the Chinese Miracle Box and only lent out to her when the situation required it. But, as of "Re-creation", she now posseses the Miraculous permanently.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - Appearance
The Tiger Miraculous, when inhabited by Roaar, is a moderate orchid panjas bracelet that has a center spherical object with a yellow tiger paw print on it that slightly resembles the Cat Miraculous. On one side, there are four rose gold chains attached to it connected to a ring of the same color each. Another rose gold chain is attached to the opposite side of the jewel that connects to a large, rose gold hoop which serves as the bracelet part. If a minor is using the miraculous, the panjas bracelet starts running out of power, they make a beeping sound, and the paw prints disappear one at a time as an indication of how much time (one print is equivalent to one minute) Juleka (or another Tiger Miraculous holder) has left.
In Season 6 onwards, the center gem is a lighter pink and no longer has the tiger's paw print. The chains, rings, and hoop are now pure gold.
In its activated mode, the tiger paw print becomes black.
In its camouflage mode, the panjas bracelet changes color and form depending on whose possession it's in:

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - Appearance
In the possession of Juleka Couffaine, it bears a resemblance to the activated form of the Miraculous, although with the chain, rings and bracelet are black and sported a purple jewel that is attached to all chains.
In Season 6 onwards, the bracelet lacks the chains and rings, the hoop turned brown with a purple-pink jewel hanging from a small black chain.
When it was worn by Gabriel Agreste, it consisted of a silver band with an indent, connected to a single chain ending in a single silver ring.
When it was worn by Chloé Bourgeois, it resembled a gold, full chain panjas bracelet with a triangular jewel that connected the bracelet through its base and the part of the ring attached to a gold chain that was connected at the apex.
When it was worn by Marinette Dupain-Cheng, it consisted of a bronze circle connected to three chains, the ends of which met in a single bronze ring. The central chain had three strong aquamarine stones.
In its reforged ring form, it was a thick band with a circular surface, similar to the Cat Miraculous, inside of it was the symbol of the Tiger Miraculous which glowed fuchsia. It used to sit on the little finger of Gabriel's left hand.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - Abilities
The Tiger Miraculous has the ability to transform its wielder into a tiger-themed superhero, granting its wielder incredible superhuman powers of speed, endurance, agility, stamina and strength. It also makes the user nearly invulnerable.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - Abilities
Its special weapon is an unbreakable Bolas, a whip-like weapon with three weighted, striped balls on one end; it can be worn as a belt when not in use, functioning akin to a tail. This can be also be utilized as both a weapon, a communicator, and an object that can be used to breathe underwater. Its special superpower is named Clout, which gives the user the ability to charge their fist with powerful energy and gain a 'sudden burst of energy, courage, or fighting spirit. In order to obtain their goal, like defeating a villain. When they punch something, the energy is released through a massive force in which, when it comes in contact with a target, causes a shockwave. The target is overwhelmed by the force and blown back, rendered helpless. As long as the superpower isn't used by a minor, the wielder can remain transformed indefinitely. However, as soon as the superpower is used, the wielder loses power and the transformation wears off in about approximately five minutes. The panjas bracelet also has the ability to give the wielder the costume they truly desire.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - History
Five thousand years ago, a mage successfully helped the kwamis to interact with humans by creating magic jewels, which were called Miraculouses. In order to repay the mage, and to live on the physical world alongside humans, the kwamis decided to help humanity by letting humans utilize their energy and powers through the Miraculous they were bonded with, which included Roarr and the Tiger Miraculous.
At some point in time, all of the knowledge about the Miraculouses and their powers was written down in code in a book called the Grimoire, with very few people knowing how to decipher the code. Miracle Boxes were also created at an unknown time to store the dormant Miraculouses. To protect and distribute Miraculouses, the Order of the Guardians was formed and existed for many years. Throughout its existence, guardians trained younger generations to keep a watchful eye over the Miraculouses and the Grimoire, which were placed in the guardians' temple.
Many Tiger holders throughout history used Roarr's power for good, like Lǎohǔ in China, who started the legacy.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - History
172 years ago, after an disastrous event where a young Wang Fu used the Peacock Miraculous to create a sentimonster and his negative emotions and imaturity led to the creature rampaging through the temple and eating and destroying everything in its path, Fu was entrusted with the Chinese Miracle Box (which included the Tiger Miraculous) by a monk and was told to run away from the mess. However, on the mountain range outside the temple, in order to escape from the the monster, Fu jumped over a fissure on the ground - accidently opening the Box and spilling all of its contents on the snow. Due to his distress, Fu didnt notice he accidently left both the Peacock and the Butterfly on the mountain, alongisde the Grimoire, until it was too late and he was too far away to come back. Somewhere along the line, the Peacock got dangerously damaged, to the point of being improper for use - but, as it turns out, no one knew of this fact until it was too late.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - History
On a previous trip overseas with the Agrestes, Nathalie found the Butterfly and Peacock Miraculouses and gave the jewels to Gabriel. In "Representation", it was revealed that neither the Agrestes nor the Graham de Vanily couples could bear children on their own, so Émilie and Colt used the Peacock Miraculous to create Adrien and Félix respectively, but in doing so, they grew sick over time and were eventually left in a condition where they fell into an eternal slumber due to using the Peacock Miraculous in its damaged state.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - History
Desperate to fix his mistake, Gabriel Agreste began using the Butterfly Miraculous for evil to obtain the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses in order to gain access to their absolute power, becoming the supervillain Hawk Moth, later Shadow Moth (when unified with a now fixed Peacock Miraculous), and finally Monarch. This decision proved one of the most significant for the history of the series, as Gabriel began utilizing Nooroo's power to akumatize the civilians of Paris, France, trying to get one of them to draw out the current holders of the Ladybug and Cat Miraculouses, unintenionally helping start off Marinette's and Adrien's journeys as Ladybug and Cat Noir, and later, the rest of the Miraculers.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - History
One of the members of the Miraculers is Juleka Couffaine, who was chosen by Ladybug in "Crocoduel" to wield the Tiger Miraculous, becoming the heroine Purple Tigress. Juleka, from that point on, became a member of the team, helping Ladybug and Cat Noir during "particularly difficult missions". From "Crocoduel" to "Strikeback", Juleka was a temporary holder, meaning she would only receive the Miraculous from Ladybug when she was needed for the mission, and had to give it back after the crisis was solved.
Félix, after finding out about his true origins as a sentihuman and learning that the Peacock Miraculous could erase his and his cousin's lifes if it feel into the wrong hands, orchestrated a plan to capture all of the Miraculouses of the Chinese Box from Ladybug and traded all of them (besides the Ladybug and the Cat) for the Peacock, which included the Tiger Miraculous, succeeding in "Strikeback".

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - History
In "Destruction", Gabriel used a laser machine to melt down the Miraculous into a pile of dust, and then reforged it into a special Alliance ring for transferring Roarr's power of Elation to any akumatized villain who wore a regular Alliance ring. In "Re-creation", Marinette Dupain-Cheng manages to recover all of the Miraculous that were previously stolen. In "Miraculous London", Lila stole all of the Miraculous under Marinette's care in an alternate timeline, which included the Tiger Miraculous, in order to render her truly powerless and to fuse the Ladybug and the Cat to gain her wish without her interference, but her plan was ultimately thwarted by the combined efforts of Chronobug and Bunnyx, and the event was erased from the timeline.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - History
After the events of "Miraculous London", Marinette, having realized both instances of all of the Miraculouses being stolen happened because all of them were kept in the same place, and with the idea that centralized power is inherently flawed, and that distributing it among members of a society is a far superior idea, restored and upgraded the Tiger Miraculous by redesigning its original design and adding the Miraculous Call: a call feature that grants the holder the ability to summon other superheroes who possess a Miraculous from the Chinese Miracle Box in order to receive aid on their missions. This new feature is particularly useful, as the new holder of the Butterfly Miraculous, Chrysalis, is even more fearsome than her predecessor. After the alterations, the Tiger Miraculous was given back to Juleka permanently - putting Purple Tigress back on the map.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - Trivia
For an unknown reason, the Tiger's concept in the English dub is Elation, and Exaltation in the French dub.
Tiger symbolizes willpower, courage, and personal strength.
Panjas bracelets, more often called slave bracelets or hand chains, have become popular accessories in the Gothic subculture.
"Panja" is a Hindi word that originates from the Persian panje, and means "hand", "paw", or "claw".
The charged mode of the Tiger Miraculous looks similar to a tiger's paw when they have their claws out.
Due to an animation error, when Juleka transforms, the tiger paw is pointing the wrong direction. The claws are supposed to point down toward the bracelet, instead they point up toward the rings.
The Tiger Miraculous shares some similarities with the Cat Miraculous:
They are Miraculous of two felines: a Cat and a Tiger since cats and tigers are related in the Felidae Family Genus.
They are both jewels worn on their hands.
Their powers don't require the tools to be activated.
Both create a destructive/powerful force that is fused in their hands.
Both powers come from their Miraculous.
Their respective holders have a confident demeanor.

title: Tiger Miraculous
text:
Tiger Miraculous - Trivia
The favorite foods their respective kwamis like, have a pungent odor.
Both Miraculous symbols are paws.
But while the Cat paw is blunt, the Tiger paw is sharper probably to illustrate that tigers are wildcats. However, Cataclysm is more destructive than Clout.
The Tiger Miraculous also shares some similarities with the Bee and Ladybug:
All three have identical transformation phrases.
The holders' respective suits are covered with black decorations, such as spots, bee stripes and tiger prints respectively.
All three have whipping/flail weapons, the Ladybug Miraculous Yo-yo, the Bee Miraculous Spinning Top and the Tiger Miraculous bolas.
The holders of these miraculous had to find their confidence. For Marinette, she had to learn self-love, for Zoé, she had to find faith in herself, and for Juleka, she had to find her inner voice.

title: Thomas Astruc (character)
text:
Thomas Astruc (character) - Intro
Thomas Astruc is a minor character of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. He is a film director introduced in season 3. In the French version, he is voiced by and based on the real Thomas Astruc, the creator of Miraculous.
In "Animaestro", after the premiere of his animated film was overshadowed and his work went largely unappreciated, Thomas was akumatized by Hawk Moth into Animaestro, an animated supervillain.

title: Thomas Astruc (character)
text:
Thomas Astruc (character) - Appearance
Physical appearance
Thomas is a stocky man with dark green eyes, black hair, thick eyebrows, a mustache, and a beard.
Civilian attire
He wears a black shirt underneath a black hooded jacket, along with black pants and matching shoes. Around his neck, he wears an identification badge attached to a blue lanyard.
As Animaestro
After being akumatized, Thomas took on the appearance of a semi-transparent silhouette of himself filled with animated pencil sketches. He also wore a Ladybug-themed mask.

title: Thomas Astruc (character)
text:
Thomas Astruc (character) - Personality
Thomas is a kind and enthusiastic man who is passionate about animation and excited to share his films with others. Although he simply wants his work to be recognized and appreciated, he is often overlooked or ignored by those around him.
As Animaestro, he became determined to prove the power and potential of animation to everyone.

title: Thomas Astruc (character)
text:
Thomas Astruc (character) - Abilities
As a civilian
Thomas is the director of an animated film based on Ladybug and Cat Noir.
As Animaestro
Animaestro could transform into virtually any two-dimensional animated character or creature he can imagine, granting him a wide variety of abilities limited only by his imagination. However, he can only move while being observed by at least one person. If nobody is looking at him, he freezes in place and remains immobile until someone looks at him again.
He has been shown transforming into:
A dinosaur, referencing Richard Watterson from The Amazing World of Gumball.
A giant robot inspired by those from the Gundam franchise.
A black-and-white sheepdog hybrid with a high-pitched voice, resembling Mickey Mouse.
Majestia, a parody of Superwoman.
A ninja.
A small yellow bird referencing the 1968 French animated series Les Shadoks.
A unicorn.
A karate master inspired by Ryu from Street Fighter, capable of launching an energy attack similar to Goku's Kamehameha from Dragon Ball Z.
An anime magical girl, referencing series such as Sailor Moon and Pretty Cure.

title: Thomas Astruc (character)
text:
Thomas Astruc (character) - Etymology
The name Animaestro is a portmanteau of "animated" and "maestro".

title: Thomas Astruc (character)
text:
Thomas Astruc (character) - Trivia
Thomas' akumatization was inspired by the fact that he had to discard a season 2 script because it "wasn't satisfying enough".
Although his fictional counterpart is allergic to almonds, the real Thomas Astruc is not.
As revealed in "Queen Banana", Thomas is a graduate of Collège Françoise Dupont.

title: Thunderbird Miraculous
text:
Thunderbird Miraculous - Intro
The  is a unknown type of jewelry that, whenever the Thunderbird Kwami inhabits it, transforms the wearer into a thunderbird-themed superhero.
It is currently being stored in the Native American Miracle Box.

title: Thunderbird Miraculous
text:
Thunderbird Miraculous - Appearance
In general, the Thunderbird Miraculous is an unknown piece of jewellery. In charged mode, when Thunderbird Kwami inhabits it, it appears as a blue piece of jewellery with red, blue and white round beadwork with a white and blue feather from the center. If a minor is using the miraculous, the miraculous starts running out of power, they make a beeping sound, and the segments start discoloring one at a time as an indication of how much time (one segment is equivalent to one minute) the Thunderbird Miraculous holder has left.
In its Activated mode, the five segments are fully discolored.
In its camouflage mode, the miraculous changes color and form depending on whose possession it's in.

title: Thunderbird Miraculous
text:
Thunderbird Miraculous - Abilities
The Thunderbird Miraculous has the ability to transform its wielder into a thunderbird-themed superhero, granting its wielder incredible superhuman powers of speed, endurance, agility, stamina and strength. It also makes the user nearly invulnerable.
Its special weapon is an unbreakable unknown tool which can be also be utilized as both a weapon, a communicator, a method of transportation and an object that can be used to breathe underwater. Its special superpower, has no known name, which gives the user an unknown ability in order to obtain their goal, like defeating a villain. As long as the superpower isn't used by a minor, the wielder can remain transformed indefinitely. However, as soon as the superpower is used, the wielder loses power and the transformation wears off in about approximately five minutes. The unknown type of jewellery also has the ability to give the wielder the costume they truly desire.

title: Thunderbird Miraculous
text:
Thunderbird Miraculous - History
The Thunderbird Miraculous was created thousands of years ago by an Unnamed mage.

title: Thunderbird Miraculous
text:
Thunderbird Miraculous - Trivia
This Miraculous' identity was confirmed by Thomas Astruc on Twitter.
The Thunderbird is a spirit of various Native American beliefs. There are a number of interpretations and stories, such as it being the ruler of the sky, having the ability to control the weather, and being enemies with certain versions of the Horned Serpent.
Thunderbirds symbolize power, protection, and strength.
The Ladybug and Cat Miraculous are regarded as the most powerful Miraculous of their box and both co-occupied the top-centre space in the Chinese Miracle Box. Given that the Thunderbird Miraculous also occupies the top-centre space of its box, it is likely that it is regarded as the most powerful Miraculous of its box.
